I may not have played a large amount of the game but I feel I've played enough to give an educated opinion.
I tried the game in hope of finding a sort of WW2 themed Battlefield game as it promised large scale vehicular combat. I was then saddened when I realized that the only combat I would be seeing is tiny 'skirmish' battles with civilian trucks in place of the large panzer tanks I'd hoped for. But before even reaching combat I had to tackle the loadout menus, which are utterly confusing and drastically over complicated and lets not forget the propaganda for buying premium currency.
Eventually, I gave in and began to enter the skirmish battles with my  new US character. This I regret. I took up position behind a rock and began firing away at the grey-green enemies against the grey-green backdrop. I stared down the useless iron sights, which obstructed my view more than aided it and fired a round at an enemy that was closing in. Hit. However I was utterly flabbergasted when the enemy retorted with a barrage  of bullets from their machine gun. I was chopped down in a matter of seconds, questioning how I could fight these bullet spewing monsters. I continued the cycle: spawning, firing a measly few bullets before being destroyed by those blasted machine guns. The battle then boiled down to a relentless spawn killing and, needless to say, I was on the receiving end.
Frustrated by my beating I navigated myself to the shop in search of my own machine gun. I then had to pick my jaw up from the floor once I saw its price tag. But rest assured, you could easily purchase it with some 'premium' currency. Against my instincts I grinded enough money to buy another american rifle - this one a bolt action as i wished to begin sniping. If the starting rifle was bad then this one must have been the worst, it traded the semi-automatic fire rate of the starting rifle for a measly damage increase and even worse iron sights. Meanwhile, I'd also  unlocked the ability to finally engage in the actual battles the game advertises. It was nothing like what I'd hoped. Instead of being able to partake in ordered offensive and defensive battles I was greeted with the barrel of some high-rank tank controlled by a guy ten times my level. And to make matters worse, if I dodged the tanks then I would surely have my brain splattered by some grey blur of a sniper on a hill at the other end of the base.
And this is where I uninstall this game. To summarise; the games concept is brilliant however it is delivered so poorly I wish I'd never been tempted into downloading. I appreciate that the game is free however it is heavily unbalanced and easy to skip to the top of the leaderboard if you've got the  dough for it. Oh, and also the vehicle controls are so clunky and unresponsive you could brew a cup of tea by the time your bicycle makes a right turn, that is unless you aren't  blasted apart by any of the methods listed above. I would recommend this game to  nobody other than those who prefer  to 'buy' prestige rather than  earn it. Maybe you will  squeeze some fun out of this game but I for one will enjoy all the saved storage base this game once occupied.

• A pretty decent soundtrack

• Bright, clean visuals
• Challenging but never unfair difficulty

• Limited gameplay (although it's $3, so it is what you pay for)

• Occasionally painful color choices
Overall, if you're looking for a cheap challenging rhythm game, you could do much worse than this.

Ends up being a cookie-cutter shooter with little extra mechanics. After over 100 hours in Dirt Rally and about 60 hours in Dirt 4 ( this account and on a different) i come to the conclusion that i have to disagree with the huge amount of negative reviews that this game received. I am not saying the Game is superb in every aspect, sure it has its flaws and problems but most of them are minor, but they get blown up into this huge mess.  First i wanna talk about what the Game does good and does better than Dirt Rally.
Weight: The Cars now actually have weight and dont feel like cardboard like some in Dirt Rally. Its a satisfying feeling when you brake and you feel your weight shifting to your front, gaining more grip in the front at the same time losing some in the back.
Career: The Career is without a doubt a big  improvment to the rather soulless Career in Dirt Rally. The Option to create your own team, get sponsors and improve your standing with them. The whole teammanagment is actually really good and a lot of fun.
Immersion: The Immersion is a big step up.  Wildlife that is crossing the Stage out of nowhere. Opponents who parked their broke down cars in a ditch. Drones that almost  hit your windshield. Brakes that start acting up and make a ugly sound, or the sound of your transmission thats working clunky and makes you feel uncomfortable.  Every little detail adds a lot to the whole picture and the immersion is really good. i only wonder why CM removed the crowd running across the track stage  you approach, like they did in dirt 3. i think that was actually really cool.
RX and Landrush. I didnt really enjoy RallyCross in Dirt Rally but i surprisningly  really enjoy it in Dirt 4. I think its a lot of fun and the cars handle great. Landrush is good too just not enough events.
Now to the things that i dont really enjoy or like much. And i hope some of the problems are patchable.
Understeer: I agree with the ppl who complain about the cars being not tale happy enough and its rather hard or almost impossible in some cars to get the tail around. Sure you can change the car setup and tune them so they kick out the tail. but i shouldnt have to use a car setup  that is rather unrealistic and you would never use in rl, just so i can  drift around a hairpin.
Your Stage: I really like the idea of your stage. but the execution  lacks. The Tile system isnt really good. they need to add way more unique tiles. because getting in a 12 km stage 3-4 times the excet same tiles has nothing to do with unique stages. Then i would rather perfer the awesome hand crafted stages from Dirt Rally. If they add more tiles into the game, then i see a chance for Your Stage. But how it is at the moment it isnt really satisfying in a long term.
Pace Notes: Now to my biggest Problem with Dirt 4. Dirt Rally had it down to almost perfection. Sure a few calls were off but i could rely on my co driver and i felt confident going fast around a track, fast down long straights. Thats not the case in Dirt 4. I am affraid to fly down a straight. Because i dont trust my co pilot. To many times that i went 150 km/h in 5th gear and then got a right 3 call 2 seconds before actually hitting that corner. No way on earth i gonna make that corner. Plus that right 3 was more like a right 2, tight.  And i think the problem with the pace notes is because of the Your Stage. But it doesnt matter what exactly the problem is. What matters is that CM fixes this issue asap.  Because i am having blast with Dirt 4 but not being able to put faith in my co driver is holding me back and i always have to drive super cautious and second guess my co driver and i can never really get in the zone and just see the track, let it rip and listen to my co driver knowing i am in good hands.
All in all i have to say Dirt 4 is a really good game. Its not really better than Dirt rally but also not really worse. Its a tid bit different. But they are both really good Games that i enjoy playing a lot. And i hope that some of the  reviews will turn from negative to positive because the game doesnt deserve that much hate. Its the Best Rally/Offroad Racing experience together with Dirt Rally in the last 12 years.

In overall, this game best enjoyable if you're completely new and never played Dirt Rally as it seems that most negative reviews come from Dirt Rally players. The only reason why I (as a dirt rally player myself) like this game is because I played previous dirts in the past and I can kind of know what i'll be expecting from Dirt 4. If you want the ultimate Rally experience, I suggest Dirt Rally but if you want to have fun but still are in for a challenge, Dirt 4 is the game for you. I've got about 45 hours in Dirt Rally, and I play Dirt 4 for the rally. I have no interest in cool actiony game modes like Land Rush or Rally Cross. I actually hope they'd just made them into separate games, one for rally fans and one for arcade fans. I see little positives in cramming them all into one game. But then again that decision was probably not made with gamers' interests in mind.
I'm torn on whether or not to recommend this game or not, but I'm leaning towards not. Dirt Rally fans can get a fun game out of this, the rallying is still pretty challenging, but also very annoying in many ways, and ultimately not very close to Dirt Rally. Here are a few pros and cons:
Pros:
-The car weight feels good, as many have stated. I feel like the angle you're braking in now matters more, and you're more likely to spin out if you don't time your braking better.
-I like the idea of generated stages. Rally should be about mostly unfamiliar roads, not the same tracks you learn by heart, like in Dirt Rally after playing it for a while. Trouble seems to be that they get too same-y and predictable because of repeating sections. But it's a step in the right direction.
Cons:
-Handling feels odd at least at first and the setups feel off. Many times it feels like the car understeers at first so you have to turn the wheel harder, but then it oversteers very easily when you do. I don't understand why the developers couldn't learn from Dirt Rally and look at how players customised the handling and incorporate it in this game. Same goes for Force Feedback, how is it possible to make it worse than Dirt Rally when all you had to do was at least include the same setup? It feels a bit like when you map a steering wheel to controls designed for a controller, if anyone has tried that in other games, like mouse acceleration for wheels.
-Pace notes are still not good. Luckily they can be adjusted to earlier or later, but they still don't tell you enough. A left four is the same left four regardless if you're coming in fast in a steep downhill or a blind uphill. The co-driver is the same monotone voice as in Dirt Rally (although a different person, mind you) which could make you fall asleep. I feel like I have to concentrate harder on listening than actual driving because there's so little inflection in any of it.
-The racing AI in rally feels incredibly random. Many times even going flat out you're behind by 5 seconds after the first 30 seconds, other times you can spin or crash through fences and still be ahead. Certain randomness is welcome due to the human element in racing, but it's really disheartening driving really good on a stage and discovering you're still behind by a huge amount because the AI somehow just seemingly turned on some kind of boost. Having played Dirt Rally a lot you can feel this is really off. It shouldn't be possible to gain such a ridiculous amount of time in such a short distance much of the time. Hell, even driving on a highway you'd need some kind of supercar to be able to pull ahead that much in 30 seconds.
-I could do without the patronizing intros and tutorials like all Forza games and the like, but I guess it has to be there for the kids. Still, driving a rally with Nicky Grist as your co-driver, things like him going "If we win this we can buy new better parts for our car" sound really, really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Imagine any racing driver saying that before a race. Is this rally or is it Forza Rally? Please keep the arcadey things in the other game modes or at least turn it off in simulation mode for a less cringy experience.
Bottom line:
Sure, this isn't called "Dirt Rally 2", but that's not an excuse to water down the rally part to include more game modes that are clearly there to sell this to larger audiences. If the game wasn't marketed so heavily as "better than Dirt Rally", I wouldn't mind, but it was clearly touted as being almost a successor to it. Therefore I unfortunately can't recommend it.

I have been playing Command: Northern Inferno for a few weeks (30 hrs to date) and I only got this larger game to enable the 'Live' scenarios in my NI game really (because both games use the same program just with differnet missions enabled depending on which you buy) - although there are loads and loads of very nice community and standalone scenarios to try as well in this larger game.
The Live scenarios are fantasy scenarios released regularly. They are based around current news stories - like the ongoing Chinese Spratly Isands, North Korea's nuclear missile testing, Ukraine, and the Syrian Conflict. I love this idea because it gives the game a current, up to the minute, real world sort of gameplay.
This is a very addictive game where you have to make use of your assets like subs, ships and planes and employ them to suit the desired strategy and complete your objectives. It might be to get air superiority, or to remove all the SAMs and then strike a target, it might be to prevent enemy subs penetrating your area or even to attack or defend a whole country. The possibilities are endless. All the units are here from modern stuff all the way back to WW2.
The GUI is a bit clunky, the map could do with mouse controlled panning, but once you get used to it there is some real fun to be had with this game. And although they are only icons on a map (you can add photos of the units as well) your imagination takes over and you really see those MIGs evading Lightnings or whatever.
So I cant recommend it highly enough for people who love realistic warfare, tech heads and wargamers who want to play out a modern conflict like the Gulf War or the Falklands War.

If you are at all interested in modern combat, weapons systems, or air/naval operations, you must buy this game. It is seriously a crime not to buy this thing when it is on sale. It includes what probably is the world's most complete database on weaponry, aircraft, radar, ships, and a number of other modern combat assets. The game is not difficult to learn at all, the mechanics are fairly straight forward and simple, where it does get complicated is strategy and implementation. If anything, it is most definitely a hard core simulation rather than a game, but the variety in the types of scenarios give a feel for operations from the tactical scale - strategic.
If you are a board-wargamer or a PC wargamer and consider yourself somewhat serious about the hobby, you need to buy this, you'll not only enjoy it, you'll be about 20X more informed about modern combat assets and operations after messing with it for an hour or two.
Multiplayer is being eventually added which will be fun, but the AI itself is brilliant. The scenario editor is powerful and amazing, you can try out hypothetical designs or whatever your heart desires. You basically can emulate every clancy novel with this game lol.
Edit: I should mention that there arent really any graphics in this game, but who gives a ♥♥♥♥. You are talking to a guy that grew up on Dwarf Fortress.
More recent edit: People complaining about the graphics are very silly to me, you could play this thing on a ♥♥♥♥ing CRT TV with windows 97 and it wouldnt make a difference, it's about NATO/DoD symbols representing real world weapons and the implications of the use of strategic force and tactical doctrine. Simply put, don't buy this game if you are more concerned about graphics than the things actually going on in game you rubes.
The developers put in a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of time and effort and there are huge programming hurdles to be figured out to make things work natively with whatever fancy monitor you may have, the program is primarily bought by government clients who have it modded (ARMY, NAVY, CIA etc) for their own use. Their specifications I would assume would take a higher priority than some guy on Steam.

If you're playing with friends, this game is usually the best place to start. The perfect blend of creativity and strategy, Fibbage plays out well with almost any croud. While there aren't many noticable improvements or changes from the first Fibbage, more of the same is perfectly fine for a game so fun and packed with content.
The only dark spot in this pack, Earwax is hardly ever worth touching. The idea is to build a narrative using silly sounds, but the abundance of fart and toilet flushing noises gets tiresome after about two rounds. Compared to the other 14 Jackbox games, this one feels the most immature and lazily thrown together.
I still have no idea how this game works, but I'd be lying if I said it wasn't a ton of fun. A great game for completely winging it and half-assing strategy.
The greatest party game ever. Bar none. Quiplash puts Cards Against Humanity to shame, and it's the perfect opportunity to flex your creative and comical muscles. You'll get your money's worth on the pack from this game alone.
Bomb Corp. is a great way to make you hate your friends. I'd strongly recommend it as a teambuilding exercise or as a way to get the quiet person in the room to speak up. Only down side is it's a max of four players (although if you had any more, the game would likely become a headache).
Just grab a few friends, and start playing!

I play these games with friends quite often, though Quiplash XL gets the majority of our time. Jackbox brings a quirky, sarcastic vein of humor to cleverly-designed party games that makes for a great time. My only criticism is that using Steam as a platform makes it a little difficult to take to other places. It would be nice if the devs would bring the game to the Chromecast platform, like they've done with the Amazon Fire Stick.

I enjoy this game. Can it be frustrating? Heck yeah! Yes there's a big grind, especially if you make more than one soldier. I have 3 German soldiers. After playing this for more than 6 months, I've discovered the type of characters I like to use: Sniper, Paratrooper, and basic Infantry for tank busting. This game is best played with other people you know to work as a team. You'll find a much better experience playing on a team which works together. Otherwise, be prepared to lose quite a lot with everybody doing their own thing. Some of the players get verbally abusive when things don't go their way. I'm pretty sure they're LoL players taking a break. It's best to ignore them.
The beginning weapons are kinda lame, but you can work to the better stuff and feel you've achieved something. Although you can purchase weapons/equipment/clothing with real money, I don't feel this is a pay to win game. I believe this because you still must grind your way up to get the weapon modifiers. The mods really make the difference between a good weapon and a great one. You can modify each weapon to either change its damage, range, accuracy, rate of fire, and stability. Often increasing one decreases another.
The maps are pretty fun. I do however wish there were more. After a while, you'll figure out the best points on the map for the type of combat you prefer. I often find myself hiding in a bush taking pop shots at anything not in armor on the way to an objective. It gets hard to Rambo in this game as there's at least one person on the other team that has a counter for your preferred style of playing.
Bottom line: give it a try. It's free to play and you just might find a good group of people to play this with.
UPDATE: 7/15/2015
It's disappointing to see they made this pay-to-win. This game has always been hard for new people starting out from nothing. I do love the new weapons and scopes they've added, but I was able to afford them using my million+ in-game credits (silver) to get them. I feel new players have to either buy new weapons with real money or purchase a membership to advance their characters now. The cost to keep a weapon repaired eats up all the excess silver made from previous missions. I feel this way because I have a group of friends who recently started playing after the update and they all made this complaint. Eventually, they purchased memberships to get ahead of the silver problem. I love that they play now, but I don't believe they should need to purchase anything with real money to enjoy the game. If this really is their new model, they better start pumping out new maps and other content faster. I still recommend this game if you can manage to keep your sanity despite the huge disadvantage you'll encounter as a brand new player.

Ok, so first and foremost: this is very Left 4 Dead. If you're not sold on that, this probably won't change your mind. That said, it adds some substantial progression, changes up the objectives from mission to mission quite a bit, greatly beats the number of levels in L4D, and gives you 5 unique characters each with their own play style.
There are problems with how the hosting system works, and the difficulty is definitely on the hard end, but the vast majority of my experience with this has been excellent.

Notes after about 15h of playing:
+ Great WITH FRIENDS
+ I loved Left 4 Dead so this is right up my alley
+ Great HIT PHYSICS, and during games I've said many times "that was pleasingly violent-looking".
+ An action packed game, full of FRANTIC GAMEPLAY and tight situations.
+ Different traits and types in weapons actually influence gameplay of a class, instead just being "a sword +1".
BUT
- ALL GEAR is given as random drops: you get 1 new item after a completed map. I didn't think this is such a bad point, but many regard it as a deal breaking thing. To me, the hunt for better gear is not so important in this game than in some more rpg-like games.
- COPIES mostly all gameplay elements from Left 4 Dead, except for the better melee combat in Vermintide. Even the special Skavens do the same things as special zombies: Gutter Runner = Hunter ; Hookrat = Smoker ; Gasrat = Spitter.
- REPLAYABILITY might be a problem if the devs do not add more maps or other content in the long run.
- NET CODE isn't the best: there is sometimes significant lag, even when playing with a friend with a really good connection in the same country.
- This stems from NO DEDICATED SERVERS.
BOTTOM LINE: I love the game, but I'm an addict for the Left 4 Dead gameplay. If the devs improve the netcode, maybe add dedicated servers, and show promise to add content, we have a winner. Right now, I can recommend the game to people a) who can play the game with friends or b) are die-hard fans of this type of game.

My review will simply be about things I wish people had told me before I clicked 'install' on this:
1.) THERE ARE NO VENDERS TO SELL JUNK TO. Too much junk? Throw it on the ground. Click 'Ok' on popup. Did it have a little hammer icon on it? Whoops, looks like it was needed to craft some crap somehow. No big deal, was probably 1 of 90 of the item needed.
2.) GOOD LORD THERE IS A LOT OF CRAFT GRINDING. Let's say you wanted to wanted to make a 'Ham Sandwich' so you got +2% damage for 15 minutes (in a turn-based game). In WoW, you'd butcher some mobs and buy some salt and then cook over a fire pit and *BAM* 'Ham Sandwich' ... but not Wakfu. Nope. Go grind mining until you mine raw salt, make 3 raw salt into "Refined Salt' and then go out in the field and skin some mobs for meat. Hope you leveled skinning! Go farming for wheat. Make 3x wheat into flour. Draw some water. Bake the bread. Cook the Sandwich. Each of those skills, the Mining, Skinning, Farming, Baking, Cooking... are all separate skills with a METRIC TON of grind and there's a FAILURE CHANCE as you're crafting. ALL THAT FOR A SANDWICH BUFF THAT WILL BE OVER IN 1-2 COMBATS. Since there's no vendor to sell crap to once you're done, you either throw it on the AH (Governor sets a tax!) and it come down after 24 hours or you put that trash right on the ground because your bags are full.
3.) SPACE FOR ALL THE MATERIALS. There's no low-end bag vendor. You get two quest bags early on, but you'll fill up soon and the "You're too full" popups always have a "Are you sure?" annoyance chaser. Nobody makes low-end bags on the Auction House, so you're left stumbling through a horrible crafting system. Often, you'll need stuff from Tailor, Tanner, AND Armor crafting lines to get an item made... and the next upgrade will need you to make 3x-10x more of those AND use dungeon boss drops. Don't forget the failure chance! Or you can spend $1USD on 9-slot bags or $3-$10 on bank slots.
This game could easily be the MMO equivalent of a 'F-ville' game. You can walk anywhere without being attacked and just grind material collection. This could honestly be the best Mother & Son, Farming & Killing crossover game of all time... but that'd be such a rare niche thing to hit. If this was Steam Market-able, then you could play the game with all sorts of loot and then sell it or trade it on the market once you'd decided it was way to grinding and directionless... but you can't. Midkine (MDK) also known as neurite growth-promoting factor 2 (NEGF2) is a protein that in humans is encoded by the MDK gene.
Midkine is a basic heparin-binding growth factor of low molecular weight, and forms a family with pleiotrophin (NEGF1, 46% homologous with MDK). It is a nonglycosylated protein, composed of two domains held by disulfide bridges. It is a developmentally important retinoic acid-responsive gene product strongly induced during mid-gestation, hence the name midkine . Restricted mainly to certain tissues in the normal adult, it is strongly induced during oncogenesis, inflammation and tissue repair.
MDK is pleiotropic, capable of exerting activities such as cell proliferation, cell migration, angiogenesis and fibrinolysis. A molecular complex containing receptor-type tyrosine phosphatase zeta (PTPζ), low density lipoprotein receptor-related protein (LRP1), anaplastic leukemia kinase (ALK) and syndecans is considered to be its receptor.

Far Cry 3 is a pretty fun game. If you're looking for a story, however, don't look to the Far Cry series. The thrill and stealth of taking over a hostile encampment is super fun. The side quests where you have to kill a leader with a knife or hunt a wild animel are also challenging and entertaining. However, the game largely remains the same throughout with the exception of a few special missions and changes of scenery: take over base, restock on ammo, do some quests, repeat. The story also feels unfinished, and you build up your arsenal until the final moment of the game and then you realize you're done. That's it. The game is well optimized, however, and the combat makes up for the lack in story. Far Cry 3 gives you well over 30 weapons and tons of gadgets to fight with. In addition, the dream sequences and drug fueled nightmares are great, probably the best I've ever seen, managing to shine light onto Jason's inner thoughts and be really trippy at the same time. I would recomend buying it on sale, but it's not too expensive to buy full price. Far Cry 4 is really bad, this game's story is like gold compared to that. I haven't tried coop yet, but I think it could be fun to coordinate an attack. It's a game about wandering around and shooting pirates with your guns. If that sounds interesting, go ahead and buy it. Overall, I rate it 8 definitions-of-insanity out of 10.

I will preface the following with the fact that I have just started messing with this sim and there may be things I have not quite figured out or missed in the cursory reading of the manual and tutorials I have viewed. That being said I really wanted to like this game and it had been on my wish list for quite a while. From the onset it looked to combine the best of the Harpoon and Janes Fleet Command series while adding a touch of depth and realism both those simulations lacked. My overall experience in just the few hours I have been trying to wrap my head around the interface is it just the opposite.  It seems to be lacking in some crucial areas. For a game that requires one to meticulously plot out every waypoint for an air asset (lest you be condemned to micromanage and entire air war) it is quite frustrating that I cannot group aircraft and load mission sets without getting them airborne first. Basically, in a sim attempting this scope of realism I should have the ability to input an entire Op-Order broken into an individual Frag Order for each unit before they even leave the ground. Beyond that the friendly AI is absolutely stupid without the aforementioned micromanagement and the ability to adjust them on the fly is cumbersome, especially if you have multiple aircraft converging on hostile airspace. The editors claim an intuitive GUI and I hate to say that it cannot be further from the truth. A miss-click here or a fat finger there and something you have spent the last several minutes or even hours trying organize and execute takes a horrible turn for the worst. I again attribute this to the unintuitive interface and the stupid AI. To be quite honest, the designers could take a page from Falcon 4.0s real-time dynamic campaign map as the ability to edit strike packages, target sets and mission loadouts was actually quite intuitive and in many ways had the same meticulous attention to detail and threat modeling Command wishes to challenge the player with. I have yet to mess with the naval component though I am concerned I will encounter many of the frustrations I am experiencing with the air assets. I am hoping that this review is pre-mature and most of my gripes are coming from unfamiliarity as I see a lot of potential in this program and am excited to see if the developers will continue to improve on this platform but as of right now it just seems cumbersome and unpolished.

A smashing co-op rat brawling game that draws heavily from and adds to the Left 4 Dead games. Battles are fought furiously over a range of stunning locales and each weapon and every class has a well-defined role to play in vanquishing the nefarious Skaven horde. Vermintide's loot system adds replayability to the game and encourages players to take on tougher missions. 9/10.
Grapes:
+ Well-balanced character classes that complement each other well and require effective teamwork on the harder difficulties. This is enhanced by changing each characters' weapon loadout - do you take a crossbow for range and accuracy or a repeater pistol for mowing down smaller rats?
+ Gorgeous graphics and thumping sounds. Fighting in the Warhammer world has never looked or sounded this good. This makes fighting/ bisecting/ decapitating/ shooting the Skaven a real pleasure.
+ Beautiful and well-designed levels that aren't necessarily the same in every playthrough (check out The Wizard's Tower level!).
+ A loot system that rewards finding hidden items and playing on the hardest difficulties (which also improves the game's replayability).
+ A range of enemies that all require a slightly different approach (although Fatshark twists some Warhammer lore to get them in their roles).
+ A solid and helpful community that play the game; sharing the location of tomes and grimoires (to improve the chances of better loot) and generally helping each other out in a game. I've only been knowlingly trolled once in 30+ playthroughs, by some fool who read the grimoire and waited till the end of the map to put a tome in a location inaccessible by the rest of us.
Gripes:
- The biggest con for me is host player dropouts. If the host drops out of a game, the map restarts. That's it. The game simply doesn't allow you to continue or even provide you the option of going to the inn to choose another mission. So you have to sit in a loading screen mulling over your fury. While this issue is generally limited to public servers, it is infuriating. Please fix this Fatshark!
- Whilst being one of its biggest strengths, the game's loot system also causes the most controversy. If players are defeated in a mission, no rewards are provided, only some crystals that allow you to unlock gear traits. The level of gear awarded at the end of a mission is also effectively down to a random number generator, which many find madening, but I actually quite enjoy to a certain extent.
- The game's matchmaking can be rather poor, attempting to find/ join missions and seemingly failing over a period of ten minutes or more. Fortunately the player can simply select a mission from the server browser to get around this gripe.

Mount and Blade: Warband defined the best of RPGs of 2010. Start out with one main character, gather your companions armies, befriend lords and court ladies, and then strive to become the richest merchant, the most brutal lord, or the scourge of the world. You must have quick reflexes and a patient demeanor though, else you find yourself in a prison for a week and lose all your abilities. Warband is fun and addictive on easy mode and unforgiving on hard, so it is a welcome to causual and experienced players; the relatively low graphics of the game make it laptop friendly. Plus, the game is steam-workshoppable, so many users have recreated vastly different scenarios -- from Gekokujo (war for Japan's Shogunate of 1500s) to the American Civil War to The War of the Five Kings (A Game of Thrones). This makes the game's replayability high and enjoyable. I recommend Warband to anyone who loves adventure and rpgs with a little dash of strategy.

At first glance, I was kinda put off by the mixed reviews, however after purchasing the game, I can say that the initial few hours I put into this game have been quite enjoyable. I owned DiRT Rally for my PS4 and it literally made me want to pull my hair out; it was not an enjoyable experience for me mainly due to the lack of difficulty and driver aid options. Conversly, DiRT 4 has a lot more difficulty options and settings compared to DiRT Rally, which is highlighted by the option between the "Gamer" and "Simulation" handing pre-sets. It is a fantastic compromise that allows more casual gamers such as myself to have a good time while still giving hardcore rally fans their own "simulation" setting, so people who liked DiRT Rally's handling style will still be right at home. Additionally, the game feels fantastic with a wheel, however I personally had to turn up the force feedback quite a bit and I'm sure that this still plays great with a controller or even a keyboard. The Dirt Fish rally school is also a highlight to test out vehicles and just scew around. Career wise, DiRT 4 introduces the ability to customize livery, pick and choose your own sponsers, and builds heavily upon the staff mechanic from DiRT Rally. There are also plenty of career races to keep you occupied for hours upon hours, with all of the rally stages randomly generated, so no two courses will ever be the same. Overall, this is a must buy for any rally fan, casual or hardcore.
EDIT: There is a constant micro-stutter that occurs every 2-5 seconds that makes the game nearly unplayable. This is a known issue to codemasters and hopefully they will fix it soon.

So I'm coming at this from the "arcade" perspective. I'm the type of racer who plays with automatic transmission, using an Xbox controller, with all the assists on. I consider Dirt 2 to be hands-down the best Codemasters game, and I was *not* a fan of Dirt Rally, because of the unforgiving and squirrely handling model. I'm not looking for a realistic driving simulation, I just want to have fun driving cars fast. So how does Dirt 4 stack up as an arcade racing game?
Well, it's kind of boring.
I knew beforehand that the game had a random track generator for "INFINITE POSSIBILITIES", but what I didn't realize is that all of the courses in the main singleplayer rally campaign were created using this generator. Which means that all the courses feel really... samey. The courses *feel* like they've been randomly generated, they have no personality, they're all a completely forgettable series of Right-6, Hairpin-left, crest over jumps, with a handful of different background scenery options.
I thought maybe the Rallycross or Landrush modes might be more fun (since I really enjoyed them in previous games), but despite actually being hand-crafted, they too suffer from courses that feel just really dull and forgettable. There's nothing like the memorable and interesting London or Japan tracks from Dirt 2. There is a fun "Joyride" mode which has challenges involving either smashing boxes or a time attack challenge where you collect icons that lower your time and avoid icons that add to it. But it's not enough to save it.
The graphics are really bad. I don't know how they managed to make the game look worse than Dirt 2 and 3, but it's definitely a step backwards from previous games.
If you're looking for an arcade racing game with a mix of offroad/asphalt driving, you should get Forza Horizon 3 instead (seriously, it's insanely good). Or just go back and replay Dirt 2. Maybe there's something here for the racing sim fans (I can't really speak for that), but as an arcade racer there are tons of better games out there.

As a huge fan of Xcom, FFT, and the Starcraft series, this strategy game had me wanting to punch my monitor. I recommend other strategy game fans try it to see what they think, as the general consensus for this game IS positive. Just not positive enough for me.
Graphics: N/A - They're okay but I don't believe the graphics for this title factor into the score. If they did, it would be a solid 8/10. Mostly because they look clean for what they are, but aren't incredible by any means.
Sound/Music: 7/10 - Acceptable. I don't think the Dubstep type music you hear in some levels fit the setting very much. The sound effects the characters give are okay. Guns sound nice.
Gameplay: 6/10 - Similar to the Xcom series, the gameplay has some dice rolls when it comes to accuracy and possibly damage done to enemies. This is both a good mechanic and a frustrating one, and on some missions, not a whole lot of skill when it comes to strategy comes into play (i.e. the Ambush campaign mission for those who've played it). You have to get a pretty good start in order to have any chance of finishing.
It's a nice touch that characters level up and get better stats. You can apparently also name your team (although I did not).
I feel like 90% of the weapons are completely useless. I ended up using I think maybe 5 total weapons throughout the game. I tried using other ones but most of them ended up being just pointless and terrible. Perhaps they're implemented to give a bigger challenge on missions? (i.e. "You have to do this mission using only p90s!")
Shield class isn't very useful. Appears to be best used for missions with low class enemies (enemies that die fast and don't hurt much). Pointman class also feels pointless. Good starting class I suppose.
Overall: 6/10 - Yes, a 6. Again, I hate this game. It has flaws that will have me never playing it ever again. However, please try it out if you're reading this and you like strategy games. You may just fall in love with it. Good luck!

Reminiscent of Tomb Raider, but in a much less primitive setting, Hydrophobia is technically impressive with a decent story to boot.  The fluid effects were awesome, although they sometimes brought my system to a crawl (it's rather dated).  The combat could get tedious, however, especially in the final boss, and the short playtime was disappointing... but for the price, I really have nothing to complain about.

Hydrophobia is a game that's got great gameplay and a decent amount of puzzle solving.  Sadly, though, it runs out of both pretty quickly.  A few more mechanics would have made it amazing, but it works with what it has.  This leads onto the game's major flaw: Hydrophobia is very short.  One can understand why this is, though, the game's levels explore its limited mechanics thoroughly, and more would have become repeditive.
The controls are a little bit awkward, it's clearly a console port and doesn't handle keyboard and mouse so well and has some weird accelleration.  It also ran my laptop very hot with the settings turned up to mid-high, but there wasn't much stuttering.  The game could probably be optimised somewhat.  If the developers had have spent more time polishing the game, it would have been quite excellent.
Overall, it's an entertaining little game.  Don't expect it to be taken away by it, but it's worth the few dollars you'll pay for it.

Review from a nerdy noob to nerdy noobs (not a super Navy Officer Rear Admiral 2.0)
So I love overly complicated games like this. Basically, if you fill a game with numbers and data for me to interpret I'll eat out of your hand like a recovering anorexic bunny.
That said, I've written a similar review for Hearts of Iron III and let me tell you that this is nothing like HOI. I mean, I pride myself on being able to grasp things quickly, but holy smokes this one is complex (I enjoy sucking and learning ways to improve my tactics via experimentation and reading the 172 page manual which is like your civilian version of Navy/AF OCS/OTS. That's what I've been trying to do but it's just a bunch of intro. You'l eventually need to do some deeper research unless you're already a Naval or Air Force officer in which case please teach me your ways).
Anyways, I'll add more to this review when I learn more about this game. Just know that it's not a pretty polished game like HOI IV. Quite literally it plays like what I imagine a Navy Intel officer would see (of course I don't have a TSC so I have no clue what they actually see. Maybe aliens but the game doesn't simulate aliens for some reason. Source: Have been abducted!). Basically, you don't zoom into things smoothly. It's literally quick movements around the map. You right click where you want your camera to center (not smoothly dragging around). Not sure how realistic this is but you'll get used to it fairly quickly.
Another thing to note is the way the game displays. Basically it's just a big map with a bunch of displays and buttons and stuff BUUUUT....when you click stuff these popups display (so it's not your typical fullscreen game either. It's like an application. This is good for this game though. Just understand that sometimes you might need to look at multiple displays. If you have multiple computer monitors then this will be perfect. I have two set up. One has the map at all times the other...well the other should have the systems and weapons info but instead has the damned manual because so far my main accomplishment has been getting my ships sunk (seriously Morocco kicked my♥♥♥♥♥and I'm leading the bloody Spanish Armadda...which is really just four ships and a sub but whatever. Close enough).
Ultimately, if you're a super nerd who likes maps and spends their free time reading military crap or you're a super soldier who does all the Hooah stuff for 10 hours a day and wants to sit back for a nice session of hooah (or hooyah for the Navy maybe...I think?) then get this game.
Seriously, though, expect to put a lot of time in to accomplish anything. I recently got this game and have thrown a few hours in and it doesn't appear that the ships I lost will be recovered...Oops. I uh...I should probably resign!

Meridian: Age of Invention is a solid little time and resource management game and a worthy timesink if you enjoy the genre. You play a professor who travels around various kingdoms testing new inventions and solving problems.
The graphic style has a steampunk vibe and the graphics themselves are reasonably good.
The story is forgetable and music chosen gets very repetitive and got turned off quickly.
The gameplay itself is a little different from other time and resource management games in that you control two types of minion. Workers and couriers. The Workers remove obstructions, fill holes, and work in the mines. The Couriers carry resources to and from out-buildings and the central hub. As new minions cost money, there's a small amount of balancing whether or not a new minion would return the investment required in purchasing them.
The game tries to mix up the genre with some levels being more point and click and quick time events than time and resource management, but you don't really encounter until late in the game.
The only negative I had was that difficulty curve (if you are going for gold results), the game seems too easy, but every 5 or 6 levels, you hit a difficult level that requires multiple attempts and strategies to beat, most levels I completed on first attempt, once you beat the difficult level, you are cruising through the next half dozen before the next tricky one.
Overall, it's a cheap game, enjoyable for the most part assuming you like time and resouce management games,  and worth spending some time on. Recommended.

Meridian is a super casual, lightweight time management game with next to no challenge whatsoever. But with such a cute art style and fast-paced levels, it really doesn’t matter as the game is incredibly fun!
Time management titles are usually classified as casual games, but Meridian: Age of Invention takes that to a whole new level with how easy it is. Which is a bit strange, considering that it has a remarkable pace for its genre, but this combination of speed and the lack of challenge create a really enjoyable combination.
Gameplay itself is not like we can find in most contemporary time management games. There are very few obstacles to clear, the focus is on Build-a-Lot type property management: you build and/or upgrade houses (with pluming and electricity) to generate revenue, which is then used for more upgrades and achieving the level goals.
The tricky part is that workers do the improvement but couriers have to transport the goods and collect the rent, so manpower management plays a pivotal role.
The developers didn’t really put too much effort in porting the controls from touchscreen, so resources need to be dragged, not just clicked on. It may sound a bit aggravating, but it also makes sure the player is constantly paying attention, eliminating much of the potential boredom that stems from repetition—resulting in a chilling, but not boring casual game with plenty of levels. Which could be just what one is needing for lazy afternoons.

Door Kickers is an immensely fun and at times highly frustrating game for all the right reasons. Tasked with commanding a team of SWAT members in numerous different scenarios, in a top down tactical manner. You need to plan and execute raids upon drug lords villa's, a hostage situation in the suburbs and anything inbetween.

You need to consider each and every detail of these raids, from the men you are picking to go on it, the classes best suited for the job and which weapons would be most effective. When all of this done, you are able to map out routes and commands for each member of your team before executing your plan. This can lead to moments of brilliance where your best laid plan completely cleans out an area without a casualty or it can end in a flashbang not going far enough into a room and your entire squad being gunned down in a doorway.

This is where Door Kickers shines, through its iterative process. Not every plan is going to go off without a hitch so to progress through the harder levels you need to learn from your mistakes, change your plans on the fly and be ready for anything that could go wrong because once the bullets start flying it can become increasingly difficult to keep all members of your squad alive and well.

The rating system also encourages multiple tries at levels, trying to get a better score or finish a challenge such as completing the level with only the one SWAT member. The game also offers a campaign mode, where the stakes are ramped up even further. As any of your team who die on campaign missions will stay dead until the end of the campaign. Adding another level of caution to your plans as the lives of your team become even more fragile.

It's through this harsh and sometimes punishing ruleset that moments of brilliance shine through as you manage to plan out an elaborate and well executed raid with all the considerations of a real SWAT leader.

Quick review:
Amazing title that takes the laurels from Harpoon. Some intense battles to be had and the number of assets available is unbelievable. The DLC are scenarious and you can have fun fighting in the Syrian Civil war and so forth and understand why somethings happen the way they do.
It is a bit let down by a lackluster AI and a confusing UI. The UI in particular is ancient and not very user friendly. Even after you somewhat get used to it you will still get a bit lost.
Long Form:
Well, if you like games where it takes a long time to do a scenario because you have absolute freedom, you are going to love this one. You can change everything in a given scenario or create your own and have fun seeing the forces pitted against eachother. You can even play vs a friend in local coop hotseat (by running the scenario through the editor).
I wouldn't call this game fun in the normal sense you usually expect in a game. You will see no images of what you are doing and what is happening. It is all abstracted to symbols. The UI is not fun either. For me, it is the worst thing about the game. It is that bad. Sure you start to get used to it but you will still struggle. Of course, tutorials and RTFM are essencial here otherwise you might get a bit lost and without a clue of why your precious ships are being torn to pieces by a rag tag force comprised of an HMG mounted on a polank of wood, some glue and an old man who has a speech impedement that makes him unable to pronounce the word turnip.
Now this game is fun FOR ME and if you are like me and like to watch numbers going down on a screen and calculate hit probabilities and force comparisons (statistics) and you have a soft spot in your heart for military hardware, then by jove will you have a blast in this game!
Seriously, even the UI will stop being such a hassle after a while and you will start seeing your simulations bear fruit. Mind you. This game has the mark of a truly realistic game in that when you win a scenario you are left with a feeling of bewildered disappointment as there are not loud noises and flashy colors saying "WOOOOO!!! You are awesome. Like, literaly the best general ever on the face of the Earth!" and you probably have no clue about what just happened in the past 3 hours while you moved your symbols about the map.
You just get a white square saying "Scenario over, now we will show you the score". underwelming really but usually ultra realistic games like this one usually don't go about blowing your horn (future update maybe?).

Hotline miami 2 is a video game. It raw, unpleasant and downright mean. Heart pumping, thrilling, intense. All words tha describe this game rather well. Its a pure video game. Story takes a second seat to the gameplay. But that is okay, as even that works, in that the "story" weaves itself into a meta-commentary about video games, that you may or may not find enjoyable. If you dont, thats okay. The game dont expect that of you.
It Hotline miami 2 fun? Yes, a lot. Is it fun for everyone? Not at all. The game is harder than the first, simply due to level/enemy design. It forces you to play a little diffrent than last time around. In Hotline 1, running, gunning and improvisation was the name of the game. In Hotline 2, planing, being carefull and thinking it through is the prefered manner of beating a level. You would think this would ruin what made Hotline 1 great, and to some people i am sure they felt that way. But if you have an open mind, you will realise that it still feels and plays like Hotline 1. Instead of finding satisfaction in a perfectly pulled of improvisation, you will find thrills in perfectly executing a plan. You still get the thrills, the heart pump, the action. Its all still there.
The music is also pretty good. Its more of what was in 1, which is by no means a bad thing.
Is Hotline miami 2's change in gameplay style a commentary made by the developers, pointing fun at how players gain attached to silly simple things such as a gameplay flow and how they might lash out and refuse to change if it is no longer familiar to them? Maybe, who knows. They can fill their game full of hipster "too deep 4 me" social commentary, as long as they keep making some of the most, thrilling, dark and fantastic games.

Contagion crashed 4 times over the course of 2 hours and with very long (3-4 minute) load times, that's really irritating.
The graphics are shockingly poor, even by 2014 standards.
The sound is broken.  For example, if you let out a zombie scream (after you've become one), it plays maybe once or twice but then you just get the animation.  You'll also hear sounds that are not coupled to direction.  Got headphones on and there's gunfire to your left?  No there isn't.  And this is for ALL sounds, not just some.  Might as well just play with the sound off as it is quite literally worse than useless.
If you die, you become a zombie.  Good luck trying to find that one survivor holed up somewhere in a huge map loaded with explorable buildings.  When you do find them, hopefully they aren't barricaded in a room (they will be) because you can look forward to getting killed quickly, then spending five minutes getting back to where they are (provided you know the map well enough to know how to get back to where you were), and get killed again.  And that's if you're lucky and they haven't moved.  If so, back to square 1 which can take 20-30 minutes of just wandering around.
You think there'd be a game timer move the game along.  Nope.  You stay in this state until all survivrs are dead.  Invariably, the survivors get bored and just die intentinally because that's more fun than the self-barricaded stalemate.  Nothing serves as an impetus for the survivors to be pushed toward action like a countdown to a carpet bombing or the last evac helicopter leaving.  Success is survival and if that means sitting in a closet with three bullets forever, your optiosn are to either stay in that closet forever or intentionally die.
What's irritating is that it's a generally interesting concept but everything about it, and I mean everything, is fail.  That this game got a "mostly positive" review is mind-blowing.  It's terrible.  I wouldn't play it if it were free.

PREFACE: Buy this game on a sale. Yes or No recommend isn't really sufficient here, because it is a mixed review.
Contagion is an FPS game where you fight to survive against zombies. The zombies can only be killed by headshots. What sets contagion apart from other games is that players can become infected. A zombie gets a bite off and you may slowly change. You lose hearing, vision grays and then you violently turn into a zombie, and your job is to kill your former friends.
Lets run through the game and see what goes well and what does not
Game play: Its fun, but its hurt by laggy servers. The server browser is bad, making it hard to find a good game. Its really fun to play, trying to find ammo, get headshots and not get bitten. Its also fun to hunt other players as a zombie. But thats where the problems start. Player controlled zombies benefit insanely from the poor servers. Its hard to hit the player zombies head, especially because its probably not where it appears on your screen. You have to spray them down or blast them with a shotgun because you just need a wall of bullets to find the head. Overall the gameplay is fun, but don't try to get competitive or anything. Its decent, but its certainly not great.
There is a good variety of Maps, gametypes, and weapons.
Overall this game is good but hurt by poor servers and a small community.

Over the past two years or so Games Workshop has become far more liberal with their licensing and fans of the franchise will have noticed a massive influx of potential Warhammer and Warhammer 40k games slated for release in the next few years. This brings us nicely to our subject today; Warhammer 40,000: Regicide.
Regicide is, at heart, a chess game set in the 40k universe and players will find themselves taking on the roll of either Orks or Space Marines in a bid to reduce their enemies to wet gobbets of flesh... You can read the rest of this review here

This game is not Chess!
It is more like the game they play on the Milenium Falcon, where Wookies tear your arms off if you lose.

Nice design!
Don't have to be good at Chess to be good at Regicide!

Sure you can compare this game to Chess, and use it to play regular BattleChess - there is even a way to make it a rather ugly looking 2D board with regular token pieces, but there are plenty of free Chess programs to choose from.
The animations and camera movement and voice samples are kinda annoying if you are playing Chess, but idk why you would be playing that game (except for novelty) when you could be playing REGICIDE!!!
When you are playing Regicide - all the animations and voices make it feel pretty damn epic..! (I turned the voices off, cos there are like 2 samples repeating and it drives me nuts...)
I've only played a few hours of the game, and I really like it!!
Regicide incorporates two different rule sets and strategies into one (awesome) new game. It does it seamlessly and in a way that makes both the Warhammer and Chess elements more fun to play!!
The new rules are very well designed, and it encourages taking risks with your Chess play. You will quickly learn that, in Regicide, any Chess gambits or strategies you usually practise will no longer work! Both the different plays, Chess and initiative, are equally important if you want to win.
Clever use of initiative can turn a few cowering prawns into a deadly band of fearless space marine, accompanied only by their captain, that somehow manage to stay alive long enough to brutalise everything on the gib-strewn battlefield... I mean Chess board.
Being able to remove a piece without capture can lead to a lot of extra strategies - and the AI appears to take account of these and sometimes compensates. Pretty neat.
A game versus the AI on Expert level lasts around 15-20 minutes. That is a challenging, but winnable level for anyone who can't remember what it is like to not know the rules of chess.
Don't bother "warming up" with lower difficulty levels than you plan to start off with - it can feel like a slog and the step up in difficulty and thinking required per level is quite a lot, so it almost made me feel unprepared after facing only the easier difficulties first.
Whether you play orcs or space marines does make a difference - there are slight advantages to both, any they require subtly different tactics to get the best out of the %'s and power-ups.
There are a few things about the game software itself that let you know it is in development, a few bugs and glitches, but nothing major.
If the game never had another keystroke of work done on it, I'd think I spent £10 on something that is decent enough already. It is very original and has a good, leisurely action movie kinda pace to it.
You don't have to be good or bad at Chess to be good or bad at this - it's Regicide.
A 3-4-player team/vs. version of this game is TOTALLY POSSIBLE!!
I hope there will be more races and an army painter, perhaps.
If there was some scenario or level or board design option, like with Shadowrun - I would be very happy.
Man, you could even make Space Hulk like levels, or make levels around pieces movement, so that they had to travel a little to reach objectives - you could have movement puzzles, Chess puzzles (but with guns!), intiative puzzles, combinations, chasms, switches, geometry and rotation puzzles... man... I would LOVE a level editor for this game.

Since I've played 12 Labours of Hercules (though I can remember Build-a-Lot), I've been more receptive to casual time management. However, where I appreciated the simpleness of Hercules and the humor in it, I'm always afraid to find complex stuff to do.
In Meridian: Age of Invention, you have to clear 55 levels with workers and carriers: you build houses, you repair some, you can work in a mine to find resources to keep building, you collect money thanks to the carriers that can transport letters, fresh food or the result of your hard work. However, the more you advance, the more you have to do, mainly because a crazy inventor is trying to help everyone (people in the desert, living on island or even a pilot). So, you end building water towers, eletrical plants, etc.. And guess what? You can tie the houses to these and get a generous income that your carriers have to take if you don't want it to be wasted. Sometimes, you have bandits that will take your money unless you give them a certain amount. Sometimes, you have obstacles that your workers have to destroy or repair so that you can advance. Sometimes, you have treasures chest with some precious gold.
However, if you end up falling short with one ressource, you have a market: pay 1000 gold and you'll get 500 building materials, pay 100 building minerals and you'll get 50 gold for example. You need to keep in mind that it can help you speed up the process.
Each level is timed and you have medals/coins corresponding as your best time. Getting a gold medal is the supreme reward, however, while some levels are easy, others will need a perfect timing and for that, practice is the best, as you can redo the levels.
Finally, between all the work on land and on water, you have some actions with the levels at the end where you need to land planes at the right base (green at the green hangar, etc...). It's reminding me of Flight Control HD, minus the collisions. It's a welcome change.
I'm not really fan of the graphics, I find them a little dark, I would have preferred more colors and cheerfulness. The soundtrack is nice.
However, while the gameplay is polished, there are two problems with the title: the in-game achievements and the crashes due to fail getcontext error. While for the latter, it can happen  anytime, some ingame achievements aren't unlocking despite meeting the requirements. Apparently, given the discussions on the forum, it's happening for many of the players and concerns the 10 hours or less trophy, the gold at every level one and the unlock all trophies (which is normal if you get a problem with these two). For now, the developers are just asking to forward your data and I didn't see any update for that for now.
Despite these two unpleasant surprises, Meridian: Age of Invention stays an enjoyable casual time management game, not too difficult. For the price, you're not robbed at all.

Overall, Dirt 4 is a good game, but comparing it to Dirt Rally is inevitable. It has a good variety of game modes, cars, and tracks that makes driving fun (or frustrating) with a wheel or controller.
Your Stage is a good idea, but like with almost anything procedurally-generated, patterns are easily identified.
Graphics are nice and pretty, but it looks like it requires more power than Dirt Rally does.
Sound is ok, but it feels like Dirt Rally's sound had better processing. It made me feel like I'm really in the car.
Gameplay and handling are a bit vague with a wheel. I can't feel the car enough. I never know if I'm going too fast for a corner. I don't get a proper sense of speed, even when everything around me is blurred as I fly past the crowd and trees, redlining on 6th gear.
Customization and team management are cool.
Dirt Academy is cool.
Co-drivers are different now. While I have a variety of voices and languages to choose from, the call outs sound too static and immersion-breaking, compared to Dirt Rally. The comments before and after a stage are cool though.
I realize that I have more negative things to say than positive. I think these can be adjusted in the future by Codemasters. There are a few other things that might need fixing, but really, I just wish steering did not feel vague and weird. It can still be a fun game if you can deal with the steering. So as of now, at this price, look for Dirt 3 or Dirt Rally if you haven't already, or maybe something else.

Mount and Blade: Warband defined the best of RPGs of 2010. Start out with one main character, gather your companions armies, befriend lords and court ladies, and then strive to become the richest merchant, the most brutal lord, or the scourge of the world. You must have quick reflexes and a patient demeanor though, else you find yourself in a prison for a week and lose all your abilities. Warband is fun and addictive on easy mode and unforgiving on hard, so it is a welcome to causual and experienced players; the relatively low graphics of the game make it laptop friendly. Plus, the game is steam-workshoppable, so many users have recreated vastly different scenarios -- from Gekokujo (war for Japan's Shogunate of 1500s) to the American Civil War to The War of the Five Kings (A Game of Thrones). This makes the game's replayability high and enjoyable. I recommend Warband to anyone who loves adventure and rpgs with a little dash of strategy.

Combat is mostly melee with the exception of one or two classes where you might find yourself using ranged more frequently, which means a lot of hectic flailing around at waves of rat-people. This can be fun or frustrating depending on whether or not that playstyle suits you.

Okay, first off I want to tell that I've always been pretty stoked about Artix Entertainment.. Played the original AQ as a 6-7 year old kid, then went on to Dragonfable etc., so ofc I had to try this game out too.
It's the first time they do anything like this.. A 3D MMORPG set in the universe of AdventureQuest and they always "Launch" their games and builds half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ They even admit it themselves and say that it is intended that way.
Pros:
- First of all, this game has HUGE potential. Artix Entertainment has proven that many times before, so just be patient, fellas!
- The game has the classic humor from the previous AdventureQuest games, which makes reading quests and item descriptions fun as always
- A whole new way to explore BattleOn, fight favourite enemies from the world of Lore + there's a band of monsters playing instruments at the Inn.
- It might be grindy, but I see this as a good thing myself.. I've always loved to farm monsters, grind for exp and materials for crafting and what not and trust me.. You WILL grind a lot in this game if you want progress.
- The admins speaks in the chats, role play as their characters and whatever, making things like server resets funny/less tedious.. Like when Cysero pressed the butten and reset the world 3 times in a row, just to spawn "Oooops" monsters in the town of BattleOn.
- You can play this crossplatform! Tablets, Mobile devices and PC are the ports at the moment.
- The gear you've equipped show up on your character & it is possible to review the gear before you buy/craft it.
- There are microtransactions but not in a "Pay to win" style. You might get an XP boosting pot that only works for 20 minutes and gives 50% more exp gained while active, but I've managed to reach max level without it, no problems there.. So yearh, the microtransactions are NOT NEEDED to enjoy this game!
-  Loot is individually shared. All you've gotta do, is to hit the monster and deal damage before it dies. Then you are guaranteed EXP and gold. So no ninja looting for this game!
- MOSTLY a nice and friendly community. I've met many people in the game, having good conversations and actually making friends. Sadly, there are many leechers, rushing to the last area, trying to get fast exp by asking over and over for help.. Other than that, pretty good so far (Y)
Cons:
- It's chunky. Both in graphics, way of controlling, the UI is designet for Mobile users and there are bugs. Plenty of 'em.
But hey, keep in mind that it IS an open beta build at the moment. I trust AE, and I really do believe they'll make this game into something big.
- Lack of variations. 3 classes so far, very limited gear but with 3 different "Specs" for each class.. They mostly look the same, if not totally.
- Level cap is at 15. But ohhh, don't think that it is easy to get to max level.. "The Bridge" is a thing all players must face one day, and it is a living hell if you hate grinding.. Also, if you want to get any EXP/progress, you more or less have to play as a Warrior and be in a group of at least 5 people.. Otherwise you wont be able to make it through and keep your sanity. Level 13-14 is 63,5k Exp, where 14-15 is 738k exp.
And at one point, the quests simply stop and you'll have to grind monsters for EXP, or replaying dungeon quests, which brings me to my next cons:
- Dungeons and dungeon keys. Oh boy, where do I start with this one..
There are quite a few dungeons in this game already, which is lovely to me personally.. I've always loved dungeons, so why would I put it in a cons??  Well...
The dungeon system works that way, that you use 1 dungeon key PER dungeon entry.  Not per cleared dungeon, but per entry. Every 3 hour, you get a new dungeon key up to 20 as a max.
And it happens now and then, that you enters a dungeon that is filled with low levels who leeches off the exp and loot, taking up a spot for other people who can actually be usefull inside the dungeon.
- No party/look for group function.  This game has no way of creating a party with friends, making it extreemly hard to farm dungeons together.. Just gotta join at the same time and hope/pray to Jeremiah Kerbit that you'll end up together.

I  have been despondent since the demise of Harpoon. I am an ex-submeriner from the cold war era. I purchased the Command, Northern Inferno package to see if it was comparable in realism to Harpoon. It took one scenario to see that it was far more advanced and realistic. I immediately bought the main Command Naval wargame. If you are a naval historian or inthusiest this is a gamers wet dream. Even if you dont play the game, the data base is worth many times the cost of the simulator. James Warships and weapons references are all here for the relevant time envelope. The very best feature in this simulator is that there are no built in rules. outcomes are entirely dependant on your imagination and the platform capabilities. You can develop very advanced tactics with only practical limitations. I can truly recommend this product for serious naval war fans.

Calling this game a "hardcore" military simulator is underestimating the scope and difficulty of this game. This is less the nice, clean cookie-cutter American hardcore where everyone is smiling and having fun and more "A Siberian Movie."
This isn't so much a game and more the civilian version of a teaching aide a military academy might use to train naval officers. (And I believe it is exactly that because I've heard the British Royal Navy uses a special version in the classrooms.) yes the price is high (and like an idiot I bought it at full price) but it goes on sale often and, again, it's not really a game but a teaching tool for military tactics.
Command is the spiritual decendant of the game Harpoon, which I played on paper with dice on my friend's living room floor because his house was bigger and we could lay out the scenario properly. Harpoon was developed by Larry Bond, a US Naval Academy instructor, friend and co-author of Tom Clancy and author of a few technothrillers himself.
The computer version was a brick wall of complexity. Command is more like that meme about the learning curve of Eve Online where it turns into a cliff with bodies piled up at the bottom, people crucified at the top and bulldozers pushing more over the side. Make one mistake in the first ten minutes and you could lose a four hour scenario.
How come it is so expensive?...Do they have to pay royalties to someone?
Very steep learning curve. Very satisfying  dropping a nuclear depth charge on a sub.

First, I purchased this game from Matrix. I realize that my review will not count toward Command's overall rating. Steam might think that makes me a fan somehow, but not at all.
Is it a good game?
The bottom line is NO. It's painful to play. Others might have you believe it's complicated and difficult. It's not at all--although looking at a database table or spreadsheet might seem disorienting at first.
This product, however, is simply and poorly designed.
I personally don't care about the windows interface or freely available NASA map (with ugly NATO icons), but simple player tasks are difficult/awkward and the responsiveness overall is choppy. Even simple map panning is awkward. The devs clearly bring the intricacies of the database to the forefront at the expensive of usability and realism.
How could realism suffer in such a "hardcore" game?
Because it is solely focused on equipment and technology (their beloved database/OOB), so the realism (and fun) of how strategy, operational art, and tactics synchronize is totally missing from the game.
The front end of the game provides no realistic (or intuitive) simulation of the needed tools and controls. The "mission editor" is about as close as they get, but even that comes off poorly considering other games.
Want to fight a modern Korean War in a theater-level air/sea campaign? You can't.
Want to implement your own Silent Hawk helicopter into a special ops raid scenario? No. You can't touch the locked database without making an approved, licensed, paid, DLC product for them.
Add to that, every single unit in the game acts with the same level of morale, surprise, training, competence, leadership, etc. The devs focus entirely on a tech database which works exclusively to model equipment traits via connected tables.
If 2 Greek F-16 Falcons go up against 2 Turkish F-16 Falcons, the outcome is a roll of the dice.
Want to setup waypoints/steerpoint for your aircraft with timing, altitude and posture settings. How about an ATO with packages and supporting flights? There is nothing like that is in this game. You can only set a reference point(s) on the ground for a unit to move to or to define an area -- in the same way you can in any simple rts. That's nowhere near professional quality planning and control for a sophisticated wargame.
The game actually plays like a really bad rts game; that has terrible mouse and keyboard commands. At this point, rts player control is ubiquitous. The devs could have at least followed the best practices already established by those folks.
Despite a basic 25-year old windows interface, you can't remap a single hotkey. They think they know best for you.
What's the real deal with this game?
As you are fighting the game's controls instead of focused on your opponent, you can be confident that the jumbled icons on the map are meticulously replicating minuscule radar band calculations for you.
To be blunt, I see a group of Harpoon modders who focus almost exclusively on milking the old Harpoon game's database with their changes. Meanwhile, they lock their database version down so that someone else can't do the same thing they did -- without working licensed/paid content through them. Their Inferno and LIVE products are proof of this strategy. Yes, you can hobble together a scenario, but only given strict areas of control and extremely limited scope... a single battle with no external influencers.
When asked by a new player just a few days ago (on the Matrix forum) about modding, Sunburn (listed as a dev) responded with one line only, "Will you pay for this?"
Interesting and telling response from a group of Harpoon hackers.
For $80 you should expect a lot more from a GAME you plan to play, particularly one that released beta tester created scenarios as paid content. Moments after I purchased the game, I made the mistake of pressing the Campaign button at the top of the opening menu screen. I was greeted with an advertisement to buy some more content. My verbal response to that would violate Steam's terms.
I think these guys are a lot better at business development than game development.

Maybe a little late, but here is an extract from C:MANO FAQ about the speed treshold of 925 kt.
Warplanes never fly at their theoretic maximum speeds operationally. Over a fighter aircraft’s 6000-8000hrs life span, less than 10% is spent at supersonic speeds. Most airframes will never even go beyond Mach 2, and certainly not while flying a combat sortie. Aircraft use a lot of fuel accelerating and maintaining those speeds, and going beyond 925kt (Mach 1.6) offers no real tactical advantages and may even be impossible simply due to the long time it takes to accelerate to those speeds and the insane amounts of fuel needed to get there. Furthermore, in many cases getting to those speeds will be physically impossible due to weapon and drop tank drag, weapon release envelope limitations, and the possibility of damaging or even detonating external stores. For instance, the special 500kg bombs carried by the MiG-25 recon/bomber variant were given a thermal protection coating to prevent the explosives from over-heating at Mach 2.35.
And let us not forget that ejection at high speeds is extremely dangerous. For most ejection seats, the chance of survival drops dramatically above 600kt or ca Mach 1.0. Even if the pilot survives he is likely seriously injured and may be grounded for good. So although the airframe and engines can push it to Mach 2.0 and beyond, the pilot simply won’t. Especially not in a shooting war.
Command takes aim at simulating a modern battlefield and therefore uses practical operational aircraft speed limitations. Theoretical specs are left out. That means most modern combat aircraft will not fly faster than Mach 1.6 in the simulator. The fuel burn rates are adjusted accordingly, and for example the F-14D Tomcat can fly 230nm Deck Launched Intercept (DLI) missions at Mach 1.6 dash. There are of course numerous exceptions and fighters like F-22A Raptor, MiG-25 Foxbat and MiG-31 Foxhound can easily fly faster. The same goes for aircraft like the SR-71 which can cruise at Mach 3.2. The MiG-25/31 series can perform intercepts at speeds up to Mach 2.35 in the simulator, and F-111s can do an amazing 800kt dash on target at sea level for delivering iron bombs. F-104 Starfighters and English Electric Lightnings have a 1150kt TAS (Mach 2.0) maximum speed to reflect their unique capabilities.
If you want an extremely hardcore strategic mil-sim then this is your game. Be warned though if you want pretty graphics then you're not going to find them here.
