Hotline miami 2 is a video game. It raw, unpleasant and downright mean. Heart pumping, thrilling, intense. All words tha describe this game rather well. Its a pure video game. Story takes a second seat to the gameplay. But that is okay, as even that works, in that the "story" weaves itself into a meta-commentary about video games, that you may or may not find enjoyable. If you dont, thats okay. The game dont expect that of you.
It Hotline miami 2 fun? Yes, a lot. Is it fun for everyone? Not at all. The game is harder than the first, simply due to level/enemy design. It forces you to play a little diffrent than last time around. In Hotline 1, running, gunning and improvisation was the name of the game. In Hotline 2, planing, being carefull and thinking it through is the prefered manner of beating a level. You would think this would ruin what made Hotline 1 great, and to some people i am sure they felt that way. But if you have an open mind, you will realise that it still feels and plays like Hotline 1. Instead of finding satisfaction in a perfectly pulled of improvisation, you will find thrills in perfectly executing a plan. You still get the thrills, the heart pump, the action. Its all still there.
The music is also pretty good. Its more of what was in 1, which is by no means a bad thing.
Is Hotline miami 2's change in gameplay style a commentary made by the developers, pointing fun at how players gain attached to silly simple things such as a gameplay flow and how they might lash out and refuse to change if it is no longer familiar to them? Maybe, who knows. They can fill their game full of hipster "too deep 4 me" social commentary, as long as they keep making some of the most, thrilling, dark and fantastic games.

i've taken quite a while to review this game but, honestly, Grand Theft Auto is taking ♥♥♥♥ing forever to load so I may as well do it to pass the time.
Far Cry 3 is an action-packed adventure containing map exploration, weapon customization, outpost liberation and stealth elements. It was created by that old band of morally bakrupt lunatics known as Ubisoft, whos' previous titles have been action-packed adventures containing map exploration, weapon customization, outpost liberation and stealth elements. I guess it's good to stick to what you know, eh?
As much as it fits into Ubisoft's usually worn-out basket of scratched disks and cracked VHS tapes, the developers decided to be a little bit edgy with this particular title. And by "edgy" I mean they added a twist of artistic finesse and packed the game full of heavy and dark themes. Of course murder, emotional turmoil and death were thrown in there as a modern gaming tradition, but Far Cry 3 focusses a lot less on glofirying the bloody action it provides and a lot more on the sort of effect it's having on the player character "Jason", who's some cocky, white, Californian kid with♥♥♥♥♥♥tons of money, out on a tropical island smoking drugs and getting drunk with hisa Girlfriend, two Brothers and three other friends, all of which are also cocky, white, Californian kids with♥♥♥♥♥♥tons of money. It wouldn't surprised me if they were all Liberals as well.
However, the star attraction of Far Cry 3 isn't the idiotic white kid you play, nor is it his dark and twisted path into the depths of insanity, but the first antagonist of the game, Vaas Montenegro. He's considered the Joker of the Jungle, the King of Rook Island, and it's easy to see why. He's batshit insane and downright terrifying. His usual encounters with Jason consist of a lot of rather disturbing speeches and rather creative attempts at murder. In fact, Vaas is without a doubt one of, if not the most interesting character in the game, and many players, including myself, are interested to see exactly what sort of journey he's been on to get where he is now. I won't spoil anything, but it consists of murder, drugs, incest and a lot of yelling.
The atmosphere the game set up was totally unique. Lost amid a tropical paradise, a pure-hearted Boy must fight against the odds to rescue his friends from pirates, whilst also having to fend off the dangers that lurk beneath the guise of the beautiful jungle, also dealing with his own inner Demons as a bloodthirsty, psychotic drug-lord serves as the author of his torment. However, that's where Far Cry 3 falls short. Halfway through the game, the story just...fails. Vaas disappears, the pirates disappear, Jason ends up on an entire second island, separated from the cast of characters we were just introduced to. The atmosphere changed from unique to something resembling the likes of Just Cause. A island covered in mercenaries and soldiers where, instead of threats coming from all different angles, the Humans are the only contenders. The game did a great job of making the jungle seem like some mysterious maze of Monsters and Demons that was impossible to navigate, leaving you wondering who you could and couldn't trust, but the entire second half of the game leaves us alone with Jason, his feelings, and some♥♥♥♥♥♥we'd never met before that the game was treating with more respect than Vaas. It feels like the entire game was building up to a moment that just reset halfway through. It....in all honesty, it sucked.
Of course, there's more to the game than the story. When I first played the game it seemed like I'd been dropped into a world full of possibilities. You can jet-ski, liberate enemy outposts, hunt dangerous and blood-thirsty Animals ands you can even wander into a pub and play poker! But that's also another reason Far Cry 3 feels a little stale. Like the story, the map itself eventually becomes a bit boring after it's shown you all its' tricks, it finds it very difficult to keep you entertained. After I finished the campaign, I just went around liberating outposts until I'd completed everything and, after that, the world felt a little...empty, like a finished box of chocolates. They compensate for that by allowing you to reset all the outposts on the map and "un-liberate" them, but the feeling just isn't the same the second time around.
You may think, with all those negatives, I wouldn't reccomend Far Cry 3, right? Well, hold your Horses, kiddies, because I'd still tell you to give the game a shot. For all its' flaws, Far Cry 3 is a carefully and beautifully-crafted game that has clearly had blood, sweat and tears poured into it. The atmosphere is unique, the gameplay is enjoyable, the characters are interesting and, in my opinion, the tropical landscape is just gorgeous. At its' core, Far Cry 3's goal isn't to wow you, or force you down a narrative path for money, not is it to pose deep, philosophical questions. Far Cry 3's main goal is to just drop you into a world filled with danger and chaos and let you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥up. And isn't that what games are all about? What are you waiting for? Get out your wallet, gear up and start burning♥♥♥♥♥♥down!

This game is an utterly overrated piece of hot garbage, and I can honestly say that it has little to no redeeming features whatsoever
Let me start off by saying that I am a huge Sonic fan. I adore the franchise, heck, I even love Sonic Adventure. But this game, hoo boy I have some grievances. Where to start, well let's start with the gameplay.
As with most of these games, the only fun levels are Sonic action stages. However, this game is different, as it has only one fun Sonic action stage. The first one. Which is pretty dang fun. But aside from that, this game is full of buggy cameras, clanky controls and unnecesarry deaths aplenty. That's my main problem I think. In a game, if you die and it's your fault, then great. It is just a hard game and you need to improve. But with this game, almost all of the deaths can be easily pinned onto the game. The buggy camera can easiy redirect your course into a bottomless pit, and the shoddy homing attack often leads to a similar fate.
But that's just Sonic. Knuckles is similar to how he played in SA1, only worse. Rather than his HUD telling you if any emerald shards are nearby, it only tells you about one at a time, which can lead to frustration when you find an emerald shard where you checked several times before. Yes, the game does give you a few hints, but they are mostly cryptic and unhelpful.
Tails is a travesty. His levels forget the Sonic monochre, 'Gotta go fast', and instead provide mind-numbing, shambling gameplay where all you need to do is hold down the action button.
But it's not just the gameplay. The character models look abysmal, the voice acting is just terrible, and the animation is often very stunted. In addition, you will often hear character's voices cutting each other off, leadign to confusion in cutscenes.
The chao garden is fun. I wont dispute that, although again kind of overrated.
The soundtrack is decent, but nothing too special in my opinion. One or two tracks stand out, but to be honest if you buy a game just to hear them, but Sonic Generatons instead.
I will end this review by talking about the final stage. It is a very overly long-winded level spanning multiple characters.  However, certain parts are so ridiculously hard in comparison to the rest of the game, that many players may nto see it through.
Buy at your own risk, nostalgia can be blinding.

If you want a realistic tactics game in the vein of a top-down Rainbow Six or SWAT 4, as many people seem to compare this to, I'd pass and get Frozen Synapse instead - it lacks the realistic veneer, but has much more meat to it. And even though Door Kickers has the appearance of realism, it's actually a grindy mobile-style game that I found to be a casual diversion more than anything, only worth the time if you can get it cheap. Not only was it disappointing, but I surprisingly found Breach & Clear to be the more entertaining "casual tactics" game (even with my reservations about that game.)
There's a lot of nice stuff here that makes it look like a top-down SWAT 5 at first glance - go codes (a huge deal!), micromanagement of inventory & team assignments, permadeath campaigns, a veneer of realism. But it's all ultimately let down by a massive heap of grind, a lack of authenticity, and a complete and utter lack of any story/narrative element.
The grind is the biggest and most pervasive problem. The game starts you out with only the absolute barebones of classes and gear available, and everything else is locked behind time-gates, requiring you to dump hours of play into the game before you even have all the basic classes available and can start to think about preparing complicated entry strategies. At first I approvingly thought this was just a tutorial bit, easing the player into the game one class at a time, but Door Kickers just keeps doing it, making you really grind to get all the classes. Eventually the levels become gated by unrealistically overpowered enemies, requiring you to go back and grind up more until you have all the best weapons and armors and whatnot. Your officers also gain XP the more you use them, so just grinding up the same team in the same mission over and over and over makes them way more effective in combat. When you consider roster space, you basically have to do this twice in order to have a fully-leveled roster, and from what I've seen from other players, this is pretty much required for the "end-game" campaigns if you want your your officers to compete with the enemy AI in anything (I certainly didn't stick with the game long enough to get that far.)
My other two points are very connected. Even though Door Kickers is presented as and often hailed as an "authentic" tactics game, it's basically just a casual puzzle game with SWAT graphics, more akin to Angry Birds than SWAT 2. This doesn't make it a bad game per say, but it just doesn't hold water when compared to games that present actual tactical problems and solutions. Enemies and missions are far from authentic, and even though you're supposed to be playing a SWAT team, every mission boils down to a terrorist hunt challenge. Every enemy is always killed, no situation is ever complicated, and the only arrests are quick scripted events during certain mission types. Compared to something like the SWAT series, which allowed for a wide range of interactions and mission types *over a decade* ago, Door Kickers seems quite limited. The only innovative thing about it is the neat field of view thing they borrowed from stealth games, but this ultimately cannot carry a game.
Then there's the lack of story. If the mechanics are amazing I could forgive this, but they're not. And there's absolutely NO story or narrative element anywhere in the game - not even the little pre-mission briefings that have always been the norm for this type of game. Every level is challenge mode scenario. Your only incentive is a high score. Just challenge scenario after challenge scenario, which eventually becomes repetative. It all might as well be hologram training. There *is* a campaign mode, but all it is is a series of linked scenarios that feature permadeath & injury memory carrying over between them, thus making them more interesting and challenging. Absolutely nothing in the way of any additional narrative connection or setup. Instead every single scenario is a simple terrorist hunt or some basic objective that often boils down to being a terrorist hunt anyway.
Plays like a mobile game.

I never wrote a review for Dirt Rally because my feelings were more complex than recommend vs not.  I personally didn't enjoy it, but I felt like it was good for what it was and that someone who was into it would think differently.
This time it's different.
I loved Dirt 2, it was just amazing, from the soundtrack to the atmosphere it created, the way the other drivers were integrated and in constant contact, the physics, the gameplay style - everything.  It was no simulator, and maybe that's why I loved it, but it had personality oozing from every moment.  If Dirt 2 was a cool friend you'd hang out with at any opportunity, this game is your accountant.  It's technical, clinical, and dull, and it manages all that while losing the (imo) realistic and difficult driving characteristics of Dirt Rally.  Having now seen it, I echo what others are saying about the team management system (that it's unnecessary micromanagement), and while that's just one small part of the game, it really sums up the feel of everything for me.
I got this thinking it was a new, less sim-like, more fun-oriented version of Dirt Rally, which sounded like exactly what I wanted, but I realize now that while that may be an alright description of this game, it's not enough.  In fact I'd go so far as to say the Dirt line of games is dead to me, and I won't make the decision to try another lightly.

I have been following this game since it was showcased for the first time. And now that I finished the campaign (at least in normal), I think I can offer some good impressions.
Vermintide offers a Left 4 Dead gameplay style in the Warhammer Fantasy setting, which is absolutely cool, because you get to go melee on waves and waves of skavens and that's fun.
Doing it on your own is not thaaaat fun, it is enjoyable if you wanted the game as bad as I did, so try at least to be in league with another friend, or well, try your luck in the online lobbies.
The game offers 5 playable characters, each with their own set of weapons. Leveling up each character just unlocks equipment space for trinkets.
At the end of each level you get to roll some dices, which determine a piece of random loot that you get (also, loot comes with different types of rarity).
If you crank up the game's difficulty, the best items you can get at the end of the level.
Spread in the most important levels there are some loot dices and tomes and grimoires, items that will generate better loot dice for the after level roll, but that will cost you inventory space and health.
The game itself is kinda challenging, if you have played L4D you will know that you have to keep moving, standing in a single point will not help you, skavens will eventually overrun you.
As it happens with L4D, there are some special skavens that spawn across the levels and that will pester you while you travel across the maps. You have the rat ogre (tank), the globadier (spitter), the gutter runner (hunter), the pack master (smoker), the rattling gunner (armored rat with a huge gun) and the stormskaven (packs of armored skavens).
If you played L4D, the first ones will be easily recognizable.
In terms of graphics, the games looks really nice, even when I got to turn some options down due to the volume of skavens present in the screen.
As far as I have played, I had no problems in connecting with a friend to play, and we were able to enjoy the campaign in normal difficulty.
Taking into account that there are some story missions and some side missions, the game still feels rather short in those terms, but playing each level in higher difficulties is what will make your experience last longer.
If you are here looking for an immersive story, I'm affraid this is not your game. If you like to bludgeon rat men for hours searching for loot and stuff at higher difficulties again and again and again, this is what you need.
The developers should seriously consider releasing some sort of expansion packs with more missions like L4D, or a mode where you can play as Skaven in a match vs the Heroes.

I've been playing AE's games ever since they first released Adventure Quest. They also start rough in the beginning of their games, but what Developing team starts great in the beginning of all games?? Not much. I'll keep this short and simple as much as possible, but try to give you as much of an idea of the game as possible, I might be a bit biased since I DO support this game.
Pros:
-Game runs better than most games that come out in EARLY ACCESS! You heard me, EARLY ACCESS! Don't come to judge a game that has been out only for a few days. It really makes me upset how people that don't understand early access and open beta/alpha are meant to test many things in the game and not be the final product.
-Social MMO. Yes most MMO's a very social, but this one especially is. If you ask for help or a question on something, most people will tell you, or guide you to where you can recive your information. If you need help on a quest, it's a very good chance people are doing the same exact thing you are doing.
-True Cross-Platform gaming! Yup you know it! It's one of the only games that actaully have TRUE cross-platform gaming. Not those stupid games where you can only talk or use a buddy cross-platform. This is the real deal. You can play with friends from PC, IOS, Tablets, and Android. At work and on break? Go on a dungeon run with friends, or work for that next level you are looking forwards to!
-Not Pay2Win! WOO!
- Hilarious content. Dev's want to build a game for everyone that we will all like and want a piece of, and I mean [E] for everyone. Not only do they want to immurse the palyer, but hurmor them as well with their none serious cut scenes.
-Lastly and the most important! Dev's will listen to everyone in the community! Game was "almost" built by listening to the community of AQ3D. It's amazing, and every Dev should learn from these guys!
Cons:
-The difference between the monster levels in zone is quite a jump in the game. You can work really hard in one area and maybe gain a level without questing, then move to the ext area, and BAM! the monster is a higher level then you already and hard to kill, so you pray and depend on the critical when you have no one to help you fight, which is sort of annoying.
-Lack of level design? No not that everything is copied and pasted, but the area in always very small feeling, and it sort of cuts off the immursion of the game, Lets say that you can kill the monsters in each area easily, but the lack of space in the area and lack of monsters really ruin it for you. I'm sure the team will make areas bigger, and hopefully they will! But for a small area the place is very well detailed!
-Crafting.... Yes crafting. Remember when I said in pros that they "almost" built the game by listening to the community? Well this is the one thing they added without really acknowledging the community in closed beta. So before crafting, you can fight and farm with friends to get that one rare drop off a monster that was a equipable item. It was fun because everyone had that one common goal! but now crafting is here, and that takes out that whole idea. Sure you can play with people to get the same items, but then when people leave and you need an item you want, some people wont help because they are getting another item that they need becasue they already have the item you need. It's also bothersome how to takes almost up to a DAY to craft certain items. Well so far open beta has added the equipable item drop again, so if the Devs take this in the right direction, I don't see the crafting being a too negative of an impact.
-Level requirement idea? I understand it's hard to grind for some levels so you can move on, but the one thing that is annoying is low level players coming to high level dungeons. There is no party system. Only 3 people at a time in a dungeon instance, so you pray there are 3 in the last dungeon group so you can have your 2 other buddies with you at all times. But when you go in, there will be a low level player waiting for higher levels to run them so they can "gain exp." the problem with this is that they are a weight for you because when you get to the last boss you need that extra member that's the same level as you or higher to kill the boss, and the low level can't do anyting to help you. So I think they need to add a level cap to this stuff if there is no way to prevent this.
-Grinding. It's annoying to have to try to grind, but I'm sure they made it that way so that you don't push all the way to the end of the game content already and get bored and leave. They want people to enjoy it and still have a focus to level up to get to the end. Again, I'm sure this will be fixed once more areas, content, and raising level cap are added into the game.
-Dungeon keys. Enough said, they are like the energizes to do mission on mobile games, except this limits how many times you can run a dungeon. You only get max of 20 keys and it takes 2 hours to replenish 1 key.
-No party system. That says it all.
Conclusion:
I think this game is really great overall though. Looking over everything (hate using the p word) and seeing its true potential, this game will come out amazing like all the other AE games they made! just give them time because they are a small team working on their very first 3D game that has freakin true CROSS-PLATFORM gaming! This team always comes through and listens to the community all the time! Don't be surprised if you have an idea and share it with them, it might just make it into the game! :D Hopefully you all support them, because if you do, they will deliver! ***WARNING! This is not a sit-down, left-click walk in the park.  I highly recommend that you first go through the tutorials.  The initial tutorials will explain almost everything you need to know.  You'll need a good full day to learn the basic controls.
***NO MULTIPLAYER (yet)
***WHO MIGHT LIKE THIS
The type of people who purchase this game are highly military minded, geopolitical enthusiasts, and/or people who work for think-tanks in Washington, who want to play out simulated real-world scenarios of any size or scope imaginable.  Surgical strikes in Saudi Arabia via US strikes against militants? You bet.  A naval blockade by NATO forces of the Baltic Sea against Russia? Let's go.  All out war between the US Pacific Fleet, including allies such as the Phillippines against the Chinese Navy? Bring it on.
***GOOGLE EARTH IS THE WHOLE MAP
Basically, they've taken Google Earth, and allowed you to have free reign to setup naval and air operations ANYWHERE on the map.  And unlike Jane's Fleet Command that limited you to a certain section of the globe, the entire world is open on this game all the time.  You could launch a B2 Spirit bomber from Colorado, and send it on a sorty to the Middle East (midflight refueling points setup as well) and all the way back.  The game hosts 35 scenarios in total, with conflict dates ranging from the 1950s to modern day.  But there are many more scenarios that users have uploaded
***JANE'S FLEET COMMAND
If you liked Jane's Fleet Command, you'll probably like this one too, however this game is MUCH more detailed and technical than Fleet Command ever was.  Personally, I like that it's more detailed.  Fleet Command meant you had to micro-manage all of your units, and this could get really hectic the more air assets you put into action.  In Command: Modern Air/Naval Operations, you're able to assign specific mission sets and other RoE factors for your squadrons before they ever take off and for your ships as well.  Rather than micro-managing on the fly (which you can still do, if necessary) you do all of the preparation heavy at the beginning of any operation.
***VAST LIBRARY OF MILITARY EQUIPMENT, WEAPONS, EXPLANATIONS
ALSO, the game comes with an absolutely amazing library of every single military piece of equipment currently declassified.  It not only lists the ships, and aircraft, but it goes down into the types of weaponry they possess and then what those weapons themselves are capable of, and what they're used for.  This library alone is worth the price.  Sure, a lot of this information may be on Google, but it hasn't been fact checked, nor is it as consilidated into one place like it is in this game.
Personally, I really love this game.  It's allowed me to play out one fictional scenario I've written about in my geopolitical book, which was amazing.  It's hard for me to have any cons with the game.  It's very technical, but that's just the way it is and I'm okay with that.

Hotline miami 2 is a video game. It raw, unpleasant and downright mean. Heart pumping, thrilling, intense. All words tha describe this game rather well. Its a pure video game. Story takes a second seat to the gameplay. But that is okay, as even that works, in that the "story" weaves itself into a meta-commentary about video games, that you may or may not find enjoyable. If you dont, thats okay. The game dont expect that of you.
It Hotline miami 2 fun? Yes, a lot. Is it fun for everyone? Not at all. The game is harder than the first, simply due to level/enemy design. It forces you to play a little diffrent than last time around. In Hotline 1, running, gunning and improvisation was the name of the game. In Hotline 2, planing, being carefull and thinking it through is the prefered manner of beating a level. You would think this would ruin what made Hotline 1 great, and to some people i am sure they felt that way. But if you have an open mind, you will realise that it still feels and plays like Hotline 1. Instead of finding satisfaction in a perfectly pulled of improvisation, you will find thrills in perfectly executing a plan. You still get the thrills, the heart pump, the action. Its all still there.
The music is also pretty good. Its more of what was in 1, which is by no means a bad thing.
Is Hotline miami 2's change in gameplay style a commentary made by the developers, pointing fun at how players gain attached to silly simple things such as a gameplay flow and how they might lash out and refuse to change if it is no longer familiar to them? Maybe, who knows. They can fill their game full of hipster "too deep 4 me" social commentary, as long as they keep making some of the most, thrilling, dark and fantastic games.

Hotline Miami 2 : Wrong Number is a game of stealth and timing or killing every one as fast as possible . One thing that I like about when you beat a really hard level is that you feel really good . So if you like running in halls and running into random rooms while killing all enemies with a pipe, this is the game for you.
Challenging, but loads of fun!

Far Cry 3. The third installment in the Far Cry franchise, although old (two new ones out as of yet) this game is still relevant, which is rare for a title over 5 years old. Far Cry 3 offers an experience unlike its predecessors and other games on the market. Present or past.
Map: Far Cry 3 is set on a tropical island in the north/south Pacific ocean (not sure ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ ). The map is amazing, and extremely large offering hours of extra content after the campaign.
Characters: All the main/side characters are brilliantly voice acted and seem realistic, towards the end, you begin to actually care about all the characters, bad or good.
The antagonist(s): Well... Vass... He's amazing. You actually believe this guy is fukn insane! He's brilliantly voice acted, all his missions are entertaining and every time you think you have finally caught him he throws another curve ball. Don't believe me? He won "Best New Character" at the Canadian Videogame Award.
Yep, Vass is an antagonist! - However, just play the game, to figure out more.
Gameplay: Hours of gameplay available, hunting, side-missions. endless forests to explore and skills to require. Enemies are enjoyable to kill.
Combat: Combos are amazing. After awhile, you actually see Jason Brody get better (after unlocking skills) and it feels awesome, simultaneously killing 3 pirates with one takedown. The gunplay is fun, however sometimes feels clunky.
Hunting: First time you hunt, it's cool. Finding more dangerous animals in the wild is a challenge, and you often die. It isn't super 'grindy' either, as there's a lot of animals in the world, with their dedicated zones. Making certain animals easy to find.  However, after 6-9 hours it's pretty useless.
Campaign.  A. M. A. Z. I. N. G - One of my favorites, due to the characters (especially Vass)
Uplay....
Deaths: Sometimes death feel stupid, or you will just commit suicide whilst running near a cliff (or at least in my experience)...  Think it has become too much for, Jason...
AI: They're pretty stupid. BUT they're still fun to kill, stealth is amazing.
- Wait this is more of a pro...
Multiplayer: Dead AF (rip)
Only because it wasn't a perfect game, I still wish the multiplayer could be worked on a bit more, but the 9 goes to the single-player alone. Thanks for reading my review, and I hope you'll get your hands on this amazing game. :)

There are so many things I love about this game. Probably namely the explosions.
I have played FarCry 2, 3 and 4 a lot. I have beaten each one probably twice at least.
FarCry 3 is one of my favorites because the island setting is in such full effect here and its really nice.
Also of course the takedowns were introduced.
A lot of people whined about the characters in this game, and I don't really understand why, I guess they were just salty and offended at how young american's suddenly stranded on an island were portrayed, but I thought they did a great job.
In FarCry 3, you care way more about the characters driving the story than in FarCry 4, at least, that's my experience. In FC4 you don't really give a ****, you just want to blow stuff up, the most likeable character is probably Pagan. This is one reason I feel FC3 is really just as good or in some times better than FC4. Perhaps it was intentional, perhaps the backlash to FC3's characters and stories was met with a return to a more simple and unedited formula of "just a badass blowing sh!t up".
Or perhaps they just chose to have character "development" in FC4 be even closer to the fourth wall than it is in this game. But FC3 gives your character a lot of motivation in the very beginning of the game, a clear direction...in 4, your character's "motivation" is someone we never meet or see, who has some mysterious connection to the villain, but it is not even hinted at in the beginning, and never shown until the end. Not something that matters *as much* in games where the focus is takedowns, explosions and fun, immersive free roaming, but it's a striking difference between the two games.
Don't get me wrong, this isn't a review of FC4, and it has a beautiful setting and features, it's great! But purely story-wise I prefer the story, character development and presentation of those elements in this game. I find that Jason's reactions to the blood and chaos he starts to see and experience - and how that changes with the story's progression - also makes it more immersive, consequential & fun; that he is a man outside of his element, comfort zone and natural habitat; again, in 4, Arjay barely reacts at all ever to anything (Reggi & Yogi's drugs aside) and is kind of all too happy to start helping people fight a war he has no stake in.
I also prefer the simplicity and power of the syringes in this one, the auto-craft heal syringe in 4 is fantastic, but I didn't care much for the other syringe changes.
In short, the atmosphere, weapons, free roam and gameplay are really satisfying, providing hours of interesting and fun gameplay - with moments that break the immersion as quickly & incredibly as everything else is usually so immersive, being spread few and far between enough to keep playing most of the time (e.g. you fall like 6 feet and die from the fall damage, lol). No but for real, things like that DO happen, but sometimes it's really funny depending on what happens. Also dying from falling can happen a lot more in the beginning and a lot less and you acquire more health. Other than those little moments, it really is an incredibly immersive game.

I won't spoil it, but there is just really no need or point to it at all, basically one of the endings is what you work towards the entire game and what anyone would choose to feel accomplished, the other choice is stupid and makes no sense (because that alternative darker "loss of sanity" or whatever direction was hinted at a lot, but not explored enough in the game, so at the end it lacks believability as a choice).
Anyway the only thing the choice influences is the ending cinematic itself so, obviously you can just watch them on youtube to see the alternate ending. It's just dumb and didn't need to be in the game. For the ending that makes sense and matches the story, what you just spent hours doing, and makes you feel good and not like you were just told a bad joke, I would recommend picking the good ending.

Well the story is basically revamping civilization but not in the usual RPG way.  This is a time management game played by levels with certain goals to achieve at each level. (Similiar to how Faerie Solitaire, Labors of Hercules or even Tales of the Orient have level goals.) Break boulders, fix roads, reconstruct houses, construct water towers, clear waterways, mine ore, etc, etc, and try to do it under the certain time limits to recieve a gold, silver, or bronze trophy.  Relatively easy because the game does not speed up like Diner Dash or Dr. Daisy:Pet Vet, and it is long because it has an actual storyline.  Not an overly complicated story as our inventor friend moves from place to place fixing things like roads and houses and bringing "invention" back to each place improving the overall quality of life for the inhabitants.
Fun, easy, family oriented game or simply a game to play while taking a break from anything or everything else.

This game first presents itself to you with a semi-sci fi type world, I like it, anything with a futuristic sci fi world, even more so if it is original is great in my book.
You're presented with a female protagonist in this game though, I don't like most games with exclusive female playable characters so that is a bit of a problem. She has a tomboy look going on from a design aspect but that doesn't help in her case because our protagonist is annoying and generic in this game due to poor writing. Her voice actor is terrible as well. Even worse than the voice acting for females in Guild Wars 2.
So yeah, the world the game is set in looks nice and is well presented, the female protagnist though is generic and just not interesting.
Very unique concept this game has, I like it. Water is the main elemental focus here, not many games do with the developers had in mind with this game.
However, they obviously did something very wrong since the company who made this game went bankrupt and the game engine they designed for it.
The gameplay is interesting at first, but ultimately it is just plain, bland, boring. The characters suck, Kate is a junk protagonist, her partner scoot or whatever his name is has halfway decent voice acting but he is boring as well. His animations are terrible as well.
Interesting at first, gets boring though. The main aspect of the game, "Water" is not used as much as it should have been, since the developers made a engine based around real physics water the water powers you gain don't show up until late in the game, very silly move on there part to feature the main reason to play the game later on. It should have been available at the start or near the start of the game, would have been more interesting.
The game looks pretty on my fairly powerful rig, I was very impressed with the HydroEngine that the developers of this game made, they may have gone out of business but they deserve praise for there work on the engine at the very least, I like it.
Not great, below par to be fair. Just doesn't seem good, voice acting is very terrible, music is generic, sound effects does have its moments of being good but most of it is junk, the enemy gun sound effects are a joke, something outta' a cheesy laser tag game.
The story is crap. Very basic but not in a good way, the female antagonist sucks, not interesting at all with her overplayed acting and predictable reasoning. Our heroine had potential to be pretty cool, but the voice acting, writing and animations are all pretty bad.
The game doesn't have very much entertainment for the $9.99 asking price, I paid only $3.99 for a retail discount and even that seems a lot to ask for, ya know for something that is basically a tech demo for a great innovative game engine. The main reason to play the game would be for the neat water physics, no game has water animations quite like this game, much potential could be had if a major developer like Capcom or Namco got a hold of this engine, but that isn't the case.
There is no value in replaying this tech demo, except of you want to experience really nice water physics.
The HydroEngine has great potential, the developers should be proud they made a unique game engine with a strong focus on water, If the engine is up for sale, I hope the buyer is a well known or ambitious developer team because the potential to make a crazy hack n slash action game with rpg elements with a water wielding male protagonist seems like a great idea to me. I would love to work on such a project myself if I had enough money and talent to make such a thing happen, I think it would be a very unique concept for a market filled with so many generic first person shooting games.
*Ambitious tech demo showing of a unique game engine.
*Great and Innovative game engine, the HydroEngine is a unique idea with a poor tech demo showing it off.
*Pretty graphics from a former indie developer, on max settings the game looks good. The water is the star though.
*Fun physics in general.
*Main female protagonist is not likable, very boring, even if the character were male he would still be boring.
*Bad voice acting from almost every character in the game.
*Generic storyline.
*Bad writing.
*Combat is boring.
*Platforming is boring.
*Missions are boring.
*Support characters are boring.
*AI is extremely stupid.
4.4/10 ~ I do not recommend this game at the price point of $9.99, it is barely a game. If you can get it for under $5 I would still be very stand offish against it, but to experience the water in this tech demo might be worth it.

The game itself contains much more variety (Talking about Disciplines) than its predecessor and major improvements have also been done (Better career mode, weight transfer). There is also a new feature which allows you to have unlimited different stages but I'll come back to that later. The team management has also been improved which I did really like.
The main problem is that Codemasters focused too much on making a game for arcade gamers. The simulation is absolutely ridiculous, if you consider, that Codemasters made this mode especially for people who liked the challenge in DiRT Rally. Even though they made progress concerning the Weight transfer, every single car feels like a FWD. You have so much understeer in a RWD, that you can't even loose your back end when applying full power with the wheel turned in!
Also the so highly praised "Your Stage Generator" is generating boring stages with the same corners. The fun lasts perhaps 10 Stages but then it gets dull. Another important part are the graphics. Even though there have been improvements, like the rain on track and rain effects (which are beautiful!) on windshield, there is a major downgrade with the landscape, bushes and colors. The locations don't feel real because of that.
Last point but it isn't really Codemaster's fault, is the lack of cars and locations. I know the licencing problem but that is not an excuse for not giving us enough content.
I recommand this game to every person who's looking for a fun game with no real interest of simulation. But for those people who liked DiRT Rally, I cannot recommend this game at this current stage especially now that they released a patch without fixing the basics of physics. I do hope that they will listen to the community.

NOTE: When i indicate that i got this for free, i mean that i got the boxed matrix store version as a Christmas gift, and used my code from that to get a free steam code, which anyone can do. I was planning to save up and buy it anyway, so o just got lucky. This is also why i bought Northern Inferno without hesitation when it was released.
Warning: long review ahead, i won't touch on everything, as a lot of the steam reviews do a good job as well.
I would definitely have to recommend Command:Modern Air/Naval Operations, if you are up to the challenge and have enough interest and patience to enjoy it.
Yes, $80 USD is a lot of money for one game. But this is actually acceptable for a number of reasons:
-Steam Refunds make it a safer purchase if you are unsure.
-The standalone Campaigns, (Northern Inferno, Chains of War, and Shifting Sands) are a reasonably priced way of trying out the game without committing to the full price.
-What you get out of $80 USD in CMANO is completely worth it, ill go into this is more detail in a little bit.
And of course if you can get it on sale, that is definetly a bonus!
CMANO definitely requires, above all else, patience. You are not going to get the hang of this in one sitting. I highly recommend doing what i have done: Downloading the printer-friendly version of the manual, print it out, along with the various manual addendums on the website and buy a three ring binder to put it all in and have the manual available for reading in your spare time as well as during the game. I have only logged about 74 hours into this (plus probably an additional 3-4 hours when steam was in offline mode), and i am by no means confident enough to take on alot of the scenarios. But i am learning.
To put it bluntly, CMANO is a wargame/simulation of Naval and Aerial warfare all over the world from 1945 until the present day and the near future (i've seen scenarios going as far as the 2030s). That by itself inherently gives you a lot to work with. But that is a massive understatement.
"What do you get in CMANO?" You should really be asking: "What don't you get in CMANO?", well not a whole lot.
Well one thing you don't get is fancy graphics that you see in other naval wargames like Jane's Fleet Command or Naval War Arctic Circle. But to be honest, those don't really add alot to the games and are really just eye candy. I have never played any version of Harpoon, so i really cannot draw any comparisons there.
As of right now, CMANO contains i think around 40 standalone scenarios, plus seven or so tutorial scenarios. If you also get Northern Inferno that is an additional 14 scenarios, which can be played individually or as a campaign.
HOWEVER, there is the Community Scenario Pack, available on the developer's website, that contains close to 300 scenarios, most of which are made by the community. This is a free download, and every once in awhile it is updated as more players submit their creations. This is absolutely a must-have, think of it as free DLC, as the scenarios go through some peer review before being put in the pack.
Also the most recent patch (v1.10) added steam workshop support, just be mindful that as of this writing (March 11 2016) many of the scenarios on there are already in the Community Scenario pack, So if you already have the pack, just check that before downloading from the workshop so that you don't have unnecessary copies of the same scenario.

As the above clearly implies, you can very much create your own scenarios. The possibilities are massive, as you have the entire planet earth to work with, as the whole program uses a Google Earth style globe.
Basically, the meat of what CMANO contains is in the two databases. These contain all the units, buildings etc (referred to as platforms) and weapons and sensors in the entire program. All put together, there are literally thousands of entries in the database. There are so many that there are actually two separate databases:
-"Cold War Database" AKA CWDB (stuff from 1945/6 through 1979)
-"Database 3000  AKA DB3k (stuff from 1980 until the present day and near future)
Some players on the forum have admitted to spending more time just browsing through the databases than actually playing. It is that huge and extensive. Much of it is available to look at for free on Baloogan's Campaign Wiki, there should be a link in the steam community discussions.
One snag is that you cannot have stuff from both databases in a single scenario, you have to use one or the other.
The sheer size of the databases means that as long as you keep within the Post-WWII timeframe, your options are, for all practical purposes, unlimited. The information in the databases is also incredibly detailed, basically all of the military hardware is portrayed in the most accurate way possible using publically available information. Obviously some stuff has some guesses about the capabilities, as the much of the details about things like the F-22 Raptor or the Virginia class Submarine are classified. There are also quite a bit of speculative and prototype units, such as the planned but never built aircraft carrier version of the F-117 stealth fighter, i think even the long suspected "Aurora" spy plane is modelled, obviously in a guessing way. One update recently added anti-torpedo torpedoes.
You cannot, however, make your own units from scratch. I think this is fine for two reasons:
1. the Devs clearly put a lot of effort into modeling such a huge amount of units, weapons, and sensors, and i think it is not unreasonable for them to want people to enjoy all their hard work.
2. most of what you would need is already there, unless you are going for something totally science fiction, i think you will find just about anything you want within the game's timeframe.
You can however, make modifications to existing units, to use an example from the dev's website, you can put the modern advanced Aegis radar on an Iowa Class Battleship.
Perhaps the best part about all of this is the developer support. They give great help, as does the community, and their free updates add a lot. It is worth it to create an account on the forums.
CMANO is still very much being built. Each major patch usually adds new features for free, For example, the latest patch added the ability to give waypoint targeting to cruise missiles. In the next one they are improving mid air refueling and air strike planning.
Perhaps there is no better testament to the quality of CMANO than the fact that it is starting to have real world applications in the defense industry. Not that long ago the devs signed a deal with BAE Systems, the second largest defense contractor in the world, to use this program professionally. This wargame definitely has the potential to become one of the go to programs for Naval and Air Force academies around the world, especially since customers of the professional edition that you and me cannot buy have the freedom to add in more realistic information (classified stuff) for their own private purposes.
Bottom Line, if you are willing to put down the money (save up for a while if you want), have an interest in the subject matter, and enough patience to accept the learning curve, you will not regret purchasing CMANO. I swear it is worth every penny, in fact it is worth much more than $80 USD, you really are getting quite a deal given how much work went into this, and the fact that the devs keep on adding to it for free, save for the Northern Inferno addon.

This game – an excellent Sim really – is truly splendid, but it’s not for everyone.
Command is the best Naval/Air simulator for 1945 through the near term future that you’re going to see without a security clearance (And some of the secured Sims aren’t as good either).  It’s long and fact and zero on trying to engage the user, which is as a good sim should be.
Thousands of hours and reams of accurate, expensive data have been accumulated here.  The result is something you can use to accurately sandbox real-life events in the news, and see deeply into a situation you otherwise aren’t going to see without joining the military and ramping up into Staff School.  Want to see the actual likely effects of the North Korean nuclear proliferation?  Check out why Russia feels they needed to invade Sevastopol?   See how a nuclear Iran would really look?  This is one of the best places for civilians to see this.  This sim can change your geopolitical awareness, if you use it well.
On the other hand, there are no dramatic first person graphics, no embedded plots, no immersive story lines.  And if you need these, look elsewhere.
The learning curve is steep, but the community support is excellent.  This game also continues to evolve, so you aren’t going to wind up with a white elephant that sits on your disk with no fixes, changes or upkeep.
Bottom line:  If you enjoy sims of this nature, this is by far the best I’ve ever seen.  And if you want something like WoW, you’re not going to find it here.

Many people here are saying "It's gr8 m8" or "It ain't gr8 m8 it's p2w" but I don't care. I will make you get this game.
First, some pros and cons
Pros:
- Large learning curve, challenging yet rewarding
- Huge addition that sets it apart - I'll explain later
- Variety of careers and roles
- Large maps that require you to make tactical decisions
- "Unspoken tactics", ie people waiting for you to enter a vehicle, or covering different positions when capturing
- Three different nations to choose from - United States, Germany, or Russia
- Extremely immersive, from the gunfights and vehicle fights to your character - I'll explain later
- Items do not carry over to other characters (fuels realism)
Cons:
- Hard to get into
- Progression is slow
- Everything is absurdly expensive, you'll probably work months upon months to get what you want
- People who spend money in game will have an advantage
Now, to explain the huge addition and the character immersion. The addition is the war. Once you reach level 3, you can participate in the war. Generals plan these battles, and the generals are players level 19+. These are not in any way balanced by the server, it is just all out war. You will need to coordinate with your team through the chat, and also help out by choosing a career to boost your efficiency. The careers are as follows; Infantry (lvl 1); Tank Crewman (lvl 3); Fighter Pilot (lvl 4); Paratrooper (lvl 7); Recon (lvl 9); General (lvl 18). In the war system, you need to claim cities. Your generals plan the offensives and defensives, and you, the soldiers, must follow the orders and reign supreme.
Last but not least, character immersion. Firstly, you start the game with three infantrymen; the American, German, and Russian. You can change careers when you unlock them. Each of your characters is also given a name. My American is Frank Petersen, my German is Ingomar Faust, and my Russian is Grigory Kaleshnik. I use Ingomar, and truthfully, have not played once as Americans or Russians. The nice part is, you would never have thought of these names. It really is nice to feel not like some kind of god, but just another guy in the endless ranks of the Army, the Regime, or the other Army. One claim I've heard is that Germans are overpowered, or Americans are underpowered. I may be biased in saying this, but no team is overpowered. Weaponry is nice, but swords would beat tanks if used properly.
Before I submit this review, the game is very hard. It is both challenging, and hard to enjoy. If you do, however, take the time to play this game, you'll like it. I dearly hope that the developer fixes the prices, because this is just absurd, and if they did, this game would be the best WWII game in human history.

Artix Entertainment are independent MMORPG games creators, being almost entirely community run and relying on microtransactions (on varying scales, their older games didn't really have them) to get by. They fund their games this way, which ties into how this game came to be, which is via Kickstarter.
. Lately, a good amount of their games have died out or gone the wrong way in terms of updates, primarily because they listen to their community instead of logically resolving issues. This is a two-sided problem; AE can't dismiss their community because they rely on their players, and they can't continue listening to their community because their games are getting
messy. (Been playing AE games almost daily for 10 years, apart from a large hiatus in 2009-2010)
Important pros to remember about the game;
- It's charming and memorable. As with all AE games, you will quickly find many things you like about the game, and these things will stick with you for a long time.
- Combat is quick to learn, hard to master. A staple with good RPGs.
- Compact yet fulfilling. You won't be spending 30 minutes just walking around to find something to do, and areas can take a while to do, keeping you occupied non-stop.
- Mobile-to-PC. You can play this game on your phone, tablet etc and instantly swap to PC/Mac, and vice versa. Make sure you log out properly though, as you may lose a bit of progress while switching if you don't.
This game has very important cons too;
- Similar to AQW (AdventureQuest Worlds), they have filled this game with grind-y quests and difficult bosses that punish solo play. If you want to get far in this game, you need to rely on players doing things at the same time as you, or friends.
- The terrains are mostly repetitive. If you're looking for hugely scenic areas like in Skyrim, this isn't the game.
- Exp and gold farming is moderately slow, and you will find yourself spending a good amount of effort and time just to get to level 7, the level which I achieved in just over 3 hours. The problem being is that they never really tell you where to go, like recommended areas for your level or monsters that scale to your level, so it's pure luck as to where you end up fighting.
Despite these flaws, it is safe to say that these
be ironed out. They update their remaining games on a weekly basis, and it is also important to remember that, as I write this review, this game is still in it's early(ish) stages. The reason I recommend this game is for this exact reason. It may not be great so far, but stick with it, put some effort in, and you'll have a headstart when they fix this game. They are very good at surprising their community.

I used to play AQ a long time ago when I was a kid, then went on to play DragonFable and then AdventureQuest Worlds. I think I've got the general idea of what to expect in this game, considering it's also free to play, just like the previous games, and it's made by a company that exhibits the same core ideas and mechanics in all their games. Before I even entered the game I expected the game to be somewhat grindy, which is exactly what it turned out to be. It follows pretty much the same formulas as the previous games. However this time it's in a 3d format.
CONS:
-Classes are NOT balanced. (I haven't tried out the Guardian yet, it's a premium class)
From my experience Mage right now is overpowered. The class can kill a target before it even comes into attack distance.
-There are elements of p2w. Which I will explain in detail below -
You want to heal, bruh? Well, you can't. Potions in the game are bought only with premium currency. While writing this I wanted to see how they work.(You receive 10 potions for free at the start at the game.) They restore a small amount of your health and have no cooldown. Essentially if you have the cash, you are immortal.
Currently there are 4 classes. For those of you unfamiliar with the game, you can equip classes like an item. Equiping the class brings new skills along with it. The classes right now are Rogue, Warrior, Mage, Guardian. You cannot heal with any of the classes that are freely available, you can only heal with the Guardian which is a premium class.
-Areas are a little unbalanced.
After I finished the prologue quests I was teleported to the town of Battleon. I was level 2. The first area outside of the town already has monsters that are level 4. In terms of other MMOs this wouldn't mean much, but here you'll get your♥♥♥♥♥beat if you fight with monsters a few levels higher than you. The issue mainly here is that they made the spawn to be around trees. You've got a tree with 2 level 2 lizards which you need for a quest where you have to kill 15 of them. What you'll need to do, which i found out after walking around for 5 minutes, is to shake/attack the nearest tree so that they can spawn. Maybe I've been left with the wrong impression, but that's what happened with me.
-The game feels like it's in Alpha.
Don' take this as a huge con, really. The situation is actually good.  Let me explain.
The town of Battleon has around 5-6 buildings. Some of them still haven't been completed and you cannot enter. When you try to enter, a window pops-up showing what the building will be. That shows that the devs at least have something planned, which will surely be implemented in the future.
-PC version could use a new UI with a normal hotbar, instead of using the phone's UI, which is really weird and annoying.
It just feels like a mobile game on a PC with that UI. The devs should really try to think of a UI for the pc gamers.
-You are limited about how many dungeons you can do.
Not sure what they were thinking here.
PROS:
-Cross-platform.
Really cool if you want to play on the go.
-Has potential.
It sure does, but it depends on how the devs will do from now on. Hopefully it won't turn really p2w.
-Well optimized. It's only 50-60 mb and it doesn't take a lot of resources to run.
Enough said.

After going back to this game after playing right at launch. I can't recommend this. I hate being the hipster that says the first one is better, but that is just the case with this one.
Where a smooth, seemless experience of murdering people floor by floor with the mask of you choice once sat; it has now been replaced by a snail's pace of a story with cutscene after cutscene, and poor level design.
Don't take my message the wrong way, because I love story in my games. The problem is some developers need to know when too much story is in fact too much story. With this second title in the series, the story slows everything down, and limits the player from being free to pick from many different masks like the first game had offered up. This makes finding your play style awkward now that they've stripped you of that.
Nearly every level is tailored to be out-of-sight gunplay, and "out-of-sight" is not a complement in this case: nearly every enemy is firing at you by the time you realize they're offscreen. Instead of charging rooms in a daring manner you now have to play this slow and almost tactically in order to not keep losing your progress on these massive levels. That's rights, these levels are massive. That also means failure will set you back a good bit of progress should you be sniped through a window by an offscreen enemy wielding a shotgun.
To wrap this up, I recommend playing the first game and stopping there after you've beaten it. This game is only a shell of the glory that the original was. I don't recommend this even if it's on sale, because all you'll end up acheiving is hope for an interruptful story that never gets any better as you inch your way through it.

This is one of those games that've been in my Pile o' Shame for far too long.
After getting to grips with the game mechanics, I found it an excellent game, which I would happily recommend to anyone who's even remotely interested in historical-style battles or RPGing - the game caters happily to both/either.
Like the game itself: this review is huge and imperfect, but tries its very hardest to be entertaining.
(I feel obliged to add that I don't have Viking Conquest.)
But I want to mention the melee combat system before I start.
If you move your mouse up as you click your button, you do an overhead chop. If you move it left, you do a swing from the left - if you move it right, you do a swing from the right. If you move it down, you do a stab.
Blocking follows a similar control scheme.
You can also hold the button down - you swing when you let go.
Just picture it: Riding on a horse, pushing slightly left on your mouse as you press your button and hold it down. As you line up your galloping steed to pass closely (i.e. within your reach) by the target, you release your mouse button and THWACK! One target down - if you time it right, and aim right. It's both easier AND harder than it sounds. You could, of course, not ride a horse if you so desired.
Not all weapon types have all attack types - you can't do an overhead swing with a lance, for instance.
Things you might like:
- wide array of ancient weapons and weapon types
- the excellent horse riding mechanics. No, I don't mean there's dudes who ride horses and fix cars. That would be awesome though, if somehat redundant give nthe time the game is set in.
- TEXTBOOK minimalist interface - has all the info you need within roughly 3 clicks, and doesn't clutter the screen.
- But serioulsy, the horse riding. You can attack from horseback. Unlike in the Elder Scrolls games. Not that it's a contest.
- A lot of reading (which I like), which is ALL skippable/ignorable (which people who don't like reading might appreciate).
- NO UNSKIPPABLE CUTSCENES. With the possible exception of the marriage ceremony. I didn't try and skip that, so I don't know.
- Your character is pretty customisable, in many ways.
- Openworld/Sandbox playstyle - one of the few games I've seen where it's actually viable to either freeplay or do quests/tasks - or a mixture of both. Try that in most other games and you'll have a hard time eventually, or take ages to level up.
- Plenty of Engrish, or something like it. It actually adds to the 'otherness' of the game, which is why I've put it in Pros.
- HMMM - DAT HORSE RIDING. Seriously, just ride around the villages. Don't even play the game. Okay, play the game. But you know what I mean. I only wish you could ride donkeys. Then I could have open this point up with HMMM - DAT♥♥♥♥♥
- MASSIVE BATTLES. Or smaller pitched ones. THE POWER IS YOURS.
- it feels intrinsicly Indie. Some folks might not like that. Their loss.
- BEST notes system in ANY GAME EVER. Need to turn in a quest, but the questgiver has moved? Ask someone in their faction where they are. Then go to the journal/log page of the quest - it's been updated with the new info! Click on the place mentioned by their faction-mate (totally a word), then click on 'show on map'. This will take you to the town/city/village on the map (I bet you saw that coming), click on it, and WHAMMO - you're on your way to them. DONE. Usually. Sometimes. You'll see.
- Possibly the most successful rendition of emergent gameplay that I've ever played. And I've played Minecraft. LOTS. Okay, not that much. But still heaps.
- I CANNOT MENTION THE HORSES ENOUGH.
- with the exception of the Blocking noise, I totally adore every aspect of the sound in this game.
- without ANY exception, this is the best, most visceral, most dynamic melee system I've EVER used. Turn off Automatic Directional Blocking for extra points.
- I left this til last, because this is a big thing for me, because it has long irritated me for reasons that don't even make sense to me: REALISTIC FEMALE ARMOUR. Or REALISTIC FEMALE ARMOR if you're American. No chainkinis in sight!
Cons:
(I wish I didn't have to write this part. But it wouldn't be a proper review if I didn't.)
- The graphics aren't what one would call state of the art. To be fair, it's a pretty old game, and I'm sure it's Indie. I think I could safely say that they follow a Morrowindesque (also totally a word) aesthetic. I actually dig it, but many people care about that kind of thing.
- It can be frustrating to fail a mission because you can't find the person to turn it in to within x amount of days. The excellent notes system help out here heaps, but you'll usually need to ask at least 3 people by the time you catch up with them, as they keep moving. To be fair, most of them ARE army leaders, which is a pretty valid reason to be moving about the map. But still, it can be frustrating. Especially if they've been captured, and you don't have a big enough army to take out the punk that captured them.
- The start game phase can be REALLY tough when you first start and don't know what everything does/means/whatevers.
- Some of the more highly strung players may be upset at the historically accurate treatment of females. In fact, I often caught myself starting fights as a female character purely for this reason, which is not really very enlighted of me, I must admit. This may not affect many people, but I found it worth mentioning.
- Some people might not like the 'raw' vibe of the game. I mean to say, it's not ultra-polished. Mount & Blade: Fire And Steel has the Polish Commonwealth in it, if that helps though, hahaha etc.
- THOSE HORSES. Oh, right. Sorry. I'm just so used to writing it now. Acutally - let me say this: I feel as though the horse graphics/animations are far superior to the human graphics/animations.

EDIT: This is a review of the VIKING CONQUEST mod for Warband.  MnB Warband in itself is one of the best games I've ever played - and has a wealth of excellent mods.  This review is tailored to a specific mod available for purchase on Steam:
Good mod, as far as MnB mods go.  A bit buggy.  Got caught in a loop just recently doing a storyline quest, couldn't get out of it.  Such bugs are exceptionally annoying if one likes to play on 'realism' mode with no quitting without saving.  There's always some disappointment when certain other 'must have' small mods aren't included in one of these packages.  I like the dedication to accuracy, but because of it - it lacks the diversity in troops that other mods or native have.   I dig Viking stuff though, so I admit some bias here.  It's fun as hell to pillage monestaries and wrecking villages doesn't have as much negative impact.  There is also a nice addition of being able to build a home base 'refuge' apart from taking over a castle and having to deal with the ramifications of that.  It's nice if you want to go the bandit route.  I just can't help but feel it lacks some of the bells and whistles from other mods, though.  It also suffers from a common problem that a lot of other mods have - a lack of enemies.  There are some very small bandit type groups, and some raiders... but they seem a bit too sparse to keep it interesting. I very much enjoyed this game and I highly recommend. I am going to go over everything that I think needs going over and highlighting pros and cons.
Controls- The controls of this game are exactly like that of Subnautica, and if you have played any successful underwater game you should have no issued moving around in the Debris environment. The FOV of this game is locked in place but I think that it is set to an acceptable size, seeing at the entire game is underwater with a mask on.
Graphics- I think that the graphics of this game are beautiful for an underwater game in the highest settings possible and the game makes it easy to determine which settings are best for your computer. However, even when put on these "optimal" settings I was still not able to get above 40fps, either having a optomization issue or some other reason I think that in order to have the graphics specified, a much beefier computer might be needed. Keeping in mind that I had a consistient 40fps throughout the entire game, so if you aren't a freak about having max fps possible then this isn't an issue. Additionally the game still looks appealing without being on max graphics.
Atmosphere- The atmosphere is definitely that of a horror game, and quite frankly this is done really well. The mixture of fogs, underwater lakes, lights, darkness, and sounds all come together to give the player a sense of "void" in some areas while in others pure claustrophobia. It allows the player to completely fall into the shoes of the main character and experience what he and the others are going through. Even when you are just told what's happening in another tunnel.
Voice Acting- The voice acting in this game are easily my favorite because, asside from simply wandering this underwater cave system, it drives the plot. The way things are said, the way that some characters cut eachother off is all planned to help bring the ending together, as well as tie up potential loose ends. Additionally, the voices just sound like real people. The actors themselves and the dialogue put infront of them is both well written and well executed.
Story- The story of this game is based on choices. There are four main choices that each playthrough provides the main character and the descision made determines the rest of the game and how the characters get to the ending. However, the ending is the exact same every time, so the way that you got there is different. Although the whole "what does it matter if the ending is the same" would usually be present, such as in Mass Effect 3, that is not the case for this game. It completely changes what you notice and everything develops and then the very end just blows it all up in your face to leave you in your chair saying "holy♥♥♥♥♥♥"
Replayability- I actually urge anyone who plays this game to play it through at least twice. This is because once the ending is revealed to you, you will go back and notice things you never noticed, things that were said that you didn't hear, and noises you heard but never understood.

Don't let it's occasional bargain bin sale price lure you in.
For a game that takes a mere 3 hours to complete, the experience quickly becomes repetitive and shallow. Essentially a D-rate Tomb Raider clone, the gimmick here is water and how water influences the game's environments, puzzles, combat, and physics. Unfortunately, the water is overhyped and not enough to make a sub-par gaming experience worthy of your time. While the developers deserve credit for listening to player feedback and releasing two updated versions of the game after launch, the game is currently still plagued with bad design and technical issues like poor collision detection, missing textures, dumb AI, and game-breaking bugs (for some).
Gameplay and level design are outright bland. The single enemy type in the game (save for the "final boss") can be easily dispatched with by using your default weapon. There are electricity and fire hazards that can be used to inflict environmental damage upon your foes, but the same tactics are used in every skirmish. The touted ability to control water doesn't even occur until right before the final boss, and at that point it really only seems to be there for that battle. What initially seem like clever and unique puzzles end up being recycled many, many times over the course of the game. With regards to level design, for a ship that is purported to be as large as a city, there are not many places the player gets to see that seem to have had much movement or life in them. The few room variations seen are mostly non-specific server-type rooms and innumerable hallways for the sake of filler. WIthout an in-game guide telling you where to go, it would be very easy to lose yourself amidst the incredibly similar rooms.
Controls can be broken into three areas: water, surface, and climbing. Within the water, controls are jittery; hindered by a camera that is cumbersome and erratic, particularly near the water's surface. For a game with such a keen focus on water, having sloppy water controls is unforgivable. On the surface is where much of the combat is found, it is uninspired. Surface controls are heavy and tank-like, and it can be difficult to get out of the way of enemy fire once it starts. When climbing, objects that can be mounted or climbed on are almost always bright red, eliminating much of any thought while moving vertically in the environment.
With regards to the writing, the main character and her unseen ally are unlikable. What I imagine the developers were going for was a protagonist/radio ally kinship like Lara/Zip/Alister had in Tomb Raider: Legend. However, between the writing and voice acting, hearing what any character has to say quickly becomes irritating. The game's overall plot manages to be confusing in its brief 3 hours. While it is clear that the ship you are on has been invaded by terrorists and you are trying to make it through said ship, anything beyond that is lost due to poor storytelling.
While this game could have brought some interesting concepts to the action-adventure genre, the ideas that were to set it apart were poorly or badly executed, making this forgettable game one to pass on.

It's Left 4 Dead, but with swords!
A statement that is both technically true and completely inadequite for what the game actually is. Warhammer: End Times- Vermintide is a dip into the gritty fantasy world of Warhammer Fantasy, where a group of heroes fight off the unending hordes of horrific rat men known as the skaven.
On the surface, it plays very similar to Left 4 Dead. You have a ranged weapon, a melee weapon, a healing item slot, an explosive item slot and a buffing item slot. And in each map your four heroes have to fight their way to a goal, accomplish it, and make it to the escape point. The differences pop up in the details.
For one, the skaven feel a little more devious than the infected of Left 4 Dead. Now, I'm sure that it's probably a bit of a smoke and mirrors kind of thing, in that the AI isn't all that different. But the practical effects of how the rat men are placed in the maps, the way they taunt and mock the players while fighting, gives the ratmen a lot more character.
Combat has a good flow to it. Blocking and doding is a massive part of it, as mindless hacking and slashing will only take you so far, especially in the higher difficulties.
Gear is tied directly to the characters. You won't be finding new weapons scattered about the stages, instead earning it through die rolls at the end of each sucessfuly completed stage. Which is probably the one complaint I do have with the game. The RNG is a tricky mistress and even with some of the new options in the latest Sigmar's Blessing DLC, it can still be very frustrating to wind up with low quality gear when you've survived a nail biting Nightmare difficulty run.
All in all though, Vermintide is a blast of a game and a joy to see the now destroyed Warhammer Fantasy world so lovingly rendered. Highly recommended!

Early initial impressions from mainly doing the aircraft scenarios. There is a lot of detail in the game and the AI seems to work well. Although if you make a mistake in setting up your missions there is no assistance and so at first it can be a little frustrating working out why your missions don't go to plan. For example if you setup a plane formation and your allocated  group of planes does not have enough planes the AI will just leave some of your aircraft floundering. I think in that respect the interface could be improved in letting the player know where there is an issue. I believe the simulation is under constant development. There are different layers of settings or so called doctrines to control your own sides AI and that can get complicated. On first look the simulation looks very basic, no next gen 3D graphics here, and it is although it uses detailed world wide terrain maps. Note a fast CPU will help since I understand the AI decision making is detailed and so I expect a lot of units could slow down the game. I've not had any issues here but I've  only been playing relatively small scenarios. The instructions are basic and so the best way to learn how to play is to see people playing it and Bunyap sims has a nice set of Youtube videos. Baloogan also champions the sim and has his own supporting web site on the military database the simulation uses. The database is very detailed and the AI uses the info it contains for its decision making. You have to import most of the database images from a fan site due to copyright issues. There are a lot of scenarious included to play through although you can design your own scenarious.  Its a shame the developers couldn't reduce the retail price so people sitiing on the fence would buy it. I bought mine in a recent Steam sale.  If you are interested in military hardware and strategy from after WWII to the present you will like this game/simulation.

Contagion is a standalone game from the team behind one of the most popular Source Engine mods, Zombie Panic: Source. This title features team-based gameplay and multiple gamemodes including Escape (objective maps), Extraction (defense), and Hunted (PvP). While it's execution on these game types is good, I'll be focusing my scores mainly on the Escape gamemode - which is the co-op objective maps.
This is a great game to play with friends, and offers variety on maps in a similar way that the AI Director does in Left 4 Dead. The maps are semi-randomized each time, including different items being in new spots and you will have different tasks to complete before escaping. For the most part, the game itself is fairly intense and very moody. Especially when your fellow survivors have turned and are now on the hunt for your tasty, sweat-soaked flesh. Yum. However, sketchy hitboxes and some jerky animations will yank you right out of the immersion. It's entertaining indeed, but it loses it's shine rather quickly. While it's a good game, it just seems to be lacking something that Zombie Panic: Source had. I can't quite put my finger on it.
