It's solid for what it is honestly, the game isn't designed to be this romanticized horror that sweeps you into a horde and you emerge with over 300+ in a killcount. This game is Faux-realistic, while it's not perfect, it goes to great lengths that most games have forgotten are important to making things far better immersionwise.
You start off usually with a firearm or two, depending on your chosen mode, and are thrusted into a "48 hours after patient zero." scenario, little ammo and zombies overbustling the streets or buildings. You can go loud and risk attracting the hordes, which drop harder than sacks of bricks on headshot, or shrug off bullets like nothing, the maps have a mix of light, and dark environments, forcing you to huddle with a flashlight as any sensible person would. There is an infection mechanic, where In any co-op or PvP mode, this will turn you into a player zombie after a short bit of time, and start hunting the other players, with a fun twist of mechanics and controls to keep the player vs zombie aspect fresh, without becoming left for dead.
If you're looking for a co-op survival horror, that is solid for the sake of keeping the horror aspect, and giving a slower, methodical take on a zombie shooter, this is right up your alley.
If not, then go, you're free to leave, nobody wanted you to read this, not even that pet gerbil that goaded you on cared enough about this review.

I know I have, at this point, only scratched the surface. Or, rather, gently rubbed at the surface, but I wish to state now that I thoroughly reccommend that you buy this game. I have been wanting to get CMANO since it was first released but just could not justify the cost.
Anyway, what is so special? I played a game called Harpoon many years ago. I played each version as it came out. This is the spiritual successor to Harpoon. There are even the same people who were so influencial in Harpoon 2 and 3 working on this version. For example Ragnar Emsoy.
What do you get for your money then?
Flashy graphics with amazing 3d models of the ships and aircraft you control? No
Great voice acting? No
Great big explosions when your weapons hit an airfield? No
A game of such depth and interest that it will keep you playing for years? Hell yes!!!
A developer who is always looking for new additions to the game? Yes
A developer who adds these new additions regularly? Yes
A developer who fixes bugs quickly? Yes!
Large community who can help you get started? Yes
The ability to create your own scenarios? Yes
The ability to modify platforms with new weapons? Yes
The maps are basic, but then this is the point of the game. You are controlling groups and platforms from a command centre. you are not looking down on the world seeing Intruders and prowlers flying over mountains. You have NTDS symbols that move across the map following your flight plan.
When creating scenarios you don't just have two sides to play with. Create multiple sides with different postures between various factions. No longer red vs blue. Want red vs blue with green who are neutral to blue but also are unfriendly to red? Easy to set this up.
This is not an easy game. If you want a game that you manually fly your intruder into Hanoi airspace during the Vietnam war, expect to destroy a missile park, (yeah, I've read "flight of the Intruder" lots!), and fly out again this is not for you. If you want to plan full alpha strikes and set up ingress and egress points yourself with iron hand missions going in first then this is for you. But this is not just a game set in the past. The platforms include the Queen Elizabeth aircraft carrier, not yet in service. There are two databases available for the game, the cold war database and DB3000. This give you the choice of so many platforms with DB3000 giving platforms from 1980 to 2015 onwards. This is so brilliant!!!

The price is ridiculously high because >Matrix Games. Naturally, this is for passionate strategy fans with great demand for realism. Even though this game focuses primarily only on naval and air control, the degree of realism is quite high.
At first you can just launch some planes and order them to engage particular enemies with few buttons.... OR you can analyze characteristics and properties of your planes, naval units, their missiles, radar specifications, etc. etc. and use that to choose certain combinations of loadout and to control individual planes' movement, speed and other properties in high detail, even though without fancy graphics.
The game offers a range of scenarios, both hypothetical and historical, yet it remains a tactically-oriented strategy, rather than something global like what we see from Paradox or even other Matrix Games titles. Nonetheless, if that's what you're looking for, then you found something worth your while.
Lastly, performance can be an issue as the game seems to be quite demanding despite its lack of great graphics. Don't let screenshots deceive you - this game will weigh on your PC unless it's adequate enough to run some of the latest titles on ultra settings.
Other than that 7/10. I'm sure there is a niche for this kind of games, and this looks like the most serious\professional strategy game ever made - a kind of game that NATO staff plays to exercise their strategic skills. As someone who studied strategy in college, I recommend it for those interested in the subject. For others? Not so much.

Built on the detailed database core of the old Harpoon series, this is certainly aimed at the serious gamer in modern warfare simulation.  As is true in modern warfare command, the game is experienced through detailed messages and digital map information provided by selected active and passive sensors.  Response, reaction, planning, and dealing with the ongoing fog of war make this real enough to be used by many current and retired professionals.  For those looking for high-quality graphics of actual combat, the Command: Modern Air / Navel Operations is certain to be a disappointment.  The real place the game is experienced is in the mind of the player.  And, like genuine warfare, it can unfold slowly and be tedious, only to suddenly hit the player with an unmanageable number of unexpected twists and turns.  Meticulously detailed to reflect actual tactical and platform abilities and limitations for warfare dating from the early 1950s into the near-future, the game includes numerous scenarios that can be played at a variety of realism levels.  Each can also be edited (allowing you to answer questions like, "Say, what if we would have had a Aegis class back in the era of the Vietnam war?").  The strength of this game is "under the hood," is modeling aspects of real-world warfare as close as it can get without violating national security.
Epic...Large....Detailed...Reminds me of work. Love this game.

In my opinion, this is a great single "squad" based top down strategy game that excites the genre of typical chess games.
Regicide pits you against another in either classical chess format or an enriched chess format that offers pawns, rooks, knights, castles,bishops, the queen , and king special abilities. It also allows stratigic powers that subetily change the battlefield while not (currently) being over powered.
A quick example is thus. Pawns cannot attack going foward, however in regicide they have the ability to "shoot" targets of oppertunity within 3 spaces infront of them. This allowed my pawn to shoot the enemy king until death. This may seem abhorant to normal chess players but I found it exciting.
With more updates, a campaign, and new races Regicide could be the PC Warhammer 40k fix many of us have been looking for.
Still with the RNG type weirdness where a unit could be safe and at other times completely boned. But with a stratigic sensibility that I believe Dawn of War could never offer(because of spam of certain units types or nerfs, etc).

Although, I love the Warhammer and Warhammer 40K universes and have read almost all the Horus Heresy books, played the tabletop miniatures and role playing games; as well as almost all the PC based Warhammer/Warhammer 40K games, I was hesitant about this game, because I kept reading and hearing references to "Chess" and I do not want a chess game and have no interest in chess.
Despite that, I bought the game anyway and WOW...was I impressed!
Even though not all the features have been implemented yet, such as the campaign for example, as it IS EARLY ACCESS, I am still having a ton of fun and cannot wait for the DLC and more features to be incorporated.
I played in Regicide mode, which although still has the different types of units moving as would their chess counter parts, and you must protect your Space Marine Captain or Ork Boss, depending what side you play, I felt the comparison to chess ENDS there.
I played against the AI twice in default mode and lost because I forgot to protect my Captain, but in the next game; even though I lost I did alot better.
The AI first brought out its "Meganobz" which for a few turns slaughtered my Space Marines, until I had my Librarian, 1 Devastor and 1 Terminator unleash all hell on it, with the fatal stroke being from my Assault Marine who dramtically butchered him with his chainblade.
Howevr, i was really upset at having to watch him kill 3 of my Space marines leaving them a splashing explosion of gore.
Thus, when the Orks started moving each and every Orkboyz forward, i replied in kind.
Soon, the frontline had  all my tactial marines, minus 3 of them against all of the Orkboyz.
All I could do was focus fire on each, as they every turn focus fired on my Captain, who took turn after turn of ranged punishment.
I was freaking out wondering just how much more he could withstand, as he only had 4 pts of health left.
I still had 1 Devestator, 1 Terminator, and one Assault Marine, along with a few Tactial Marines, but the enemy still had both Stormboyz, and Loota's, even after I killed all their Ork Boyz.
At this point, the Orks sent in the Orks with the Jet Packs and had me down to 3 Tactical Marines, my Captain, my Devastaor and Assault marine.
And, my poor Captain was taking even more punishment despite all my attempts to protect him.
Just as I felt my last 3 Tactical Marines and my heavily wounded Captain might be able to take out the Ork Boss and his two remaining Orks, they got lucky and pop shotted my Captain taking his last little health left away and winning.
I am still learning and I get better each time I play, and the game is VERY addictive, as the animations are AWESOME, BRUTAL, and BLOODY. The game really rubs it in when a marine or ork gets killed.
The voices are AWESOME and the Orks true to their way, are HYSTERICAL in what they say even though they are not trying to be funny.
This all combines to an emotional game experience, where you really FEEL for your losses....as I found myself saying out loud to the Orks:
"oh I can do that to you too!"
"Oh you want some?"
"I freaking hate you"
"Yeah, how does that feel?"
Since 1992 when I first started PC gaming, I have never done that!
Man, I was really getting into it.
Anyway, please remember this game is in Early Access, and will get more to it, but even now just playing Regicide is FUN!
However, there are some bugs regarding multiplayer where you try to start a match and instantly die.
But  despite that, its a fun addicting game, and even for people like me that are poor at chess it is so COOL to just say "Heck with it" and start firing weapons to make up for your lack of chess skills.
However, you are constantly trying to balance your chess strategy with a Warhammer 40K Squad Strategy (Firing Weapons etc).
For too much of one or the other will result in your defeat.
Case in point, my last opponent was first pwning me in warfare, i.e. shooting etc, so I played chess to make him nervous and break his focus, but then he outmatched me chess wise, so I resorted to weapons.
Thus, you have to be on your guard for chess moves AND Warhammer 40K squad tactics.
Its an awesome combination.

Okay I am writing this review after the tutorial and one Regicide skirmish game in an early access game, as I feel have a good idea of where this game is and going. I am a massive old school Games Workshop fan.
This game is chess with the added abilities of space marines and orks. You play your normal chess moves with auto kills for taking pieces through the usual methods. However, you now get three initiative points, which allow you to fight as if you are on a 40K battlefield, hunker down, throw grenades, activate shields etc.
This means that the usual boring game of chess (sorry chess heads, but I grew up on computer and war games with dice), is now replaced with a much more tactical battlefield experience. However, you can always just use this game to play to standard chess rules if you want, ZZZZZzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz....
An example would be - oh no I have ended up diagonal to a Space Marine pawn, but have two Orks adjacent. They use initiative points next turn to shoot him up close once each, they pass their hit check and there is one dead space marine. The chess nerd sitting opposite cries into his chess book.
At the moment we only have skirmish mode with two factions to choose against various levels of AI or human players. However, a campaign mode is planned where you can level up your pieces, and I can only assume that other factions will be added at a later date to spice things up (maybe as paid DLC though).
I think this game is definately going to be worth the current asking price. However, as it is only an early access game, there is always a risk involved. As long as they add what they have promised, then I think the risk is worthwhile. I might wait for the campaign mode to be finished before playing it heavily myself though.
Then it will be...For the Emperor or Waggggghhhh depending on which way I decide to swing.

Regicide mode completely made me forget about chess, and really does a good job of capturing the violence of 40k, with the strategy of chess. However, the computer player wasn't so lenient, and kicked my♥♥♥♥♥in both chess and regicide mode.
The game is in early-access, so it is rather bare-boned at the moment. There is no campaign or progression, but the devs have stated they are going to only have a 2-4 month EA period so fingers crossed this content is quickly added.
Voice-acting and music is suitably awesome, but some gun-fire sound effects seem muted and dull in comparison. Space Marine (the game) this is not.
For 15 dollars, its a 40k-themed battle chess with awesome presentation value as well an additional game-play set of rules. After playing a few more games I would say that this game is much better than most people may think.  The chess aspect of the game is present, and you can try to play the game as a typical chess board game.  However after moving your piece you then get to initiate what basically comes down to range combat.  Your typical have 3 initiative points that allow you to attack the other players soliders, or to use skills to either boost the effectivness of your own troops, or damage and weaken the enemy.  This adds a whole new layer to the game, as you could have a sound "chess" game strategy, but even when a peice is cornered, you can still fight and potentially turn the battle around in your favor, without even ahving to move a single peice.  Played a game where the Space Marine Commander was the only one left, but I couldnt corner him, and he was slowly tearing my boyz apart.  In the end I won but how qucik was able to turn around with only one piece made me rethink some of my strategies for future games.  Overall I still believe that this game has a ton of potential, is fun and enjoyable, and is worth at least trying. This game is great. It's like Minecraft, except you don't really have to mine.
The building of structures is not horrible, but it's not forgiving either. I've seen and used better, but I've also seen and used much much worse.
The crafting and tech tree is brilliant, best I've seen in crafting games. When you craft a new thing, like a knife, now you can also craft new things like sliced bread and meat. I haven't dabbled in much alchemy so I don't know if after I craft Mayonaisse that a sandwich would be next, but I'm eager to find out! On second thought, maybe I need to tame a cow, milk it, then make cheese first....Hmmmm....
This is the kind of rabbit hole you fall down in this game. That's why I say the crafting and tech tree is the best ever. It's designed to make you want to explore it deeper. I haven't reached it yet, but I can definitely see the bottom or end of that tree being a big sad for me, but that's the only downside and, being that this is still EA, maybe the bottom will get deeper!
The survival is kinda harsh. If you explore on foot early on, be prepared to die. It's not so bad because your items will still be there, so if you have a good sense of direction (you'll respawn at a locked spawn point in a given world) you can just make a weapon quickly and go kill the beast that ate your last incarnation then retake your own loot.
That brings up another point about this game: It's not simple to get started. I've enocuntered two different ways to start this game, one for the hardcore purists and one for the casual.
If you're hardcore you start in hunter mode. Get weapons fast. I like the pistol crossbow. You just kill every predator you find and feast on them to survive until you eradicate their existence entirely. Then you can safely gather the massive amount of materials you'll need to build a base and secure survival. Next up will be building a ship so you can go conquer the wilds of another Yland. Remember to kill all the predators first, lad.
Or
If you're casual, you can just open up your saved game seed in the editor, drop every material resource within a few yards of your spawn point, go and hand pick nearby predators and fling them to the other side of the Yland, build a small structure and plop in some crafting stations, then save your handiwork and then play it in explore mode again - stay away from the wrenched thumbnail.
I've yet to try out multiplayer because all my friends are squares when I tell them to get this game, but meh...There's enough here to keep me entertained for a while.
10/10 for depth and ease of use

This review may contain spoilers.
if you loved Hotline Miami 1 for its theme, the neo 80s art style and music by artists such as Mitch Murder, Perturbator, M.O.O.N and the likes, you have come to the right place. A lot of love for details went into the level designs, the music choice to fit the overall theme of each stage and cutscene to make each setting truly outstanding and surprise the player with ever newer elements.
While the overall art style, the continuation of the first game's story takes off in a graceful manner, the overall gameplay went from a well organized mix of challenges and a bit of a grind from the first game to a mix of luck and pure grindfest. While in the first game you were able to see the imminent danger, be it whether ambushing russian mobsters behind furniture, ready to spray their bullets all over the main protagonist of the game or a general overview of the different rooms on a stage, making it easier for you to plan your assault into the area..
in this instalment, more than often, you have a hard time seeing the approaching german shepard or mobster with a shotgun or AK, spraying bullets your way which hit you just enough so that you hit the ground is just a massive gripe that will end in a spree of replays until every possible action by the opposing forces has been memorized to a point where any single movement of the main character is dead on and the margin of error is non-existent.
In addition to the much, much harder difficulty and grindier gameplay (from a playthrough on 'normal' difficulty, by the way), another thing that I had a hard time dealing with in this instalment was the fact that each stage was locked to a specific amount of characters, compared to its predecessor. While I understand that this is done on purpose to keep the story intact, it is not incredibly meainingful to not have the option of picking whichever character you like once you finished at least one playthrough and wish to replay a certain stage.
All in all while staying true to the original formula of the first game with the stage themes, the kick♥♥♥♥♥neo 80s soundtracks, the continuation of the story and the truly unique characters, which are given additional exposure with the designed environments they live, work and interact in, in terms of the game and gameplay itself it's a much, much harder and way less forgiving game, where it gets much closer to being a grind, similar to games like Dark Souls or a "I wanna be the guy"-esque randomness in enemy behaviour and difficulty setting than being what the main instalment was very successful at: being a well balanced challenge that still remained demanding enough to give it another try.

Door Kickers is a top down strategy game where you plan out routes for you swat units to take and clear out the baddies.  There's customization, classess, the every slight presence of RPG elements, and robust and rewarding gameplay.
But this is a game I am torn on.
On one hand, it is very well made strategic and tactical experience with LOADS of content to keep you busy if you love it. However, even with its varying levels of difficulty and what should be endless costomization options to suit each level, the gameplay gets stale very fast.

To be clear, I absolutely love the gameplay and all of the ideas that are brought to the table, but it is needlessly big.  It's like going to see a movie that has a lot of good stuff but it goes on an hour too long.  Now in videogames, that shouldn't be a problem, you just don't play the extra stuff, but here's the rub:  you are paying for it.
The $20 price tag is my only issue with the game.  Other than that, it's perfect for a quick play every now and then and delivers all that it should.  If you like strategy games and it's on sale for say, $10 I highly recommend it, but there isn't enough here to justify the 20 dollar tag.

Door Kickers is a top down, tactical, strategy, shooter, hybrid developed by Killhouse Games.
The core gameplay of Door Kickers is controlling a squad of trained SWAT team members as you clear out various locations, ranging from drug dens to warehouse's. The player can pause the game and enter planing mode. In this mode the player and set where their team will move and face to cover every angle. In this mode the player can also prep their squad to breach doors, throw grenades and set various other orders. Once the player resumes time the team will do the actions in real-time, the squad can also be controlled in real-time.
The story comes from the games campaigns. Each campaign has permadeath for the squad members, so if a squad member dies in the first mission, they will not be available for any other mission, unless the first mission is restarted. Multiple campaigns with different difficulties, lengths and missions add a fair amount of replay value to the game. Campaigns, however, are locked until the player reaches a high enough profile level. Door Kickers also comes with single missions, some being training missions but most being more challenging. A random mission generator is also available. The player can choose the size of the map and how difficult it is, adding even more replay value.
Door Kickers has various classes to be unlocked, from shields to breacher's, all with their own tools, weapons, and customizable names. There are well over 100 weapons and tools for the various classes. Players can complete missions any way they see fit, charging in with assault rifles and shields or stealthy with suppressed submachine guns. Players have complete control of how they execute a mission.
Door Kickers does a fair amount right:
Has a large variety of guns and classes
Has great replay value from various maps and game modes
Addictive
Fantastic sound design
The art style fits well
Door Kickers does a few things wrong:
The player must unlock the campaign
The guns can be expensive to unlock
Doesn't keep the player interested over time
Can be to easy/hard based on skill level
Surprisingly hard to remain stealthy
Overall Door kickers is a solid title. With a price tag of $21.99CND, it is a bit pricy for someone who doesn't commonly enjoy this genre of game. If Door Kickers goes on sale, pick it up and try it out, it's a great deal of fun and great for killing some time.

Can I recommend this game?
In it's current state, no I cannot. At least not to your average player.
I wish I could write a more positive review, but I can't lie to myself or to the developers and players.
Here's my ethos before I continue: I've played Artix's games for many years. Played Battleon back in 06, Played AQW during it's Beta back in 08 and still continue to play it every now and then despite not liking it's current state. I backed this game on Kickstarter and I am currently an Epic Founder for this game.
So here are my basic PROS:
- Developers constantly listens to the community. This is a quality I 100% admire epsecially since nowadays developers never take advice from the people who actively play their product, which leaves said product to crash and burn.
- Developers reward it's players and are very generous when it comes to appreciating it's fanbase.
- Cross-play! A gimmick that's never touched by anyone and I'm glad to see an ambitious idea actually becoming a reality.
- The writing never takes itself too seriously and is self-aware.
- Wow! An MMO that isn't Pay2Win! Holy smokes!
- Art-style is really nice.
Now to the dreaded CONS:
- GRIND GRIND GRIND GRIND GRIIIIIND!!! Expect to repeat doing to same dungeon about gorillion times just to level up from Level 8 to Level 9, or to obtain a few hundred gold.
- Speaking of dungeons, you can only do 20 dungeon runs at a time. You recieve 1 dungeon key every several hours or so, making the grind even more "fun".
- The crafting system is absolutely horrendous. In most games, you already risk life and limb and spend many hours just to obtain the materials to craft the item you desperately want. Well in this game, not only do you have to kill yourself over getting materials, they nickel and dime you over crafting the item itself. You have to spend A LOT of gold just to craft an item, and on top of it all, you have to wait for the crafting to be finished. "So you broke your back getting materials to craft that ancient rare sword? Give me half of what's in your wallet and come back in 24 hours!"
- Progression is bad and EXP gain is low. I see Level 8 players desperately trying to kill 1 skeleton because the transition between areas are too high. You go from an area where there are Level 7- 8 creatures to an area where there are Level 10 - 11 creatures? I guess we the players are suppose to grind more in the dungeons beforehand, but golly gee I wonder what's limiting my grinding!
-  It's not worth spending gold on low-level gear because they cost so much to begin with, you'll outgrow them really quick, and you'll find objectively better gear way later. Due to the horrendous grind it's hard to farm for more gold. So enjoy having really crappy gear for a while.
CONCLUSION:

Do you have a lot of friends that come over to your house? This is a perfect party game. Instead of an emphasis on gameplay skill or quick reflexes, these games are much more focused on wits, intelligence, and humor. It's perfect even for people who don't usually play video games. We all know that one time when we went over to a friend's house to play Mario Kart/ Super Smash Bros or something and he crushed all of us without even trying because he's the only one who owns the godamn game damnit. There's no such advantages available here, since the game is mainly trivia/ humor based.
Another great thing is you don't have to go fiddling around with any Xbox game controllers or anything like that. There is a cool browser based system where you just have to enter a code at jackbox.tv, using any browser. This means anyone with a smartphone can easily connect to the game they want to play as long as they have an internet connection. This is genius stuff, some of the games can have up to 8 players so instead of having to fiddle with a bunch of tangled wires/ teach everyone the controls, it is simple enough to set up and play. I've had good success using Valve's Steam Link paired with this game on a large TV with a group of people, it's always a good time!
The party pack comes with these 5 games below, although you'll probably only regularly play 2 or 3 of them.
Fibbage:
This game is played a lot I think, essentially some trivial question is given that nobody will likely know, it's pretty obscure stuff like "What did Abraham Lincoln get as a present from this random governor on Independence Day?" or something similar, players have to input a good lie they think may fool everyone else, and then everyone chooses from a compiled list of lies from players and one truth embedded within. You get points for both fooling others and picking out the truth. Always a goofy fun time!
Earwax:
Essentially Apples to Apples or Cards Against Humanity in audio form, everyone gets a prompt, and is given a list of random sounds to choose from. This can be pretty fun, like a prompt would say "Superman, while drunk." and you can respond with the sounds *Loud, Long Fart* followed with *Man Screaming*. However, the issue with this game is you don't get to hear the sound before you play it so sometimes the results are not what you expect.
Bidiots:
This one is complicated. Everyone is given a different subject to try and draw on their ♥♥♥♥♥♥ little smartphones, and there's a set price to each art piece, which is kept hidden from players. Everyone gets only a few hints as to how much each piece is worth, and they take turns bidding on each art piece at an auction. Whoever makes the most profit wins. This can be pretty fun but there's quite a bit of strategy involved. It'll probably take a couple of times before people understand completely how this game works, but it's one of the deeper experiences in here, there's a lot of strategies like "fake bidding" to raise the price of a piece you know isn't worth anything. Pretty fun but you need a group that's willing to learn a bit about the mechanics to get the most out of it.
Quiplash:
Pretty popular game, a prompt is given and people write what they think would be the funniest response to it. After this, people vote on what they think is the funniest/ most apt response. It's mostly humor based, from what I can tell. I actually found this game kinda boring, there wasn't enough structure to keep my interest for too long, but you might like it.
BombCorp:
Kind of a simpler Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes, this game has you defusing bombs with a group of friends. You essentially shout out instructions on how to defuse a bomb and somebody tries to defuse it without it going off. This game only has 4 players maximum and is probably better suited for a smaller group of dedicated people. There is a psuedo-story mode and looks pretty fun, but I haven't played it much.
Jackbox Party Pack 2 is a fun selections of party games that will always be a hit with friends, unless your friends are big lame-os who hate fun.

Jackbox is a lot of fun for having friends over—like four board games, but all you have to do is turn on the game. No pieces to lose or complicated set-up. Quiplash and Fibbage are especially fun with groups, though all the games are enjoyable. Make sure you have some way to stream the game to a TV or put it on a laptop everyone can see, though. Apple TV, chromecast, etc. will all work.

+ Insane complexity.
+ Size of the database.
+ Gameplay.
+ LOTS of automated processes, no need for micro-management.
+ Relatively easy to 'jump in' if you have played Harpoon series before.
+ Excellent support by developpers (last patch had changelog of 40+ A4 pages).
+ Watching map full of half circles fighting rombs.
- Hard to explain to your girlfriend what you are doing in the middle of the night.
- Sometimes unintuitive UI (due to complexity and large variety of possibilities).
- Larger scenarios can need quite a powerful computer.
- NOT FOR EVERYONE. You need to find some military geek in you to play this.
First of all, take a look at the screenshots. This is all you will see. No fancy graphics, but a map full of symbols...
I bet you get excited, didn't you?
This is not a game, it's a simulation. Very complex. Difficult. With steep learning curve.
But once you get into it, you will LOVE IT.
UI is good, but _sometimes_ unintuitive and you need to get used to it.
Complexity is mind blowing. Well, for example - algorithm that calculates radar reflectivity, besides many other factors, takes into an account speed of rotation of aircraft's jet engine fans plus angle of reflection from it. And everything is happening on your desktop computer. In real time.
No words can describe the emotions when you try to hunt down this bloody Sovremenny-class destroyer with your Kobben class submarines. Then, your girlfriend comes in and asks what you are doing. Well... how can you explain to her, in simple words, that you are ambushing Baltic Fleet with 4 Kobben-class submarines? (This is probably the biggest flaw of the game)
I spent most of my time in the scenario editor. And it is not what you think. You can turn on time flow and play the scenario against yourself within the editor, switching sides from time to time. This is more like your sandbox and playground.
I researched military power in my region, replicated all squadrons and units. Read dozens of wiki pages, followed twitter and facebook accounts of military units. And had lots of fun checking out my 'what if' scenario.
I payed full price for this game and I would pay for it again.

Effectively a spiritual successor to Larry Bond's Harpoon series.  Like its predecessor, graphics aren't much, but you really don't need fancy graphics for something like this (if you do want graphics similar to Jane's Fleet Command, Global Conflict Blue may be more up your alley).  Has LUA scripting support.  Word of warning though: If you don't enjoy staring at tons of unit/weapon tables, this is probably not the game for you.  As of the writing of this, while naval/air combat is simulated quite well, ground combat really isn't there quite yet.  Important to note that the devs constantly update this game.  Regarding the price:  I bought it for full price, I've personally gotten more than my money's worth from it, but considering it's a very niche game: if you don't KNOW you'll get your money's worth out of it, I would recommend you purchase it when it's on sale.  Last point: Be prepared to learn.  This is not an easy game that you can just pick up and play very successfully.
A small note about the new "Command LIVE scenarios" DLC.  I personally like the concept of ripping stuff straight from the headlines to wargame.  Not everyone may be fond of this, however.

While expensive at the get go.  This game.. no... this simulation is by far the most complete simulation for Modern Air/Naval Simulations.  The Database alone is worth the price.  I would highly suggest this simulation for anyone looking to replace Harpoon with something much more modern!  (I have owned this simulation since launch and have invested many hours into it.  I recently installed the steam version (Which Matrix gave all owners of the simulation steam keys when it launched on steam.  If you choose to buy one simulation this year, make it this one!!
The best of its kind.

EDIT: If you see this on sale, and you liked the idea enough to check out reviews, buy the thing.
Apparently, they picked the Blue Pill.
Has a pretty good database of military ships, aircraft and weapons. Its cheaper than a subscription to Janes. There are a lot of decent scenarios written for this game.
That all said, this is still a game, when it could be a simulator (which is how it is advertised). It cant seem to pick between game and simulator - UI that makes life harder than it has to be, which is an absolute nono for a game, then a very realistic list of units to pick from - that do not follow realistic performance or tactics, especially the aircraft.
In fairness to the games developers, the game does handle ship to ship combat in the modern age, very well. Its aircraft still need a fair bit of love.
This is a game that for the longest time, I held hope that there was some chance that issues would be attended to - and if they were, the game still has that potential to be a fantastic military command simulation - but there is seemingly no interest in realism for the sake of reality.
For $30, this would be a fantastic game. At over 3 times that however, its simply not worth the money.
EDIT - Having spent some time on the latest build of 1.07, Ive decided to revise my fair price upwards to $45. A number of very much needed improvements have been added since my last serious amount of in depth play, granting the player significantly more control over their units.
All other things being equal, one thing you cannot fault the developers on is their update cycle. Comparing 1.01 and 1.07 goes to show what an update cycle SHOULD look like. Many other small developers could take note.
EDIT - With 1.10, Id pay $50 for this title. Controls are better, aircraft are smarter, a host of much needed improvements. Kudos again to the devs - literally the only thing at this point making this review a not recommended is the price tag. The title still doesnt scratch the realism itch hard enough for me, but it is still an enjoyable game.

Command: Modern Air/Naval Operations in the press
AWARDS / DISTINCTIONS / NOMINATIONS
War Is Boring – Best War Games of 2013: “This isn’t just a game. It’s a simulation that’s as close as many of us will ever get to real Pentagon simulation. C:MANO, as fans call it, is a real-time game that boasts an incredibly rich—and unclassified—database of the aircraft and ships of the Cold War and beyond. [...] I strongly suspect that this game won’t prove any less accurate than the government’s tippity-top-secret simulations.”
Usenet (CSIPGWH) - Wargame of the Year 2013: “I had no idea just how epic this thing is.”
Eurogamer.dk – Best Simulation of 2013: “Command is already, in its v1.02 incarnation, not just a technical marvel, there are still rough spots, but certainly a technical achievement of admirable caliber, and admiration is not diminished by the fact that it is made by only four men. [...] If you look a little into the future, there is no reason why this could not be the ultimate operational and tactical sea and air war simulator on the market.”
GrogHeads Readers Choice Awards 2013 – Digital Wargame of the Year and overall Digital Game of the Year: “Our Digital Wargame of the Year was certainly a worthy title holder, as Command: Modern Air/Naval Operations pulled in first place over several other acclaimed titles.”
Eurogamer.dk – Runner-up Wargame of 2014: “Command was Simulator of the Year for 2013 (we switched category). Since then its development, just as we predicted last year, has not stopped. All of the past year new free updates to the game have been made available that have refined and transformed what was already the high point of the genre.  With its latest 1.06 update, this stunning sea and air-land war simulator gets even better: in particular, there are new options for flight operations (Surge and Quick-Turnaround air operations) and an even more advanced scenario editor.”


REVIEWS (v1.05 / WOTY)
Martin Wiinholt, Eurogamer.dk : “CMANO: ‘Wargame of the Year Edition’ is a perfect-10 on the road from here: there is simply no other game (or simulation) doing what this game does. Whether you want to explore the current conflict in Ukraine, create a scenario that reveals aspects of a potential conflict between China and its neighbors over the oil in the South China Sea, or you want to try to see Israel bombing Iranian nuclear facilities, CMANO can handle it. For the last year it hasn’t left my hard drive. One can never never truly ‘finish’ it – whether you are studying military history at university or if you just love the intellectual challenge of strategy and tactics, CMANO delivers on all counts. It’s the gift that keeps on giving.
For this reviewer, CMANO is one of the most important wargames that have come out since the original Harpoon in 1989, and as such it should be rewarded: 10 / 10.”
Maj. Erich Swafford MD USAF (ret),
: “Command: Modern Air/Naval Operations belongs in the library of anyone who has even a passing interest in Air/Naval warfare, students of warfare since 1945, and also just wargamers in general who like a fun game. Like Battles of Napoleon, Combat Mission Beyond Overlord, and War in the East – this is one of those classics that will never leave my drive.
No matter what new game comes out, I always find myself coming back to CMANO because of its unrivaled ease of use and its ability to simulate events which would otherwise be totally inaccessible. This is probably the most important wargame to come out since I started in the hobby back in 1979. It’s pretty much what we all dreamed about having back then, and to now have something this professional-grade available for home use is just nothing short of amazing.”


REVIEWS (v1.00-1.04)
US Naval Institute : ““Command” will find a following not only among civilian gamers but might have value among military, government, and policy circles as a simulator of modern warfare. […] what time the designers did not spend making graphics and interface attractive were spent on building a game that depicts modern warfare on an unmatched scale. […] [This] is a game with broad appeal for everyone from casual gamers to government users looking to model unclassified, informal simulations. It likely will be the main choice for hard modern warfare simulators for years to come.”
SimHQ: “the interface is full of thoughtful details which add up to a very easy-to-use system that’s both intuitive and powerful .[...] I started playing the other night at 8pm, and my wife angrily tracked me down 4 hours later. I told her I thought I’d been playing about 45 minutes, and I meant it. She wasn’t amused, but I sure was. The game pretty much grabbed me and hasn’t let go. [...] If you’re into modern military hardware, what-if matchups or historical conflict analysis, this wargame is definitely what you’ve been waiting for. [...] Command is, if you’re into the subject at all, an investment in something which you will quite likely still be enjoying for many years.”
Out of Eight Reviews : “The powerful yet relatively easy-to-use scenario editor includes a map of the entire world and essentially every plane, ship, and submarine used by any country the past sixty years; it’s a tool that should be fully embraced by the community. [...] The flexibility to manage what you want and automate the rest certainly expands the appeal of this realistic military simulation. The AI does a good job following directions and behaving intelligently, and provides a good opponent for the battles. [...] The exhaustive unit research, flexible scenario editor, handy automated mission system, and relatively accessible interface will make Command: Modern Air/Naval Operations appeal to any fan of realistic military strategy games.”
Armchair General: “To sum up: Although the price tag might seem a bit much, this game is well worth every cent of it. If you have even a passing interest in the subject matter, then this game is for you. Command: Modern Air/Naval Operations is, without a doubt, a seriously fun, intense, involving simulation of modern naval combat with nearly infinite replay value. It is a more than worthy successor to Harpoon.”
: “The amount of content provided with the game is baffling. I was blown away by the amount of details, customization to our fleet, how I could control every aspect of the scenario without ever feeling overwhelmed. That was mostly due to how the user interface works. Sure, it still needs some work when assigning missions but overall it was a pleasant surprise. Last, but not least, community help and how Warfare Sims handles it. Tons of new scenarios in a matter of months! New database stuff, its amazing! Before buying DiRT 4, I'd recommend asking yourself what you're expecting from the game.
A Lot of players were expecting DiRT Rally 2, as DiRT Rally was a really well made Simcade rally experience (even if some of the physics were questionable at times), and this is due to promises from the Dev that the game would be "much more like the real deal than DiRT Rally". These promises and expectations were sadly not met.
However, a lot of players were expecting DiRT 3+1, while DiRT3 had a much more arcade feel. I was in this camp because I had not heard the developers promises of the game being more sim than cade prior to purchase.
This has led me to be more than happy with DiRT4. I've played multiplayer with friends and I'm currently level 20. (Not the best, I know, but I feel the review section here needs more input.) Great times and many laughs have been had.
If you buy the game expecting more of a sim with realistic handling you might find yourself regretting your purchase.
If you buy the game expecting an arcade experience you'll most likely love your time playing.
If you buy the game expecting to drive slow cars fast down cliff edge courses then you'll get what you're looking for.
Edit-
I play on the G27 Logitch Racing Wheel.
The first 30 minutes of the game will feel really bad if you play on anything other than controller. The game neglects PC users who like to set up the game prior to playing as it forces you into a course without the chance to set up and test your rig. You will not have a chance to edit control or graphical settings until you have completed or are in the process of the tutorial. This was a terrible design feature but did not affect my long term enjoyment.
TL;DR
Buy the game if you want a fun simCADE rally experience. If you were hung up on promises of sim handling and physics that would never break your immersion, then I'm afraid you might want to avoid this game. However I still do recommend that everyone gives it a try if they can look past their expectations.

Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number
Just like the first, Hotline Miami 2 is fast, brutal, challenging, and loads of fun.
Gameplay
For the most part its like the first, you go into a room and kill everyone inside. But things have been tweaked, but that's not bad. In a way Hotline Miami 2 is easier than part one, but its also harder. You will notice that you can easily take a single bullet, but in the first game if you got shot with a silenced pistol you died most of the time. But its made harder in other ways, when executing enemies it takes longer and stages or larger. The first game had plenty of masks to choose from, now you only have 7 masks that have perks, but all of these masks are new, with the exeption of Jake, and Tony has been changed slightly. Masks arent the only things that provide perks, in certain levels you can choose from weapons or techniques, in total, there is 8 starting perks. In the first game you only played as Jacket and Biker, but in this game you play up to 13 characters, in terms of gameplay they all play the same, with the exeptions of a few like Beard and Evan.
Soundtrack
In each level there is a different song, unlike the first where songs were used more than once, with that in mind the songs are just as good as the first.
Story
The story in Hotline Miami 2 leaps back and forth, some events happen during, before and after the first game so you will see some characters from the first game, like Richter, Beard and Jake. The story line is much deeper and longer than the first.
Conclusion
In the end, Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number is an amazing game with a deep storyline, amazing soundtrack and addicting gameplay. If you buy this game, you will get a good 20 hours from this game, and endless replay value with the level editor coming soon

Doorkickers is TOTALLY COMPELLING.
You maneuver your team (often just two operatives in the early missions) through a space, using a waypoint order system - and you can pause at any time to issue new orders or completely change your plan. And every map has slightly randomized enemy placement, so you can't just learn the board and precisely plan for it; one run thru will go wonderfully, but on a second try for more points, both operatives will be killed when the enemy placement changes just a bit. So it becomes not about learning the maps, but learning good tactical discipline, regardless of the map. And enemies are smart; I've been snuck up on and ambushed.
By going back through the early missions several times with untested, rookie operatives I was able to unlock the Assaulter class quite quickly - what has been described as a 'grind' looks a lot more like skill refinement, to me. When I got to a campaign mission and was completely owned - repeatedly - on the second map, I realized my command of my abilities was quite lacking, and went back to polish up. I've also been watching some enjoyably brief Let's Plays (by RedatMath) and seeing I haven't even used certain tools in my early arsenal, like the camera wand or breaching charges. So complaints of having to grind for simple tools don't resonate with me - the game feels like it's asking me to gain mastery with my starting toolset before widening it. Overall, I'm finding it a very enjoyable tactical hole to climb inside; there's always another way to handle a room, another challenge from a room with too many entrances, and another door that needs to be viciously kicked and stormed through.

This is perhaps the best 3D sonic game from 15 years ago, but it hasn't aged well. Here's my poorly-organized "review":
Just like in the first Sonic Adventure game, you can play as several familiar "hero" characters, including Sonic, Tails, and Knuckles. In addition, you can also play as a few "dark" characters, including Eggman, Shadow, and Rouge. There are three stage types: running until you reach the end of a level whilst going very fast (Sonic and Shadow stages), making your way through an area in a mechanical bipedal "thing" whilst shooting things with guns and lasers (Tails and Eggman stages), and hunting for jewels or keys whilst flying (Knuckles and Rougue stages).
The best stages are the Sonic and Shadow ones; they are very fast and are a blast to play. The Tails and Eggman stages are slow in pace, which becomes boring in later stages (you go through them wondering "when can I play a Sonic or Shadow stage and have fun again?"), though the shooting parts can be fun. Finally, the Knuckles and Rouge stages are the worst: you can only hunt down one jewel or key at a time, unlike the prequel, which showed how far or near you were to all items at all times. The first few Knuckles stages are pretty fun, but the ones near the end of the game are a crapshoot; you just have to explore massive areas for ten or fifteen minutes before you find what you're looking for. Plus, if you want to get an "A" score, you can't access the hint computers, so these stages become nothing more than a boring guessing game.
The story is more complex than those found in past Sonic games, but not by much. I won't explain further in fear of spoiling it for you...
Outside of the stellar Sonic and Shadow stages (and tedious/mundane Tails, Eggman, Knuckles, and Rogue stages), there are boss rush modes, a fun kart racing game, a multiplayer racing game (this is surprisingly fun), and more. However, perhaps the best part of the entire game is raising Chao--little Tamagotchi-like creatures. I've spent dozens of hours feeding, training, and breeding these things on the GameCube version of the game. Maxing out all of your Chao's stats, giving it a name, training it, breeding it, and sending it to school is incredible. Maybe I'm blinded by nostalgia, but I just can't explain how much fun this is.
If you grew up playing the Sonic Adventure games like I did, and want to experience some sweet nostalgia, get this game. Otherwise, this game may not be for you. The game hasn't aged well; the graphics are poor, the camera is weird at times, it is riddled with glitches, and the voice acting is terrible. These things may persuade you against getting the game, but if you're blinded by nostalgia like I am, the imperfections add to the flavor.
Notice: As of 2016.07.12, I have collected all 180 emblems, earned an "A" rank in all stages, and have maxed out my Chao's stats to 99. This was all done in about 42 hours.

This is my first review of a game on Steam, and just rightly for a game I have high hopes for. I recently found Wakfu because of the animated series on Netflix. The show itself is fantastic, and after learning it was based off a game, I had to  give it a try. I have some expirence in MMOs and turn based games; Ultima Online, Star Wars Galaxies, and Final Fantasy series as prime examples. That being said, I am still in the early stages of playing Wakfu, so these are only my thoughts so far.
I was intially a little disappointed at the limited character customization menu. That being said, the art work and animation on the characters themselves are beautifuly done. Once I created my character I began my journey on a pretty straightforward tutorial and was very impressed with the environment designs. But, It was after the basic tutorial I really started having issues. I know going in that I am coming into a whole new world of characters and terminology, but it started to get confusing. While still doing an early NPC quest, I became easily lost in navigating the user interface. I did not feel like the hot keys for combat were clearly explained or mapped propperly. The HUD icons seemed too small and placed too far apart. The objectives for the early quests also seemed somewhat vague and confusing.
This is just my initial assessment of the game, and will update my review accordingly as I play more.

Wakfu is a turn-based MMORPG, with a great variety of characters and builds, and a heavy dose of grinding.
I found the first hour enjoyable, but the tutorial leaves a lot to the imagination, and there is a steep learning curve when entering the actual game.
My main problem with the game is the combat system. In combat, there is a timer for every action, and when you're a new player, obviously you want to read what all your spells do and what your enemies are weak against, read passive buffs/de-buffs, etc. But the timer is way too short to do any of that, and seeing as you have enough action points to complete multiple attacks/spells in a go, it is a rush to complete your turn.
Secondly, the combat area is split into tiles/squares, each one accounting for 1 movement/range. Now, when casting a spell or attacking an enemy, you have to ensure that you have clear line of sight to the target, and that they are within range - which means, inside of the minimum and maximum range.
When you move your character, as there are often so many obstacles on the map, it is really hard to tell whether you will be able to attack the enemy with a spell, from the tile you are moving to. This means, if you are playing a spellcaster (and all characters have spells), you may sometimes waste a whole turn just trying to stand in a position where the enemy is in range.
There is also no basic 'attack'. You can't just hit someone. Your basic attack is determined by the weapon you are holding, and the weapon will have a predetermined attack range and attack area. For example, in the tutorial you receive an axe, this weapon attacks three squares around your character in a big sweeping motion, and if you have an ally nearby, the ally will take damage from the swing.
Basically, the combat is too complicated to have a timer, the tile system seems quite broken, and the information needed to make the learning curve less steep, is not very accessible. The tutorial itself was of no help when coming to the actual game.

I didn't even get to trying Fibbage 2 yet and I would heartily recommend this pack for Quiplash and Earwax alone. Quiplash is basically a Cards Against Humanity with slightly fewer horrendously inappropriate prompts, where everyone votes and instead of playing an answer card you fill in your own blanks. Bomb Corp is passable and Bidiots is, while interesting, a not-quite-Drawful that gets extremely long in the tooth. If you have any remotely artistically inclined people, Drawful is still an excellent reason to get the first pack, but for my money, while it can be hit or miss on a round-to-round basis, Earwax is by far the hardest I've laughed at something in the last decade. It feels like I have a social life again, and I'm just using Skype screensharing. (Just make sure whoever's hosting has a decent upload rate, and I'd recommend at least 4 people for the best experience.)
Ultimately I think it boils down to whether you want to try to draw wolf parades, Cthulhu, and abstract concepts like "burger time", or if you'd rather hear "what most men think goes on inside a uterus" depicted with sound clips of firecrackers, lasers, clowns, pig squeals, sawblades, and ghosts. Either way it's hard to go wrong.
And there's still Drawful 2 and Jackbox 3 to look forward to. God bless you, Jellyvision, your PC port of the new YDKJ may have been♥♥♥♥♥♥but you're still masters of your craft where it counts.

Vermintide takes the L4D formula and improved on it tremendously. It is just as unpredictable and replayable with the added loot mechanism. The loot system is pure RnG and with my luck, I rarely get good rolls - but I try not to get hung up with the loot. I still unlock and find enough weapons to give my plays some variety. It is not a Diablo replacement for me, but an improved L4D. A good communicative team with a strong common understanding is far more important in this game.
The level designs are top notch and the maps are full of detail which create interesting atmosphere. The sound and music complements the action exceptionally well. I've played about 6 maps so far and i've been impressed with all of them. The Skaven AI do behave like the sneaky and cunning vermin they are - creeping up or dropping behind you to steal a stab in your back. They are annoying and extremely satisfying to butcher en masse.
The melee combat is impactful and satisfying. Far more so than L4D's. Also, getting quick ranged headshots and clever item use is more crucial than ever to survive. Many of the special Skavens like the gutter runners, ratling gunners and pack masters are really overpowered against individual heroes. They can easily take out a straggling player. This game can be unforgiving even at normal difficulties and requires good team tactics to succeed. Try playing alone with the (weak)AI BOTs on your side and you'll realize just having 3 more characters fighting on its own will easily get all of you killed. This game is not to be enjoyed as a single player game.
In terms of bugs - there are still some weird stuff like mobs hitting you through walls, clipping animation and fps drops when things get really busy, but otherwise I havent encountered anything gamebreaking. To me, it is a good game for a fair price at this stage. I just hope the developers will continue to be generous with content and reasonable with the pricing for future content. This game and Fat Shark has tremendous potential and I would love to keep playing this game for some time to come.

Best game I've ever played TBH. The perfect mix of storyline, missions, side quests, crafting and best of all a massive and beautiful to behold open world sandbox, populated by not only frequent patrols of enemy militia, but also some very dangerous wildlife indeed. You can basically do what you like and approach the game from whatever angle you prefer, it'll support just about any style of gameplay.
You'll never tire of the possibilities open to your imagination in this game. Do you go all out for liberating the radio masts? Or do you concentrate on recapturing militia controlled settlements for the freedom fighters? Perhaps complete all the missions and challenges such as killing a whopping tiger just with a bow and arrow!
Maybe concentrate on crafting yourself better loot and weapon carriers so you can build up your income quickly, sounds easy enough - shoot deer, boar and various other animals and birds, but the sound of your rifle shots will carry and pretty soon a militia patrol will hunt you down. Or on the other hand you might never get to skin your pelts before a pack of dingo's or a hungry tiger or leapard move in. I loathe the komodo dragons most of all though, they are relentless.
The horrors aren't all on land mind. After you've been chased away down to the river by overwhelming firepower, think twice before jumping in and meeting the mother of all crocodiles! Ditto the sea and it's hungry sharks. Talking of the sea there are some great boats - from jet ski's up to some armed coastal craft, and you'll be able to hit fast and run with these, and even hold back and use the hmg.
But I think the best thing about FC3 is that you can do things you can't do in other games, but can do in real life. An example; I had to take out a guard tower protecting a small port. The settlement was crawling with rasta speaking militia hippies. I planned on taking my knife to as many as possible to try and even up the odds in a shootout later. My mission was to break some people out of a lock-up. I had a sniper rifle as well as an AK47 (recommended as most of the militia carry them), but I didn't want to raise the alarm and couldn't sneak up on him.
But there was a king cobra snake in the long grass about 5 meters from the ladder. So I threw stones to bring the guard down the ladder and searching, then it was a case of leading him to the long grass where the snake was and wallop - one guard silently killed by nature! Perfect, I love it when a plan comes together.
The atmosphere is superb as are the sounds like angry militia saying what they're going to do with you when they catch you! Even more creepy is when you're misjudged the time and the sun's gone down, and you're miles from anywhere in the jungle. Then you hear the wild goats bleating in fear, and slowly but surely the growls of a tiger getting closer and closer, and you chose that time to take out just a light SMG!!
You could while away your entire life with this great game.

TLDR: This game is 10x better than minecraft, 5x better than ARK (I liked ARK a lot). Favorite Sandbox Survival/Game Dev Tool.
This game is hands down the best sandbox survival game I've played. I'll list a couple of the pro's and cons of the game.
Also! this game is very new as of my writing this, in fact my friend currently has the only dedicated exploration server (hosted by
.
PROS:
-Amazing music
-Amazing Art Style
-Crafting Seems endless with lots to do
-Lots of different crafting stations (locksmith table, kiln, spinning wheel, tanning rack, smelter, foundery, energy table, etc.
-Advanced technologies in crafting (you can build cars, ships, generators etc.)
-Building can be extremely detailed and is extremely satisfying when you finish.
-There are multiple Ylands! each with their own "Biome" or environment and wildlife. Ranging from Polar Bears, pumas, leopards, panthers, wolves, wild boars, goats, and bunnys (Don't know the others).
-Multiplayer!
-Item specific "Inventory Upgrades" things like an Herb Bag to store your plants and grass to make rope and potions, a seashell container to condense materials for dyes, a potion belt for potions, a seed box for seeds, etc.
-EVERYTHING can be placed excactly where you want it. If you press 'V' you will enter placement mode. Where you are able to rotate and posistion anything to place down, Including your inventory bags listed above! (you can place your herb bag on a table you made and have it be a portable/placable inventory for you and friends to use!). This made interior design SO MUCH FUN for me compared to any other game. It was easy to build a shelf and put anything I wanted on it, or put silverware on my table, etc.
-Full length Books!? I found a full edtion of robinson crusoe! 317 pages! WHAT
-The list goes on and on But I'm getting tire of writing this review lol.
CONS:
-BUGGY Af at times, things like: your gravestone can sink your ship and you need to break it to unsink your ship. We can thank Early access for these bugs. (although these bugs are annoying I haven't yet run into anything game breaking).
+most bugs can be fixed with a re-log
-MUSIC although its amazing, there is little to no variety, kinda like default minecraft music.
-Ships are pretty buggy right now gradually getting more stable.
-Multiplayer doesn't have dedicated servers, unless you pay for a hosting service like me and my friends have, you can only play with friends if they are playing or visa versa. (you can run your own dedicated servers but it is password locked on the forums)
+This is currently being worked on and is getting progessively more and more stable for me and my friends.
-Building although detailed and rewarding is VERY tedious. If you are wanting to build a log cabin, it'll take you a couple solid hours and some good ol fashioned deforestation to build it. It's not like minecraft in that sense.
-THE LEARNING CURVE is pretty steep. Since crafting is so detailed and in depth there is a lot you need to figure out before becoming efficient at it. It can get annoying not knowing what to do.
Conclusion:
This game is ♥♥♥♥ing amazing. It's by far my favorite survival game and thats only one mode we're talkin. The Pros HEAVILY outway the cons and the game is TEEMING with ORIGINALITY. It is a game that I really want to see grow and develop. I think this game has great potential.
This is a very expansive game. I would definetly recommend playing with your friends though as it can get lonely.

Honestly? As fun as this game gets to be at the end (at least, somewhat), the main ability that causes fun in the game, namely being able to manipulate the water and stuff in it, comes really close to the end, is quite limited, and it doesn't give you a whole lot of time to adjust to it. That's what really hurts it in my eyes. If they gave you more time with that power, more variations on it than just a pillar of water (possibly even puzzles with a 'parting the seas' kind of thing), and a bit more puzzling than shooting, it'd be amazing. As it stands, slightly meh. The ammo, while giving variety, is mostly useless. You only have to use one of the four extra ammo types at the very end, and I found myself using the default (and infinite, and chargeable) ammo type.
Something I would have loved to see is a large area or two where you could get to play with the water manipulation, have it be more central to a puzzle than 'Move box, throw bomb, etc', and just more variation on the power.
It's rather short, kinda worth it at bottom sale price, but it's not as stellar as it could have been. It's just a side effect of dated tech, really.
In general:
Environment: Captures the feel of a dying ship quite well.
Story: Leaves A LOT unanswered and feels kinda flat at the end.
Gunplay: Works well enough from what I played, variation mostly underused.
Movement: Works very well, though a bit tedious to move through water that's just about at swimming depth at times. Swimming is nice and fluid.
Ability: Fun, but not enough time to get used to it, nor enough done with it.
Graphics: Good enough, but I'm not the type to insta-praise graphics that try to be ultra-realistic for the time.
Water Physics: Best. Just.. You can tell that's were a lot of effort went when developing the game.
Overall? Par for the time, minus a good bit for the lack of puzzle variety and power utilization, plus a bit for the water physics.
5(ish)/10. If you're looking for a decent game for about a dollar (during the current sale), feel free to get it. Just don't get your hopes up too high.
Review system: Meh/Bleh. Needs a more.. Precise thing than just Yes/No for reccomending it. But then again, I'm just asking too much from Steam there.

Is it worth buying? Maybe.

If they manage to do all that, the game would be worth at least 29,99.
Final Score 7/10.

So, i was not sure about this game, at first. I did not want to shell out the considerable price for a game i would not use. Granted i have not played much, but thats not for a lack of wanting to. Normally i get bored easily with RTS type games. They just get too samey for me, for various reasons.
But, as is obvious, i took the plunge. I had read and seen enough to warrant a gamble.
I did not regret my choice...
This is not what i would call an RTS (even though it is, sort of). There is a complexity to it that makes it interesting. I cannot just pick this game up and win instantly, by spamming units and just overwhelming the opponent. I have to work with what i have got. Also, i need to really know about the unit/s i am commanding. I need to know what they have in regards to all manner of things ranging from weapons to sensors.
I need to think before i attack. Tactics. Real tactics. Guns blazing often gets you killed.
And then there are things such as creating missions in a scenario. Instead of just directing my units by clicking on a spot on the map and hoping i find something i can set search patterns, or direct units to patrol. and the AI will actually do it without completely messing up by expecting me to babysit them all the time.
Another refreshing thing is the combat itself. The best thing i can compare it to is a tabletop wargame. It essentially rolls a virtual dice, in the background, for hits and misses, with modifiers that influence the outcome, of course. To me that represents something that some RTS's are missing, and thats individual skill. A bit like the UFO games with the people in your unit having their own skill sets.
For me, though, the icing on the cake is the scenario editor. I can create so much. I have recreated the Falklands War. I created WW3 I even created small scenarios such as pirate hunting. This is all done because there are so many tools at your disposal.
Now, i know a lot of RTS's have mission editors. But not to this extent. At least none that i have played.
I love naval combat. So this filled a niche that was missing in my game library. Dont get me wrong, the air combat is just as good. But i have a history of family members who were Royal Navy. So there is a bit of bias. I always loved hearing about tactics and ship types and so on...
Which brings me to another point, that may seem odd to some people but others may be able to relate to: I am unable to serve in any of the armed forces. But if i could i would. This provides me a small amount of satisfaction in that i can at least play act, in a way, i can feel like i am commanding a ship in battle or a wing of Air Force jets. Something no RTS has ever given me.
Anyway, i could go on and on about this game.
It is a great milsim. Dont let the price put you off, its dear for a good reason. You are not buying a game that you will forget next week when the next AAA title comes out. Its something that will make you come back for more. Understamd, though, this game has a steep learning curve, and i urge you to read the manual that is available in the Forums section of the CMANO community. It helped me a lot. And also Youtube is your friend.

This game is fun! Really fun! Right off the bat, after downloading the game, CMANO has monopolized most of my game time.
I even have nominated this for a new category in the 2016 Steam Awards: The Under the Radar Award.. haha.. get it?
This game though is probably not for everyone.
It's for people who love simulations and RTS games. Those who are into action games, platformers, and shoot-em-ups would probably want to avoid this. If you enjoyed Warcraft, Starcraft, the Total War games, Civilization,  Warhammer, the Wargame series (EE, ALB and Red Dragon), then this game would be worth considering.
AND, if you are an old geezer like me and have sneakily played Harpoon on the office PC during the late 80s/early 90s then this one is a no brainer.
Watch Baloogan's YouTube videos on this game. I have spent hours watching his games and have learned a lot from it. His videos are what gave me the final push to get this game.
For some reason, Steam has a problem tracking my game time. My guess is that the initial loading screen is what it tracks (that screen stays on after loading the game screen which I turn off the first few times) and not the game screen itself.
The learning curve is a bit high but not too high that it becomes frustrating. For me, the difference between frustrating and challenging is that frustrating is when you just want to get it over with in order to move on and challenging is doing it again and again until you are satisfied while enjoying it each time.
This game is challenging.
Graphics are basically limited to the unit symbols and the terrain map.. basically its your imagination (best to dl the image mods to have a mental picture of the units) that drives what you're seeing on screen. Reminds me of old Infocom ads in the 80s, how the brain is the best graphical processor around.
There are a lot of mission scenarios. The page says 40 but after downloading the community pack, I have another 177 (!!!) scenarios that cover engagements all around the world! And there is an editor where you can even make up your own scenario.
To give you an idea of the missions, the first tutorial mission was to bomb a couple of land targets that are protected by SAM installations. I launched a couple of F14s to patrol the area, set up Prowlers and Hawkeyes to monitor the area and jam enemy radar, then set up my strike force.
I still haven't got a major victory (only a minor one; ran out of ordinance and had one bldg still standing). But I'll get back to this mission later. Going back to this mission and repeating it didn't feel like a chore to me.
In the second tutorial, I had to micromanage one submarine through 4 stages sub v sub, sub v boat, sub v boat with a helicopter patrolling the area seeking you out, and finally sub v land target.
Units are intelligent. Just send out the mission order, define the conditions and send them off. You can have them do the mission automatically or manually control and guide them.
Much has been talked about the price. I got it on sale but still it was a bit high for me that I really had to think five times whether I should or should not. I'm glad I did.
I think about it this way, I have spent much more on games I haven't played yet and some that I never will play again.
Just to set expectations:
1. The first thing you'll notice is that the game rests above Windows UI (similar to how Excel or Word launches). This took me by surprise since I initially thought that it was a subpar game because of it.  But don't let it fool you, the game is top notch regardless. Plus using dual monitors is easy because of this.
2. The graphics. Much has been talked about it but to quote Cypher from the movie The Matrix, "But there's way too much information to decode the Matrix. You get used to it. I...I don't even see the code. All I see is blonde, brunette, red-head"
3. Sound. There is none to talk about. It's really basic that I just play it without my headphones on.
4. The pacing closely resembles how the pacing would be in real life. Missiles takes minutes to hit targets. Your planes need time to be loaded up, taxi to the runway, and launch.
5. Planning and strategy. When a scenario loads up, a pop up with mission details come up. It's best to read it and familiarize with the scenario. The overall strategy is laid out with some helpful tips but you must still have to plan out how to execute it
6. The Database. Much has been written about its extensive database and boy, it really is. It's like a big technical manual of every weapon, vehicle, and even installations around; complete with its history, and the different versions and iterations around.
7. No multiplayer. I really can't comment on this because I'm happy already with the way its set up but some would want to try this out in MP but sadly it isn't an option.
8. UI comes out clunky and there's no immediate accessible keyboard control guide. After awhile though like most games you'll get the hang of it. But if I have to complain, it's the UI really.
Command: Modern Air / Naval Operations is 100% really about the gameplay.
Anyway, not sure if this review makes much sense but I wholeheartedly recommend this for people who love the genre and are deciding whether to get it or not.

It's really, really good. It's got enough stats to make the nerd in you smile contentedly and enough complexity for real Simmers to enjoy meddling until their hearts content - yet it remains totally accessible to plebs like me, who really would love to know how to play a game like this properly, but haven't the patience to learn it.
Just a few re-runs of the tutorials, then dipping my toe in the Scenarios and I'm already comfortable enough to fly a sortie or two, travel undetected through enemy waters in a Sub or activate a Battle Fleet for full on Naval warfare. I've even been launching Tankers for refuelling and electronic surveillance planes for better Radar. That kind of logistical detail is the stuff I usually get lost with.
The best thing about the game is once you know the interface and the main enablers to get your icons rolling into the sky or out into the sea, the AI does allow for micro managers to step in or out of the action. I'm not a great micro manager so I just oversee them (to make sure the odd unit doesn't go off on it's own doing something weird, which has happened occasionally - turns out that's my dodgy Doctrine settings!). But the beauty is, you can take control at any time if it's a part of the battle you want to get 'on the ground' with.
I love this. The Database alone is worth the money if you like reading technical stats (which I do) but the gameplay, despite the standard UI's attempt to prove otherwise, is fully engaging and  absorbing. I hate losing planes or ships to enemy fire and when they go down, you feel it. There's a level and depth of realism you wouldn't expect from symbols on a chart.
10/10 for me - specialist game for sure, but if you do like this kind of sim to begin with, then you'll want for nothing from this package.

REVIEW
The gameplay isn't bad but I wouldn't say extraordinarily good because it's not. The game appeals to military enthusiats and hobbyist. It's not particularly difficult to understand the game but then again I'm pretty familiar with most military units and weapons.
