As is, right now, avoid this product. It's Jagex having taken the original concept and having altered the format significantly while not having bothered adding in any content of substance. The hit detection is way off across all the modes, the building method is sloppy and slow at best. Want to run your own server? Too bad, Jagex is having none of it, aka, when they decide to axe the servers, the entire game will die as well. They added in a sloppy voice chat function as well with no way of seeing who's cursing you out or even if your mic is working.

Content wise, it's not worth the $10. Maybe after a few patches and content influxes, sure, as is, no way. It's unpolished to a high degree and it was rushed out the door after they purchased the original from the Dev, who no longer works on this game at all. They've tried to avoid criticisms by slathering on plenty of "We will eventually X" and "In the future, y!" but even so, it's not worth the price point. I picked it up for $5 during the Christmas Sale and even that felt like overpaying after having spent a good 5 hours in it. There are a handful of modes, zombie infection, TDM, base blowing up, but they all feel lacking and unpolished.
You wont be spending more than 30 minutes in their toted "persistence" before a map change because there's simply no reason to anything but destroy, and with the addition of the Miner, you can flatten most places easily. Building is in itself another matter entirely, what with the removed color palette for block selection and the simple second delay before placing one block after another, forcing you to use the prebuilt structures which are a handful and albeit useful, rather awful at most things. Gone are the days of spending several hours on a single huge map, instead they've ramped up the pace to a point where building anything but with the prefabs is utterly stupid.
It's a shame what they've done to this, overall, but hope does lie in the future, if you can call it hope instead of a marketing technique, which is what it is, with the game's current state. They may say it's a "finished" product, but when their own server's and gameplay can't stand up under any real scrutiny, it's a fabrication or downright lie.
tl;dr: Don't buy this. No LAN. No party system. No good game beneath the voxel-based explosions and bland texture work.

NOTE: DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. REPEAT, DO. NOT. BUY .THIS. GAME.
All caps aside, allow me to explain myself. See, Ace of Spades was once a brilliant game. It was extremely simple, yet very innovative, the gunplay actually felt satisfying and there was a genuine sense of tension when you're tunnelling to the enemy flag, knowing that at any time, they could hear your digging, discover your tunnel and shoot you in the back fo the head before you can even react. Defending was no different. Was that digging you hear simply a teammate fortifying the flag, or an opponenet looking to grab it from beneath? Basically, it was a simple, yet very deep, strategic and psychological sandbox shooter featuring huge maps that can be torn apart or built on at will. Though in that state, I'd have gladly forked over $15-20 for it, it was gloriously free to play.
Then, things took a turn for the worst. See, Jagex, a UK based developer best known for Runescape, purchased Ace of Spades. Gone were the simple rifle/SMG/shotgun selection, replaced by a system of classes. Gone was the focus on trench warfare and steady and gradual construction of both defensive fortifications tunnels to bypass said defences and gone was the highly satisfying gunplay. The introduction of jet packs and The Tunnling Cannon (a gun that removes a long line of blocks, effectively carving out a tunnel in a matter of seconds and giving the oppposing team no time to react) turns the overall game into one of twitch reflexes rather than a more drawn-out game of trying to out smart your opponents. Don't get me wrong, faster, reflex-based shooters aren't a bad thing by any means. However, there are many games that are designed from the start to be such a shooter, and as such do a far better job of things than Jagex's Ace of Spades (Tribes Ascend comes to mind).
However, all is not lost. The old Ace of Spades, from before Jagex got their claws into it, still lives. To play it, simply download the client from here.
Then head over here for a server list
Now you can start playing some good Ace of Spades, the way it was meant to be played. Anyone who has even a passing interest in shooters needs to try it, at least once.

I saw this game a while ago before release, becoming mildly enthused by the idea of a 4-player co-op game that looked this good. But I wasn't sold on it, wasn't sure the gameplay was actually good as Skyrim really put a damper on my enthusaism for a first-person hack and slash game.
Now over a hundred hours later, with many laughs with three groups of friends who I regularly play with at work lunches, weekends and during evenings, it's clearly taking the cake as my favorite co-op game.
The voice acting and characters are interesting and have a story to them that makes me curious about the Warhammer setting I had not cared for at all before. The combat mechanics are easy to understand but hard to master, and you'll notice yourself improve as you play, blocking blows and looking out for your teammates becoming easier over time. The theme of the world is wonderfully coherent in its design and gritty, a perfect counterbalance to the often cheerful banter between the player characters.
I hope Fatshark can keep this game profitable for a long time, so we can enjoy more of this in the future.
Now, to mention a few negatives I'd have to say they've made a poor system for newcomers as of this moment (dec 2015). The community travels upward to higher difficulty settings as they continue to play, so unless there's an influx of new players like during a sale, they will most likely find themselves struggling to find a group that can tolerate them on a difficulty they are comfortable with.
It's something Fatshark should be wary of and something a new player should expect to some degree. It's fixable by simply shifting reward incentives somewhat, so hopefully they'll address it in a patch in the near future.
In addition, if you are playing the game solely for the gear, get ready to feel underwhelmed at the end of games. The game rewards you fairly well and there are fallback systems that lets you redeem a bad reward (especially after the Blessings of Sigmar DLC), but its by no means overly generous or controllable. It's a game of dice (literally), and if you are the kind who want nothing more than to perfect your gear then it will take time. However, for me personally I'm glad that there are goals around 130 hours in, and although I don't have the optimal setup just yet I know I can at least play for my own amusement and maybe get the fated Veteran tier handgun.
So, all in all, this game has really been worth my money. See you in Übersreik.

I tried, I really tried to get into this game. But here is my perspective:
The game is quite nice but I do not reccomend this to brand new players. It really is not new player friendly, and the dungeons are very difficuly for new players. You need patience to play this game.
It is turn based, and the combat system is unique but what made me (as a new player) leave this behind were:
Dungeons that are puzzle based, really give you zero hints on how to beat it. You are forced to use google on this and you cannot leave a battle unless you quit the game. Other tactical based mmos allow an "escape" feature if the battle is too tough or you need to leave, this however does not.  This right here is a red flag for me.
Another feature that didn't really keep my interest is the quest system. For new players, if you log off, you have to manually try to find your quest destination as most do not give you a compass (quest tracking tracing feature).
So in summary:
Pros
____
Unique battle system
Tons of classes
Small Patch and Download
Cons
____
Not new player friendly.
Map layout can be confusing for new players.
Google how to beat puzzle dungeons (new players).
No hints on puzzles from in-game.
Can't leave in the middle of a battle without logging out. (no escape or flee chance option).
Overall: Do tons of research and look up guides if you are new to Wakfu. If you are a veteran, then jump right in.

While this is certainly a good game, as a fan of the original, it seems to be lacking.. something.
No, it isn't the music- that much is great.
Is it the characters? It might be.
Sure, I miss using Jacket, but that's not it either.
Is it the gameplay? Well... yes, and no.
The original had a very unique level design. While listening to the raw and brutal beats of the first game, you couldn't help but lose yourself in the ferocity and play to the sheer power of the music. It was unique in the sense that it gave off a rhythm of sorts. God help the one who used strategy in the first title. I can only commend Dennis and Jonatan for creating such an amazing, instinct-based shooter.
With this title, that instinct is still there- however, slightly subdued. It offers a much more streamlined approach to completing levels- whereas in the first title, it was up to the player to decide on how to complete the level. There isn't much versatility anymore. What I mean is simply put, there is usually one good path to completing each level in this game. You can try to take a harder route, but it will most likely end in failure. There is little to be gained from rushing in without a strategy. Some folks may like that. Fans of playing by ear and switching styles on the fly may not.
As for me, I'm a bit on the fence. As I mentioned before, I love the first game. I do love this game, but in a different sense. It seems to me that whatever they tried to accomplish in the first game, they succeeded in this game. Everything is much more polished than the first. You can feel it, you can see it, and you can certainly hear it. The music choice in this game is much more calculated than the first.
Sure, the beginning may stump players, but trust me- everything is explained. Any question you have during the beginning will eventually get answered. They do a great way of sending off the series with a BOOM.
But is it worth $15?
The short answer is: Hell. Yes.
The music is great, the graphics are great- just know this before you buy: This game is relentless, this game is brutal, this game will have you cursing out loud at your computer while you're playing at work. This game is Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

I want to like Wakfu I really do, but it has to many glaring flaws for me to recomend it.
Lets start with the pros.
+ great art
+ Interesting classes
+ fun combat system
+ Interesting lore (including the anime)
Now... to the cons
- no quests: Wakfu lacks quests and expects you to just be happy raiding dungeons on your own without anyone telling you to. This is doesnt work as you will soon find yourself tried of doing nothing but running into the same dungeons over and over. Which might have been ok if...
- dungeons suck: sad but true. The dungeons are ok on your first play through, but without a party there is no real strategy to beating them, either your strong enough or you're not. And even when your playing with friends to make the experience more engaging, once you beat a dungeon your basicaly done. Sure you might grind it for drops but their fun has long since gone. The dungeons never change so once you have beat it once, unless you are AFK, you will always beat it from that point out. This could have worked if there were a ton of dungeons, but there are maybe 5 per area and you wll stay in each area for about 10 or so levels which can take mutliple dungeon runs to acomplish. And yet even this might have been ok, if getting epic loot was fun, but...
-the loot sucks: the loot variety is small, like really small, and without random stats attached to any of it there is no reason to get it. You will raid a dungeon once, get the loot then never return, or better yet just buy it off somone for cheap because since everyone has the exact same loot its all worthless! Which could be ok if leveling your character was fun, but...
-progression sucks: Its basic gaming design to make sure the player isnt doing the same thing at level 100 as they were at level 1. That will not happen here, sure you will find leveling up to about 25 or so, engaging, but from then on out your character will not change at all. You will be using the same combos over and over and over again with no real motivation to change it up, the only thing that will change is how much damage they do. But luckily there is somethign other than fighting, there is crafting so that....
- crafting also sucks: The game doesnt enforce you to have one job, you can do any, because of this your job is worthless. Everyone just makes anything they need themselves and ebcause of this everything on the market is either dirt cheep or super expensive. The idea of running a armor making store sounds fun, untill you realize no one will ever buy from you when they can just make it themselves and earn exp while doing it. This has an easy fix (force people to have only a single job) Which the games text says is how the system works! But it doesn't and they havent fixed it, so it fails.
So in short Wakfu is a game where your character doesnt grow past level 25, in which you grind repetative dungeons for borring loot. To the tune of no story and no meaningfull jobs or minigame to complete. Sounds fun no?

A staunch but concise defence of DiRT 4:

I like this game. I also really liked DiRT Rally. Expecting the same from both games however, is asking far too much of both the player and the developer.
This game is absolutely, in no way bad.

See, DiRT Rally was like Dark Souls. An incredibly finely crafted experience that would see you throw yourself at a stage over and over and over and over until you finally got it right.

DiRT 4 is not this. DiRT 4 is far more player friendly but for good reason, you never see the same stage twice (without asking for it). DiRT 4 with DiRT Rally’s level of challenge would be borderline unplayable to a large amount of people. I can honestly say, if I want to be punched in the face, repeatedly, by a game. I will play DiRT Rally.

I don’t find much wrong with this game’s handling, it’s very liberal with its speed but that’s not a bad thing. With the way gravel feels in this game compared to DiRT Rally, it would likely be far too slow in terms of the campaign if you had to grind out each stage as you learned it rather than blasting through them.

Oh, and try the FWD Pug. It’s incredible.

Hydrophobia, a cross between adventure and third person shooter. The game starts on a giant ship which houses tonnes of people. You play as a mechanical engineer who is trying to foil the terorist attack on the vessel.
The game is relatively cheap at $5 (I got it for about $1 at sale :D). The main selling point of the game is the water mechanics. You can control the flow of water to open paths and even defeat enemies. The water graphics are really good (it looks and moves fluidly).
Now for the bad points. Although the water graphics are good, other models (ie. characters, environment) seem somewhat bland. The voice acting isn't that great either, nor is the story unfortunately. The biggest problem I had with the game were lag spikes. Alot of lag spikes. Although it's a single player only game, it lagged and even freezes (for a few minutes at a time) on me in several areas even after lowering all the graphical settings to bottom. I play games like retribution and crysis  fine with minimum lag, but this game struggles to run for some reason. The third person shooting is also clunky as the movement controls aren't great.
Overall, the game does try to be unique with the water mechanics, but it doesn't make up the the under par graphics, story, controls and bugs. I haven't finished it (due to the bugs), but after spending 2 hours in it I'm not really compelled to play it. Save your money people.

When I bought Hydrophobia, I was expecting dynamic gameplay revolving around an awesome ability allowing the manipulation of water. Upon playing the game, I realized this is not much more than a repetitive tech demo for water physics. The gameplay is alright, but I found it to be quite boring. When I finally attained the ability to manipulate water, I found it to be lacking in functionality, and discovered that it is only useable on the final boss and in a few rooms before it.
I also realized, that in order to attain 100% completion of the game, you need to be able to accomplish a difficult and unclear task on the first attempt. After failing the task once, it can not be attempted again. The only way to get 100% at that point, is to manually delete the save and to restart from the very beginning. This can be tedious to do as the task is found at the end of Act 1 or the beginning of Act 2, so you have to play for quite a while to get back, and you also have to reattain every medal that you might have had at that point, which in my case was all but two or three.
The game includes a feedback option that allows you to choose aspects of the game that you did or did not like. Upon researching the company that made the game, I found out that they went bankrupt and that the feedback is now meaningless.
Overall I'd say that this game is extremely disappointingly repetitive and lacking in gameplay, but I suppose that it is worth its low price.

This is a game about water. Oh, all right; the game is actually about shooting people in first person view on a sinking ship, but that's really besides the point. Hydrophobia utilizes a proprietary engine (the "HydroEngine") that realistically renders the ebb and flow of liquids, and this feature is the game's main attraction. Watching the waves crash around is fascinating; it really is quite impressive technology.
The rest of the game is quite ordinary, however. The PC version is significantly improved over the original released on the XBox,  and features entirely new levels and a story that actually closes satisfactorily. But it is nothing we haven't seen a hundred times before and - once the thrill of watching the water move drains away - there's little reason to come back to the game.

Command is one of the best games that I've played in the last several years, and has given me hundreds of hours of enjoyment (note: this is not reflected in my Steam time, as I purchased it originally from Matrix). It provides a much more faithful model of modern air and naval strategy than any other game out there, vastly better than the Wargame series, and aligning with many other real sources. I don't think that there's any better simulation with both the depth and width of this.
There are a few issues. The UI is very hard to get used to (and the learning curve is rather steep) - while the interface looks like Google Earth, it doesn't work anything like it, and takes some time. The keyboard shortcuts are somewhat annoying to find, and are really, really nessecary to play well. It also requires something of a powerful CPU, as I'm running on a upper-mid-level notebook i7 and can't go much past 30x time acceleration.
The game certiantly is still under development. A number of features remain to be added, such as a time-on-target strike planner (what other game even needs one?) and "surge" air operations are forthcoming. However, the developers are very active and responsive, and the game constantly improves further. This is augmented by an extensive community of scenario creators that have done some fantastic work (I'm especially a fan of the Caribbean Crisis scenarios, where Venezuela invades the ABC islands).
All in all, I would highly reccomend this game. I think that the $80 I originally paid for it was entirely worth it, and the $60 price is more than justified. While I wish that they would reduce the price further, I think that if you have even a passing interest in modern military you should spend the money.

When you place objects (chests, furniture, walls, etc.), you get a 2 minute timer during which you can move/remove them. While this is certainly a good game, as a fan of the original, it seems to be lacking.. something.
No, it isn't the music- that much is great.
Is it the characters? It might be.
Sure, I miss using Jacket, but that's not it either.
Is it the gameplay? Well... yes, and no.
The original had a very unique level design. While listening to the raw and brutal beats of the first game, you couldn't help but lose yourself in the ferocity and play to the sheer power of the music. It was unique in the sense that it gave off a rhythm of sorts. God help the one who used strategy in the first title. I can only commend Dennis and Jonatan for creating such an amazing, instinct-based shooter.
With this title, that instinct is still there- however, slightly subdued. It offers a much more streamlined approach to completing levels- whereas in the first title, it was up to the player to decide on how to complete the level. There isn't much versatility anymore. What I mean is simply put, there is usually one good path to completing each level in this game. You can try to take a harder route, but it will most likely end in failure. There is little to be gained from rushing in without a strategy. Some folks may like that. Fans of playing by ear and switching styles on the fly may not.
As for me, I'm a bit on the fence. As I mentioned before, I love the first game. I do love this game, but in a different sense. It seems to me that whatever they tried to accomplish in the first game, they succeeded in this game. Everything is much more polished than the first. You can feel it, you can see it, and you can certainly hear it. The music choice in this game is much more calculated than the first.
Sure, the beginning may stump players, but trust me- everything is explained. Any question you have during the beginning will eventually get answered. They do a great way of sending off the series with a BOOM.
But is it worth $15?
The short answer is: Hell. Yes.
The music is great, the graphics are great- just know this before you buy: This game is relentless, this game is brutal, this game will have you cursing out loud at your computer while you're playing at work. This game is Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number.

This is not Dirt Rally 2 and by some of what Codies said before release, you'd not be a fool for thinking this might include much of what made Rally the first real threat to RBR's crown. Sadly for those looking, that pure Rally feel has been largely removed for Dirt 4.
Those looking for a continuation of Dirt 3's full arcade feel and gnarly dudebro vibe will leave pretty dissapointed too.
That said, this is clearly not a bad game, it's actually still a pretty great game and easily the best of the rest, so to speak
Those that found Dirt Rally too hard but still want a Rally focus, more realistic feel with a fairer challenge aimed at the average-decent gamer will find a lot to like here. The handling is a good mix of sim/arcade, you can't just throw the car around with abandon and you have to pay attention but it won't test your patience like Dirt Rally did either.
I can't speak for controller users but it feels pretty great with a wheel, not quite up to Dirt Rally's feedback detail but again, ahead of the rest in the rally genre.
The team mangement aspect is also a nice touch, could be a bit more fleshed out but the systems in place add another little layer of progression and immersion.
The procedural generation for stage layouts feels pretty deep for it's first appearance, repetition is a little noticable but nowhere near as bad as it could have been (No Man's Sky *coughs*). Stages tend to feel pretty unique and I really hope Codies continues with this system going into the future as the posibilities could be endless if they kept tinkering with it.
The sounds are awesome too, the cars growl, pop and spultter like proper rally beasts. Not a fan of the soundtrack (too commericial) but that's a personal taste issue and most of us will turn it off in racers anyway.
The only real beef I have, is with the Rally locations. 5 feels like a slight tease, 7 would've been a better number. An Icy asphalt rally like Monte Carlo, a gravel/tarmac mix like Japan or a hard gravel rally like Greece would've done nicely here. DLC maybe?
That gripe aside, I'm still having a lot of fun playing this and it definitely deserves better than a mixed rating so it gets a thumbs up from me, a solid 8.5 out of 10.

Best rally game i've ever played. This is coming from someone that has played pretty much every rally focused codemasters game as well as the famous richard burns rally. Contrary to what most negative reviews have said here the physics as a whole is actually objectively better in Dirt 4 compared to Dirt rally.
Weight is massively improved and the aerodynamics noticeably better, you no longer drive on the moon which is great. The overall grip level may be just slightly too high but thats open for debate but the general consensus seems to be that the rear end has too much grip on gravel, especially on older rwd cars making it very hard to powerslide through corners which is a shame. However the game feels very realistic and the claims that its an arcade game is just silly.
Graphics 8/10
Inconsistent is the best way to describe the graphics in Dirt 4. Trees, grass and flora looks pretty mediocre even on ultra and in the distance looks pretty terrible. On the other hand the lighting is absolutely phenomenal and captures reality better than I have ever seen in a game before. Driving in the sunrise in Spain is mind blowing. The weather looks fantastic especially the rain.
Sound 10/10
Gameplay 9/10
I have already touched on the physics aspect of the game but looking at what Dirt 4 offers in terms of gameplay I have to say its everything I want in a rally game. The stage generator is not perfect but overall its great. After playing for several hours at the same location you will start to recognize corners and sections but thats pretty much unavoidable in a video game. It is still much harder to memorize stages and you never know what combination of corners that is in front of you so I definitely prefer it even though it could see some improvements. The AI is too slow on "tough" (the hardest before you unlock fearless) in general, too slow AI seems to be the standard today for some reason, I really hope the "fearless" is going to provide a big challange.
Overall 9/10
Some things that prevents this game from becoming unbeatable ;
- Too slow AI
- Stage generator could be more interesting and challenging, lack of really narrow sections, unpredictability and variety
- No Finland ;(
- Too much much grip in the rear, especially in the older cars
- Not enough locations. So many cars but only 5 Locations to race them on, please add more locations in dlcs! I would love to see more rally countries, more rallycross and landrush countries as well because its lacking right now.
Do I recommend this game? YES. The only reason you would not get this game is if you can't accept anything that isn't
Dirt rally or just hate rally games in general, otherwise get this fantastic game. The negative reviews here are completely unjustified as many has already pointed out.

First things first " Dirt 4 is NOT Dirt Rally !!!! " This aims to be unbiased, impartial review.
Dirt 4 Review from someone with 526 hours in Dirt Rally, 16 hours in Dirt 4 and limited rallying experience. I was cautious when i saw the promo`s and read the media blurb and thought .. Do i , or Dont i , buy it ?? I brought it and 16 hours later this is the review below...
Dirt 4 can be played in 2 modes , ARCADE, with every assist and helper on or SIMULATION, which is supposed to a full on sim experience, In a way it is and it isnt owing to the Physics.
: Codemasters have improved upon Dirt Rally and made worse at the same time in Dirt 4. They seem to be like a cross between Dirt Rally v0.5-1.0 physics and Dirt 2-3 physics. Cars have more weight in that dept and are more squirly/twitchy under braking and over crests, jumps, etc. So you need to manage weight transfer and setup/position the car for the turn/road ahead as IRL rallying. Theirs way too much grip on the rear of the cars, even on AWD/4WD/RWD cars, compared to Dirt Rally.  CM are supposed to be looking into rectifying this in a future update.
ARCADE should have current Dirt 4 physics and SIMULATION should have Dirt Rally V1.5-2.0 Physics. You get the normal rear car view (ARCADE MODE), incar and bumper cam views as per Dirt Rally. Default incar seating will need to be adjusted to your liking if you use drivers incar pov (I do) using the 4,1,5,2,6,3  keyboard/keypad buttons .
: it`s no where near as good as Dirt Rally was in the FFB Dept, but even that had problems at release. Hopefully CM fix this problem. As for the cars , theirs not a lot of car talking through the FFB , compared to Dirt Rally.
: This is a major graphical improvement over Dirt Rally, as theyre more severe and look so much nicer and clearer.
: This is a major improvment in the sounds of the cars and in general. Theyre so crisp and you can hear every single creak from the engine , brakes , suspension , etc.
: Major improvement and downgrade at the same time in the gfx dept. Trees, Grass, Logs are not as nice. Cars and service area look nice and clear. You get to choose your setup from ULTRA LOW to ULTRA which alters all gfx settings to make game look much nicer.
: A major improvement over Dirt Rally, more clearer, cleaner and everything is so much easier to find.
: So much improvment since Dirt Rally. Where you start your career and go up through the rankings from 1-100 to get better sponsers , cars, mechanics , etc. Online rally mode, where you race against other racers on randomly generated stages, Like ghost mode without the ghost cars as your fellow racers.  You still get the dailys, weeklys, Monthlys, Specials , etc . Just the leagues have yet to be implemented as of writing this review, But they are coming in the future.
: Gymkhana has been added from Dirt 3 to Dirt 4 and has been renamed to " Dirt Fish, Rally School". You get set driving tasks and how to learn to drive a rally car and knock over some cones, balls, etc.
: The jewel in Dirt 4`s crown , a infinate amount of stages that you can generate and race on and share with friends, according to CM. After a while you get to think , infinate stages... erm.. why are so many sections (Tiles) keep repeating, throughout different stages ?? Re: Spain .. Left 2 , Right 2 , Left 3 , Right 3 to name some.
: You get more RX stages, 5+,  than with the 2, from Dirt Rally. RX in Dirt 4, is the same as Dirt Rally, so if you liked this in Dirt Rally, You will love this in Dirt 4. You get some nice old and new cars in RX. Some come from the Group B era.
: This is the same as RX but in a stadium with Trucks , pickups , buggys , off road cars, etc.
:

1. The audio and visual are top notch.  It sounds amazing and looks very detailed.
2. Quite a few new tracks and cars (new tracks from dirt 3 and some new from dirt rally)
3.  You can create your own stages.  Based on length and difficulty.
4. The co driver calls are great and sound very fluid
Cons
1. Even on hardest setting/mode the AI seems to easy..
2. Wish there was a chat box in lobby  on online racing with others
3.  Race spotters could talk more about time behind you. Only talk about time  ahead of you when you cross the starting line.
Sim mode is getting a lot of criticism from from everyone.
Pros
1. The breaking and suspension are great
2. So many options in set ups!
3. Able to buy upgrades for your car
Cons.
1. I do feel that the grip is way to much(like everyone is saying)  1/4 or 1/2 way thru an e brake hairpin slide. The grip kicks in.  I cant seem to fully slide through corners.
2. Set ups in dirt rally made or broke you.  You can do default set up and finish stages no problem.
3. Pay for repairs during a stage.  No money? Cant fix your car
4. Brand new car.  Co driver says it's miss firing at start.  Or she mentions the transmission having a problem. You can hear the transmission malfunctioning. Go to service area. No issues found.
Overall game
Pros
1. You get to name your own team and chose the color/patterns on your rides!
2.  So many online daily, weekly or monthly races to chose from.
3. Dirt rally school and the challenges are quite a bit of fun and everyone can learn something.
4. They added a review mirror in rally cross for outside of car view.  It's great!!
Cons
1. When you create a set up you have to go back to it to rename it.  Extra step
2.  I am getting quite a few crash reports daily.  Either during a race or going from practice to service area it crashes.  Im %100 positive my PC is well above the min specs.  High and ultra mode is no problem.
3. Faculties seems great but having a staff seems almost pointless?  It would be nice to extend contracts like in dirt rally.
4. Already hard to find online racing lobby's.
Other than the non stop crashing, the weak AI on hardest settings and the too much grip in sim mode the game is really nice.  I'm hoping a few updates fix some things.  Nobody these days are fully happy with games that are released.  This is a much better game than dirt 3 that's for sure.  I just wish the Sim mode was more challenging like dirt rally was.

DiRT 4 isn’t perfect, but it is a whole lot of fun.  As of today on Steam it’s rated as “mixed” by the player reviews, and that seems way too harsh to me, it’s a great game and it should be higher than that IMHO.  I own all of the DiRT games, so to give you a scale how I value them I rate them like this:
DiRT Rally > DiRT 2 > DiRT1 > DiRT 3.
Now, where does DiRT 4 place on that scale?  It’s tough, but it falls on either side of DiRT Rally, so top two DiRT games ever for me, but I’m not sure yet WHICH side it falls on.
PROS:
- Presentation (UI and menus)
- Car handling & physics
- Career mode is well done
- Music, some really catchy tunes
- Car customizing, best of any DiRT series?
- Replays (thank you for sky view)
- Accessibility (both gamer and simulation mode)
- Stage generator means lots of replayability
- Weather effects are great
CONS:
- Stage detailing could use more diversity (early impressions though, might just need more time with it?)
- No hill climbs!!!!!!!
- Overall graphical quality seems less than I expected
- Rallycross and Landrush (if you like them then cool, both are worthless to me!)
It’s fun and well done, and I’m glad I bought it.  Not sure yet if it can replace DiRT Rally for me though, I’ll probably end up playing both from time to time.

This game may seem fun, and it is, but it's completely ruined by its incompetent report system and balance issues.
Ever hear the phrase, "A few bad apples spoil the bunch?" Well, this is, "A few good apples don't save the bunch at all."
A few issues with this game:
1. People will ruin your fun time to enhance theirs.
I haven't played one game without it being full of idiots. They shoot your mines and run them over, and if you're in an AA gun they want, they'll throw a grenade and teamkill you in order to steal it. They have friendly fire off, but for some reason, friendly explosives still kill you.
2. The tanks
The vehicles perform like a dream, only that most vehicles you'll see are tanks and planes.
There should be a limit on tanks, say, 3 for small maps and 5 for large ones. But no, there can be a game with all tanks and nothing else. Tankers will surround you spawn until the few infantry players that crop up from time to time come in to capture it, and if you try to leave the building the tanks will destroy you. Spawns occasionally have anti-tank weapons, but you might as well be using a fly swat to stop a bank robbery. Tanks should be weak to anti-tank weapons only, and all anti tank weapons should be instant kills to all vehicles.
3. The reporting system
This ties into #1. There is no reporting system that I know of for players that don't teamkill you, so the tankers that spawncamp will get off scott-free, and those who blow up your mines also escape justice. There should be a symbol beside everyone on the scoreboard that you can report or salute. Salute being for wanting to play with them more often and report being for reporting them to the devs, if they even still care about this game.

Let's start saying I like this game. It's fun, there's different ways to get to every objective, lots of tactics involved.
You need luck too, but that's just a minor thing, and it makes things even more realistic.
Graphics are nicely done, sound could be better (so... my "Angela" has a male voice?) but it's good enough, maybe a few more character customization options would be nice.
HOWEVER, there are two things that prevent me from recommending the game.
BUGS
I've just completed the "Cartel Beach Party" mission, it took me about an hour to get three stars in it. That's because the plan I was using (which is the one I think is best to accomplish this goal) relied pretty heavily in having two shields and two assaulters, with shields opening the doors to small rooms while assaulters had to flashbang and then kill the guys in the bigger areas, plus the final shootout in the living room. The problems here are four:
1. Shields ALWAYS turn their back to a door while opening it, getting hit AT LEAST once each time.
2. Shields sometime go through the doors before opening them, exposing themselves to enemy fire.
3. Enemies can sometimes shoot through walls if they're close to a unit.
4. Units sometimes get stuck in front of doors with their guns lowered, exposing themselves to enemy fire and not reacting.
This is far more than what I can stand, considering these bugs compromised my mission to the point I had to restart it 20+ times to get lucky enough not to get hit.
STARS
The Stars system is beyond frustrating. You get X stars based on how many stars you get in a mission, and they only count once (unless you get a higher rank, in that case the latest obtained stars are added). With items costing 10+ stars, and with stars being non-farmable, a poor equipment choice will doom your missions to failure.
I got 3 stars on almost every mission up to the first rescue missions, and (probably) wasted my stars in not-so-good equipment. Now, I can still progress in the game, but I think my units would last longer with, say, a better armor.
They really need to change the Stars to something new, or at least make them farmable.
In the very end, it's a shame this game has these two problems. Other than that, it's a great game.

Had to Edit this review due to massive changes in the game since it was written. Prior to this, it was 57 of 67 Helpful, and I recommended it.
However, due to these changes, I can no longer recommend this trainwreck of a game.
It seemed like they made such good decisions with the initial steam release. Class fixes/overhauls to make them useful and fun again, removal of most of the "pay to even play let alone win" mechanics.
But then they redid a number of classes, again. Including my beloved Zookeeper Osa. What once was the only class I genuinely enjoyed, with a stable full of pets I could summon 3 or 4 pets at once with, has been transformed into a shadow of it's former self with only a single pet allowed, some stupid new buff/energy system, and all my previous skills (and thus my gear) being rendered mostly useless.
This is on top of the LOOOOOOOOONG-awaited "Hero" system turning out to be complete♥♥♥♥♥♥ Everyone was expecting this new system that let you use Alt chars on the same account as Sidekicks/Party Members, since previously, everyone had multiple accounts anyways with alts in their party - so we figured, "Cool, they're going to implement a system to make this official and easier on both us and the servers."
WRONG. The Hero system is a monthly subscription, which costs more per-char you want to add, and highly overpriced. People were waiting for this to come out and be the game-saver, what made the community skyrocket, instead, people quit in droves, major cities that once had dozens or hundreds of shop bags out are now empty, and the pop has dropped outside of the French servers.
They also took the main neutral gathering point, the Temple in Astrub, and literally deleted the entire area where everyone had their shop bags and socialized and had duels at, so there's no room to do anything social there anymore. The developers. actively. removed. socialization. On purpose.
What was once a good, fun little game has been destroyed by terrible decisions. RIP Wakfu.

The water physics alone are worth the experience. On top of that, however, you get a really engaging storyline with some unique puzzle solving and platforming that keeps changing up the gameplay enough that you don’t feel like you’re doing the same thing over and over again.

Hydrophobia is a 3rd person action / shooter based around some great water dynamics. The water will flow from one room to the next, raise, lower, put out fires, and electricity will damage anything near it. Its a lot like being in a Zelda water dungeon.
This is a good game with gameplay mechanics that are on par with big budget games like Uncharted and Batman: Arkham Asylum. It has the ledge climbing, destructible environments, swimming, camera hacking, wall cover, sneaking and even a Navi, which is similar to Arkham Asylum's detective mode, which will let you find encryption codes on walls, open doors from a far, hack consoles with a mini game, access cameras.
There's a great balance between problem solving, shooting and exploration. There are only a few guns and really you won't need any other gun but the default phaser that you can hold the trigger to charge for bigger damage. There is a cover system, but I rarely used it. The downside for some purists would be the aim seems off since there's a 'target lock' system. What I mean is aim near something you can shoot and it lights red and will still count as a hit. Its not the best, but it stays in the realm of good. Even though the game encourages you to drown foes, electrocute them, blow up barrels and so on, it didn't really seem like I killed anyone in cool ways other than exploding barrels.
The controls feel good, aim, shoot, move, move camera, roll (although I never used it once), jump, sneak, weapon wheel, diving, emerging, sticking to cover and so on. The heroine's movement is just a little stiff, but that's one of the only downsides to this game.
The story is good for an indie action game, terrorists have taken over your cruise ship and you need to stop them. You've got a helpful voice that chimes in and tells you what to do, but it never feels like too much instruction. There are things left for yourself to figure out. There's even a nice waypoint to guide you in the general direction if you chose to use it to make the game easier for you to stay on task. It will always show you a dot on the screen where you need to go, but getting to that point is on you.
The game looks great, with really nice water effects and camera sprays. The voice acting sounds good and there are an over abundance of cut scenes at the start, but they ease up in frequency as the game goes on.
I've got the game on PSN and PC. Graphics wise I'd say PC is better, but it seems to be a beast on my PC's processor and not the graphics card. It is a game best played with a controller. The downside with PC is the camera feels chaotic.
The game is short and sweet. The whole single player campaign is like 3 - 4 hours (I completed it for PSN) and at less than $5 I'm fine with that. There are challenge rooms to extend the game's length. It doesn't overstay its welcome and its a game that makes me want to play other things that the developers come up with, but alas they're defunct as of 2012.
Beautiful water graphics!

Not at all a perfect game, Hydrophobia is a little mediocre as a shooter, and it's low budget shows from time to time. Individual segments feel hit or miss, but give it a try though and you will find some uniquely fun puzzles and water based combat.
The water is the real star here, as Hydrophobia's developers seem to have made the game as a showcase for their fluid rendering engine. (Before going bankrupt shortly after) The water effects and physics are the best I have seen to date, and the sinking ship feels oppressive and urgent. Its a lot of fun just to play with the water in the ship's corridors.
Taking it for what it is, I had more fun in Hydrophobia's campy, sometimes muddled world than I have had in most AAA titles.
The only thing this game has going for it are good water physics. Everything else is a  mid 90s cover shooter with some environmental puzzles and lots of swimming and drowning. 6/10.

TL;DR: As a long-time recreational (170 hrs) Dirt Rally player w G27 wheel, I'm enjoying Dirt 4. I still flip between the two, and think they complement each other well for my personal rally interest.
Performance-wise, my GTX 970 and i7 rock it on high detail. Tried out ultra, and that geeenerally ran around 60, with a few 3-5 second stretches of 15-30 fps that could really eff up my groove if it was in the middle of a technically demanding section of a stage. Maybe I'll pick up a GTX 1080 next year. I def like DR's color palette more (feels more photorealistic?), but I'm surely biased with my DR in-game time. Lighting and shadows are considerably more interesting now -- it's easy to almost get distracted by the shadows from trees playing across my in-game cockpit as I drive a late-afternoon Michigan stage.
Tips I found online, for all the people complaining about the understeer:
Watch Porkhammer's most recent (6/12/17) Dirt 4 videos on Youtube. He notes he had to do some considerable in-game tuning to his car to induce oversteer. Also, turn off all assists (obviously) in difficulty settings.
In Career mode, you start out in the fairly low-powered R2 FWD car that is quite obviously NOT a 500hp drift monster. The default tuning is set to very safe or stable values. Don't expect to flick Scandinavians all over the place. >.> In fact, all cars appear to have very tame default tuning. Many default setups have major understeer, poor gearing, and weak braking. You're going to have to do some manual tuning to learn and get the most out of each car.
To induce oversteer so you can slide the car into corners, stiffen the anti-roll bars, lock up the rear differential, move the brake and torque bias to the rear a bit. It's abstractly a lot like buying a real car and modifying it to your tastes. Hope that gets you started! (Note: IRL I have only changed oil+filter, headlights, wheels, and other basic maintenance; no idea about how true to life the abstracted tuning game mechanics are.)
Thanks to Dirt Rally and Assetto Corsa, I've gotten into local amateur racing (both autocross and rally), and have some time on and offroad. I am OK at it (beat a 2014 Corvette on lap time! 60-second track running almost entirely in 2nd gear, plus he'd just bought the car), and have barely figured out how to slightly drift and powerslide my dinky 150 hp daily driver. I can routinely enter turns just enough to make my tires chirp all the way through, and I'm aware of my FWD understeer as well as the effects of weight transfer. I've also experienced several moderately major skids and near-accidents in my working life. More than that, I'm not skilled enough to say.
At my level of experience IRL, the Dirt 4 physics feel pretty right. With default tuning, if I turn into a corner at a Sunday driver pace, the car shifts its weight a bit and makes the turn. If I hit the same corner faster, I can really feel the car dig in and weight transfer definitely affects my steering and braking (often inducing the Death Wobble if I overcompensate). If I blow into the same corner at something stupid fast, then the wheels fly out from under me, and yeah, I'll go sailing across the curve and off into the outside ditch or trees. I've taken curves hard on gravel roads, and sure, the tires slip, but it's not supposed to be full-on ice-skating.
Dirt 4 feels MORE right than Dirt Rally, which I always felt was still a tiny bit floaty. In Dirt 4, the car really feels like it has actual weight -- as if Dirt Rally was minutely dialed up a bit. I think it's great. I don't know what kind of cars racing gamers drive IRL, but when you hit a hairpin or acute corner on gravel at 20-25 kph, the car doesn't gracefully skate for days. You have to really chuck it into the corner. I realize my driving IRL is not high powered, but neither have been the cars I've been using in Dirt 4.
I've tried some other casual racing games (Forza, NFS) in addition to pCars and AC, and I can see why a lot of gamers (especially ones who leave really short negative reviews and quite possibly don't even have a driver's license) coming from a more casual style of driving game might complain about Dirt 4's understeer and overly grippy driving (yes, rear end sticks too much and all that, but it's not glued to the road, as evidenced by plenty of Dirt 4 videos showing drifts and powerslides -- it's a matter of degrees, not some tragic gamebreaker). If floaty cars are what you know, then this game is not for you.
I loved Dirt Rally, which surprised me as it did everyone when it came out. So when Dirt 4 was announced with a stated commitment to continue offering realistic physics, I jumped on it. Some of the reveals and mentions of other race modes like Land Rush made me slightly worry about whether there'd be a return to the much-lamented dudebro vibe of Dirt 3. And when the first Dirt 4 reviews came out saying the physics were a step backward, I worried again. Thankfully, my fears were unfounded. I think Codies balanced a pretty good overall package (menu UI, career, service area, dialogue, soundtrack, all that jazz) for larger mass appeal than Dirt Rally. I personally loved Dirt Rally's low key, minimalist soundtrack (but can see how it was a budget choice as well). Not as much of a fan of Dirt 4's more mainstream soundtrack, but I can see why they made their choices.
I had both high hopes and reservations for My Stage (the majority of games featuring procedural mechanics tend to make for "lots and lots of the same" gameplay). In play, it looks and feels very smooth and well-blended. But when I crank a level up to max length and complexity, I see 3-4 repeats of 2-3 specific turns. Well-made but definitely noticeable, like watching Michel Gondry's awesome music video for the Chemical Brothers' Star Guitar (though the music vid deliberately used the effect). I sincerely hope Codies will expand the game database of stage components, but that doesn't seem like a thing they'd do. Hell, I'd pay money for a track components expansion.
To new interested players, I suggest you check the reviewer's playtime. Also (thankfully), some reviews have qualified their history (how much Dirt Rally time, whether they care, etc.) or experience level. If some random guy reviews this game after 1.5 hrs, ask yourself what he can possibly have figured out about the tuning and handling?

This game...  What words shall I use to describe this game?  "Promising"?  "Nostalgic"?  "Retro"?  All the words before this sentence are words I would NOT use to describe this, "game".  Sure, it looks great, and it truly is a great idea, but whoever tried to put this, "vehicle", if you will, into motion, forgot that unlike bicycles, bigger vehicles need complete engines to work.  At the most, this game is comparable to a small child's tricycle;  it's nice to look at, and seems fun, but once you start using it, you realize things aren't really working out.  Maybe, though, if the frame was made bigger, and the little cheap wheels were exchanged for profressional grade wheels, you would have something you could enjoy looking at and using.  Of course, this is a weird comparison, but what I'm trying to say is that the developers could've taken a bit more time to perfect the game.  I like the idea, but like a newly tarnished silver cup, it needs more polish.

This game is basically a warhammer version of L4d series. Pro's are that the game is fun to play and that team cooperation makes a HUGE difference whether you will succeed in completing the mission or not which is a big plus in my book (selfishness is not rewarded here). Con's are that since the last update enemys can litteraly materialize out of thin air around you or worse, behind you, which kinda feels unfair to me (it was the main reason why I stoped playing L4d2 back in the day) since there is nothing in the world you can do in order to prevent the following damage you take by these spawning foes. Another major issue is the reward system which to put plainly - SUCKS BALLS. If this is the developers attempt to cause through intermittent conditioning an addiction to the game amongst the game's players than it might not be working as planned. This is the main issue for the increasing lack of motivation that I feel to continue playing this game. There is ZERO correlation between how good you played through the round you just finished or the amount of dice, tomes and grimoires you collected during that round to the quality of the loot you will receive. You can have the most amazing round and still recieve crap items. In fact, it seems that that is the default mode. After finishing more than 100 different rounds of the game I can testify to only about 3 good drops. Thats it. And my main character still doesn't have anything close to the weapons it should have at this point. Last point, the game crashes. Not as bad as a few weeks ago but it still happens about every tenth game. Also, if the games host leaves the game the game will restart which is just lame and frustrating. I hope the developers fix these issues in the near future. The bottom line is that the game is a lot of fun to play but still has several major issues that should be addressed.
10/10 would tell new players to pick up tomes and grimoires again

So, where do I start?
I just had a little Dirt Rally session after playing 25 hours of Dirt 4 and I felt that it's time to review the game comparing both of them. And do not tell me that "it's not Dirt Rally 2, it's Dirt 4" - for God's sake it's still Dirt after all.
Mainly I'm going to review the Rally side of the game since that's what most of us care about.

Coming from 200 hours of Dirt Rally I might be a bit biased, but still, here we go:
Pros:
+ Ending a stage by slowing down and stopping manually is much appreciated.
+ Service area is well made.
+ Asphalt handling feels better than in DR.
+ Sounds and music are ok.
+ Multiple game modes to keep things interesting.
Cons:
- Low on content (too few locations, stages and liveries).
- Graphics: Flat and cartoonish compared to DR.
- Performance: Had to set quality to medium to get 60 fps, DR runs fine at high.
- FFB: Feels dull, uninspiring and non-intuitive compared to DR.
- Physics: Feels too grippy in most cars, too difficult to slide. This is just my opinion, though. Others might disagree.
- "Your Stage". Generates generic, boring tracks which all look and feel exactly the same. It has a lot of potential, but the total absence of trackside objects and unique, interesting sections make this function pretty much useless. I really wanted this to be great, but it just isn't. It's boring. After generating five stages, you feel that you're pretty much racing the same boring stages over and over again.
Fix "your stage" and some of the other stuff mentioned, and I might change my mind, because the game has a lot of good things going for it. But for now, this is definately a thumb down. Sorry.
If rally is your game, then go for Dirt Rally instead.

Heres the reasons why i like dirt 4 more than dirt rally:
Finally theres an FOV slider which makes the co-pit view feel better than dirt rally (Went back to dirt rally and the view felt bad).
The simulation mode isn't as bad as people make it out to be, I race mainly the newer cars rather than the classics (classics supposedly have problems) and i find the handling to be better than dirt rally, the handling makes the car not slide as probably due to the weight (Note: I am using the computer). I also found it difficult to adjust at start, but when i got use to it I found it better.
Crashing is a hell of allot better as they dont reset you straight back onto the track, this enables you to crash in spectaular fashison and have to get back on track in real life (I have crashed allot).
5 locations which all feel different, tarmic feels better on spain than germany in dirt rally, wales is amazing to drive with a great mix of forest and openess which looks beautiful, michigan (probably spelt wrong) is the fast track in the game - I do still miss finland from dirt rally as i new that when i took that track i was going to crash majourly (use to end up with radiator damage and engine damage), sweeden is always a ♥♥♥♥♥ to drive (Always struggled on sweeden even in dirt rally).
Gamer handling also works great and feels allot more easier than dirt rally handling. I switched to it and it feels easy and is probably perfect for those people who played dirt 3.
Your stage is pretty decent, however it starts off and still feels allot more generic than dirt rally (less bumps and jumps). However it doesn't get old for me, as every few days i play this game, I still haven't learnt whats coming up around the corner (everything feels new). This to me is better than dirt rally.
Weather is amazing and way better than dirt rally. In dirt rally the rain never really threatened my view of the track. In dirt 4, heavy rain and fog make it incrediably difficult to drive as i cannot fully see the track. This makes it difficult to drive and go fast and i have crashed allot from taking a corner to fast in these conditions. Also i have noticed conditions changing on track (light rain to heavy rain to light rain).
Music is the best it's ever been with tracks from different artists. The music in dirt rally was so similar it bored me to death. The music in dirt rally makes it a joy to listen to, especially in the replays and when it's loading into a rally.
Replays are great and i never used this feature much in dirt rally. In dirt 4, I am using this to look at how well i did and its even better with the ability to select any music out of the sound track to listen to.
Attention to detail is magnificiant. As i person who has only played the codemaster rally games (never played any other), I love this aspect and it makes it feel more realistic than dirt rally. I love the fact that after a crash i sometimes cannot here what type of coner my co-driver calls out (comes up as question mark on screen). I also love the fact that animals can jump infront of your car, helicopters can fly low and drones can get close to your car as you drive. I love the fact that after the finish line you have to drive up to the marshel (this felt weird the first few times, as i forgot you had to do this as I was so use to dirt rally. I also always almost crash past the line sometimes as i want to keep my speed up and dont want to slow down before the line). I also love the fact that the service area more feels very similar to what professional rally drivers use. I also love the fact that you only have a number of tires per stage/stages so you may have to get to the end of the stage with a punched tire (imposible in dirt rally as you would be able to use any amount of tires), also you can now fix the radiator on stage. Finally, I like the fact that parts can break on stage depending on the quality of the parts, you can hear the gear box or brakes not working right and your co driver may mention this.
Sound is still amazing as dirt rally. I do enjoy having different co drivers and having the return of nicky grist (Personal favourite - Loved him back in colin mcrea rally 3, especially in split screen as i played the crap out of it).
Graphics, I am not that big on the graphics in video games and are more happy to have it run, as i dont have the greatest/powerfullest computer in the world (Geforce GT 740M - Laptop). I do really enjoy the graphics for dirt 4, as they fell allot more colourful than that in dirt rally. The attention to detail might not be there (probably due to your stage), but the color makes it better than the washed out look off dirt rally (wales can also be done in sunny weather). I am running on low settings.
The ability to upgrade your facility is amazing (upgrading gives you better stuff) and the hiring of your team is done in a better way compared with dirt rally. I like the fact that if you dont own a car, you have to pay money to pay to enter in with that car (don't worry, you earn allot of money, so it doesn't really effect you too much).
Buying cars is also better, as you can buy them first or second hand. The difference between the two is the quality of parts (second hand cars will break down allot more than brand new cars). Also it's cool to have the ablilty to pick the colors of the car and team and stylise it to your choise (Also can pick driver (simialr to f1 where you create your own driver and name him) and team name.
Other game modes - Havent really tried them out, as i mainly like rally driving. Rally cross has felt really similar to dirt rally and theres more tracks. Landrush i tried once on simulation - found it difficult but did not have car set up right.
Career is also decent, as it is allot more better than dirt rally and feels similar to the previous dirt games.
Things I would like codematers to add:
- More location in dlcs. Please bring back finland, as this is the one location that i really miss. Also please create a New Zealand location, as the roads around new zealand would be awesome to drive on (great mix of gravel and tarmac).
- More bumps/jumps for Your stage. This could be a possibility in a patch or next game.
- Handling for older cars needs improving in simulation (codemasters mentioned this themselves in video and other steam users have also reported this). Have not really used these cars (mainly modern cars used)
Theres no real negatives that i can think about.
Overall, I definately recommend dirt 4 compared to any other codemasters game, as it feels way better and more realistic than the other ones. I recon that it can be fun for those who are new to the series or those who did not enjoy dirt rally and those that are looking for a hardcore experience. I can easily see myself putting in 90+ hours into this game, especially with all the different stuff it has to offer. Also if your new to the series or want to get better I would suggest trying out dirt academy (in game) to give you some lessons and videos to help you get better.

A review from a player who plays racing simulators with a wheel and shifter and loves Dirt Rally. Dirt 4 improves upon areas that were weaker in Dirt Rally, including team management, career, upgrades and repairs. The freeroam park is fantastic to play in, the driving to the marshell at the end of the stage is a great touch and the random events during stages such as a broken down car on the side of the road really adds to the atmosphere and is a huge improvement over Dirt Rally.
However the biggest drawback in my experience so far, is one of the most crucial aspects, the stages. With much love and praise expressed over Dirt 4's new stage generator, I was excited and then dissapointed. The amount of times I've seen a right 6, left 6, open hair pin right in Spain is annoying, 110, left 5, left 3 in Australia, or a right three, rocks on exit in Sweden and a number of other quickly recognisable sequences. Many of these sequences appear frequently, sometimes twice or even three times on the same stage, making those sequences easy to learn, but also taking out the fantastic unique and challenging sectors seen in Dirt Rally. Every stage is predictable, the calls on point, and the width of the track the same. I miss the well designed, individual, unique rally stages we saw in Dirt Rally. Obviously the biggest advantage is you can't memorise an entire stage like Dirt Rally, however you can memorise the sequences that constitute these stages, making almost every stage recognisable and the same.
The physics are also slightly different, cars are hard to slide, grip is immense and it doesn't feel like you're driving on dirt/gravel and this is in simulation mode. Another dissapointment was the loss of the feature which allows for H pattern + clutch and sequential depending on the car you're driving.
Hopefully updates will improve the standardness, predictability and almost charactlessness of the current stages in Dirt 4, improve physics and add some more features, but until they do, I would certainly not recommend Dirt 4 over Dirt Rally. If however you are looking for an entry into simulators and are not sure if it's for you or not, Dirt 4 provides an easy introduction, allowing for both simulator and arcade to go hand in hand.

Fans of Frozen Synapse, Breach and Clear, and other similar tactical games will love Doorkickers, and with good reason - it has a lot to offer, whether you're a meticulous perfectionist or you prefer to run your plans fast and loose. Since you can pause the game to revise your plan (or even alter it in real-time) at any point, it's entirely up to you how active you want to be in guiding your soldiers through each level. You can even try to run a mission with a single trooper. Outside of missions, you can spend the stars you've earned to unlock new equipment for your troopers, and experience will unlock small skill improvements. All the elements of the game come together fairly well - the differences in classes and weapons are small enough that players who aren't concerned with meticulously min-maxing their loadouts can ignore them, but still significant enough to allow for lots of tactical options. The simple controls mean you can create plans and revise plans very quickly and easily.
Doorkickers does have a few issues, particularly with the control scheme. It's sometimes difficult to predict what a particular trooper will do in a particular situation, particularly if you're the kind of player who likes to plan the whole mission out ahead of time. For example, if you order a trooper to breach a room with a flashbang, and that door is already open when he arrives at it, he will head in without throwing one, sometimes leading to his death. Multi-story buildings don't allow you to create plans past the first story. Missions with lots of troopers will clutter up the screen with countless paths and orders.
Perhaps most frustrating to me, as someone who is used to Frozen Synapse's determinism, is the element of randomness in every engagement. Sometimes the difference between a good plan resulting in success or total failure is up to random enemy unit placements and split-second chances, meaning that to get that perfect 3 star score, you sometimes just have to keep running the mission until the stars align and everything goes right.
But I think it says something about how much fun Doorkickers is that despite these annoyances, I'm still heavily recommending it. I've had a lot of fun with it so far and it's great for a quick fix of tactical gameplay. As I'm writing this, it's on sale for 2.99 which is a fantastic deal.

I normally don't enjoy playing MMOs and usually keep away from them (why? I have no idea), but Wakfu feels different. This game has an Isometric viewpoint with turn based tactical combat. Its PvP is balanced and its paymodel fair, which is something you dont see in F2P games often here on steam.

I played Dofus for years. I always said that Dofus is great game and you won't ever find game like Dofus. How wrong I was. Wakfu is like evolved Dofus. Sure it lacks some things we didn't even know we like in Dofus (e.g. you don't get all skills at once so you have more time to learn using them), but generally Wakfu is even better. Why is Wakfu so special? You have to use your brain while fighting. Of course you will have some skill pattern, few skills you will use again and again, however you have to know where to go, who should be killed first, etc. New monster means new type of battle. And another great thing Wakfu offers to its players is economy and ecosystem. There are no NPCs for buying/selling, everything is on players. Another thing, that depends on players is nature. You can gather plants, you can cut trees, but if you want them to grow again, you have to plant them. And monsters as well. Also everyone in certain area can get bonus, because special NPCs who take care of areas will tell you how much trees they want there, how much monsters, ... And if they are pleased, players get temporary bonus stats. I am not saying everyone will love the game, but I think everyone should at least try.

I must say that this game already outgrow and far more entertaining from it's predecessor DiRT 3. Physics is like DiRT Rally and the new 900° tuning wheel and virtual arms is now more engaging in the cockpit view. With the combination of amazing graphics, car details, effects and textures adds more to realism. If you are into racing simulation games, I highly recommend this one.

This game is a good game for people who are new or never even heard of Rally. I would totally recommend it. However, for people who want a proper life-like Rally simulation game, I would recommend DiRT Rally. The physics on this game when put to simulation could not be compared to DiRT Rally. Simulation physics wise, DiRT Rally is a much better game than DiRT 4.
There are a good amount of cars that is in the game but they removed some of the cars from DiRT Rally. (Come on, add the Toyota Celica GT already! Such an iconic car and has been missing since DIRT Rally) If only they just added it on instead of removing them. I would say the same for the track locations. They put in new locations compared to the previous ones in DiRT Rally, but only 3 new ones out of the 5 as compared to 6 from DiRT Rally. Stop removing cars and tracks already! Just add the new ones on top of the old ones for more content for newcomers of the game, and nostalgia for the ones who played it before!
The new feature "your stage" is a great addition, allowing the user to create unique tracks. However, it becomes repetitive after a while, using the same sections in different parts of the SAME stage. Sometimes, it is even the same section that you have just finished few seconds ago.
I love the addition of creating your own team, having your own sponsors, your own livery and colors. If only there was an option that could allow the use of iconic liveries on your cars, because that livery just fits the car and no other livery can match it.
I love the new addition of landrush. It's like rallycross, but with trucks and buggies, which makes it even better!
In conclusion, DiRT 4 is a great game. No matter what kind of gamer you are if you are looking for a casual rally game to have fun or for a sim-like experience, this game is a great choice. But not my recommendation if you want a full-sim rally experience, for that, DiRT Rally is your best choice. The tracks are great, the physics is even better than DiRT 4, the cars are great but not as many as compared to this game.

I am going to be completely honest, I do not like this game. They got everything right from the sound to the graphics, to even the new generated tracks. But they messed up on one thing that killed the game (in my opinion), the physics. It's more of a "Arcadish" game than dirt rally, and it's a little bit of a shame. If Codemaster realized that the majority of the Steam audience are Sim Racers they would of gotten the majority of the audience happy. I had a feeling deep in my gut,  before it even came out that it was not going to be as good as its successor, Dirt Rally. 
 
There's a reason why this game has a 5 star rating on the PlayStation Store and a lot of people are saying it's a good game. If you're just a casual who plays on a controller, you'll have a very fun time racing these cars. That's not a bad thing, just for me it's not what I hoped for as I have a full Sim setup that I use all the time for Dirt Rally and other racing titles.  
 
I do have to give them credit, a lot of the stuff that they put into Dirt 4 for can easily be transferred to a new game in the Dirt Rally series too, and if they added the regenerating tracks into it, I think that would be heaven for me and many others. So I'm giving this game a thumbs up. Even though it's not meant for me it doesn't mean it's a bad game. Everything works, there's no bugs and for the general audience I think it's a great game. But it's not for me, and any other hardcore Sim racers. If you want proof and own this game, try driving the Lancia Stratos in both tittles, there's a hell of a difference.

Why make a new game that's a lot worse than the previous one? Dirt Rally is so close to perfect in it's driving mechanics and the progression. In Dirt Rally the tuning is OK, and it's very low-key and well presented. Dirt 4 however, has much, MUCH worse driving mechanics, the progression is extremely limiting and idiotic, and the presentation is Americanized to the point of vulgarity.
In Dirt Rally the rally notes are sometimes wrong, but they're dynamic and very immersive. In Dirt 4, all I can say is that they're not horrible.
The only thing I can think of where Dirt4 is actually better than Dirt Rally, it's that it runs slightly better on my computer.
Seriously. Just get Dirt Rally. It's such a masterpiece of a rally game, Dirt 4 can't compete in a million years.

As I said in
, The Jackbox Party Pack is a wonderful idea for a party game. Unfortunately, the second pack is mostly disappointing.
My most immediate gripe is that it is such a shame to see this as a separate game, as opposed to DLC for the first party pack. Switching between the two during an evening is an annoying waste of time and shows that the developers aren't particularly interested in creating a long-lasting product. After purchasing it was also disheartening to see that the main menu was less stylised than the moving game boxes from the first game. A small problem, yes, but it just comes across as a lack of effort.
Moving onto the games themselves and it is clear that you and your friends will spend much less time with this selection of games than the last. Bidiots is too confusing and not gratifying enough to be a good party game. Bomb Corp also doesn't work well in this setting either, although when playing with just you and one friend it does have a small amount of fun to it. Talking of fun however, the rest of the games are more enjoyable. Unfortunately one of them is just more Fibbage. This does mean a wider selection of questions for those who love the game, but it is again sad to not see this as DLC for the first pack or integrated with Steam Workshop. The last of the games (Earwax and Quiplash) are the most enjoyable and fresh. However, they can both get repetitive more quickly. Earwax is fun to play to laugh at the silly sounds, but is rather lacking in real gameplay and Quiplash is perhaps too difficult to keep everyone laughing.
After mostly having an absolute blast with Jackbox Party Pack 1, it would have been nice to have seen more work gone into new games. However, overall the sequel just doesn't put as much effort in as its older brother and still lacks DLC and Steam Workshop support. Such a disappointment.

This is the closest game I could find to be considered a hidden gem. And I think is deserves that title.
Take control of a SWAT squad during many different terrorist encounters, thoroughly cleaning out the building by the time your done. Use the many squad members you make in your down time to change your strategy for each level.
Most of the time you'll have to save hostages, but you will encounter the occasional bomb, arrest warrent, drug situation, or have to just clean house. As you complete missions, you level your used squad members, not only improving their combat skills, but also giving you doctorine points. Doctorine points being used to upgrade the different classes' effectiveness.
You'll meet alot of doors blocking your way along you career. But kicking them down isn't the only option. You can silently open them, loudly flash them, or (still loudly) plant C4 to burst them open. And that's just normal doors. You'll also face locked doors that can't silently be opened, but have to be picked, which will alert enemies close enough to hear it. As you can see, this is were the strategy kicks in. To this day I can hear "loud?" ringing in my ears while playing PAYDAY 2. As much as it hurts me to say this so blandly, "you can go in loud, or sneak in silent." But I have to cut this guide short before it gets to long.

I then decided to think this over a bowl of tortillas along with some delicious salsa. Sure enough, when I came back, 11 players had joined of the server. I dived in.
In this server I saw this one enemy aimlessly running in an insurgent cave. I shot him and, mistakenly thinking I had ended his life, reloaded. He shot a burst at me, which I mostly dodged by proning. I then witnessed the man teleporting a few meters in front of me and once more behind me. Was devine work at play here? I wasn't sure, but I was glad to be alive. The insurgent didn't get this chance. A teammate bravely came to my rescue and shot him dead, sending his body ragdolling an impressive distance away in a supernatural manner. If you came here looking for a review on contagion you made the wrong choice, but if you wanted some scones, you made the right choice!
Ingredients
225g/8oz self raising flour
pinch of salt
55g/2oz butter
25g/1oz caster sugar
150ml/5fl oz milk
1 free-range egg, beaten, to glaze (alternatively use a little milk)
Method
1.Heat the oven to 220C/425F/Gas 7. Lightly grease a baking sheet.
2.Mix together the flour and salt and rub in the butter.
3.Stir in the sugar and then the milk to get a soft dough.
4.Turn on to a floured work surface and knead very lightly. Pat out to a round 2cm/¾in thick. Use a 5cm/2in cutter to stamp out rounds and place on a baking sheet. Lightly knead together the rest of the dough and stamp out more scones to use it all up.
5.Brush the tops of the scones with the beaten egg. Bake for 12-15 minutes until well risen and golden.
6.Cool on a wire rack and serve with butter and good jam and maybe some clotted cream.
