I am a huge fan of the Hotline Miami series, Hm1 was so fast paced, high octane, hair pulling, heart pounding, I couldn't stop playing it, and pretty much beat the game in one sitting, justw ent back to find the masks and replay some levels. But i loved it so much, the sheer amount of options you had and the way each level could be played using different masks was almost limitless.
Then came wrong number.
Wrong number has absolutely none of the elements that HM1 had, instead replacing fast paced gameplay with boring levels that were packed with fat guys, windows, and no options except for memorizing their positions and shooting them out, one by one. Wrong number is just so bad. They took the original formula we all know and love and wrecked it. You can't see any of the enemies, because they are all maddeningly offscreen enough so that if you try to advance, you end up getting shot, and then next life grab a gun and shoot them, rinse repeat.
I'm not normally a person who picks up on the bad quirks of gameplay, ♥♥♥♥♥es about frame rate or graphics (unless they are REALLY bad), or nitpicks on a game. I usually enjoy every game i pick up, mostly because i only pick the ones i really like and get a lot of enjoyment out of them.
But i can't overlook this monstrosity. The storyline isn't captivating at all, i'm restrcitedf to pick between some truly horrible masks, i can't play the characters i really want to play, and most of them are terrible. I hated them giving the masks personas, like making them real people. it kills the allure of the mystery, the countless that have come before, the meaningless slaughter too many have engaged in, some that truly loved it and some who despised it.
Don't buy this game.

I play this game almost everyday (Under the name Harvey if you're wondering), I had written a review for it before but i am rewriting it since there is a newer version.
this game is utterly terrifying, the combat is fast and brutal, the detial is gorey and gritty (Reminds me personally of Fury and BOB), You have to work together and know how exactly to use your class to win let alone survive, To win you have to fight dirty; Kill or be killed and kill with discrimination (Fighting dirty does not mean spawn camping please do not do that)

I highly reccomend playing it at full volume if you're using headphones, the sounds are perfect, while some sounds for the weapons arent as Authentic as some claim, they all sound just like Real guns and opperate accordingly, The weapons are an absoulte joy to use, personally to me, There is nothing like emptying an M1a1 Thompson magazine on a Nazi from 7 feet away.
The Vehicles are absolutely Awesome, When you Fire up a tank you can practically smell the exhaust, They take alot of practice to get the hang of using, they certainly require some balls espically for the Allied tanks, but the Boom of the gun is satisfying and hearing a shell soar past you is intense
Lastly, the game is pretty active, ofcourse only 2 servers are occupied, but its not rare for the infantry server to be completely full, and for the Tank server its usually full on Sundays. the community is great too, nothing to be intimidated by, like with all games youll have the S'talker and the two players bickering about god knows what, if you ask a question about the class you're using you're likely to get a straight answer.
Anyways, thats all i got for a "New and Improved" Review, I hope i have convinced you to try out this mod, I unintentionally left out some detials on how the game itself functions but im sure the other reviews explain such things.

I really enjoy this game even with it's consistent stuttering which is still annoying. I would also add that sound effects need work in terms of mining or doing anything in a cave (keep the volume low for the sake of your ears). The music is quaint at first but now it reminds me of an elevator and I almost never have my headset on anymore. Between the mining and music you too will put the headset down.
Content: I have roughly 67 hours into this game so far. That would break down into maybe 4-5 hours of failed early games just to get the swing of things and 60+ in my current explore game. I find myself running out of actual exploring to do as there are a limited number of Ylands although I've read that I must also explore the ocean floor which sounds fun. However, on land I feel like I've taxed the content of it's current state. I did not build a car because a propellor pack is simply the most advantageous way to travel on land and I would guess that my car would be constantly crashing into the hundreds of objects dotting the landscape. The crafting tree is massive. Hundreds of items to craft but sooooooooo many of them either strictly cosmetic or rather useless until properly stat'd.
Weapons and armor have no visible stats and offer few noticeable differences. I haven't actually rechecked it yet but I can tell you that it takes at least a dozen bullets from a rifle to down the strongest naughty creature and I'm almost certain it took the exact same number of stone crossbow bolts to do that. Not to deny the pew pew power of the mighty crossbow but I think shooting actual 'gunpowder in casing' cartridge ammunition should a little more damage but alas.
Content is still a positive element for me - there is a ton of stuff and many many useful things to collect to force users to make a choice of what to carry.
Playstyle: Standard digging and chopping mechanics if a little more focused than some other titles. Combat hitboxes are a bit strange and hard to figure out but once you discover how OP ranged weapons are you won't worry about melee any longer anyway. Exploring is fun although most of your generated Ylands are fairly close to the main land while the sea appears to continue endlessly away from them. I have sailed a good distance away but still haven't chanced a very long straight trek to find a map edge (which I suspect is far far far away).
Overall: Very fun and easy to sink hours. Fun finding and creating things to open an ever expanding tech tree but once you start making progress more rapidly you find the content wall rather quickly.

Dirt 4 is a strange creature. On one hand it gives a Rally Sim enthusiast everything you'd expect, and more. On the other hand as soon as you leave Dirt Academy where you are shown few basic of rally driving, suddenly experience gets ruined. Dirt Academy provides you with mixture of both loose stuff and tarmac, I really enjoyed driving both Subaru WRX STi NR4 and BMW e30 M3 around the area. Phyiscs seemed really realistic, breaking distances felt OK especially with Subaru, and you could powerslide with throttle and weight transfer properly. Moving to actual rallies- either in career mode, or Your Stage generated stuff- makes you really excited at the beginning, but as soon as you try your first gravel stage everything is ruined. Personally I felt really mad at Codemasters for ruining such a great concept with bad physics, and I still consider those to be terrible. The only way to enjoy the game is to stick to tarmac (Spain) because it feels strongest out of all locations. If you are into RX, then you will experience totally different car handling- they trully did a great job making RX physics. Before I end I would like to get back to the actuall beginning of D4- when you first run the game you are asked to drive a test stage. The problem is you are forced to play with assists on (even if you choose Simulation in a prompt), also my Logitech steering wheel was setup terribly by default, so I drove throu the stage thinking what's going on... They also should make it more clear how to setup peripherals linear/ raw/ 1:1 for those who use steering wheels and pedals.
Overally I am dissapointed and I am not going to enjoy this game. I had high hopes, but unless they fix grip levels I am not going to fall into their promises. This is probably the last Dirt I bought ever. If you are looking for a sim you can enjoy, forget it.

This is without a doubt my favourite Codemasters game yet.
The car selection is good, although hopefully they add more cars with DLC. All the favourites are there at least (Lancia Delta HF Integrale, Peugeot 205, Evo X, Mini, etc.). The physics are superb, however it's not as 'loose' as Dirt Rally, so fans of that game may be disappointed. The game offers 'Simulation' and 'Gamer' physics modes, so both sim fans and casual gamers should be satisfied.
No two rally stages are the same due to 'Your Stage', CM's new track generator. The stages are fun and don't feel repetitive, but admittedly they lack the character of Dirt Rally's stages. There is a small, but decent selection of landrush and rallycross courses as well. Again, hopefully CM will add more in the future.
Speaking of landrush and rallycross, they don't feel nearly as fleshed out as the rally and classic rally disciplines, but I wouldn't go as far as calling them an afterthought. This is first and foremost, a rally game.
I'm playing in simulation mode with a controller, ABS set to 3 and automatic shifting turned on. Now, I'm no hardcore sim racer, but I'm consistently getting podium positions at 'tough' AI difficulty. As far as I can tell, that's the highest AI difficulty the game has to offer. While this is certainly a confidence booster, I really shouldn't be doing this well. Hardcore sim fans will be disappointed. It's also worth mentioning that the game doesn't include CM's 'flashback' feature, at least in simulation mode. Personally, I don't miss it. I like that the game forces me to live with my mistakes.
Performance is mostly good, although most people should turn off 'blending' and turn crowds to low for a substantial increase in FPS. In terms of graphical fidelity, the game isn't particularly impressive.
Dirt 4 has its issues, but in the end this is some of the most fun I've ever had in a racing game. Five stars.

Simulation physics model feels fine. I've done rallyX, been a rally marshal, driving on US rally stages. I have no problems getting cars to rotate, and definitely feel understeer when I'm going too fast. I haven't done much driving in anger on pavement, so I can't really comment on that, but it feels about right to me. Not sure what folks are complaining about. The biggest change is that cars feel heavy compared to Dirt Rally. I don't know how many times the rs200 did a front flip in DR after hitting a rock/yump. That doesn't seem to happen in this game.

Coming from DiRT Rally to this game takes some getting used to, but the end result is an extremely rewarding rally experience.  The tracks may not feel as tailored as those of DiRT Rally but there's a seemingly endless supply of them.  Combine this with the varied time of day and weather settings and there's no end to the variety.
The online challenges also add a lot of fun.

Other things like bugs and glitches, sometimes I even complain about hit reg. My point is this game has come a long way, and I remember the days when it had the old hud and sights. The maps have significantly improved and the spawn locations aren't to painful. But there are still ways you can get spawn killed once you leave the zone. I've grinded my German Infantry to rank 12 and finally managed to unlock the scope on the Gewehr 43, and I think this was my biggest accomplishment in this game. Took me about a year, probably because I kept going on and off with playing the game. Oh it was worth the grind, it is fun shooting people from a distance more accurately than trying to aim down iron sights and hurt my eyes. I believe this game could succeed like when it first had positive reviews, as only if the developers put more effort to make this game great. And to also be more communicative to the H&G community.
This game is a great to play with friends just to fool around. Just make sure you fool around during a war. Also to talk about wars, people actually communiate and cooperate. I sometimes take leadership to try to guide my teammates in battles. They would listen and we would eventually get things done. Of course I rarely see Germany get any bonuses during Wars, probably because the developers believe Germany wins every single war. You wouldn't see any cooperation in non war matchmaking. If you want a more serious output in this game, try joining a faction and participate in the war. That is the place where you can get more serious, just make sure you don't  go to far and get frustrated.
------------------------------------------------------------------
Now finally, my verdict.
I would recommend the game at this time.
------------------------------------------------------------------
This is because my gameplay so far has been very positive, I haven't run into many hackers or bugs or glitches. Hit reg is probably the only bug I would ever complain about. It's more fun for me to play in a war and communicate and cooperate with my teammates. Grinding is not a big concern for me, but at least make it so you earn more credits when doing actions in game. Once again I believe this game has potential still, and hopefully you can give Heroes and Generals a try.

You will not find a game like Wakfu anywhere. This has to be one of the most unique MMOs I have ever played. Strategic grid based combat, unique classes, a beautiful art style, and a magical story are all found in this game. Try it out for free with a couple friends. Form a group. Have a laugh. Try to beat a dungeon. Specialize in a craft and trade with each other. Propose Friendly dual or attack a player and become an outlaw. This is truly a multiplayer game.

Pros:
+ Amazing when playing with friends (feels like you're part of a team/party in something like final fantasy)
+ Good game design decisions all around
+ Some classes offer WAY more difficulty then others
+ Classes combine well with eachother in combat
Pro/Con:
+-  You get all of your abilities very early on (You get to do stuff in the early game)
+_ You cant sell things to NPCs, everything is done through the "auction house"
+_ Can be very grindy (alot less with friends, but still grindy)
+_ Alot to learn (for sure if you take the more difficult classes)
+_ "fast-travel" is basicly free aslong as the distance isent super long
Cons:
- While everybody gets their own drops in a fight, harvesting materials (like trees or ores) are not instanced, thus making it a race for resources if alot of people are around (thankfully they do grow fast and in the case of trees you can replant them yourself)
- Alot less fun solo, you do get a companion that you control yourself, but still way less fun then an acctual player
Overall, this is the first game to make me quit out of time consumption and not out of boredom, highly recommend it, for sure once it acctually hits open beta.

Overall I give this game (as of 8/5/2014) a 7.5/10. I'm primarily more in to the FPS and MOBA genres, but the visuals of this game were enough for me to give it a try. To start, the art-style is beautiful, the soundtrack is pleasant and gives the game a nice ambiance, and the animations are amazing! The gameplay (from what I've played so far, which is the tutorial) feels a bit slow, and I feel like the tutorial was unnecessarily long (although I believe you can skip it to begin playing the game), and the controls took a bit for me to get used to, but other than that I feel like this is definitely one of the better MMO's you can find on Steam (not to mention it's free!). I'd say download it, try it, and see if you enjoy it.
This is the first MMO I've played in a long time, and it's probably one of the first turn-based strategy games I've been able to play for more than an hour. My opinion is more focused from the average FPS/MOBA player's point of views, please keep that in consideration while reading my review.
(9)
The only reason I decided to try this game when I got a hold of a closed beta key was the visuals of the game, and once I entered the game they really, really impacted my overall thoughts on the game. The game is beautiful, and the art style is perfect. Not to mention the game's animations are amazing, they truly and firmly "say what needs to be said"... if that makes sense. Not to mention character customization is great and makes you really feel unique. The only reason I didn't rate the game's visuals 10/10 was because majority of the playable characters all seem fairly feminine and cuddly, while my goal when I was creating my character was to be masculine and fairly intimidating. In the character creation, I didn't realize there was an option to switch from male to female and actually thought several of the male character choices were supposed to be female! Regardless, the game is GORGEOUS and fresh, there's no doubt about that.
(6)
When I first tried the game, the controls weren't really what I was used to. Being a primarily FPS/MOBA gamer, it definitely felt weird left clicking to where I needed to be and right-clicking on things to interact with them, and one thing that really bothered me at first was the fact that there wasn't edge-scrolling and that the camera wasn't centered on my character the entire time (although I have suggested on the forums to add edge-scrolling and/or the camera focusing on the charcter), and a little bit in I felt a bit tired of clicking everywhere I went, so I feel like the controls weren't the greatest but still worked enough for me not to give up completely.
(8)
The game's soundtrack is great, it has this... warmth to it I guess, and it really makes the experience pleasant for me. The sounds are good too, and I feel go almost perfectly with the visuals! A few sounds are a tad bit annoying to hear, like these little rabbits (known as "Woodlets" I believe) that did this sort of... giggle, and it slightly bothered me after hearing it (or a certain variation of it) every time I attacked one of them. Other than that the audio is great and well-fitting for the game's style.
(7)
The game plays fairly smoothly, from what I've played (the tutorial) it seems like the game is mainly just accepting tasks and engaging in them (like most MMO's), but the tasks aren't always the same thing over and over, so it doesn't really get stale. The game is a bit slow-paced though, which I'm not very used to. The combat is good, and the spells are unique and fun to use and learn. The only reason the gameplay got a 7/10 was because the tasks seem slightly boring and overall not very exciting (to me). Regardless though, I feel like I'll definitely be coming back to this game to play several more hours.
Definitely try, it's a quick download and is a great experience, I'd highly recommend this game to any gamer (besides my brother, the only games he plays are those of the Call of Duty franchise... that poor, sad little man.)

This is such a great little game that came out of nowhere and has hooked me in for the past week or so. It starts off as a survival game but expands into an adventure as you advance in the tech trees and start looking for new islands across the sea. Mechanically it strikes the right balance where the survival aspects aren't a chore and are actually enjoyable. The game constantly surprises me with random locations, like finding a random underwater base with scuba gear that gave me flippers, turning me into an underwater rocket; a blown out abandoned building with cannons in a snowy landscape; an immense cave network filled with hordes of mutant leopards...a lot more, but you get the gist.
It's a weird, wonderful and exciting survival game, has a crazy amount of content already, and even includes a creator mode and a workshop, where you can create random game modes and scenarios.
Really looking forward to seeing how this game develops, and REALLY looking forward to the NPC addition in the future. Total gem.

This could honestly be amazing. I love the concept. Sure, the German equipment is OP as all get out, evidently the devs drank the 'Germans had the best everything' kool-aid, but whatever.
However: the rate at which you get money is completely unforgiveable. Even with a premium account. Whether the match lasts 10 minutes or 40 minutes, you're gonna get maybe 3-5k credits per match. Every grenade I throw costs 122 credits. I could very quickly burn through all of my earnings in a single match...which is before gun ammo, vehicle repairs (don't even think about tanks. I generally get a pretty good kill ratio in tanks and repairs keep me in the poor house for *light* tanks). You can unlock the PTRD reasonably quickly but good luck affording it, it costs ~240k. That's right, assuming you net 4k every match you only have to play SIXTY matches to unlock it. (You'll end up having to play far more).
These gather rates would actually be fine if I didn't have to pay for repairs and ammunition, bleeding me dry every game.
I absolutely love the concept but for real it feels like a cash grab, you know? I understand you have to balance it so that you can make money - it isn't free to run or develop the game, but things like World of Tanks manage to make the game enjoyable and not overly grindy without exorbitant repair and ammo costs.
If they rebalance the gather rates and tone down the Germans a bit (I get tired of having someone with an MP40 kill me at 100m while they eat two of my SVT-40 rounds and shrug it off), I would absolutely recommend. In the current state, I cannot.
EDIT: Oh, don't forget predatory gold pricing! One month of premium is 2400 gold.
You can either buy 1400 gold or 2200 gold.

My expectations were rather low on this title, but after 16 career-events i can say: thumbs up in nearly all aspects. It´s way better than Dirt Rally (178 hours so far).
Controls: All my stuff works flawlessly and with SimVibe it´s the pure awesomeness
You can map functions like shifting to different devices now and i can shift with paddles or sequential shifter as i like. Doesn´t loose the mappings after a restart anymore.
Graphics: I can run 4k@60 fps with a bit higher settings (high with some ultra-details, GTX 1070) and no fps-drops in the rain like in DR. Much more beautiful lightening and the crowd have more polygons. Can´t see any downgrade here like some people were saying.
FFB: Can´t really tell, because running full Sim Commander FFB with my Accuforce Pro like always.
Physics: Wales, Sweden and the tarmac-physics are IMO the same with improvments. No more (only) fluffy snow-banks in Sweden anymore and better avoid them. The grip on the other gravel-stages are more like Finland than Greece, but watching onboards this seems more accurate and they have lots of grip for real;). The cars have more weight and not flying anymore over every crest. It´s a bit easier to drive in a positive, IMO more realistic way.
Stage-Design: The career-stages are fixed and looking like hand-crafted. Would like to see a bit more tarmac-variations at Spain. I will miss the handbrake-corners at Baumholder or this tarmac to ice stages at Monte and hope for DLCs.
Career: Much more opportunities to spend money for and more motivating so far. AI gets tough as well a bit later.
Land Rush: Great physics and action. Really tough to handle this buggy. AI seems tough as well.
Rally Cross: Just tried a few laps and seems like the same than DR, but wasn´t driving it that much.

I wouldn't normally write a review so soon after getting a game, but I seem to have had a much better experience so far with the game than other reviewers and I wanted to share that. I've been wondering if I've even been playing the same game as other reviewers.
I have 140+ hrs in Dirt Rally and got to be OK at that game. I play with a Thrustmaster T150 with addon pedals and shifter.
TL;DR: Dirt 4 is an improvement on a great game in almost every way.
- The procedural stages don't feel as characterful as Dirt Rally's. I especially miss Monaco and Greece.
- The graphical performance isn't as good; DR looks better at the settings I need to get 45–60FPS on my GTX 750 1GB.
+ More stage variety
+ More music
+ More career depth
+ A little more depth with the cars
+ More breadth in disciplines
+ Easier to find people to play head-to-head multiplayer with
+ Online leaderboards are more beginner-friendly, because there's more tiers at the bottom
+ Free-roam for tuning and practicing maneuvers.
+ Tons of small UI refinements
± Physics are at least as good as DR, more likely better. I'm not an expert on these things.
The handling model definitely feels different from DR. I put every setting as difficult as I could at first, except for setting ABS to 1, and I felt like I was learning how to drive all over again. I don't think it feels any less realistic or easier. I've been sliding off of gravel stages left and right in a AWD car and constantly losing the back end in AWD/RWD, in ways I never did in DR, so I really don't know what people are talking about with there being too much grip. Reviewers with actual rally experience on the Dirt subreddit also seem to agree that D4's physics are more realistic than DR's. Coming from someone who's mid-tier at best in sim rally, I think people interested in a serious rally sim should absolutely pick this up.
Dirt is a fantastic franchise IMO, and D4 continues to improve on that. I don't use the assists that would make the game easier, so I would read another review for that, but the core gameplay here is very accessible and scales in difficulty well. I think this is the best game in the series yet and wholeheartedly recommend it.

Who wouldn't want to roll around at the speed of sound? Sonic Adventure 2 Battle on the GameCube was my childhood, and now this great (and sometimes not so great) game is in HD?! Buckle up, since we're escaping the city!

I'd honestly give this a mixed review if I could. But to be fair, my thoughts are mostly positive.
The Sonic/Shadow parts can be pretty fun when you get used to controlling their speed. Successful homing attacks and light dashes always make you feel like a badass. The camera can be a bit bothersome, though.
The Knuckles/Rouge parts are as terrible as everyone says they are. I don't mind they way they both control, I just wish the levels were made around those controls instead of frustating treasure hunts that last up to 20 minutes! And again, terrible camera.
Surprisingly enough, despite everyone's criticisms, I really like the Tails/Eggman parts. I'm not gonna act like they were the most revolutionary levels I ever played, but I thought locking on to targets and shooting stuff was really fun. I even liked the platforming for some reason! The camera can get kind of bad, but not AS bad since these levels are slower.
In the end, it was an interesting experience. Unlike many, I never owned a GameCube so I never grew up with this game. I'm sure if I had it at the time, I might've enjoyed it as a kid.

While the game starts you with very simple missions, the scenarios quickly become more complex and interesting. I found the large variety of weapons and different strengths of the classes really engaging as the game became harder. It's equally fun to try to plan out the entire mission or just individually guide each soldier in real time.
My only negatives are some interface issues and slightly too high spread on enemies. Interactions with doors can be clunky and thrown grenades/flashbangs don't always go where you want. Enemies can hit hostages at pretty wide angles at times forcing you to restart. Late game enemies can have some frustrating RNG on their armor which can force arbitrary restarts as well.
All in all, a really fun little game that quickly starts eating up huge chunks of your time.
You need a challenge in tactical and strategic thinking? This is your game. But remember: While you making progress it's getting harder everytime.

Also frustrating was the final boss fight, which was way more difficult than it should have been due to the aforementioned control problems. I also experienced game-halting bugs at more than one point in my playthrough, which could only be resolved by restarting from a checkpoint (which thankfully, are placed liberally). In summary, the overall setting and concept is cool, but it is hampered by spotty controls and a few too many bugs and glitches for my taste. Worth checking out for cheap price.

Look, if you happen to be a childhood fan of AE and their games: AdventureQuest, Dragonfable, Mechquest, AQ-Worlds, etc. Then you probably won't have any problems getting invested into this one. Town's the same, menu's the same. It's the natural progression into 3D games.
That said, much like their other games. AE has a tendency to release their games to the public the instant they have a functional handful of maps and mobs. Less so a beta than a proof of concept, and this isn't the first time they've done it. My advice would be to wait, because right now there simply isn't much to do, unless you want to snag some early game loot that you might feel will be removed later, such as event items and Alpha-Beta rewards. Otherwise, wait a bit.
Now, as for the game itself. It's an AE-game through and through, and you might be forgiven if you found it eerily similar to AQW. The 3D graphics aren't bad, and the cartoony-anime style certainly has a bit of charm to it, but the added dimension to graphics doesn't add much to gameplay. You still have a selection of static skills that could easily be counted on one hand, locked to a class, which can be swapped out at will. The starting selection is still the basic holy trinity of Warrior - Rogue - Mage, and they don't really bring anything new to the table.
If there is one new addition to the system: that would be the crafting system. Way it works is that for a good chunk of weapons and armor: instead of just buying or finding the thing, you need to collect a certain amount of materials, and then visit the correct NPC and pay a nice chunk of gold to craft this into whatever you might be after.
Admittedly not entirely new. What this really means is that NPC's will be selling you trinkets for more than merely gold. But then, it hits a bit of a stumbling block. Each weapon or armor piece has a crafting time. And even after you've collected fifty bear arses and handed them alongside your life-savings to the Blacksmith dejour: you still find yourself having to wait 24 hours before you can collect your Bear-Butt Cloak of Cold Protection +59
Unless, of course. You pay a small amount of microtransaction currency to ''speed'' it up. And that's when the game rears it's ugly head. A game with microtransactions isn't new, and AE games have done this for ages. But it does start to more like certain freemium games you might find on mobile, and this might turn certain people off.
Even stranger, there's a good handful of NPC's that outright have a shop for the sole purpose of selling you crafting materials that you then give right back to them to craft a weapon. You buy bits of leather only to spend it on making that shiny new armor at the same store. You might wonder why this overly complicated mess is in the game, since you can just as readily find vendors outright selling the things you need. Unless, of course: it exists to have those 24 hour crafting times peeling away at your patience.
Finally, while the advertised multi-platform cross-platform gameplay between PC and Mobile phones is a reasonably interesting idea in theory. In practice, a multi-platform game needs to work on it's weakest devices, and in this particular situation: the location of the buttons, the touch-style menus, they all give the impression of a mobile port. This could easily be fixed by switching up the interface to something more PC-friendly, and the company very well might. But at the time of this review, it's clunky.
In summation.
Pros: Multiplatform Game is an interesting idea, and has potential. Appealing Graphics, Fun for AE Fans.
Cons: Multi-platform fails to meet that potential, and the game feel like a port. Microtransaction mechanics akin to a freemium mobile game, it's just not remotely finished.
It's still free, and if you have any curiosity, it's worth a shot. But otherwise, give this game a few months before you pick it up.

Don't be led astray by the primitive graphics, Warband more than makes up for it in gameplay. Many games claim to tailor the story to your decisions and to a degree, they do; but the end result is more often than not the same and the choices you make don't really affect anything. Warband, on the other hand, doesn't have a linear story at all. The story you'll find in Warband you must find out for yourself; if you're like me, you can ignore everything about it and just play the game. The story really doesn't matter. No two games are the same. Your goal is to rule the world, either as its king or as a member of the faction that does it. Of course, the latter could be considered easier, but you'll find that even taking over one other faction will take many dozens of hours.
You could treat Warband as a battlefield simulator, the massive fights between hundreds of soldiers on each side are glorious. However, you do need to figure out the little tricks to the game to really figure out how to win. For example, in the beginning of one of my playthroughs I had made my entire army into bowmen and continued upgrading them along that path. No bandits could touch me, the early siege I took part in was simple and I only lost a few men, in general; I wasn't worried about dying much. Then, heavy soldiers came; on horseback no less. The arrows couldn't pierce the armor of the three soldiers well enough and the horses ensured my men couldn't get away. Fifty crossbowmen, and myself, gone in a matter of minutes to three heavy soldiers. The rest of the army didn't even get to me before that could happen. Unfortunately, this is where the frustrating part of the game starts; you need to start all over again. Yes, you're still a part of your faction and sometimes you get to keep a party member, but in general you're left all on your own again. Rebuild your army and try again. Unfortunately, I found with time, building new armies was hard; especially when your faction's constantly telling you to help them in battle and complain when you don't because you'll lose all your men, again.
If you're looking to take over the world a'la civilization, without the sophistication, Warband will work. Just expect it to take a couple hundred hours first, to get started.

Is this game better than all previous numbered Dirt (and CMR) games? Definitely! But is it better than Dirt Rally? Well...
Handling: You all probably know from those toxic players on forums about the grip being a bit too grippy on gravel surface compared to Dirt Rally. Yes, that's really true, but it's not as bad as they are saying, and I really whouldn't say that they made it more arcade. You just have to tune your car properly and everything will feel a lot better. Terrible default rally cars setups are really the only (quite big) downsides of Dirt 4's handling model. There are definitely a lot of improvements as well. Cars don't feel like they are filled with hellium anymore, braking distance is longer and the car is pretty much uncontrollable once you lock your wheels. Tarmac handling is much better (it was terrible in DR since V2 handling came out), rallycross handling was also improved a lot, buggies and trucks are fun and really hard to control with their massive oversteer, etc... all in all the handling in Dirt 4 is a lot different, but not at all bad. Terrible default setups are easy to fix, so let's hope that Codemasters will petch them later.
Visuals: Well it's definitely not very eye candy game, but I find visuals a bit better than in Dirt Rally. Especially the lighting was improved and it's also more colorful and crispier (you can finally turn off motion blur). Cars definitely look better, as well as crowd next to the roads. But on the other hand it's also much more demanding on ultra settings. I had to lower some settings from ultra to high to get steady 60 FPS on my GTX 970.
Sound: Just incredible. Codemasters outdone themselves again. Car sounds are absolutely perfect, there are even more sounds that weren't present in Dirt Rally, especially when you damage something (grinding noise of damaged gearbox, flapping wheel after puncture, etc), and the soundtrack is also great, just like in previous Dirt games. Well not as good as in Dirt Showdown, but still a lot of great tracks to listen to during replays.
Career and Team management: A big improvement over all previous Dirt games. They finally separated all disciplines and you can freely choose whichever mode you want to drive at the moment. There is no need to complete a landrush race to unlock new rally stage anymore. They added podium finishes, workshop, improved the car upgrade and repairing system over the simplistic D:R model. Team management was also massively improved over Dirt Rally. Now you can create your own team, make your own car liveries, buy bigger garage for more cars, hire PR guy, choose sponsors, etc...
Your Stage: Well I had to update this part after 40 hours of playtime. Previously I praised how great it is, that the game is not limited to just a few stages, etc...  but now, after those 40 hours, I find it really lackluster. There are only a few blocks of tracks that are repeating themselves constantly, and not just during the championship, but even during one single stage! Srsly, rally in Dirt 4 is one big DejaVu moment after another. I was defending Your Stage with words like "It's still better than having just two stages per location", but nope, it really isn't.
Conclusion: (Had to change this previously overwhelmingly positive part as well) Yes, it's true that they improved a lot of things over Dirt Rally, but they also managed to make Dirt 4 rally part less entertaining than Dirt Rally. I have played DR for 240 hours at the time of writing this review and I am still enjoying it quite a lot. But when it comes to Dirt 4, I am pretty sure that once I complete Career mode, I will not be coming back since Your Stage is a big disappointment. Yes, rallycross, buggies and trucks are a lot of fun, but those will not entertain you for a long time, since there are only a handful of tracks for each mode (not to mention that 3 out of 5 tracks for rallycross are just ported from DR). I am still recommending this game, since it is a big improvement over all previous numbered Dirt games. But while improving a lot of things even over Dirt Rally, they downgraded rally part of the game a lot. Your Stage has a potential, but they will need to improve it A LOT to make it entertaining without constantly repeating the same sections over and over and over again...

Hitboxes are wonky. (Torso 1-Hitkills, Headshots sometimes not working, etc.)
The above lag can ruin shots and close action, mostly because the game crams over 1,200 people onto a server.

Bullets don't go through 2-inch thick walls

I recommend only because the game is in early access. If this was a full game, I do not think it would fit the title of a "full game."

In truth, it is like neither of these games.
Except perhaps in that you're playing a military-ish squad of dudes with a variety of weapons and tools available.
You drag your cursor to tell your individual dudes where to go, not to directly move them, the idea is that you're setting a plan (or altering a plan as needed) and then your SWAT team members execute that plan, shooting at any evildoers along the way. And you can only see what your squad can see via line-of-sight, which means controlling the direction your dudes are facing is of equal importance; it works nothing like most shooters, most of the real gameplay is in the planning stage (in my opinion at least; you actually can play it by ear with some degree of success but you'll almost never get a perfect run doing it that way)
Reminded me a lot of Hotline Miami (1), in that, you're gonna screw up a lot, you're gonna swear nigh incoherently A LOT, but somehow still manages to be really really fun, and when you pull off a perfect mission its like SCREW YOU I AM THE SUPERIOR MIND (after failing it to comedic effect 9000 times first). And the fact that restarting and trying again takes next to no time at all, which is good because if you had to watch even a short loading screen every time you restart a mission it'd get tedious real fast.
Lots of content, and if it isn't enough for you somehow, full Workshop Support (new maps, skins, guns, FULL support). And a mission generator, which I'm pretty sure everyone uses to cheap some achievements but I've heard it can also generate actual fun missions of whatever difficulty you like (which can be refreshing after you run out of interesting racial slurs to let loose after you've done something marvelously stupid and screwed up an otherwise perfect run on a really hard mission)

I missed the Left 4 Dead train as it left the station.
L4D2 was my first experience with the series. I played through it once and didn't ever go back. This game has a similar concept in that you'll run through a mission with 4 players (bots will fill in for missing people but they suck) who each have their own strengths and weaknesses. Many comparisons have been made between the two games, but I thought I'd specify that I have little experience with the L4D series, while still acknowledging the similarities.
Gameplay is tight. Overall the game runs smoothly; things work as you would expect, and there aren't any drops in framerate even while streaming. The melee combat is visceral. Swinging an axe feels as it should. Blocking with a shield and then swinging it at your attackers to knock them down is very satisfying. Rapiers are quick and nimble. 2-handed weapons are slow yet powerful. This isn't rocket science, but it feels right. Ranged combat is equally tight control-wise, but seems less effective in most cases. Crossbows are slow to reload, but pistols/shotguns and long bows feel much better. The ranged abilities coming from staves are very effective at range.
The variety of Skaven is nice. Not only are there differing skins for the regular grunts, there are various types that are bigger and badder than their normal counterparts. Fighting a Rat Ogre for the first time was a magical experience. The armored Stormvermin come in packs and are tough to take down. The gunners, hook rats and assassins are a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ as are the poison cloud creating globe-throwers. There's no lack of challenge either. Normal difficulty still takes its toll, and the hard difficulty is almost too hard, at least at the lower levels with crappy gear. But there's a couple of extra difficulty levels that I haven't even seen yet, so there's going to be plenty of replay value in this game.
As is common with most first person shooters of this era, you have a global experience level. The interesting bit here is that it's not tied directly to any of the game's five classes, so you don't have to level each individually. Each level you're rewarded with some gear, but each time it's for a different class, so none are completely left out. Also, when completing a level, there is a dice game where you get the chance to earn better gear. The devs chose to keep with the traditional Diablo/MMO formula of color coding rarity, and so far the best I've come up with is a some blues. Each time you level or dice roll, the gear can end up being for any of the classes, so that's a nice way of avoiding an annoying individual grind. Gear is primarily weapons, though there are slots for trinkets, and you can change out your helmet, though I haven't seen any of these drop just yet. You can also find extra loot dies and collect tomes for extra dice that will help with your end-of-level rolls. At the very least, this system gives quite a bit of replay value if you're the sort that wants to completely kit out your characters (I am).
After each level and dice game, you'll have the option to vote for what comes next. You can replay the same level, move onto the next or go back to the Red Hook Inn, where you start your journey in the first place. Here you can access your inventory (swap out weapons and gear) the mission map (where you can choose which level to play next) and access the forge - a powerful tool. The forge allows you to fuse, upgrade and disassemble items. Fusing requires five items of the same quality, and combines them into one item of the next quality up (5 whites = 1 green and so on). Weapons earned from the dice game often have locked traits that you can unlock in the forge, upgrading the weapon with passives. These upgrades require essences earned by disassembling items. It's a basic system but it works well and I have seen some decent stuff come out of it.
The recent free DLC "Sigmar's Blessing" has also added a shrine and new trinkets so that you can "pray" for new items using the colored tokens you get from breaking down unused gear. You can be specific and choose melee or ranged weapons, and the particular character you want the gear for. This helps cut down on the grind a bit, and is particularly nice if you only play one or a couple of the characters with any regularity.
Overall, I love the game. It's been compared to Left 4 Dead, and I can say that it has a similar feel, though these small systematic upgrades give it a better replay value than L4D did, and the devs have already stated that more levels and classes are yet to come. I'll be playing and talking about this game for a while to come.

AdventureQuest 3D is so far innovated for a concept that should be simple, Cross-Platform gaming.
To remind people of what Cross-Platform gaming is here's a short summary.
Have a friend playing on Android? but you play on PC, fear no more all you need to do is log on to the same server and play.
Nothing will change except somebody will be stuck with Touch Controls while you use Keyboard and Mouse.
I love the concept of Cross-Platform games because it unite people no matter what platform they prefer, that's why I think AdventureQuest 3D is interesting so far.
Now time to touch more features.
Gameplay: This is a very very barebone MMORPG, there is no Skilltree for this game you only get 4 moves no matter what class you chosen. There's a simple crafting system very easy to understand, downside is you got to wait until the item done crafting.
There are 4 classes (Warrior) (Mage) (Rouge) (Guardian) This game class system is kinda disappointing with the classes so far. also quick note the Guardian class require you to buy a membership type of deal.
Combat is also very simple since you can only use 4 attack I don't think I should spoil the surprise of the combat.
All you need to know is the game is Real Time Combat not turn-base or anything bizarre.
Graphics/visual: Don't expect this game to compete with new games in term of graphics, everything look very simple but you got to remember this game can't be very advance because that will cause problem for the mobile users.

It was snowy, me and my buddies were in a forest. On our way to occupty a lumber camp, that wasn't too far from our FOB. We walked through the forest, completely aware of our surroundings, with our hands and butts freezing cause it was too cold. It was quiet for a moment, until suddenly we get ambushed by Germans.
Me and the guys dig in quick as possible, our pointman screams out "RETURN FIRE!". We clash in a lenghty firefight, until the Germans had gotten the upper hand with an MG-42.
We were being suppressed and we knew that we had to retreat back to our FOB, we were all shaken and scattered around the forest. A few guys tried to retreat back but were shot down by the MG-42 before they could even stand up and run.
One of the guys in patrol who was next to me popped a smoke infront of the Germans POV so they couldn't see us, he then grabbed me and said "Come on, we gotta move!". We tried running back to FOB, under heavy fire from MG's and rifles, we ran and ran, we were tired and exhausted. I took a hit on my foot causing me to trip and fall down onto the ground. The guy behind me tried to get me up before he took a fatal hit to the chest. I continued my retreat towards the FOB, a few minutes later, I found myself wandering in the forest, alone, no weapon, no ammo pouches.
Until a German popped up infront of me, he aims his rifle at me, but doesn't shoot. We both looked at eachother, I stood infront of him unarmed and he was infront of me with his rifle aimed at me. From the look of his face, I could tell that he was afraid, confused and tired, just a normal human being sent out to fight.
I take one step forward and *BOOM* I fell on the ground, bleeding out and slowly losing breath as I watch the snow cover my body...

Oh goodness where to begin.
Hotline Miami the original had this absolutely bonkers plotline involving the main character - Jacket - just going in and killing people because a phone told him too. There was also a pretty awesome retro aestetic to it too which might lead to seizures.
Hotline Miami 2 is an altogether different beast. It's more of the same (especially since it was originally meant to be a DLC followup to the last game) but at the same time it's more. There are more enemy types, more NPCs, more dialogue, more plot, more gameplay, more awesome music, and a lot more frustration too. If you haven't played Hotline Miami the original yet or haven't played it in a while, do so now. Just do it, trust me on this, then read on. Or read on and then play the original. I'm not your mom.
The plot of this game takes place a couple years after the original, there's also more cutscenes and dialogue (a majority of it skippable if you load the level from the level select sequence first). But it skips around a lot, makes absolutely no sense, and won't be entirely satisfying, though satisfying enough all the same. Don't worry too much about it, it may take you a few playthroughs, notes, and help to piece it together. The answers are all there. Sorta.
Following up that whole "more of everything" thing, the levels are bigger and harder too. Enemies can and will shoot you off screen meaning if you don't have a good grasp of a level you can spend upwards to 30 minutes just trying to make it through a three minute level. This game's hard, and it gets right into that difficulty from the beginning. Basically, this is a sequel that you REALLY shouldn't skip the original to play, despite looking and sounding REALLY awesome.
So I guess whether or not I recommend Hotline Miami to you - random person - is whether or not you can answer these questions:
1. Did you like the original game?
2. Do you want to play MORE of the original?
3. Do you want it to be more difficult?
4. Do you want it to be more varied?
If you can answer yes to at least three of these, then this is the game for you. If you said yes to two of these, then maybe wait for a sale. If you answered yes to all four, then stop reading this review and pick this game up. Just do it. I'm your mom now, and I'm telling you that you want this game. Don't question it, you'll be too wrapped up trying to figure this game out to think about anything else. And dying a lot. Seriously, game's ♥♥♥♥ing hard.

While not the worst game in the franchise (looking at you Infinite Warfare) Ghosts isn't necessarily the worst either. The single player campaign is solid with the plot of your typical cheesy action movie; it's dumb explosion-y fun with your typical over-the-top action sequences. The Extinction co-op mode is surprisingly fun (Solo is pretty difficult, but doable) with a move and defend the point kind of playstyle. The only real downside is the multiplayer. In my opinion, Ghosts came with some of the worst multiplayer maps in a long time. Alongside the drab color palate, enimies tend to blend into the maps making it extra frustrating when you die to that guys that's just sitting in a corner (which the poor map designs tend to encourage a camping playstyle).
Overall, if you like CoD for the Single player and Co-op modes, it's definitely worth picking up (on sale). However, if you're more interested in the multiplayer, I'd pass (still has a small community playing though). You can typically find the game and season pass for like $30 on HumbleBundle during holiday sales, so if you're interested in picking it up, you may want to consider grabbing it then.

The pace of this game is painfully slow, and it's a lot of grinding for money and soldiers after losing all your soldiers and being enslaved after a risky all-or-nothing battle. Just to be chased down by a leveled enemy and starting over again. Graphics have an indie feel in combat and a computer board-game feel otherwise. Gameplay is repetitive with a lot of waiting and frustration.
Now that I got that out of the way, this game is a game changer in the realm of Medieval RPGs. The hand-to-hand combat system is the best that I've seen in medieval combat games (Elder Scrolls should learn from this). Battles can be epically large and intense. And at the same time, you're commanding your own army! How cool is that!?! And you get to seige castles and shi+! Commands are sophisticated but quicky become muscle memory, so multi-tasking isn't a real issue. I'm really looking forward to Mount & Blade 2, which seems like it's arm-deep in development. Meanwhile, you should play this game!

After playing Chivarly I figured there wasn't another medieval sword game I wanted to play. I tried Mount & Blade and do not regret purchasing it.
The reason why I support this game is it tried to take a different approach to gaming. From the user interface (UI) to the actual game play. I'll start with the story in which the game asks you questions in what type of adventurer you are (merchant's son, nobles son, peasants son etc...). From that it gives you a set of attribute points and allows you to add a few extras before you begin the game. I'd like to add that the creator(s) of this game added a great feature which makes exploring the world as well as the towns/castles a lot easier. Pressing select (or some keyboard button I'm not familiar with yet) while in a city/town/village allows for quick options to pop up (which means quick travel). You need to go to the tavern? Boom use your controller to choose it. Need to hit up the noble's hall? Boom hit select and use your joystick to select it. Wanna leave town? No problem. Because of this - the game by itself is notable.
The game starts with you on a horse on a overhead map you can zoom in or out on. From this screen (which is paused unless you decide to move your character), you can view notes of mission logs, party stats, inventory and so on. This by itself adds an extra dimension to the game.
There is a lot to do in the game and factions you can side with. You can pledge allegiance to a faction (by approaching the king) and you can start asking for titles of land/castles or become the marshal and lead the king's armies. You can go at it by yourself but it's quite difficult as a faction can start swarming you. The player goes around asking nobles if there is any tasks you can do for them. Sometimes they ask you to pillage villages of other factions to start a war or a fight. Some tell you to go collect their rent. Along the way you may run into interesting characters (doctors, mercenaries, vagabonds) that would be interested in joining your battle party. Individual soldiers can be upgraded and given roles (such as cavalry, archers, footmen etc...). Those vagabonds also can be upgraded to your needs, such as if you want someone to be a good engineer you can focus on that and then have another person focus on training your units. To recruit soldiers you need to go around to villages and attempt to recruit from there. As the game progresses so do what the factions do - meaning villages can be looted by other factions or just renegades. Renegades can also chase you around if you are not careful. You beat them you can win some cool things, lose though and you might become a prisoner for them.
Fighting in this game is somewhat comparable to chivalry. You need to be facing in the right direction in order to block or get a hit. Like chiv though, it will take practice to figure out how to properly attack and defend. There is no shortage of variety when it comes to armor, horses, crossbows, longbows, swords, pikes, spears etc... There are tournaments that you are eligible to enter at certain times if not you may enter the arena and go spar (and make some money depending how you guys you knock out). After a battle you can also (depending on your prisoner capacity level) hold prisoners. You can ransom them off in taverns and it is a good way of making money.

My opinion.
The audience for contagion is and always was limited:
Players today are use to tripping over ammo/health, auto save/quick save features and a minimap. Challenge frustrates/bores these types of gamers. Not saying we are all this way but there certainly is a percentage of this type. I have heard many people complain, especially on barlow and biotech escape, that the game sucks because they are not being spoon fed where to go next. Contagion involves some degree of thought and their are a number of people in this world that are unable and unwilling to use their minds.
A trolls paradise:
The escape game mode is one of if not the most popular game mode... and its a trolls paradise. From TKers, to Griefers, to Trolls. This completely ruins a new players experience and in many cases pushes seasoned players away also. While vote kick would be a bad solution its a very poor excuse not to have addressed this problem. There are system that could be built to improve this aspect. Even a "report player" option from in game would do a great deal to improve this situation... yet, here we are YEARS later and nothing has been done. The devs wont even put the current precepts for reporting a troll into an easy to create thread and sticky that thread so the community has the knowledge and tools to police itself.
No friends allowed:
Playing with your friends in an online co-op game should have been a major consideration but players are forced to jump though port forwarding hoops to play exclusively with their friends. This becomes an even bigger problem when a seasoned player tries to introduce a new player to the game and has no place to do it. Mix in a bit of trolling and its hard to get friends and family excited about this title. Yet again this is a problem that is just now, supposedly, being addressed after YEARS of stagnation.
Poor Server Diversity
There once was a time when we had map and game mode specific servers. If you wanted to play the police station on escape hard all night long you could do that on one of the hundreds of official servers. At the time I repeatedly asked for a Biotech-Escape-Server (if even just one) I was ignored and now we have even less server diversity than we had in the past. Hundreds of servers with only slight variations.
Poor Stability
On both the client side and the server side this build of the game is NOT stable. Too often you get into a great game with a bunch of great players only to crash yourself or have the server crash and dump everyone. Depending on time invested at that point many players just sign off in frustration. This has been reported over and over again without any official recognition of the issue.
Bugs, Bugs and more bugs.
Not only are their a number of bugs... they are never addressed. With the new DLC 6 months ago there are now more bugs than ever.
-Holiday content 6 months after Christmas
-Poor zombie pathing, stuck zombies and dead spots
-Zombies that AOE attack when agroing doors.
-Zombie that hurt you through doors and
-Doors that insta explode if a opened on a zombie?
-Doors that get stuck partway
-Sights/accessories that disappear from the Remington shotgun
-Shotguns that ghost fire 2 rounds when only actually shooting one projectile.
-Hang on round restart bug on some of the escape maps
-Bleeding ceilings
-Doors that are not able to be interacted with for seemingly no reason.
-Zombies that starve to death once they get stuck
-Textures and Assets that don't load correctly
Now we were told that after the DLC we would return to regular updates which many of us interpreted to mean regular patches like way back in the day. This position is now said to mean regular updates as in posts but even that is not being done. GW was introduced to this community as the new voice of monochrome. He promised to update us regularly on the progress the team is making and as of today has not made a single post on progress. He is either bad at his job or their is no progress to report. Monochrome wont confirm one or the other.
Bad or Lacking Mechanics
-Gun bashing is worthless, it should be used as a way to either pin a single zombie or to try and keep 2 or 3 zombies at bay hoping hoping to kill a 4th before it reaches you or have players kill them while your the bait. Instead it serves to merely annoy a zombie before it hits you.
-Zombies do not have weapon-specific deaths, so you don't have satisfying finishers on enemies when you use a shotgun or use certain melee weapons, They just sort of faint in slowmo after headshots.
-Zombies do not try and bite you. They don't grab you, instead they just flail at you hopelessly until you die. It would have been good for a NMRiH style struggle to get a zombie off you in time, the more injured you are the more difficult it would be for a tense surprise encounter.
And that leaves me to the final problem. Broken promises, twisted words, and possible lies. No one knows why contagion is not being worked on other than the developers. Its clear we are not returning to regular updates. No progress is being reported and many of us suspect they have broken their assurance that the development of Project Ageless will not affect the development of contagion. People do not like being disrespected in this manner and it has created a very negative community. One can only make positive suggestions and be ignored so many times before they just go on the attack. This feeling in the community is also driving players away.

This game has been on my wishlist for two holiday sales. Since I usually don't buy any "wargames" or straight up shooters I was hesitant to buy it, but finally gave in, when it was 50% off, thinking what's there to loose with the steam refund system?
To my astonishment, it's a "simple" strategy game and that's just up my alley.
Plan your way in with your squad, level them up, get new equipment and defuse dangerous situations: rescue hostages, defuse bombs, kill hostiles, save the day.
The game itselfs has a huge amount of levels out of the box and with a superb workshop integration can be expanded indefinitely by community made levels and items. It's also really, really easy to make your own maps as a level editor is already integrated int the game. If you don't want to make anything too fancy (new texture, objects, round rooms) you'll be extremely happy with the in-game options for designing new levels.
It really is a steal for any price (if you're looking at this review and the game is also 50% off, don't hesitate and just get it!)
Here's the checklist of what you can expect:
PROs:
+ huge amount of levels
+ great replayability (play with different squad members, play with different equipment, play from different entry-zones...)
+ adequate learning-curve (easy levels to get used to the mechanics)
+ ability to play any level at any chosen time (no unlocking levels, everything is available right from the start, though not every level is a good idea to play right away)
+ controls are great with and uncluttered and handy interface
+ squad members can be renamed and given their own design
+ great steam workshop integration
+ integrated level editor
+ price for what you get is absolutely adequate
+ replay ability from almost any starting point within a level
CONs:
- campaign mode needs better warning for what happens to killed squad members (once you've figured it out though, you'll remember forever)
- not all stats on items are relevant when equipped
Overall: 8/10

I missed the Left 4 Dead train as it left the station.
L4D2 was my first experience with the series. I played through it once and didn't ever go back. This game has a similar concept in that you'll run through a mission with 4 players (bots will fill in for missing people but they suck) who each have their own strengths and weaknesses. Many comparisons have been made between the two games, but I thought I'd specify that I have little experience with the L4D series, while still acknowledging the similarities.
Gameplay is tight. Overall the game runs smoothly; things work as you would expect, and there aren't any drops in framerate even while streaming. The melee combat is visceral. Swinging an axe feels as it should. Blocking with a shield and then swinging it at your attackers to knock them down is very satisfying. Rapiers are quick and nimble. 2-handed weapons are slow yet powerful. This isn't rocket science, but it feels right. Ranged combat is equally tight control-wise, but seems less effective in most cases. Crossbows are slow to reload, but pistols/shotguns and long bows feel much better. The ranged abilities coming from staves are very effective at range.
The variety of Skaven is nice. Not only are there differing skins for the regular grunts, there are various types that are bigger and badder than their normal counterparts. Fighting a Rat Ogre for the first time was a magical experience. The armored Stormvermin come in packs and are tough to take down. The gunners, hook rats and assassins are a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ as are the poison cloud creating globe-throwers. There's no lack of challenge either. Normal difficulty still takes its toll, and the hard difficulty is almost too hard, at least at the lower levels with crappy gear. But there's a couple of extra difficulty levels that I haven't even seen yet, so there's going to be plenty of replay value in this game.
As is common with most first person shooters of this era, you have a global experience level. The interesting bit here is that it's not tied directly to any of the game's five classes, so you don't have to level each individually. Each level you're rewarded with some gear, but each time it's for a different class, so none are completely left out. Also, when completing a level, there is a dice game where you get the chance to earn better gear. The devs chose to keep with the traditional Diablo/MMO formula of color coding rarity, and so far the best I've come up with is a some blues. Each time you level or dice roll, the gear can end up being for any of the classes, so that's a nice way of avoiding an annoying individual grind. Gear is primarily weapons, though there are slots for trinkets, and you can change out your helmet, though I haven't seen any of these drop just yet. You can also find extra loot dies and collect tomes for extra dice that will help with your end-of-level rolls. At the very least, this system gives quite a bit of replay value if you're the sort that wants to completely kit out your characters (I am).
After each level and dice game, you'll have the option to vote for what comes next. You can replay the same level, move onto the next or go back to the Red Hook Inn, where you start your journey in the first place. Here you can access your inventory (swap out weapons and gear) the mission map (where you can choose which level to play next) and access the forge - a powerful tool. The forge allows you to fuse, upgrade and disassemble items. Fusing requires five items of the same quality, and combines them into one item of the next quality up (5 whites = 1 green and so on). Weapons earned from the dice game often have locked traits that you can unlock in the forge, upgrading the weapon with passives. These upgrades require essences earned by disassembling items. It's a basic system but it works well and I have seen some decent stuff come out of it.
The recent free DLC "Sigmar's Blessing" has also added a shrine and new trinkets so that you can "pray" for new items using the colored tokens you get from breaking down unused gear. You can be specific and choose melee or ranged weapons, and the particular character you want the gear for. This helps cut down on the grind a bit, and is particularly nice if you only play one or a couple of the characters with any regularity.
Overall, I love the game. It's been compared to Left 4 Dead, and I can say that it has a similar feel, though these small systematic upgrades give it a better replay value than L4D did, and the devs have already stated that more levels and classes are yet to come. I'll be playing and talking about this game for a while to come.

I have played the GC version for my entire life, so after getting the HD PC port of this i gotta mention three things:
1.They ripped off some features in the game that should be part of the base game (Chao karate, for one)
2.These ripped features can be attainable within the DLC, that you need to buy additionally
3. The 'optional' DLC is required in order to collect ALL the emblems within the game.
in other words, you can't finish the game or even enjoy it to the fullest extent without coughing up an extra couple of bucks or cents (if it goes on sale)

Don't be led astray by the primitive graphics, Warband more than makes up for it in gameplay. Many games claim to tailor the story to your decisions and to a degree, they do; but the end result is more often than not the same and the choices you make don't really affect anything. Warband, on the other hand, doesn't have a linear story at all. The story you'll find in Warband you must find out for yourself; if you're like me, you can ignore everything about it and just play the game. The story really doesn't matter. No two games are the same. Your goal is to rule the world, either as its king or as a member of the faction that does it. Of course, the latter could be considered easier, but you'll find that even taking over one other faction will take many dozens of hours.
You could treat Warband as a battlefield simulator, the massive fights between hundreds of soldiers on each side are glorious. However, you do need to figure out the little tricks to the game to really figure out how to win. For example, in the beginning of one of my playthroughs I had made my entire army into bowmen and continued upgrading them along that path. No bandits could touch me, the early siege I took part in was simple and I only lost a few men, in general; I wasn't worried about dying much. Then, heavy soldiers came; on horseback no less. The arrows couldn't pierce the armor of the three soldiers well enough and the horses ensured my men couldn't get away. Fifty crossbowmen, and myself, gone in a matter of minutes to three heavy soldiers. The rest of the army didn't even get to me before that could happen. Unfortunately, this is where the frustrating part of the game starts; you need to start all over again. Yes, you're still a part of your faction and sometimes you get to keep a party member, but in general you're left all on your own again. Rebuild your army and try again. Unfortunately, I found with time, building new armies was hard; especially when your faction's constantly telling you to help them in battle and complain when you don't because you'll lose all your men, again.
If you're looking to take over the world a'la civilization, without the sophistication, Warband will work. Just expect it to take a couple hundred hours first, to get started.

Interesting TD concept with mediocre realization!
First of all, I was very skeptical when I downloaded this game, because it looks... not good at all. After I played a little I confirmed my thoughts, this game has a low quality visuals, but I also found some interesting features.
The story is simple and unnecessary. You came to planet and found hostile aborigines. You task is moving to the centre of planet and cleaning enemy forces. Nothing extraordinary!
The most interesting part for me was the tech tree for towers. You have 2 basic tower: a depot for marines and a techlab. Each one has 3 upgrades. For example for outpost you can research 1) +1 marine (equal +50% dps); 2) grenade throw ability; 3) Training, which increases attack range by 40%. After you research any of upgrades, new towers unlocks.
+1 marine unlocks the barracks, which puts marines on the road. Training unlocks the outpost tower with better damage and attack range.
Each new tower has 3 upgrades too. 2 of them lead to new towers. New towers save  upgrades which were only before them. It means tower lose grenade throw ability if you gone with "Training" path. It's really interesting to unlock new towers and make decisions which tower needs all side upgrades and which one needs to be upgraded to next tier. This is the first TD game with such mechanics, so only because of it I gave the game a positive review. Because, it was fun... for the first couple of hours.
But the game have a lot of negative sides. The filling of waves are boring, monsters and their abilities are usual. I think the balance of towers is average too. I found some of them are owerpowered and some totally useless.
Pros
- Interesting concept of techtree for towers
- Skill tree. You get stars for completing levels which could be spent on different 16 passive skills
- No bugs was found
- Cheap
Cons
- Poor visuals and animations
- Boring enemies with usual abilities
- Boss fight are extremely disappointing
- Game becomes monotonous after the ~10 missions
- Balance issues
