I will give this game a huge thumbs up, and I definitely recommend it to people who have the patience for early access games and enjoy a relaxed survival experience solo or with your buddies. I am able to look past the bugs and focus on the gameplay, but I will objectively address the bugs after a quick overview. My friend and I started off and had a blast messing around, building a ship and getting lost at sea for a few hours. It was absolutely fantastic having a fishing contest, shoot sharks, talking and pretending to be castaways documenting our time aboard our ship. That moment when we saw land for the first time in ages was a particularly memorable experience. I think the wildlife AI is good, though the ability to tame would be nice. I think we could use more creatures, but that isn't very urgent. The sea is quite barren of life, though. You guys aced the plant life! I love it to pieces! I love the variety, the practical applications and the look it gives. There is a lot of time for players to advance into different "time periods" and that is definitely cool. Ships are awesome, though for something that is so central to the gameplay I do think that more types, sizes, and uses are needed. I think the hull should be hollow for maximum space. Now for some bugs that need to be addressed. Though I personally am able to look past them, they are present and can get quite annoying and I know that some players will not tolerate any trace of bugs, even in early access. Here they are:
1. Putting a chair on a ship and then sitting on it will send the ship spinning around, flying up in the air and/or sinking underwater unpredictably.
2. Walking around on a ship tips it over too much. I think that it is a good touch, but it is over dramatic. I'll walk from one end to the other (horizontally) and the thing will start tipping almost vertically and sometimes flip.
3. My friend complained many times of not being able to see entities like trees, items on the floor, chests, furniture, plants etc.
4. I am sure this was mentioned several times, but when starting a world, the recipe for the Saw and Anvil do not appear even when materials are in the inventory. It requires restarting the game.
5. Firing a gun at a predatory animal (bear, wolf, etc.) when out of their agro-range sometimes does not do damage to them or even provoke them
6. Rain and snow penetrate walls, roofs, and furniture
7. I'm not sure if this is a bug or not, but if I fell a tree and it falls on me, another player or an animal that entity does not take damage. The tree falls straight through them...
- Ships appear to be suffering the most bugs.
Those are all the major bugs I noticed thus far, and I will be more than happy to edit my review as these issues are fixed, and also expand the list if need be. I created this list out of genuine desire for them to be fixed, not angrily and as blind criticism.
Some other things I would like to see added from the game include tamable animals, less barren oceans (maybe more animals, shipwrecks, sunken treasure, etc.). Maybe dolphins, whales, fish, mantas, rays, crabs, eels etc.
I also think that airships and floating islands, flying whales, more birds and a whole world up above would be really cool.
- Something that I think is an absolute priority in terms of adding is a better spawning mechanism. I am aware that you don't want to make dying inconsequential, but the current status is totally frustrating and will alienate many players. Likewise, dying out at sea is way too unforgiving. How am I supposed to get my stuff back? I'm basically better off starting completely from scratch (which happened on two occurrences).
- Another thing that should be high on the list is adding more danger. There is no danger save for the unfortunate encounter with a hostile carnivore. Nighttime is just annoying as opposed to a challenge and that needs some work. The main point is that the game currently lacks any active dangers.
- The food system seems incomplete; there are many different kinds of food but it is not apparent that any is superior to the other. I can eat a fish or a few mushrooms and be fine. It feels empty...
- This is slightly controversial, but what if there was a thirst system?
- Add-ons to mounts (of which I think we need more of, by the way) like saddles, saddlebags, armor, etc.
By the way, I absolutely love the music and sound effects! They are incredible.

this game is great, the story is told in a non chronological order and is very engrossing as it ties into the first game and its story going further into the identity of beard and exploring the character jake's storyline which i found to be quite interesting. you are also introduced to manny pardo a police officer with a dark secret (that you will discover if you play the game) who is trying to hunt down a serial killer the police force is calling the miami mutilator (inspired by an actual serical killer active in miami in the late 80's and i believe early 90's when the game is moslty set). it also shows the player jacket before his 50 blessings incident where he fights alongside beard in a war against the russians in hawaii, this is another very interesting area of the story and helps add variety to the gameplay (you do play as beard however which is a nice touch). you are also introduced to the fans, copycat killers of jacket and other 50 blessings assassins.
when you play through the second game it feels like you are experiencing a story that had been planned out since the birth of hotline miami's first chapter.
gameplay in this game is also amazing. there is an improved lock on system and a lot of the scenes (missions) do not have a mask selection screen at the start (only the ones where you play as the fans or jake) they have a gun selection screen for beard in the war, cosmetic modifiers that grant abilities for son who i actually forgot to mention, he is the son of the russian mob boss you killed in the first game and has quite an interesting storyline, no selection screens are present for other characters, you also can get a shotgun out of your boot when playing as pardo in one level.
you can sometimes be shot from outside the boundries of your screen in some cases when you do not use the look mechanic effectively which can be irritating and there are also a few bugs i got mostly minor, excecpt for one which i only saw happen in hard mode where some enemies could walk through walls and completely butcher you, very annoying. the graphcs are good for a game made on the gamemaker engine with detailed environments and good effects when shooting or when something explodes e.g NUKE!
the presentation of this game is amazing with a brilliant techno soundtrack to carry you through the levels and somethig comparable to the hitchcock effect where your mind fills in what is not detailed in the action in this game letting your imagination run loose as you picture a guy with a shotgun running around a building gunning people down and smashing there heads against the ground, for that reason i would say this game is probably more violent (from my perspective) that something like gta or postal 2 (postal 3 was♥♥♥♥♥♥so... yeah).
overall i would give this game a 9.8 or a 9.9 out of ten as it is held back by some bugs but still remains as an amazing experience with a fair bit of replayability with its hard mode where levels are flipped and more enemies and more challenging enemies are added, i have completed both hard and normal mode.
so yes this game is one of the greatest games i have played in a long time and is as good if not better then the excellent hotline miami 1!

This game is, to put it lightly, very deep.
You begin the game by answering some questions about your character's past: what their parents were, what they did in their youth, their job, and why they left. These questions affect your starting stats, and could give you a early path to nobility. That is if you even decide that nobility is the route you want to take.
Let's take a moment to talk about the "goal" of the game.
There isn't one. The game never says "Congratulations! You've won!" The closest thing you can get to "winning" is taking over the known world.
If I had to pick one flaw in the game's design, it would be that the game throws you in, and expects you to hit the ground running. Once you finish making your character, what you do is up to you. Want to join a faction? Do it. Want to be a merchant? Do it. Want to lead a rebellion? Do it. Want to be a bandit? Do it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

A little late to the party here, but here's my review:
Volume is a functional stealth game, and that's the most complimentary thing I can say about it. There's nothing here that hasn't been done better in other games, and I see no reason to play this game over any of the other excellent stealth offerings on Steam. The presenation and visuals are bland, and the level design isn't creative. It never felt like I was being challenged, or being provided with a set of tools which I could use in a way I wanted, as opposed to a specific way that the game was designed for.
The worst part of the game for me was the voice acting, which is atrocious and KEEPS. ON. GOING. Whoever wrote the dialogue needs an editor, badly. On top of that, if you pause the game when a clip of dialogue is playing, the entire clip starts playing again, which is the annoying cherry on the♥♥♥♥♥♥cake.
If you're really desperate and this is the last stealth game on Steam, then maybe buy this when it's dirt cheap. Otherwise, play anything else instead.

Unfortunately, the game turned into an unplayable, stuttering mess as time went on and I could not figure out the cause. Lowered settings, uncapped framerate, windowed mode, and making it the only running program did nothing for the performance. Temperatures, memory, and CPU usage appeared to be normal too.
Other games run normally.
For reference:
Windows 10 64-bit
GTX 970 v378.66
16GB of RAM
As for the game itself, I did not like the disjointed storytelling, the writing for the protagonist that tries to be a regular guy, or the level design which felt rigid. The latter is probably due to the game leaning much more towards the puzzling side versus stealth (at least for the first 41 levels or so). Don't expect varied approaches in the manner of Deus Ex, MGS, Dishonored, or Sniper Elite 4. Jumping over walls was also disorienting and I didn't like the camera motion. The abstract art style also didn't help me connect with the world or characters.
On the bright side, the game presents the player with 100 campaign levels to solve and offers even more with player generated content. If you're able to run it without trouble, you could end up spending a good chunk of time on all those levels. There are also leaderboards for time-to-completion which is always fun, especially since the levels are relatively short (several minutes or so for some later ones depending on your speed). The soundtrack has a pleasant ambient quality to it and amps up whenever you're seen. I thought it to be quite good. You'll hear plenty of strings, let me tell ya.
Regrettably, due to the technical problems I experienced, I'm unable to recommend the game.

Played every Codemaster rally game, mostly loved them all. I feel that in 2017, there're still way too many compromises in a lot of aspects. I want to recommend it really bad, but I can't get over the frustrating things. It's not as joyful and easily approachable as previous DiRT <number> games, yet it's not DiRT Rally either. Could've been both of them, but is none of them.
PROS
- I really like the singleplayer features, the custom team liveries, management, progress, joyride
- Car selection is great
- Tracks look awesome and alive
- You don't grind upgrades for every car for the whole eternity, you just buy them if you have the correct R&D!
CONS
- AI is completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and will try to erase you from the planet Earth anytime you go near it.
- The "realistic" driving model has this annoying snap oversteer ANYTIME, ANYWHERE thing going on, even front engined all wheel drive cars (???)
- The second last and last difficulty are completely unbalanced, the former is way too slow and the latter is way too fast => no challenge / no chance
- Odd choice of music, that's subjective but it's far off DiRT 2 soundtrack
I will most likely change my review after a longer period, when I just get used to the frustrating bits.

If you want a rally racing simulator this is the one to get. There is variety and quality, multiple disciplines and sets a nice "real rally" mood. There is non-simulator/simulator driving modes, so even if you just want a fun time you can try it.
On the simulator side, physics feel fun and perfectly tuned. I don't know how accurate to life this is, but it's seriously fun and feels challenging and rewarding.
Cars feel more intuitive than in Dirt Rally. Graphics are nice. There is a driving school. Career mode is more immersive than in Dirt Rally.
Your stage will make you feel the adrenaline of trusting your co-driver.
Don't take the "is easier than Dirt Rally" critics too seriously, most of us have never driven a rally car in a competitive context so "harder is more realistic" can be said with care. So if you have spent 300+ hours on Rally it  would be natural to adjust your tactics to accomodate Dirt 4.
Wherever you come from, if you like cars or rally I believe you wont be dissapointed.

As you'll probably know, 'Darkest Hour, Europe '44-'45' is a modification for the original Red Orchestra, set on the western theatre of the Second World War focusing on the beach landings in Normandy, which is shown by it's content, map design and models. Content wise, it obviously expands to that theatre and period, including its weaponry, vehicular combat, mapping etc. It contains most of the same mechanics from it's mother title, with more added features.
Personally, I have been casually been playing the mod for quite a few years, and enjoyed it everytime I give it another go, so be it with myself, or a few others. At this current moment, most servers and community input rely of the 29th Infantry Division, a unit for the mod which is known to be the main playerbase. I believe it has been active for quite a few years, keeping servers up for pubbers and members alike with a mature and friendly enviroment. Of course there is other smaller units which are always to be present, but if you are interested in such affairs, the Jackboot forums contain that sort of infomation, if that's your cup of tea.
The original Red Orchestra is known for its realistic approach to the First Person Shooter, and may be a struggle of patience to regular FPS players. Aesthetic eye candy from such titles is not the focus here either, and will only be of interest to those of the period, and having the needed patience for it's pace.
+ An alternative to Arma.
+ Enough content to compete with Ostfront.
+ Active units and clans to participate with, if interested.
+ Atmospheric, giving a sense of realistic combat.
+ Runs well on most systems.
+ Free.
If you were to be picky, apart from some small animation and sound quality issues, the only reason you would dislike parts of the title, would be it's entirety due to it's mechanics. It can appear very sluggish at times, in terms of gun handling and such, but as said previously, it's aimed at those wanting a more realistic experience to the usual FPS style. Being a mod, it's obviously going to build on the original, not take away.
In comparison, it is the best/ only alternative for the ArmA 2 Invasion 44 modification, if you do not have a 'beefy' system to handle it, and is easier to set up if you would rather play it casually. The public playerbase is fairly active currently, but will reduce over the years.

A Developer from Artix Entertainment had requested reviews from players after only being in OPEN BETA for one hour which is a bit of a joke but I have enough to make a review so here it is.
Quick Review for those with more time on your hands.
Is it worth playing: Not really there are better games out there for free Unless you intend to play on tablet or android
How would you rate it out of 10? : A solid 4 Its a game equivilant of Meh
Would I recommend to others : Nope Id suggest playing Adventure Quest Worlds instead is it a lot better constructed considering it is a sider scrolling web based game.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The first and biggest issue is the fact that this game was originally aimed at PC players of AQWorlds as the next AQ game and yet they spent so much time making the controls work for mobile/tablet users that they have forgotten how make it interesting for PC players.
Character Customization : It is pretty standard and not a lot of variations even with the added barber shop into the game so not alot to talk about there.
The Pathing and quest system are a joke because as of right now after you finish the tutorial you and just smack bang in this town that you are expected to know the layout and locations of everything with just random NPCs offering you quests for NPCs that you cannot find by a tracker or even in the quest information. So you are literally screwed from the word *Go* and If you have no prior experience of the game YOU ARE SCREWED.
Now onto Monsters : At the moment of writing this it is in Open beta so its to be expected that things need to be worked out, But currently I was dealing 1/5th of the damage I was being dealt by monsters of the same level as myself and for the sake of arguements I was a fully geared warrior  So it makes zero sense that I should be getting destroyed by one monster as the same level as me.
Combat system: This is where I believe that Artix Entertainment has done quite well for themselves because the actual animations of the attacks are quite good so in that regards I commend them But due to the long drawn out animations it would seem that where I as the player would get one special move off the opposing monster/s will be able to get 2 or even 3 attacks off therefore rendering my damage pointless because they have caught up to my damage spike and even done some more which inturn requires me to demolish my supplies of potions that I have/had.
UI/Menu : Again I honestly think Artix Entertainment has really done well on the UI and Menu system, For a phone or tablet game, There is no need to restrict PC users to such a simplistic and just empty screen and weirdly enough they have locked the chatbox to the topleft of the screen even though ther is nothing else on the bottom left, Which is another indication that they only thought about phone and tablet users.
Sounds and Music : I think the Music is alright not the best but what the hell its better than nothing am i right ? but when looting or attacking it suddenly gets extremely loud and every time you loot a monster it is preset to make the sound of a chest opening when your opening a bag, Now thats just lazy because it doesnt take a lot of time to make 2 different sounds for different containers of items that monsters will drop. The attacking noises are extremely loud for really no reason in really random areas, Such as making that trademark *Sheen* Noise when it is swung but it is so loud if you really want to listen to it Id Highly recommend making the sound very low.

Back in the day, Sonic Adventure 2 was considered one of the best Sonic games. Today, i can say that this game sucks. Period. To be honest, i had much more fun with the original Sonic Adventure, except for fishing. That game had 6 gameplay styles, but this one has only 3. Sonic and Shadow stages are easily the best part of the game, and the reason many love this game. However, some stages aren't much fun to play, because of the challenge. There's nothing wrong with that, but as a whole i prefer the Sonic stages of the original Sonic Adventure. Do you remember the E-102 Gamma shooting stages? They were only okay, but at least it's story was short. Here, Tails (which i also liked on the original) and Eggman stages are the same, but much longer. It gets boring and repetitive after a while. And the Knuckles stages are back, but are worse for two reasons. First, the radar only shows one piece at a time, so the stages take much longer to complete. Secondly, Rouge stages are the same, so you get more of this bad design choice. Some reviewers said that because only the Sonic and Shadow stages were good, they only enjoyed 33% of the game. But no. The bad stages take a longer time to complete, so i would say that only 20% of the story playtime was fun. On the plus side, the hub world is gone and the bosses are better. The story is improved but still sucks, and the soundtrack for me is much worse than the original. To get all the emblems, you need to replay the stages over and over and over again. It's a chore. But there's more good stuff. The Chao garden is much improved, and this time i actually cared a bit for it. And there's also 2-player multiplayer, which is actually good. I also need to mention that the Steam version is much better optimized that the original mess of Sonic Adventure DX on Steam, only playable with a mod pack. There's also leaderboards if you enjoy that kind of thing. But the "Battle" content is locked behind a DLC purchase, a terrible practice by SEGA. Despite everything, in the end i can recommend this game on sale if you enjoyed this game back in the day or if you want the best chao garden version available. The dark and gritty fantasy world of Vermintide should make any Warhammer fans right at home. You find yourself in Ubersreik; a large human city in shambles while being overrun by large rat-like creatures known as the Skaven.
This game takes inspiration from a few big games, the most noticeable being Left4Dead. (Which is not a bad thing) There aren't many games out there like L4D, and since I've been praying for L4D3 to come out for years now, I'm happy to see another developer make a L4D style game so well. That's not to say this game is just a reskin of existing games. Vermintide has a fun and easy to jump in to combat system, making use of many weapons from daggers to giant war hammers and even to flaming combustion magic if you choose to play as the Bright Wizard.
Vermintide also sports an interesting loot system. The 5 classes all start with completely different weapons that all function differently and have different stats. As you complete campaigns, you will get guaranteed weapon drops for leveling up, but also a chance to get rare loot by rolling dice at the completion of a mission. Your party can improve their odds at getting better loot by working together to bring certain items to the end of a campaign, adding a huge risk vs reward element.
Check it out with some friends and have some good fun.

I didn't like the humour of the game and the dialogues were longer than the actual levels, so I ended up not paying attention to the story at all. While the voice acting could be good for a few characters (the game even has Andy Serkis!) it was the most annoying part of the game for me.
The soundtrack, on the other hand, was amazing. Futuristic sounds, both relaxing and exciting, but also orchestral pieces worthy of Hans Zimmer's "Time". Everything fits into the game and sounds good.
However, the most important part of a game is its gameplay. And boy, it's so good.
Imagine Metal Gear Solid 1 without combat. Instead you get different gadges with cooldowns (lures, stuns, veils,...) and have to find your way through 100 (!) different levels with different kinds of enemies. It's like a stealth game combined with simple puzzles. The difficulty doesn't vary much, it's never too easy nor too difficult but always feels rewarding.
If you like the gameplay of the MGS franchise, you will definitely like Volume.

Sometimes a sequence of a few timed jumps is needed to get the blue cube to its target, but it's never a frustrating experience. It's just giggly fun. The game makes use of the Steam Achievements to add some more giggles by throwing an achievement your way for about anything you do in the game. You will easily get 118/118 achievements in half an hour. Seriously, if you want a cheap half hour of pure innocent fun, pick up
when it's on sale.

. In

But they take the achievements joke a bit too far in the second game: you simply get 3 achievements for anything you do. In the first game, you get an achievement for starting a level and for ending a level -haha- but in the second game you just get three achievements for each level and for each and every action that yields an achievement. Then there is
which has over 1000 achievements!
is already taking it too far, so that's just over the top. It's only for people who want to artificially increase their number of completed Steam Achievements, but not for anyone else. So just leave it at the first Zup!-game and give the others a miss.

280 hours in DiRT Rally / Master level / No assists.
I only tried Simulation Mode with no assists.
I tried both FWD starters, the 306 Maxi, the Hyundai R5, the 208 WRX.
I really like DiRT 4 handling. It's the first time in a game I directly understand the car I'm driving. When switching from the G27 to a real car, it feels incredibly similar.
I love feeling the weight, I love how you can feel the wheels in the wheel, when losing grip or regaining it.
Change of heights really changes the car movement.
Handbrake is less of a magic save button.
Now as soon as you lose contact with 1 or 2 tyres, you really feel it and it's easier to adapt your driving, because it seems the car responds in a coherent way.
---- Edit with more details while I'm answering a question ----
I've never driven a Rally car IRL, so I believe only rally drivers could answer this question honestly. And even there, 2 rally drivers if not experienced enough could be contradictory depending on their drivestyle, car settings, different car parts...
As far as I'm personnaly concerned, I find the physics more realistic even if not perfect. I drove different road cars IRL, old and recent. I find the F2 extremely satisfying compared to DR. When getting out and driving my 206 it's actualy scary for a minute because I'm still in D4 mode.
For the 4WD I'm kinda mixed but on the good side of things.
I tried the Group B Peugeot 205 the most, and I like it a lot. I didn't like the one in DR despite using it. I like the power transfer better surely due to the weight changes.
I find the R5 really great, I don't feel like I'm abusing the game anymore but actually using a top notch car well engineered.
For the RWDs, a lot of people are saying it doesn't slide enough.
1 thing is they're specificaly tuned to fit all players. It's good for me because I'm not good at RWDs, but you'd have the impression of driving a modern Mercedes or BMW because it sticks to the road.
I suppose you would need to tune the camber and differential, maybe brakes to get something more DR alike.
For the WRX and RX2 cars, they're a beauty to drive, and translate perfectly what you can see on TV.
The old Mini is also very well done.
As a whole, I think the weight really helps to make all the cars easier to apprehend. It's for me the biggest improvement, paired with the FFB, making me prefer D4 over DR.
The suspension of the cars is pretty good, even if they does not show on replays.
In the specifics of each cars, unfortunately, only real Pilots could enlight us, and always remember there's good and bad practitioners.
What I think would make the game even better are these:
- Better torsion of the chassis
- Volumetric dirt and ground (Like in the game Spintires), to mix the grip levels during a track (RX tracks have some kind of cool holes to drive under rain). It would also affect order of passage and RX tracks
- A tiny bit more precise and fast suspension feeling
- Real damages of the car that would impact the driving (sidewalk poping tyre, damaged roof that would affect aero dynamism and futur rolls)
- More difference in the track details, I want to feel I'm really having a trip
A lot of people are mixed on this game, but I'd say they're too far hooked on the Sim Racing habits. I personaly refer to what I drove in real life, and D4 is the first time I can get behind a wheel and instantly feel the car with intuition.

So ill start this review of with a small story.
So about a year go I was trying to choose between whether to buy Door Kickers or Breach and Clear during a sale, to me they both looked really interesting and fun to play so it wasnt an easy choice, but eventually I decided to buy Breach and Clear. I downloaded it, hit play and started to play, I really enjoyed the gameplay that it gave me but it was to short and didnt have much variety in the equipment I could give my soldiers, so I was still curious about Door Kickers and really wanted to play it, so about a year later I purchased Door Kickers.
I started Playing Door Kickers and I immediately new this game was far superior to Breach and Clear, It contained much more content and variety in gameplay, as you have a much wider range in how you will will breach a building and what equipment you will use doing so.
If you Have Breach and Clear and you enjoy it, Door kickers is 100% for you, or if you are trying to decide between Breach and Clear and Door Kickers, I would personally choose Door Kickers, I am not saying Breach and Clear is  a bad game i just think Door kickers is much better.
One thing before I get into what is good and bad about the game I just want to mention something about the price
-PRICE- I got Door Kickers for like 3$ or something and it is DEFINITELY worth that amount but the game is usually 20$, and I think this is pushing it a little to much as there are many other games out there for this amount that contain much more content, but if Top Down, Tactical games are your thing This is worth the 20$
-Now to what is Good and Bad about Door Kickers-
-PROS-
- Lots of Variety (In how you breach Buildings and map types etc)
- Provides hours of fun tactical gameplay
- Many Primary and Secondary weapons to choose from
- Nice graphics for a Top Down game
- Easy to Run (You dont need Optimus Prime to be able to run it)
- Easy to learn controls (also very smooth)
- Can play custom maps from workshop
- Can offer a real challenge on some maps
- Plenty of missions
-CONS-
- Doesnt really have a storyline
- When multiple troops paths cross or are close together it can be hard to tell a troop which way to look etc
- A little expensive, but if you like topdown tactical games or its on sale its worth it
Overall I think this game is one of the best games you will find in its genre, best suited for people that enjoy tactical gameplay, and the biggest downfall is its price even though its basically worth the price

Back in the day, Sonic Adventure 2 was considered one of the best Sonic games. Today, i can say that this game sucks. Period. To be honest, i had much more fun with the original Sonic Adventure, except for fishing. That game had 6 gameplay styles, but this one has only 3. Sonic and Shadow stages are easily the best part of the game, and the reason many love this game. However, some stages aren't much fun to play, because of the challenge. There's nothing wrong with that, but as a whole i prefer the Sonic stages of the original Sonic Adventure. Do you remember the E-102 Gamma shooting stages? They were only okay, but at least it's story was short. Here, Tails (which i also liked on the original) and Eggman stages are the same, but much longer. It gets boring and repetitive after a while. And the Knuckles stages are back, but are worse for two reasons. First, the radar only shows one piece at a time, so the stages take much longer to complete. Secondly, Rouge stages are the same, so you get more of this bad design choice. Some reviewers said that because only the Sonic and Shadow stages were good, they only enjoyed 33% of the game. But no. The bad stages take a longer time to complete, so i would say that only 20% of the story playtime was fun. On the plus side, the hub world is gone and the bosses are better. The story is improved but still sucks, and the soundtrack for me is much worse than the original. To get all the emblems, you need to replay the stages over and over and over again. It's a chore. But there's more good stuff. The Chao garden is much improved, and this time i actually cared a bit for it. And there's also 2-player multiplayer, which is actually good. I also need to mention that the Steam version is much better optimized that the original mess of Sonic Adventure DX on Steam, only playable with a mod pack. There's also leaderboards if you enjoy that kind of thing. But the "Battle" content is locked behind a DLC purchase, a terrible practice by SEGA. Despite everything, in the end i can recommend this game on sale if you enjoyed this game back in the day or if you want the best chao garden version available. For newcomers, i recommend to stay away from this game and play the original Sonic Adventure DX instead if you must choose between one of them. Hell, i think that even Sonic Heroes is a better game.
For those wondering this game does have controller support.

This is a classic game. It'll be celebrating it's 15th anniversary this year, and it still stands up well. What always drew me back to this game on the DreamCast and GameCube was the selection of mini-games in addition to the main gameplay. The levels are well designed, the characters control fast and easy most of the time, and the story is by far one of the darkest and deepest given in the "Sonic the Hedghog" series.
Another great element I always enjoyed was the Chao Garden. You find a Chao Key, collect animals and Chaos Drives, and finish your level, and you are granted access to the Chao Garden, where you can raise 8 Chao per garden (Normal, Dark and Hero), so you get to take care of a total of 24 Chao.
What are Chao? Simply put, they are virtual pets that are given the learning capacity of a small child, and can learn an assortment of tricks and skills based on how you raise them or leave them in a class or even compete in races. They thrive on love, and there are consequences for them being abused (they likely will not reincarnate after the end of thier life cycle, meaning all stacked progress will be gone forever). The artificial intellegence programmed into them is pretty good, and you'll soon see them pick favorite characters to be tended to, as well as have preferences for food, and become either crybabies, bullies or little friendly critters (again, this is a reflection of you as the player).
That said, this game has always held up greatly, and it's nice to see a port of it that also restores the original features of the initial DreamCast release, in addition to the GameCube version, as many options were left out when the game was ported to a Nintendo console. This is easily the definitive release, and a fan favorite, so I highly recommend you get this if you are either new to the series, or just want to relive the epic that is "Sonic Adventure 2"

The first time I opened it and walked around I got the same feeling of wonder that I had when I played Minecraft for the first time back in alpha. I was overwhelmed by the amount of crafting options and couldn't wait to try everything out and explore.
All that said, there's a few too many bugs to recommend it at the moment; even for an early access title. To name a few:
- Inventory becomes unusuable after a few hours, items begin to bug out and can't be selected
- Ships randomly sink and bob around when on board and placing items, even when anchored
- Fall through the world when using a ladder on board a ship or even just stationary on ground
- Using one ladder, whether stationary or on a ship takes you up another one nearby putting you in some obscure location
- Ships will sometimes lose turning control or won't move at all
- Logging off onboard a ship and coming back only to find yourself in the ocean
- No dedicated servers yet
Those are just the major bugs I can recall off the top of my head. The problem with a lot of those issues is that they will break your progress forcing you to start over. In some cases those issues can be resolved by logging off/on but having to do this multiple times in a session gets real annoying and fast.
I would recommend following this game though. It can only get better once the major kinks have been worn out.

Mimpi is a puzzle-platformer, developed and ported over from mobile devices to pc by Silicon Jelly.
The video review is here:
You play a small dog and embark onto an adventerous journey.
On this journey you might encounter some puzzles. The puzzles in this game are fairly easy for the most part, but some made me use hints. In the mobile version you unlock hints via microtransactions. In this version you can collect them in the levels or play a little bit of tetris.
As of 22nd of January the tetris minigame is fixed.
In a puzzle-platformer you might do something else other than solving puzzles. The platforming in this game is decent: You have quite good control over your horizontal movement, but in terms of jumping you really don't have that much control over your height. That might come from the fact that the game is played with virtual controls on mobile devices and therefore can't be that accurate in that regard.
After each level there is a hidden object minigame, which is a nice change of pace.
One playthrough of the game can be done within about 2 hours. When you want to go for all collectibles though there is a little bit of replayability.
Conclusions:
All in all I have to say that the game is worth giving a shot, it's 4.99€. It is a very well made mobile port and I'd consider it worth the buy.

At first this game seem to be a worthy investment. It throw out of the window the arcade, repetitive and boring gameplay that standardized L4D; focusing on speed runs from point "A" to "B" slicing and gunning through hordes of zombies and "specials", just to arrive to a "safe house" full of weapons and ammo, and repeat the same thing two or three more times in order to finish a map.
Contagion focus it self on cooperative gameplay, management of resources (weapons and ammo), map exploration in order to find those resources and find a one of the three randomly generated scape routes. The gameplay is a "relistic" survival zombie game, were only head shots kills zombies, attacks from them cause infection and ammo is littely found.
The problem is, the game has bugs since it early access like zombie pathfinding, charcters skeletons, animations..., there is no lobby and kick system, to play multiplayer with your friends only you must have your own server, there is only a few maps to play and to make it worst there is no modding community fix that. There characters are lifeless and boring, they only swear bad words and that's it. L4D is FAR MUCH BETTER in that aspect and also in the maps.
Contagion has good mechanics, but L4D has better characters, better maps and better modding support. A great zombie game would be the mix of these two games OR a remastered first person edition of Resident Evil Outbreak.

But in general, the game is a lot of good, visceral fun.  The combat and especially the vehicles just felt right -- so much so that finishing off the various side missions after completing the main story was a joy instead of a chore.

Now I need to get the other games in this series...

Take a journey with me through a twisted mind; a place where things aren’t quite as they appear, and where surprises await you on every screen. This strange new land is filled with undocumented creatures and mechanisms that are as entrancing as they are dangerous. But these lands are no place for a dog to be separated from its owner, and you will need an eye for details, as well as the ability to think laterally, if you are to return Mimpi to his master. If you can navigate your new surroundings, acquaint yourself with the locals and solve the many tricky puzzles that await you, just maybe he can make it home.
Mimpi is an odd creation, like the mutant offspring of Monty Python and Sergeant Pepper, on a mutual acid trip. Its vast sprawling lands are filled with fantastical mechanisms and beasts, all awash with vivid, eye-searing colour and a cacophony of bewildering sounds. Despite its simple, papercraft appearance there is detail by the bucketload, be it in the behaviour of its mythical creatures, the movement cycles of obstacles, or the complexity of the game’s puzzles.
I could never quite pin Mimpi down to just one genre though, finding myself in a complex action platforming set-piece one moment, and a tricky pattern-based puzzle the next.  Progression hinges on your ability to spot patterns in your environment and put them into practice at some point later in the game. So, whilst that pretty design you saw earlier on the wall didn’t look significant, it almost certainly is.
Environments are  brilliantly random and destined to raise a smile, and maybe even an eyebrow. Each location is packed with detail, as well as a number of friendly and hostile creatures who can aid or hinder you on your journey. I can’t say I have ever played ‘Simon Says’ with an overgrown jungle flower before, but I think I liked it – perhaps even more than I enjoyed playing volleyball with the elephant/foot hybrid animal. To be a fly on the wall of Silicon Jelly’s development offices would be both an enlightening and scarring event, for sure.
Don’t mistake the game’s friendly appearance as an indication of its difficulty; Mimpi‘s canine odyssey is not for the faint hearted. As aforementioned, if you can’t think outside of the box you won’t be able to make your way to the end of the game. Its puzzles can be brutally difficult if you don’t know what you are doing, and seldom will you be able to fumble your way through them. If you manage to find enough lightbulbs though, you can buy hints to help you progress. For a change of pace you can also give Mimpi a makeover with a variety of different costumes.
Silicon Jelly have done a bang-up job porting the game from mobile to PC, and the gameplay never misses a beat. Despite the action lending itself more to a touchscreen, the keyboard and mouse control scheme is intuitive and responsive, too. My only gripe is the oversized mobile phone game interface. A quick re-jig of the menus for PC version would hae been much appreciated, and given a better initial impression of the game, but you can’t have everything, I suppose.
Mimpi is a small dog on a big adventure and you’d be missing out big time if you don’t join him for the fun. It’s a game of joyous discovery that rewards an inquisitive mind with some of the wackiest, off the wall humour curently on the Steam platform. It’s also a generous game, too, with a decent amount of content to keep you scratching your head into the wee hours.
Good dog, Mimpi. Good dog.

I've been playing this game off and on since it was released in early access, and after seeing the game evolve and continue to show life, I have finally made the choice to suggest this game.  However, it is not for everyone because it can be difficult.  This is the kind of game people play when they want to show their skills or completely ruin someone's day.  When you die (or become infected), you become a zombie, which then turns your gaming experiencing into a hunt for flesh.  Sometimes people
join servers just to infect all other players.  With 5 game modes mixing up 9 different maps, this game actually provides a large amount of content.  The game lets you pick from 12 Characters, and lets you play with up to 8 players.

It's a great concept, executed rather well. The problem comes from other players, who will frequently run ahead to either get themselves killed to grief on the survivors (as it's too easy playing as a zombie - more on that in a bit), or just to finish the map before anyone else, often leaving new players lost and confused.
Additionally, it's far too easy to play as a zombie.  Zombies have four times the survivor's sprint, and can duck faster than bullets fly in order to avoid headshots.  Speaking of which, headshots are the only way to kill a zombie, which is fine, but not so much when a shotgun at point blank doesn't even make them stumble.
Zombie players will often simply hide around corners, waiting for a player to walk by for a single swipe - hoping to get the RNG on their side for the infection chance.
All in all, the game has the potential, but until zombie mechanics are changed to balance players versus zombie players, don't get this game unless it's on sale, of unless you have a group of friends and a closed server (or enough friends to fill a server by yourselves).

The first Hotline Miami introduced a novel style of gameplay; very fast paced, hyperviolent, a paradoxical mix of planning ahead and thinking on your feet. The story was increasingly ambiguous and left a lot to interpretation; whether this was a good thing is up to you. It wasn't without it's flaws, however; most of the levels, aside from the last few, were largely routine. Get a phone call, go to the building, kill everyone, leave. Occasionally they spiced it up (like with the sudden van barreling into you, remember that? Yeah, we all do), but beyond that, you won't remember each individual level. And to add to that, it was a rather short experience.
Hotline Miami 2 kept all the good parts of the first game, while ironing out the flaws. For starters, instead of only one protagonist, you have about a dozen (not all of them are likeable; Detective Pardo is a complete jerk, and Jake is dumber than dirt. But what did you expect from cold-blooded mass murderers?). Much like the masks in the first game, they each play differently, only now they're more unique. For example, one of the protagonists is a bit of a pacifist and refuses to pick up lethal weapons, sticking solely to bats and golf clubs. This makes him vulnerable in long-range combat. However, the flipside to this is that he can unload firearms, which not only prevents the enemy from picking it back up, but also extends your combo.  However, you can still beat enemies to death by accident during takedowns; do this too often, and he'll go berserk.
Like I said, each protagonist has a different playstyle; you usually can't choose which protagonist you play as, but each of the levels is specifically designed to match the style of your character. This means that how well you play depends on how well you can adapt to your character, and that's really good. It also makes each level much more memorable.
Story-wise, the game answers a lot of the questions the previous game left. It still leaves a little bit up to interpretation, but you can usually piece it together with information the game gives you rather than just guess. However, I must warn you that the game's ending is rather abrupt, and a bit of a downer. One of the characters even not-so-subtly alludes to that near the end of the first act, and he's not kidding.
The game is also considerably longer than the first game, and additionally features an extra hidden level (I'll let you find that one on your own, but here's a hint: you unlock it in the level called Withdrawal) and a hard mode if you still want more. And let me tell you, that hard mode... It does it's name justice. If you barely made it through normal mode, don't even bother with hard. For the completionists among us, the achievements are mostly fair and doable, and are truly a test of both skill and your ability to find secrets... With exception of one achievement, which involves killing 50.000 enemies. Even if you've done all the other achievements, that one will probably still take a while. And to top it all off, the game mockingly insults you for getting all the achievements.
Then again, it does introduce it's own set of flaws. For one, the game is buggy at times. One of the most unique playstyles in the game allows you to play as two protagonists at once, one wielding a chainsaw and the other wielding guns. You control the chainsaw wielder, while right-clicking makes the other guy shoot his gun. This is a lot of fun and allows for some really fast combos, but here's the thing; the gun guy's pathfinding is horrible, and he tends to get stuck behind objects. Not to mention, it's even harder to aim than normal because the bullets come from somewhere behind you. This wouldn't be as big of a problem if they let you control the gun wielder while the AI controls the chainsaw, but no. And then there's the fact that the game is downright unfair at times. Remember those annoying windows from the first game? The developers got really carried away with those in the latter half of the game. And besides that, it's really random when enemies can see you. I can't remember the amount of times where I failed to lure in an enemy that was in my way, decided to try another strategy, and then suddenly that same enemy snipes me because I walked past a window loosely in his line of sight halfway across the building.
And remember how I keep praising the unique playstyles of the various protagonists? Well, the thing is, not all of them are useful. In fact, the very first characters you play as, Martin the Pig Butcher and Corey the Zebra, are probably the worst in the game; Martin has no special abilities that I know of, and Corey has a roll dodge that allows her to avoid bullets... Which sounds cool on paper, but you're left wide open once you stop rolling, making it very situational.
But you know what? This game is still a ton of fun. I found myself unable to stop playing it after I beat it the first time, or even the second time in hard mode  (and let me tell you, it's saying something when I still want to play a game after all the bull hard mode put me through). And to top it all off, the game's soundtrack is AMAZING. Yes, with all capital letters. The first game's was pretty good, but this one really sells the various levels (oh yeah, and each level has it's own track, which helps make them even more memorable!). I can't really name any favorites, as they're all great, but some of the more memorable tracks include Decade Dance, Sexualizer, Roller Mobster, The Way Home, and Le Perv (uncoincidentally, each of those plays in the last level of one of the game's acts. Clever pacing).
So, should you buy this game? Let me answer that question with a question: You really do like hurting people, don't you?

Because at the core, we have a mediocre timing puzzle game. It's ok, but nothing special.
And the flaws are many. In order of appearance:
- First time, the game starts in a 320x200 window. Have fun finding video options to change resolution. (And don't expect it to ever show the active setting.) The menus are confusing and counter-intuitive, pressing Escape doesn't just go back, it triggers irritating "Y/N" confirmations, and in the main menu, where you actually *expect* the Y/N question to quit, it throws you back to the intro screen so you have to press Start just to re-enter the menu to quit.
- Tutorial is bad, nothing is explained. Shift makes me hug the wall? Space to sneak corners when hugged? I randomly tried keys to find out! Is that arrow cursor ever good for anything? I still don't know.
Gameplay and story feel utterly disconnected.
- Level presentation: Is that map description just cosmetic in-game blurb, or actual comments from devs to players? Where is my best time, is it saved at all? What the hell is "PAR"?
- Story presentation: It took me a 2nd look to realize the tutorial was over and I had just played the first 2 story missions. (Actual storytelling won't happen until 6 levels later...) Who is Gisborne? Who's "The Banker"? The Queen? The game mentions these people as if we're supposed to know them, without any introduction. It's "in medias res" (short-story style) done wrong. About as engaging as reading news about an election of some country you never heard of.
- Art style: I really like the polygonal visuals. But there's no difference between the Banker's room and the Queen's room. It all feels the same. There could at least have been smarter use of color schemes.
- The sneaking animation is a joke. Guards can see you across obstacles, unless you press Shift. But you don't duck. As if touching a table made you invisible.
- Levels are mostly about collecting crystals. If they want to make it more than a puzzle game by adding a story, at least they could have given us a reason for why we need those crystals, or bring some variation to the objects we collect. The "collect tokens" thing makes it feel like "Stealth Super Mario", and not in a good way.
- Voice acting: great VA for Alan, the simulation AI! The player character VA on the other hand is... well, as another reviewer put it: "twee British person who streams a video game." No offence, but it sounds like "Hey, I'm reading this from a screen, but actually I don't give a f***." Maybe getting a Youtuber to do the VA wasn't the best idea, and even then – C'mon, I've seen LetsPlays with more exciting comments.
- Music: When you get spotted, music suddenly gets louder – and makes the VA lines (that comment your failure) inaudible. It just sounds like a mess. And the soundtrack is like, 1 track. Makes it very repetetive. They could at least have altered between 2.
Bottom line: The kind of game you play 1 hour per week, then stop before it becomes too repetetive.
"We'll broadcast this to all of England," the protagonist proudly proclaims at some point. Huh. I think I'd rather watch Premier League.

I've tried playing this a few times now. I have Red Orchestra 2 and thoroughly enjoy that, plus the Rising Storm adaptation for the game. Both of those games are brilliant and a lot of fun to play. However I had a shock playing this mod.
First thing I noticed was the graphics (ok small point in the main look of things). But there was a noticeable jump backwards, and it looked about as good as COD2 to me, which was surprising considering RO2 is actually very well detailed on the whole.
The gameplay. Now without crosshairs is standard for all of these games. But playing without them for Darkest Hour just made it impossible for me. I do well on Rising Storm and RO2 online, but on DH it was just a nightmare. The game seems buggy and difficult to get into, aiming seems to be luck rather than knowing what you're doing and people can run around and hipfire for some stupid reason and kill you a lot easier than you can kill them in aiming. So many people tried to say on the server i was on that DH is more realistic than RO2, I call that a total lie. It's just completely screwed over the basis of the game it was modding on.
I understand this is a mod and I appreciate the Devs hard work for it, but right now I cannot honestly recommend this game. I hope in the future when I try it again it will be a lot more playable. I'd recommend they look at Rising Storm and take tips from the success there.

I picked up Door Kickers during the summer sale, planning on spending some time in it while I was stuck using a laptop out of state. I was pleasantly surprised in many ways, and while this title does have a few setbacks it is a fairly fun indie title that I can't help but praise.
Door Kickers is a top-down 2D tactics game, meaning I will critique it less for level of detail and more for art-style and consistency. The official content is appealing to look at, though a SWAT team wearing tan uniforms is an odd sight. Community-created content varies, but in general the game looks fairly decent. My primary complaint is that textures will become blurry as you zoom in. You'll also notice that the enemies you face will regularly use the same sprites, and that levels reuse quite a few assets between each-other.
This game features fairly decent audio design, but my main complaint is how repetitive the ambient sounds are. You'll start hearing the same voices on TVs and radios, and the same shouts emanating from mooks before they are helplessly gunned down by your troops. Eventually, you'll find yourself repeating the TV announcers in your head, staying a second ahead of their words. I will complement game for its soundtrack, though; it works well, is pleasant to listen to, and suits the style/setting of Door Kickers.
This game performs very well on virtually any system, due to its 2D sprite-based nature. No issues there, as I would've hoped.
Door Kickers revolves around planning out an entry route for a SWAT team in various situations, where your primary goal is typically to eliminate all hostiles and possibly defuse a bomb in the process. It is fast-paced, unforgiving, and fun to play. However, there are a few faults with it. The unlock system prevents you from accessing very interesting content such as the Stealth class until after you've spent multiple hours in-game, and the planning system seems to be developed with touchscreens in mind, which makes the process of modifying orders that have already been created very difficult at best. Despite this, I still found that it was fun enough to last for quite a few hours, and I still haven't finished even a third of the game's content.
Door Kickers does well in this regard, featuring a built-in mod menu and map/mission editor. It doesn't allow for extensive feature modification, but new weapons, armor, maps, and enemies can be created with ease, and existing ones can be modified to your heart's content. I definitely approve of the game's position here.
Door Kickers is a very fun indie title to waste some time on, thanks to its light weight, fast-paced yet tactical gameplay which is sure to appeal to fans of Rainbow Six or Ghost Recon. However, I don't believe its production value is quite high enough to justify a purchase at full price. It's definitely fun, but it isn't quite $19.99 wholesale fun. I will be keeping my eye on the development of its sequel, 'Door Kickers 2 - Task Force North', however, as that title looks like it will have considerably higher production value and quality.

TL;DR 5/10 Lovely pictures; stressful assembly; AP2 is slightly better on timer expectations than AP1; same exact engine/game
These are lovely mosaics; unfortunately, color matching to your expected vision of the picture is usually not helpful at all; adjacent pieces almost never match in color.  Instead, you are intently focusing on matching shape continuity (By contrast, most jigsaw puzzles are assisted by color matching.)
Only 5 pieces are available at any time.  Pieces can be dropped into the correct framed position at any time.  The button in the upper right corner provides a mechanic for the game to reveal the correct placement of a piece, every 30 seconds.  Because of restricted availability of pieces that must be dropped into the center of a void, this mechanic cannot be realistically avoided for a more challenging experience, unless you memorize piece locations from previous runs.  Especially at the beginning of assembly, this mechanic must be used wisely to create good reference points for shapes.
Using earned coins from level completion, the 30 second reveal can be refreshed earlier. Also, coins can be used to add 30 seconds to the completion timer.  Of course, full Achievments require 3 star completion under the expected time limit (or limit + paid extensions.)
I just finished AP2 and found it slightly better for realistic expectations on the completion timer than AP1.  In AP2, I never spent any coins to refresh the 30 second reveal button or to extend the timer.
Unfortunately, the last 2 Achievment require the player to earn 1,000,000 coins.  I completed all puzzles with 3 stars, accumulating 530,000 coins.  Like most any puzzle, there is not much replay value.  Redoing the first 1 piece puzzle 500 times at 20 second intervals is the quickest way to grind through their broken achievments.  Monotony for 3 hours?
These Achievements are flawed by the developer's failure to beta test their game with even 1 single test-player.

I haven't played for a few days strictly because I know my next race is a snow course and I can't talk myself into putting myself through the frustration, especially true because it's 5 segments long.  Other than that, I'm still enjoying the game and would recommend it.

Will eventually update this review after getting a bit more into carrer mode and other more game-y aspects, but as a DiRT Rally veteran with hundreds of hours spent there, I must say that the handling model in simulation mode remains absolutely intact. The FFB needs some work, but the game is pretty much a worthy successor.

Dirt 4 has been enjoyable to me so far but I can understand how some hardcore Dirt Rally fans aren't satisfied. Many of our tactics and tendecies do not carry over into Dirt 4. I can't slide into corners as aggresively as I could in Rally. It is a different game and it takes a few hours to start getting the feel. Both gamepad and G29 racing wheel have felt great.
I am playing sim mode all assists off and it isn't too easy for me. On wales there were plenty of times I slammed into a tree or flipped my car barely finishing a race. When you crash in this game it isn't just going to be your radiator that gets damaged. My engine was so busted on a rally that I wasn't able to accelerate past about 65 MPH. Weather effects such as fog or rain can appear on your run depending on what position you start. Fog is very debilitating and its either rely heavily on co-driver or take it more cautiously to avoid a big crash. Nightime is more brutal than in Dirt Rally. Not only can your lights break but they can also malfunction on a perfect run leaving you blind. Random events such as crashed rally cars from a previous run still on the road or an animal crossing the street really adds to the immersion.
Dirt Academy is one of the cooler new features to DIrt 4. Just trying a new car in freeplay or doing a score/smash attack challenge is a cool way to learn a car without doing an event. With Gamer and SImulation handling its clear Codemasters is looking to widen the audience this game was meant for, and make it more accesible. This is not Dirt Rally 2 but it is an improvement in many ways over Rally. I will be playing both games because they offer different handling modes, cars, and locations. I love Dirt Rally and Dirt 4 is great too.

Simulation physics are simply not right. Far too much rear tyre grip when on the racing surface, but if you as much as touch a blade of grass, suddenly you have no grip. The massive amount of rear grip every car has means the cars auto-correct any slide before you have to. This isn't how rally cars drive, you can even just watch an external video to know this isn't correct.
If it wasn't for the glaringly obvious physics issues, I would recommend this game. Graphics are good, sounds are excellent, the stage generator is pretty good, the career mode and rally features (competitors cars, running order, etc), team management are all pretty good. It's generally an improvement on DiRT Rally in every way...except the most important area, the physics. This needs resolved, even if it's just moving back to DiRT Rallys physics.

I picked up Door Kickers during the summer sale, planning on spending some time in it while I was stuck using a laptop out of state. I was pleasantly surprised in many ways, and while this title does have a few setbacks it is a fairly fun indie title that I can't help but praise.
Door Kickers is a top-down 2D tactics game, meaning I will critique it less for level of detail and more for art-style and consistency. The official content is appealing to look at, though a SWAT team wearing tan uniforms is an odd sight. Community-created content varies, but in general the game looks fairly decent. My primary complaint is that textures will become blurry as you zoom in. You'll also notice that the enemies you face will regularly use the same sprites, and that levels reuse quite a few assets between each-other.
This game features fairly decent audio design, but my main complaint is how repetitive the ambient sounds are. You'll start hearing the same voices on TVs and radios, and the same shouts emanating from mooks before they are helplessly gunned down by your troops. Eventually, you'll find yourself repeating the TV announcers in your head, staying a second ahead of their words. I will complement game for its soundtrack, though; it works well, is pleasant to listen to, and suits the style/setting of Door Kickers.
This game performs very well on virtually any system, due to its 2D sprite-based nature. No issues there, as I would've hoped.
Door Kickers revolves around planning out an entry route for a SWAT team in various situations, where your primary goal is typically to eliminate all hostiles and possibly defuse a bomb in the process. It is fast-paced, unforgiving, and fun to play. However, there are a few faults with it. The unlock system prevents you from accessing very interesting content such as the Stealth class until after you've spent multiple hours in-game, and the planning system seems to be developed with touchscreens in mind, which makes the process of modifying orders that have already been created very difficult at best. Despite this, I still found that it was fun enough to last for quite a few hours, and I still haven't finished even a third of the game's content.
Door Kickers does well in this regard, featuring a built-in mod menu and map/mission editor. It doesn't allow for extensive feature modification, but new weapons, armor, maps, and enemies can be created with ease, and existing ones can be modified to your heart's content. I definitely approve of the game's position here.
Door Kickers is a very fun indie title to waste some time on, thanks to its light weight, fast-paced yet tactical gameplay which is sure to appeal to fans of Rainbow Six or Ghost Recon. However, I don't believe its production value is quite high enough to justify a purchase at full price. It's definitely fun, but it isn't quite $19.99 wholesale fun. I will be keeping my eye on the development of its sequel, 'Door Kickers 2 - Task Force North', however, as that title looks like it will have considerably higher production value and quality.

Note: This review applies to both Zup! and Zup! 2
These are to my knowledge, very original puzzle games. What little there is in terms of graphics and physics is very well done. There are many things, however, that prevent me from recommending them:
- Length and Lack of Content: 20 minutes each, if you work quickly, like I did. My time played on the second one is higher because I left the game on while I went out to do an errand. The music is just a few bars that loop over and over again. Perhaps there's something in the background that I'm not hearing, but it's so quiet that it doesn't make much difference. The music doesn't go anywhere.
- Ease: There is in theory some strategy involved, but you can win most levels in a few tries by just randomly clicking. I managed to beat the final level of Zup! 2 on my first try, with only one mouse click. Perhaps this was intended as a grand explosion finale, but most other levels were like this, too.
- Broken Puzzles: On many levels, you can win by skipping large portions of the level. In many cases, there are many ways to solve each level. I don't mean that in a fun "alternate solutions" kind of way. I mean that randomly clicking will often beat the puzzle on the first try.
- No Replayability: Some games offer much less than this in terms of content, but are fun games that I would highly recommend. Tetris, for example, has much less content than this game, but is highly replayable. After you've beaten this game once, there's no point playing it again until enough time has passed that you've forgotten all the solutions (not that it would be that hard to figure them out again, anyway).
- Achievement Spam: If you're looking for achievements, this game has them. Many of the positive reviews for this game cite achievements as a key feature. I earned six within my first sixty seconds. That's one every ten seconds. I got both games to 100% completion in the short time that I spend playing them. To be clear, I earned over 200 achievements in about 40 minutes. I had to replay one of the levels, since it didn't register the achievement for that level the first time. It only took me about ten seconds to replay it, though.
- Better Options for the Money: For the same price, you can get a full-length pixel art RPG by some random indie developer. Generic? Sure. But you could actually have fun playing a game for hours on end. There are so many really good games out there for the same price, or even less. For such a low price, I don't feel ripped off by the developer, and I wouldn't really mind if I couldn't get a refund. Seeing as I can, however, I think I'm going to get something else.
Overall, I think the concept shows enormous potential, but you won't find any of it in these actually existing games. I hope the developer refines the concept in the future, and makes a more challenging and engaging game.

The product so far is great. It is currently in
open beta, and updates are very regular - according to my experience there are at least 3 updates are released every week. There have only been 2 reset updates (again, since I started playing), in which every player's stats were reset to level 1. However, the equipment you had before the reset was always carried over. Whether it was nerfed, buffed or otherwise tampered with is another story.
When you begin the game you are prompted to login, then create a character. The first few stages of the character creation are very basic; class, colours and gender. Once you're somewhat content with the outlook of your character you can continue to the intro, there are a few cutscenes but nothing major. There's the basic tutorial given here, or atleast you're given some time to figure them out for yourself - get a feel for the game. Let your true intuitive self be brought out!
After the intro you are sent off to battleon, the main afk slash chit-chat area where you can chill with the people who've maxed out their characters and have either nothing to do or want to do nothing. These people are usually more than ready to help out a newb, and this is the point where you ask yourself, "what do i do now :?". I feel this is something Artix Entertainment (hereby called AE) could improve on, perhaps put a big floaty GUI-embedded 3D rotating arrow pointing straight at your chatbar which you click on when you have literally zero clues what to do. Or just make a question mark... idk budget.
If you do figure out where to go, (Esc -> Travel -> Greenguard), then you should be prepared for the grinding that's about to come. Currently you have 15 levels to grind through, and depending on your performance during the intro you might only have 14! Gearing up is especially important during the lower levels, since you can barely 1v1 a monster around your level range, even if you have a 1-2 level advantage against them. The (current) end-game items are the nightlocke weapons, you can choose between the sword, axe and staff depending on your game strategy.
Most MMORPGs create characters that only have one job; to fill a role in a quest, ie just stand there and do nothing. Talk to them once and they never do anything again. However, in AQ3D these characters are treated with more respect and diligence, they are given a Craft Shop, in which you can use mob drops to craft items in advance for the next area. Although these have a slight p2w notion to them, since you can use real currency to buy the actual weapon instead of farming the drops and waiting the craft time.
Pros:
•Very lightweight, I managed to get this game running on a dusty laptop I had from 2002! (Dual core 1.2ghz and integrated graphics with 32mb vram)
•Extremely positive community, the mods, beta testers and players share a very strong rapport. I dont think there are many other games out there with a community like this.
•Frequent updates; if you post a suggestion or a bug issue, it is often given some form of response within a month. AE is by no means a large company, but they still bring out more fixes than triple A developers do.
•Lots of playtime. Although most of it is grinding, there's always something to do.
•It's going to be F2P! There's no risk of investing money into the wrong game, it's free!
•A lot of lore. If you like story, this game has too much to share.
•There is a large catalogue of items you can craft,buy or get as drops, and most of these items (weapons, armour, quest drops etc) have a small line of text. These texts can be puns, descriptions of the items and sometimes just nonsense. I personally find it fun to get items just to read their colour text.
Cons:
•The graphics are heavily outdated. However, this is mainly because AE is going to be making the game exactly the same for Andoid and iOS devices. The game can also fulfill the nostalgia of Adventure Quest veterans, who played the previous flash-based games.
•Player base is somewhat small, and is mostly just American players. There are times when the rooms are empty, and you often cant solo.
•Leveling your character gets boring. Grinding gets boring. Farming dungeons gets boring. Trying to find new quests gets boring. Crafting items gets boring. Idling at Battleon gets boring. Without anybody to do things with, this game is quick to outlive it's shelf life.
•Very little customisation when it comes to character creation and on-screen GUI.
Overall, the game is heading in a good direction. The developers are committed, the community is good and the story is rich.

This is in my opinion one of the best Sonic The Hedgehog games ever.
I have been playing this title for 15 years, on the various platforms, and most recently I have installed a copy of it on my Steam account.
This game represents SEGA and Sonic Team at their peak. The graphics are fluid and run at high frame rates. It scales well to Full HD and it just works, all the time.
The game is diverse, the storyline weaves and bobs and the levels are challenging. This is no easy game, many other Sonic titles are far easier to play and get high scores with, but this is what we would call "old school". The coolest aspect of this game is the new abilities of the characters, for example, Sonic can grind on rails.
The music, by the band Crush 40 and others, was especially apt for this game and I loved it. The game also introduced a few new characters to the franchise (Rouge the Bat, Shadow The Hedgehog) and also sheds some light on the origins of Dr Eggman and his evil ways. For the first time, Dr Eggman is a playable character.
Diverse levels, from Ancient Egyptian pyramids, Jungles, and into space, there's something for everyone here.

I was going to make this a negative review, but I'll explain why I didn't.
It's important to note this game has only been out for a few days, and I've already seen one patch.  Small patch sure, but its a good sign.  So tamper any critism (which I mean to be constructive) with that in mind.
PROs.
-The art style really grows on you.  Its more dynamic then it looks at first glance, and its visual simplicity allows for complexity where it matters.
-The crafting system is awesome!  There is A LOT of stuff you can build, which is amazing.
-I am yet to leave my initial island, but even there the exploration has been fun.  I've been killed by a lot of wolves. And almost by a shark (he became dinner.)
-Night time is actually kind of terrifying and storms are no joke.  Get caught in the cold and you'll die.
-The microtransactions are cosmetics and emotes.  Absolutely unneccesary for gameplay, as theres already a lot of options, but a great way to support the developers or distinguish yourself if youre in a server with friends.  Which is where I'll segway into my complaints.
CONs
-Server management is non-existent.  To my knowledge the only way to play with friends is for one of you to host a game.  This has many issues.  For a game that will likely grow and expand via cooperative gameplay, there is an immediate need for additional commands for server admins (and support for dedicated servers in general.)   As items that fall/are dropped on the ground stay forever as best I can tell, things get cluttered really quick, so a "clean" feature is a must.  Or at least have the server wipe itself when restarted.
-Server sync seems to contribute to most of the bugs we saw.  I would say all of us playing (we had five online at one time) have average to above average internet speeds.  We all play online games regulary with no issues and have hosted cooperate games of various types before.  I don't think our internet was the problem, but something was definitely causing syncronization problems, and after reading other reviews, is the likely culprit of most problems people are having.
-To elaborate, with the exception of the host we all had issues with items becoming invisible (this seems to be a common problem) even after only short periods of time.  Usually this was fixed by logging out and logging back in, but when doing so we often got kicked back with the "Server Host is Unavailable" error message.  Or even worse after logging in only the terrain topography would pop in with our player head floating and unable to move.  Many times, it wouldn't even let us begin loading the server at all .  These bugs are what have driven me to postpone any further play time.  Of the 16 hours I have listed, at least a solid 2-3 of those were spent in menus trying to load into a server.
-Taking a break from server issues, inventory management and item placement need a lot of work.  Having a lot of stuff is awesome, having no way to effectively organize it is not.  Sorting features for chests and personal inventory management are critical.
I still have to give the game a positive review.  I spent hours trying to get back into the servers because it really is that much fun to play.  Should the server issues get patched up here in the near future I'll gladly return, but not until then.
