Let’s start off with a short MG34 rampage from war 413 when I stole a german’s MG34.
Heroes and Generals is one of the best damned WWII FPS games I’ve ever played.
Played it a bit in early alpha before it came to steam and didn’t enjoy it much at the time (too early alpha for me)
Got started playing back in Patton build of 2014 when the game came to steam; since then it’s been the primary game I play for a number of reasons, mainly because while I both love (and still play) Red Orchestra 2 and War Thunder – Heroes and Generals fills a uniqe void in this era of WWII FPS gaming.
For example, in most other WWII FPS games you “choose” your class and that’s it – you’re stuck with that loadout.
In H&G not only can you own MULTIPLE characters that are customizable (right down to the camo on their guns) but you can also switch freely between characters (switching classes require that you be in a squad with an Auxiliary seat) during a match to better suit the situation.
For example, say I’m using my “main SMG infantry” character and all he has is SMG + AP nades.
Suddenly the enemy team players spawn several tanks to bother my team – I can switch characters to my “Anti tank” character after I die as the Main SMG character and better help my team push forward.
This also applies to situations where if the enemy brings out snipers (aka recon) I can switch to my “infantry sniper” character and counter them.
At high level play it’s 90% mind games and knowing where your enemy is/will be based on map knowledge and 10% luck.
Many vets such as myself have literally been playing thousands and thousands of hours and as such knowing the map and it’s “spots noobies hide” is easy.
Another thing I can’t recommend enough – GET A GOOD GAMING HEADSET, it truly helps since 50% of the time you’ll hear your enemy before they see you (and vice versa).
TLDR: Go back and read it, if you’re looking for reviews and see a long wordy one it’s usually (not always though) worth the read.

This game is exactly what's on the tin.  It is a platformer and a puzzle game together.  It has a semi-retro feel which will look familiar to fans of Cave Story, as a weapon-leveling mechanic is also present here.  You break tiles in groups for big points, collect the experience, and avoid hitting the spikes and obstacles.  This would be an excellent game, if not for one key component missing from all puzzle games of this type: The ability to drop pieces faster.  In essence, if you spend 15 minutes on one attempt, to get a high score you will have to survive at least as long.  It really is a silly element to miss, as it has been around since Tetris, and has been included in absolutely every other falling block style game made afterwards.  If it weren't for that, this would have been a much better game.

Looks very much like Tetris Attack and other "Match 3" grid-based puzzle games, but this time there's a controllable character involved who's INSIDE the puzzle area!  Blocks are shot to destroy them (with adjacent matches destroyed at the same time), creating an ever-shifting landscape to traverse as the player dodges spikes from below and traps falling from above.  The goal of the normal game is just to survive for as long as possible (each level containing different traps and visuals), with unlockable challenge levels placing traps in set locations for a very difficult platforming gauntlet.  The game is loads of fun to play, taking two seemingly unrelated genres and mixing them together in a seamless and easy-to-understand way.  It does suffer from some laggy/glitchy issues that can ruin a run at the worst possible moment, though.
NOTE:  The game also has multiplayer in some form, but I have never played it and thus cannot comment.

The game is all about twitchiness, response time and speed, so this can get quite frustrating.
Neat little game, what you see is what you get, but just know going in that the best way to play is with a keyboard. That didn't work out great for me, so I can't recommend it, but if that works for you going in don't let this review dissuade you!

A lot of people have asked me to write a review on this game. I'm really not a review kind of guy - in fact I think I've only done one review before this. However, having played rally games since 1998, perhaps my input can be of some aid to those who are hesitant to spend money on this title. I also have 1777 hours played in Dirt Rally. I feel that this helps a little in forming my opinion on the game.
I'll keep it simple. I will list the pros and cons. While subjective, I don't feel like they're biased because I love the DiRT team, though perhaps because I love rally titles.
Let's start off with the pros.
·Rally school. (or DiRT academy I guess) is highly informative and will teach you some really helpful techniques, narrated by Jen Horsey. No matter how experienced you feel in the art of rallying, it certainly can't hurt to brush up on your skills. I picked up on a couple of things myself I never thought I'd be able to do.
·The improvement of handling over DiRT Rally. This includes cars having actual weight, improved aerodynamics (no more randomly bouncing off protruding rocks at the roadside, no more mid-air turning when taking jumps at an angle), more realistic braking distances. The DiRT team have done their homework, and it shows. It feels amazing regardless of what car I am using. Mind, I'm not exactly a fan of modern cars, but so far even those have been enjoyable to me, which was unexpected.
·Career mode. By far the best one I've ever seen in a rally game - and I haven't even played through it yet! I think I came about halfway (40 hours played on a separate account upon recieving an early press release key), so it will take a while. You can choose whether to compete with your own (handpicked!) team, or be a driver for hire and race for other teams. You can improve your staff, as well as upgrade your staff's facilities. Nice one, Codemasters.
EDIT: How could I forget to mention this! You get to choose your own team name! You also get to choose team colors for your car, as well as numbers, patterns... your name will be put on the side window of your car (or the front fender, depends on the car!), and you can also choose what colors these should be! There's so much lovely customization here.  You can choose up to four separate colors for your team's livery, and whether they should be gloss, satin, or matte to the finish. There's also metallic and carbon finishes.
·Upgrade system. This too is a massive improvement over Dirt Rally. The cars no longer have bad performance as you buy them; they're quick from the word get go. The upgrade is of their parts. Bad parts makes them more prone to breaking down or cause issues on the stages. Good parts last longer and will not break as easily. And it really makes a massive difference. I will give a prime example; I attended the weekly Group A event last week (before game release), with a sh*tbox Ford Escort Group A that I had bought used for an owners' club daily. The game warned me that its equipped parts were substandard, but I didn't take much note of it. By my logic, as long as I was driving well, the car would hold up. Nuh-uh. Halfway through the rally, my rear suspension collapsed! I later learned that it was both of the rear springs that had snapped. I had to drive over 5 kilometers with this and it was the most agonizing and amazing virtual rally experience I've ever had.
·Damage system. If my above story didn't convince you, I don't know what will. It's just on a completely different level than Dirt Rally. Driving through night stages with bad parts in your car can be especially interesting. Lights can start flickering randomly, or cut out completely. The intercom between you and you co-driver can also stop working at times. You will have misfires even though you're fresh out of service. Yesterday I was on Twitch, and saw Quirkitized become absolutely thrilled as he wrecked his first career event by plowing into a tree at speed and being forced to retire.
·The immersion. I have driven through stages where birds near blocked my view, where helicopters actually did block my view by blowing up dust in my face. Animal crossings. Drivers waving for me to slow down, because they've broken down or crashed ahead. Low-flying drones nearly clipping my car. The co-driver moving his (or hers) lips when talking. The look of commitment on the drivers' face. Driving up to the marshal after crossing the finish line. The service area; the fact that you can clean your car between stages! It all adds up into a beautiful experience.
·The improved graphics. This seems to be one of the topics people moan most about, but like it or not - the graphics really are improved. I've seen enough Dirt Rally to know this without any doubt in my mind. The reflections are beautiful, the lighting is gorgeous. Textures are crisp. Granted, I cannot max the details in this game, but someday I will...
·Your stage. It's better than I expected. I've enjoyed many, many stages from this tool and put on Youtube - and there'll be more to come!
·Improved sounds. These become most apparent when using dashcam or headcam, but they've improved the noise of several cars as well. The Ford RS200, Lancia Delta S4, Lancia Delta Integrale, Seat Ibiza Kitcar, Lancia 037, Peugeot 205 T16... to name a few.
·The soundtrack. I'm liking all the music I've heard in the game so far, and that's rare. Especially in a rally game.
·Improved force feedback. I set it up the same way I did in Dirt Rally, and it feels a lot better; more refined. I especially like it on tarmac. I feel the car perfectly through the wheel.
If you'd like good wheel settings, take a look at gheeD's & Kakkela's guide here:
I think that's all for the pros. Now for the cons, of which I can think of three... plus a tiny one.
·The rear end grip. It's a little too much, and it regains way too quickly after performing a handbrake turn, or any kind of slide really... why they've done that I cannot fathom, but I am fairly confident that we will see a fix of this. If not... well, I'll probably keep playing, but be a little disappointed as well.
·Sweden. It's a little too dumbed down and simple now. I wish for punishing snowbanks, but now you can just drive over them like it's nothing. It is not my favourite location thanks to this, so I choose Wales as my favourite instead.
·The tarmac. While they did improve the feel of the cars, and the FFB (massively!) - watching the replays, the movement is still off. It feels good, but looks wrong. Pretty much. I shouldn't be bothered about movement, but I just am. Shame on me.
·Please let me disable the mouse cursor! :D
Well, I hope this review has been helpful to somebody.

This game is pretty fantastic.
Pros:
+ I dig the graphics (Lighting effects are superb, character models are interesting, and nothing looks shabby)
+ I dig the sound (the accuracy of the sound effects, in specific, make the game really immersive)
+ I dig the combat (Axe/sword/hammer swings "feel" like a solid connect, ranged combat is about skill, and nothing is super easy. You can die at any moment if you aren't on the ball)
+ I love the feel of the game  (I feel paranoid of things sneaking up on me in other games now because of vermintide).
+ I dig the character progression through gear (as opposed to games that are similar, which have none at all or just kind of drop the ball on this).
+ The voice acting is superb (and often funny, which is hard to do in a horror/suvival game I think).
+ It's a DAMNED GOOD Warhammer game (which seem to be few and far between).
Cons:
+ The community is sparse late at night (really not a big deal)
+ The randomness of the drops at the end of missions can be super frustrating or can make your night. Tends to be tedious if you like to play a specific character.
+ A few bugs here and there. Nothing game-breaking, but one exploit on the "Horn" mission really needs to be fixed.
Conclusion: Buy the game. On sale, full price, doesn't matter. It's Left4Dead2 meets Borderlands meets Diablo in a Warhammer Fantasy setting. Unless you kinda hate fun, you won't be disappointed.

I went into CoD: Ghosts with low expectations. "One of the worst in the franchise", "Garbage", "Awful" was all I had read or heard. After playing through the single player campaign, maybe the review calling this "One of the worst in the franchise" was right. But in a franchise I enjoy as much as CoD, the worst in this franchise still makes for a pretty fun game. CoD Ghosts takes you to the near future where oil rich South American countries form "The Federation" in order to take over the world. Your team of specialized soldiers AKA Ghosts are one of the last lines of defense. I felt Ghosts was kind of unique in that there are 18 levels which take about 20 minutes each to finish.  And all the hallmarks of the CoD franchise are here. Great gunplay. Big set pieces. Globe trotting level design. The maps are super varied. Wanna kill stuff, in the deserts? Check. How about the Jungle? Yep. Underwater? No problem. SPACE?!?! YES!!!!11 I really had a good time playing CoD: Ghosts. Was it perfect? No. The CoD formula is maybe a bit TOO familiar, the load times are pretty bad and the story was forgettable.  Would I pay full price or even 50% off MSRP? Absolutely not. I bought a key for under $10 and that was totally worth it. Overall CoD: Ghosts gets a hearty recommendation from me. The gun play, varied levels and set pieces were enough to satisfy. 7.5/10 from me.

Ylands is a great low poly game filled with expansive landscapes, beautiful weather systems and intelligent AI. The game strives to give be a hyper realistic survival simulator where you can interact with anything in the game and use it to your advantage. Where as most survival games offer you the "fight or flight" option, Ylands forces you to fight for your life in most situations and this is something I love. In what world can a human outrun a panther?
The crafting system is where this game truly excels. The crafting system is very intuitive and when you finally get the materials to craft what you want, it feels incredibly rewarding. Instead of being able to just build what you want, you have to build the components and then the completed item. This adds many more hours of potential gameplay. While most materials are found in abundance others are very scarce and require time and patience to search out; such a coal.
Another things that I can appreciate is how the weather affects your character. Stuck in a cold or hot area of the game? Enjoy watching your screen strobe for the next 20 minutes while you attempt to find your way into a more 'normalized' climate. Players must constantly be aware of this and work around the conditions presented to them by either clothing their character properly, building fires, or taking shelter.
The last thing I would like to address is the exploration aspect of the game. Finding randomly generated chests or structures around the world is exciting and when you crack the puzzles requires to enter/open them it feels like you're really making progress.
All in all I would say this game is incredibly well designed and I look forward to spending many more hours pondering over the mysteries that the world has to offer.

Don't get me wrong, levels 1 and 2 are great fun. Kills are satisfying and the games are entertaining. Getting that new gun, or jeep, or grenade is a great achievement and you will have even more fun using it. Then you unlock level 3....
You are then given a choice of Tank Gunner or Infantry. Ofc everybody is like YEAH TANK until they find it costs about 71x their current money and you will likely lose money in level 3.
So you enter a battle as Infantry. You get on a bike to cross the map faster and you get headshot by somebody the other side of the map out of your sight. So you try a new tactic of being stealthy and attacking the sniper, except you are FORCED to go through a chokepoint of some sort and you will most likely explode. You then you go to capture a point, but find that they have a single invincible tank firing its 1-hitting machine gun at you.
I really want this game to be good. Levels 1-2 were good. Level 3 is not fun. At all.
They give you an amazing, fun experience and finish it off with a terrible one to try and lure you into buying some op stuff so you can live longer than approximately 13 seconds.
And for those of you wondering: once you get to level 3 you cannot go back to level 1-2 without creating a new account, even if you have another level 1 guy you get put with higher levels.

An unique and fun game that kind of feels like a combination of Tetris and the platforming genre.
In short, you pick an outfit and each outfit has different stats and abilities, then you pick a level. On each level, you have to destroy colored blocks to obtain items that will power up your character as you accumulate them. Attacking a block of a specific color will damage all nearby blocks of the same color and they're all destroyed together. As you play, the game will be constantly throwing more blocks for you to destroy (and sometimes the game will throw entire rows at the same time), along with certain traps like cannons and dynamite levers. Also, you can't ever clear all blocks because the bottom is filled with spikes. There is no way to beat a level, you just try to get as far as you can while collecting stars to unlock the next levels.
Besides the usual levels, there are also challenge levels where you just have to survive for a certain number of seconds while the game throws multiple traps at the same time in a pre-designed pattern. And there is actually one thing at the very end of the game, which I won't spoil openly. But for those who want to know:
There is also a splitscreen multiplayer mode where players compete with each other, destroying blocks in their screen in order to send more blocks to the opponent and seeing who survives the longest.
Not much to mention in terms of cons, really - it's a well done and fun game.
Certainly recommended.

Disclaimer: I have not played multi-player, or Co-Op. So far Story Mode only which I have beaten. If you want the short of it skip down to summary.
First off performance. This game suffers from some pretty bad stuttering. After searching around on the forums this appears to be a big problem due to poor optimization and it being a bad console port. I assure you my hardware is definetly not the problem (4.0ghz Quadcore Skylake Processor, 16gb of 3200mhz DDR4 RAM, and a AMD R9 290 Graphics card with 4gb of memory. The game was also installed on an SSD). Everyone's solution, especially for people like me with Radeon Graphics Cards, was to downgrade to DirectX 9. I did and after tweeking a few settings the stuttering stopped for most of the time but I still see massive performance drops (down to 5 fps!) occasionally. It seems to happen in some areas of the game while others are perfectly fine. And even when I am not having that issue, the game will not constantly stay above 60fps, even on the lowest graphics settings. It averages around 75 to 125 fps on relatively high settings but dips down to as low as 45 briefly. That's pretty pathetic since games much older than this looked better and ran smoother on older hardware and software using the same engine. This game came out, what, 4 years ago?
The gameplay is fun and the main quest line is entertaining, but like most Ubisoft games it quickly turns into a process of wash, rinse, repeat. Outside of the main story you spend most of your time climbing towers to unlock your map, then go kilI the pirates to liberate their camp, do it again. Throw in some "go here and kill this guy/animal" quests here, add a couple of racing or gun challenges there and you have Far Cry 3. The story content was very good over all but the ending felt a little rushed. You spend so much time fighting your way through the first half of the game to just have the second half go down like a row of dominos. I also got the feeling you were supposed to develop stronger feelings and relationships with the friendly characters than I did but there was such little interaction with them I ended the game not feeling drawn to any of them and didn't feel strongly about making a big choice between two groups of friends at the end of the game. You spend much more time learning about and interacting with your enemies which are very well developed. Not the most sinister villians I have ever seen but they most certainly will make most people's skin crawl. Each one crosses lines and is horribly sick in their own unique way.
By the end of the game I was still unable to find a fix for the performance issues and the fact this problem has not been fixed is insulting to the consumer. It's bad enough the standard is to release unfinished games to the public but to not fix them after release? I really hate to give this game a bad review because the voice actors, the writers, the people who designed the environment, they all did a phenomenal job. It was the programmers and the bean counters who forced them to rush that dropped the ball. Push come to shove though, I don't care how good the game is because having this game still so buggy after all these years is pretty much a scam. So it has to be a Thumbs Down. I still recommend playing it though if you can get it at the right price ($5.00 or less sounds about right to me) and you have some good hardware to play it.
Summary: Gameplay is moderately entertaining, the story is interesting, and the antagonists are well developed characters who you love to hate. However poor performance makes it a chore to play this game at times, the personalities of the protagonists allies were somewhat lackluster, and the ending feels a tad rushed.

Beautiful game. Very unique style that, for the most part, works well with the game, conveying cones of vision and cover/shadows well (with some exceptions).
The music sounded really nice, but I can't say I like that way it was implemented into the game. A suddenly epic "thump" when you get sighted is completely out of touch with the rest of the music, and gets very repetitive as you play along... Didn't help with the flow at all, in my opinion, quite the contrary.
Ok, the game itself. Not a fan either... A big part of that may be because I just decided to try it, without any motivation to do so. That said, what I saw didn't seem particularly impressive or original.
The game itself is solid, mechanically. You have a wide array of different gadgets that I can imagine being put into creative use. Some of them. The biggest problem is how the game compartmentalizes them into sets of levels/obstacles.
The game is incredibly linear in 2 different levels: how you simply go through 100 levels, one after another; how each level itself is very linear, consisting of going around it collecting gems to open the exit, and then reaching the exit. There are "lore" pieces throughout, but these follow the same linear path as the gems do. They don't provide an extra layer of challenge or detours.
Back to the creative use of gadgets. As the levels are very linear, the game gives you some levels with gadget X, and then moves on to Y. Then to Z, etc. They don't really overlap (with very few exceptions). What this ends up meaning, is that some gadgets are essentially redundant. Their functions overlap, with some being objectively better than others in similar functions.
This... is weird, but seems a natural progression for the compartmentalized nature of the levels, I guess. Since each item is isolated, their functional overlap isn't really a problem.
This plays a large part in what we're used to with Stealth games, then? Where you're presented a fairly solid challenge, but then can combine a wide array of tools to overcome it. This to say you expect very different tools and ways to combine them.
The main think I dislike is how linear it is. It's just a set of small challenges. There are no optional objectives (like not getting seen, getting extra data, incriminating someone, etc. etc.), the point is really just following the planned path of each level and moving on to the next one. It made the game incredibly boring, to me.
That said, I think this may appeal to people who are very into stealth games. Assuming you like the game loop a lot, you'll probably want to constrain yourself to never getting seen, completing the levels faster, etc. This is all fine, and I hope this is the real point of the game?
Because otherwise, if you're expecting to be surprised, there isn't much here. The levels are too short, and the enemies too transparent, which creates some silly moments.
Some people called this a puzzle game, more so than a stealth game. But then, you'd expect that most levels required a certain element of "outside the box" thinking, using the gadgets in unpredictable ways to overcome a particular challenge. And then building on it, etc. etc. But that isn't really the case. The game seems to guide you for the whole set of 100 levels. There might be some slight deviations for each player, but the levels' paths are mostly telegraphed, and don't really require much experimentation and "aha!" moments.
Anyway.
I don't know, maybe I just wasn't in the right mindset to enjoy this game.
If there's anything to take from here (in my perspective) is the artstyle. That was pretty amazing. Both when levels start and when enemies attack you, the way it affects the geometry looks really great! And, in general, I liked the way the game looked.

The pinnacle of the downfall of the once acclaimed franchise,
manages to showcase why regular Call of Duty style gameplay,
something more in order to be truly successful.
As always my experience reflects the singleplayer campaign and nothing more.
So, lets start of by saying that visually the game is pretty good, even for the standards of this period. That is not say it's the prettiest title you'll ever see, there are some low-res textures here and there and some explosion effects look dated, but for the most part the environment and shading visuals are pleasing to the eye. The guns themselves look and feel great to use and there's plenty of variety to find during the campaign.
Gameplay wise... well it's CoD so here we go again. Quick time and scripted events, shooting galleries, vehicle combat, yada yada, we've all done it so many times in the past and while there's a certain fun factor to the game, I still felt bored during some of the things I've experienced many-a times before. There's the addition of Riley, an attack dog, who you will only experience in less than 20% of the games' standard 6 hour campaign. Riley is gimmicky, albeit interesting at times, and serves nothing more as cheap padding to the heavily flawed campaign of Ghosts. You can control the dog during a few specific missions where he will instantly kill enemies with a neck bite, seeming more like a rabid animal and less like a faithful companion. For me that felt really awkward and totally out of place for a CoD campaign but to each their own. Some of the missions have very interesting settings (space and underwater) which add a certain degree of immersion but upon reflection there's also a sense of ridiculousness to them if you look at the whole picture.
Naturally, if you like the CoD style gameplay, there's really nothing more to evaluate a
Call of Duty game other than the story, characters and progression. And this is where Ghosts fails extremely hard.
The story is nonsensical to say the least and embarrassingly cliche at most. Characters and events are shoehorned in with absolutely none or minimal explanation, backstories are never explored and the premise feels completely 'alien' to any CoD veterans. So South America is the new boogeyman (bye bye Russia/China) and their new Federation is at war with the US. It seemed like Infinity Ward wanted to create something new after the Modern Warfare saga but their writers seems to have run out juice and have resorted in recycling the same material and tropes over and over again.
Bad guy wants revenge, blah blah, we've already
that before in any of the other CoD games. Nothing new, nothing groundbreaking, nothing to get you excited, just one minor twist at the very end of the game (with no explanation by the way) only to allude to a prospective sequel to the story. Thanks, but no thanks. The main antagonist Rorke is completely devoid of any depth, your friends are your typical 'badasses' elite troops with zero traits besides their tautological badassery and generally the only sort of likeable character turns out to the dog Riley, who again behaves in combat like a tiger on steroids.
To add insult to injury, there's even technical issues with the game. Huge loading times, even on SSD, stuttering during level loading, even some FPS drops here and there. Absolutely unacceptable for a game that's 4 years old running on a GTX980.
The sound design is good for the most part but the soundtrack is completely forgettable and adds nothing to alleviate the mess that is the storyline.
All in all, even as a die hard fan of Call of Duty singleplayer campaigns, Ghost left me utterly disappointed. While I did appreciate (for the most part) and tried to enjoy the same gameplay mechanics I've experienced since the very first game of the franchise, there's the need to spice things up a little bit, to experiment a little; usually the story, characters and music would be enough to give the game a thumbs up despite the repetition of the gameplay. However this is not the case for Ghosts. I really don't particularly care for any of the characters, for the story itself or if there's ever a sequel but for now I'm willing to forget this very forgettable addition to the series and move on to something else. Even if you're a huge fan like me, I wouldn't blame you if you skipped on this one.

The full price of $19.99 is a little expensive in my opinion however at 85% off during the summer sale this game is only $2.99 and it is well worth it. Door Kickers is a very nicely made strategy game with multiple classes of units such as assaulters with automatic rifles and breachers who carry a shield and are more resilient to enemy fire. When Starting a level you can attempt to plan the whole mission out from start to finish or micromanage your unitis in real time. You are also able to pause the action to adjust your plan if needed at any point during a level.

I consider this game a spiritual successor to the original Rainbow Six titles. You select your roster, change their loadouts for the mission, plan their points of entry and the paths they'll take during the mission, then you watch it all come to life. If you're quick enough, you can change your squad members' tactics on the fly in real-time, or you can just pause the action and make your adjustments from there. All in all, this game feels very good and it's easy to lose hours retrying one mission just to make it come out perfectly.
Unlike Rainbow Six, you actually have to unlock all of the different weapons and specializations which gives the game a bit of an RPG feel, if not a bit frustrating for people who immediately want to use an assault rifle. There's multiple stock campaigns, and a good amount of user-created content as well. If you're looking for a true spiritual successor to OG R6, and are willing to settle for top-down graphics, this game is for you.

Loading screen tips are grammatically poor and engrishy for some reason. My hair is clipping and wigging out, models clip constantly, the dialogue is *beyond* ridiculous.. like, I get it, it's a lot easier to write obnoxious tongue-in-cheek meta dialog than actual dialog, but there's a line where it's twenty times worse than just the same ol' "you're the great hero to save the world" shtick. It also strikes me as ironic that they immediately take jabs at spending the first portion of gameplay wading through tutorials.. and then proceed to make you listen to an obnoxiously written little "evil" demon drone on and on and on as a tutorial.
Visually it's decent if dated - I assume due to the cross platform aspect. Classes are stale as can be to begin - warrior/rogue/mage. Video options were mininal, and I found NO keyboard binding options, no mouselook settings, etc. So good luck if you want to change pretty much anything.
As is, I cannot recommend it. I'll readily admit it's mostly personal taste - maybe you can look beyond the positively idiotic dialog and find something interesting in yet another mage that shoots a DoT fire/stun lightning and pretty much nothing else. Each class appears to just have four skills and I don't see any kind of progression within said class from the UI or game's explanation. The animations look decent enough and there's some spell effects and all, but everything is just a bit off sync, causing it to lose any and all "oomph" that it may have visually. Maybe down the line when they actually DO add a bunch of classes and make them more interesting and the server errors and such calm down it'd be worth a poke, but that's only if you can stand what looks like some pretty stale MMO-style play with very limited skillsets and minimal-to-no progression.. and you can overlook some especially horrid writing. Other annoyances really confused me a bit, until I figured out what the heck was going on, mainly link-a-pix: it may appear to not having all the pairs - this is because it doesn't show the whole playfield, it's zoomed in on just a part of it.

Puzzler World 2 is, unsurprisingly, a framework for several different types of puzzles.
The Sudoku works, and lets you take basic notes, but it's not the best Sudoku game out there. The Crosswords are very difficult, because this is very obviously a UK-made game, and you would need a lot of UK-specific knowledge to solve them. Link-A-Pix puzzles are pretty neat, and the big ones get very challenging. The rest are too simple for an experienced puzzle solver, even at their hardest.
The interface isn't very good, but it works well enough. The puzzle instructions are insufficient, but most puzzles aren't that hard. The bonus puzzle/hint system is enjoyable, and necessary if you're not an expert at UK crosswords. Master Mode lets you cut right to the toughest challenges. There are definitely enough puzzles to keep you busy for a while.
This is definitely for puzzle fans only, but caters to beginners, casuals, and experts.

I can recommend this game on these two conditions:
1. You've played the first one and want more of the same, plus some new-ish puzzles; and
2. You can get it cheaper than £4.99 (I picked it up for, I think, 49p - which came with the first Puzzler World).
A reviewer has claimed that one of the achievements is glitched - it's not. I've gotten all the achievements in this game, so it's definitely not glitched.
Some good things:
1. Sudoku starts off with the 2×3 grids, as in the first Puzzler World, but after a few of these you start getting the standard 3×3 grids. I think this is a nice progression, which was lacking in the first one.
2. The music isn't quite as annoying as the first one, although the default volume is too loud (it can be changed).
There were a few annoying things in this follow-up to Puzzler World:
1. The Link-a-Pix puzzle are now zoomed in, and you have to pan up/down, left/right to see the whole puzzle - this cannot be changed, you cannot zoom out to 100%. Very annoying.
2. Some puzzles were pointless, such as the colour in puzzle or the fill in a piece with a dot puzzle - they require no skill at all.
3. Fitwords is weird - you can't type the answers. You have to 'grab' the word, then slot it into the grid.
All in all, I think even if you spend £4.99 on this game, you will get a heck of a lot of hours of puzzling with it. If you just want achievements, it'll take you a few leisurely hours. If you want all the in-game trophies (which are not part of the Steam Achievements), you'll basically have to finish the entire game!
I think there are worse things to spend £4.99 on, but only buy this if you enjoy doing things like word searches, crossword puzzles, sudokus, that kind of thing.

Far Cry 3 is one of those open-world games that actually makes you feel you'd want to explore the Rook Islands with its varied wild flora and fauna (hostile or indifferent), as well as the various enemies (pirates or privateers) and with the Rakyat assisting at times. The story missions are quite a lot of fun, and if you level up properly none of them are very difficult (i.e. do the stealth kills and try to take down outposts undetected to get extra XP for the skills).
You started out as a party guy Jason Brody, who can't do anything. Your brother Grant was the ex-Army, and somehow you ended up captured on this island held by pirates and right in the INTRO sequence your brother got killed and your mad dash to freedom ended up with you diving over a waterfall, but you lived, and you woke up in a village, and handed your first mission... and a wimply pistol... get up this tower on top of the hill, and activate it.
From there on, you steadily progress from a wimpy adrenaline junky to a fearsome killing machine capable of mowing down squads of professional mercenaries with LMG or assault rifle, hit wings off a fly at 100 yards with a sniper rifle, blade dance with professional knife fighters, stealth kill like a ninja, as you liberate the Rook Islands from two megalomaniacs, Vaas, and his boss, Hoyt, while recovering your friends one by one.
The islands are beautiful, and the animals behave independently of you. Goats and Buffalos and pigs and more wander the landscape, and predators like bears, leopards, even tigers wander the wild hunting them, and if you get in the way, you as well. In the ocean there are bull sharks and regular fish, and in the swamps there are crocodiles. Yes, it's a ton of fun exploring the place. There are small villages, pirate and merc outposts (that you can liberate... by killing everybody), unoccupied villages that were sites of atrocities, more radio towers you can deactivate, plus for the obssessive collectors, various artifacts to collect, such as 120 relics from the past cultures (including one from Chinese history!) letters from the Japanese WW2 occupation (plenty of bodies left around), memory cards left in outposts detailing the sordid narc industry links of Rook Island, as well as different animals and plants (they go in the survival handbook).
There are also untold number of caves, underground passages, leading to totally unknown areas deep within the bowels of the island that makes you wonder if you're playing Tomb Raider. :D Indeed, the radio towers and many other sequences do require a bit of jumping and climbing to accomplish.
Even on the surface, there are random things happening. Friendly and enemy jeeps patrol the routes. Enemy soldiers will patrol, and sometimes, force march prisoners / slaves on the road. You may engage, or not as you see fit, but they are excellent source of XPs, as valid as any one. And animals do roam the island, as it is wild out there.
There are plenty of side missions, some of which are handed out by locals, like "help find my daughter, who ran away with boyfriend!" in addition to the story missions. Furthermore, conquered outposts often have bounty missions (kill a pirate or a merc and his minions) as well as "path of the hunter" missions (hunt down X animals using provided weapons). (HINT: you only have to use the same CLASS of weapon, not the specific weapon. If they provide a regular .45ACP, bring your customized .44 Magnum or .50AE Desert Eagle)
Ah, speaking of weapons... lots and lots of weapons. Pistols, sniper rifles, shotguns, assault rifiles, grenade launchers, light machine guns, special weapons (including recurve bow), and signature weapons. Some weapons can be customized with different type of sights, extended magazines, even a suppressor. And there are different paintjobs available too. Add the oddballs, like repair tool (welding torch), flamethrower, and even a flare gun... and things can get interesting indeed. Did I mention that many vehicles have mounted weapons, like a HMG that you can wield?
How you tackle mission (usually involving killing everybody at a certain place) is entirely up to you. Run and gun? Snipe and hide? Silent and deadly? Lure and ambush? It is all up to you. When you have the best sniper rifle (.50 cal with suppressor two-stage zoom scope) you can kill even a heavy with a single shot to the head from afar. There are also sometimes captured predators that you can "liberate" with a shot to the cage, thus letting it attack the enemies in the camp for you! Remember, bonus points if you were never detected (1500 xp instead of 500 xp).
I have tried many open-world games before, from Far Cry 2 to Mercenaries 2, from GTA 3 (and sequels) to many others. Far Cry 3 stands above the rest because it is so well balanced. it doesn't unlock too many skills (some require you to unlock via story missions) at once, no matter how much XP you accumulated. it also doesn't unlock the 2nd island until well past 75% point. At each point you are reminded of the stakes you're playing with... the lives of your friends that may still be in pirate's hands, and each and every one will be scarred for life. The villians are psychopaths, but interesting psychopaths. And the other characters that you meet? They all have their own motivations, which may or may not match your own.
Somehow, FC3 just struck the right balance between too "scattered brained", i.e. "Too many choices! What do I do now?" vs. "where's the freedom? I am bored, I want to do something ELSE"... And there are plenty of variety in the missions as well as outposts. On the hunt missions, you have to use the specified weapon class/type., which can be challenging, such as hunting tigers with a pistol, or bears with a shotgun. On the bounty missions, you are to kill the one or two "leaders" with your blade. The rest are up to you with no restrictions. Just keep in mind in late game there can be two leaders with a dozen minions around them, and killing them all can be a difficult endeavor, esp. if you can only knife the leaders.
The skills you learn are divided into three categories: crane, shark, and spider, which of which has a different "tree". As mentioned before, they are unlocked by progressing in the story missions and can be learned by spending "skill points" which are earned by every few thousand XP. And they add a lot of fun abilities, such as chain takedowns, knife throw take down, grenade takedown, double take down, death from above, death from below, and so on.
There are bazillion crates scattered on the island, each containing some artifacts and/or money. You can further loot the bodies (enemy or friendly) for more artifacts, many of which can be sold for $$$. If you have killed some fauna, you cna often skin them for making containers / slings for ammo, wallet, and so on, and it's the only way you can carry more weapons, more ammo, even more money. In fact, you can also craft herbal medicine from the plants you gathered (which are generically divided into "colored leaves", and you need X of Red and Y of yellow and so on. As you progress you'll learn other formulas, like animal repellant, hunting instinct (lets you see animals, even behind hills), as well as herbal medicine that just heals you, deep dive potion that lets you go below 60 meters deep, and more.
All in all, Far Cry 3 is a ton of fun with variety of missions, side mission, as well as plenty of freeform encounter play. The story of growth and one man's journey from wimp to hero is the story of the player. And THAT ultimately, is why it's so much fun.

You will get cornered between rising fireballs and a falling block you couldn't see for the text telling you how awesome you are, and as you jump free a fire trap block will conk you on the head, you'll teleport above it because of how the squash logic works, and instantly die.
Then you'll hit restart anyway because the soundtrack is so good.
It mixes so many different games that you can truly say it's an idea of its own.

The action takes place on one screen. You can move left, right, jump and fire. You first stand on two layers of blocks as blocks start to fall continuously from above. Your job is simple: avoid them, shoot them and don't die. A block takes 3 or 4 hits to be destroyed but all blocks of the same colour that are adjacent to each other explode in the blast. Destroy lots at once for a big score and don't hit the bottom - the spikes cause insta-death. Your quick-thinking decisions will involve where to fire from and which block of blocks to wipe out.
It's a pixel-art style kept simple. You have a map of an island which is your level-select screen. This has six unlockable areas denoting the six levels to play and the main idea is to try to get your best score on each and attempt to beat it with later playthroughs. Some players will attempt to crack certain conditions to unlock more characters.
This is a fast-paced game requiring quick-thinking and quick-reactions. One false move insta-kills you, often prematurely, and this unforgiving nature of the game can make things frustrating. Emotional players will need to be prepared to yell at the screen in despair on more than one occasion - and the fact that you need to wait through a load of animations to get back into the action after death, might just make stress levels worse. Despite this, most patient and balanced individuals will enjoy the blast.
4/5

Honestly I wasn't hoping for much when playing this game, just wanted a fun zombie shooter that I could play with a friend. It didn't need a bunch of bells and whistles, I just wanted it to be fun. Unfortunately the few times I've played it has been either boring, frustrating, and/or tedious.
The ammo seems to be a bit random, the first playthrough was fine. The ammo was a little scarce, but as long as you played slightly conservatively it wasn't a problem. The last 2 times playing the ammo was basically nil. I spent most of the game just running around the zombies because I didn't want to waste ammo (or using a bat)....and yet after 40 minutes of playing, my friend and I had only picked up 3 ammo total. Funnily enough one of the places we had to go to was a gun and ammo shop that we were supposed to "stock up" on to prepare for the level...and yet there was only one thing of ammo and every single weapon at the place had no ammo. That kept happening, I picked up 7 or 8 guns in a row  throughout the playthroughs which were ALL out of ammo and nothing to be picked up. It just became frustrating.
Another big complaint I have is that the maps are generally quite big, yet several areas have absolutely nothing in them (besides zombies). There are lots of deadends and places that just serve no purpose at all other than to make the map look bigger. You have to search for a single item or location, yet the maps are so big that it just feels incredibly tedious making progress/finding items in the game. You go to one location, are told to find said item, have to go to the other side of the map to grab the item, then go back to the inital location to activate it or trigger something, and so the cycle continues.
Then in my most recent playthrough my friend and I were stuck for about an hour. We couldn't understand how we were possibly missing something, had gone through every single room and location at least three or four times. Finally we googled a walkthrough, and turns out that a door that was supposed to be triggered opened just didn't work. It glitched out for some reason, we rewent through the steps (that we previously had done correctly) and nothing would fix it, so we were just about to quit out of the game...when it crashed. That basically sums up how well my experience has been when it comes to Contagion.

This is another game where I wish you had a third option besides just yes/no. But since I do not think it's a yes then I have to choose no.
This game has way too many flaws to recommend which is a shame because I think it expanded on Left 4 Dead by adding different types of game modes and being able to ADS.
The biggest problem with the game is that it crashes all the time. If you finish a game and decide to switch to another server "crash". If you are waiting for the next round "crash". It crashes at least once every game session I have with it. I have friends who play and it happens to them also.
The other problem are bugs/glitches in the game. For example, in extraction mode survivors can get stuck and will not move, even if you tag them to follow you. I've had this happen on numerous occasions. Other times they just get stuck on ladders and you have to go all the way back when you realize they're not following you to tag them to unfollow then tag to follow again but take a different route so they don't get stuck on ladders again. Another problem with extraction is the route to lead the survivors doesn't always show up on the phone. So you're left wondering which way to go. Then there are glitches where you get stuck yourself and basically have to kill yourself to get free.
Other issues are gameplay issues. There is no mini-map. I don't have a huge problem with the concept of not having it except you have no idea what to do and where to go on a bunch of maps. The hints on the phone aren't helpful. For example on Roanaoke PD there are a couple of escape routes in the game. I'm not going to give anything away except that once you find the armory it doesn't tell you what to do next so you're left roaming around until you get somewhere that triggers the next hint. Obviously after you've played it you now know but for new players they'll have no idea and this is a long play session map. It's just annoying. If there were at least arrows or something to point you in the right direction that would be helpful.
While I do enjoy playing this game with friends, I think until some of these major issues are fixed I can't recommend this game. Some of these have been complained about for a long time so odds are this game isn't going to be improved. If you get it on a cheap sale it might be worth it otherwise there are better zombie games out there.

This is my first review and because I enjoyed this game I figured It was a Decent place to Start. I appologize if its to long or seems a bit haphazard.
Vermintide is a very compelling and enjoyable first person slasher that is pretty much a blend of Chivalry, Killing Floor and  Left 4 Dead, that is set in the Warhammer fantasy Universe. Having played each of the five classes and completed the first five missions, I am still amazed at how ballenced each class is, although at the start some classes are easier to play than others. Players must utalize each characters unique weapon set and cooperate in order to prevail. Normaly having a class that take practice to become decent would be a problem if there were only 4 four charecters like in L4D, but thankfully you have five characters to chose from so you will always have two characters to choose from (the one your currently play as along with whichever class is open). This means you wont be "stuck" playing a character no one else wants.
Your level applies to all five characters, but as far as i have can tell, ranking upgains you two things. every rankup grants you a weapon, and once you reach lvl 33 you earn better weapons after each rankup. As for the gameplay, it is truly spectacular. When playing this game I actually fear for my life as a horde of rats pour from the sewers and surround my triends and I, and we realize there is nowhere to run, or when my team stupidly angers a patrol of stormvermin and they stop there marching and let out a screaching battlecry as they charge towards us. I have enjoyed most every game I Have played thanks to the stunning level design and the brutal melee combat. For me at least  I find the story gripping and immersive, if not a little repetitive, but like Killing Floor, Vermintide turns the repetative rat slaying into the driving factor that has you wanting more.
There are however two major problems I have encountered when playing this game.
First of which is that i have found that if i want to actually finish a level, you either need a very cooperative team (unlikely) or you need to play a private lobby with friends. That being said L4D had the same problem so ive gotten used to it, but its still a problem.
The second issue is related to the console or PC you are playing vermintide on. If you are like me, and have a gaming computer, then you might encounter some serious FPS problems if you set everything to max. Even with most of the extras turned of or on low there are some parts of the game, Primarily large rat hordes that drop my framerate down to very frustrating 12-15 FPS. Like Dead island vermintide requires solid CPU and GPU in order to play at max video settings.
Even with those problems which, although they are problems, dont really take away from the masterpeice that is Vermintide.
Overall i would give Vermintide: End Times a 8/10, and would Recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a decent first person slasher.
(this is based on soly on my experience playing this game by no means reflects what other players experience).

NOTE: most of Vermintide's failings have nothing todo with the actual game itself, Which is a 10/10, but like most online Co-op progression based game there is a  50/50 chance that you are paired with competent and cooperative teammates.

Like many of us, I got angry at this game at release day. My mind was sooo set on Dirt Rally's aura as a rally simulation and it's non-flashy appearance. First I hated Dirt 4's menus and the whole idea of pleasing everyone. Also the gravel physics were way off IMO. Refunded the game and "cried" for few days. Then watched some youtube videos, read people's comments and decided to purchase the game again. Wanted to know why people actually like it so much. My expressions of the game so far (21/7/2017):
Pros:
+ It's FUN on a controller in gamer mode. Just pick up the controller and GO!
+ Audio is fantastic!
+ Rallycross and asphalt physics are greatly improved.
+ Spain is sooo much better than Germany in DR.
+ Rain, fog etc. weather effects are one of the best out there.
+ Your stage is easy to use and it makes it easier for guests to compete against me in rally.
+ Performance is fine on single screen (i5 7600k + 1060 GTX).
+ Graphics are actually quite nice when you turn them high enough...
Cons:
- ...but the graphics also need a bit of tweaking. I have problems running this pretty enough on triples. Dirt Rally looks just fine on triples and the performance is great. In Dirt 4 you have to turn AA pretty high to get rid of the jagged edges. There is too much performance cost over the gained graphics upgrade compared to DR. Also (personal preference) I'd like to see less cartooney look, as in Assetto Corsa.
- Wales and Australia are too colorful on sunny conditions. Wales looked better in DR.
- Repetitive Your Stage. Stages don't feel natural. They're just a line of seqments. Compare the codriver in DR and you'll hear the difference.
- You can't map two controllers at the same time. For example I have to connect th8a shifter through my t300. It won't work in USB mode together with the wheel. FIX THIS! In DR everything worked just fine.
- The rear end of the car is too grippy. Just look at the replays on youtube. Cars with high horsepower WILL lose their tail on gravel. Now there's not enough throttle control on 4WD cars.
- FFB feels wrong to me. It was the same in Dirt Rally on it's Early Access phase (The worst con IMO). FFB feels like there's a lag of some sort. Can't really feel the nuances of the road.
Conclusion:
Hope Codemasters are listening their customers and attend to those well known problems with future updates. I don't think Dirt 4 is worth 55€, but if you can get it 40% off and you have a pc that can run it on high/ultra graphics then meh, why not. I don't usually play with a controller, but this game rocks with it in gamer mode! All in all gamer mode is great. Simulation mode needs to be updated and lots of things fixed. Honestly I think they'll make another game rather than fix this.
At this point in time, this game is not worth the full price if you're looking for a Dirt Rally replacement. Refunded.

As a sequel to the first puzzler world (hence the 2 at the end), I think it adds to the original premise of 'a ship load of puzzles' and expands on it adding new games and tweaking existing ones. Whilst some of the games have been tweaked to be 'easier' to play, personally some of them were a little annoying, such as having to drag around link-a-pix as it zooms in really close. Would really appreciate it if they had a zoom function on it to put it to how it was in the first puzzler world. Of course this allows for bigger puzzles (such as the ones featured in the master mode.
Also implemented is the tokenator, or the spinnywheeltokengame which whilst it appealed to the 'ooh spinny thing' side of me, the token animations take about twice as long as the original puzzler world, which were just a little too long for my liking in the first one. No skipping this either so, everytime you beat a puzzle, you have to spin the wheel, wait for it to stop, watch the token bounce around for a bit and then redeem and then see all the tokens pour out like a game of coin solitaire. Whilst this is flashy, and probably what most of there budget went onto, slows everything down especially if you're going through puzzles fairly fast (some of them can be done in 10-15 seconds, such as the silhouette (I don't quite understand that game either?)).
One thing that is amazing and probably makes this all okay is that you can spin the wheel backwards! Yes people, backwards compatibility! (Insert new-gen console jokes here).
Some features they haven't included though such as screen resolution, it looks terrible even on my 1080p screen so windowed is the only way to go if you are a low-resophobe. I have puzzled on it full screen and it's not too distracting but it looks much nicer windowed.
Also, whilst the in-game trophy system are a great incentive to actually clear all the puzzles, something the first one lacked as I stopped playing after about 200 (will return when I beat this though... probably), I feel a little let down with the steam achievements. Exactly the same as the first in requirement, I don't see why they couldn't have just linked the trophies with the steam achievements... This would've also removed the fact that there's no point in beating more then 10 of each puzzle in the original.
I got this in a bundle (with the original) and probably paid about 20p for it. For 40 hours and only halfway complete (my GCSE maths tell me that it would therefore take about 80 hours, without taking the exponetionally rising difficulty of levels in further stages and brie, tea and wee breaks (I'm so british). Adding all that in could be around 100 hours). 20p has never seen so much mileage. Even at a fiver, you'll be stuck to find a game that will last you a good 80 hours!
Despite some flaws, this simple game gives you a lot for a little, you'd be mildly braindead to not see the value in that!

Hotline Miami 2 is an ambitious take on its predeccesor. Adding a large scale story to what was originally a small scale game. The issue here is, bigger isn't always better. Hotline Miami 2 suffers from far too many changes without any effort put towards sharpening the feel of the first game. Levels are more open ended, leading to more off screen deaths and seemingly less stealthy approatches. The storyline has been strectched to a giant plot with a dozen new characters and locations. The only problem is, the story jumps from each of these moments and persons so rapidly that every area and character seems underdeveloped. We never get any quality time with any of these peices, and the mask selection has heavily restricted as to put the game and the player on rails. Now I'm not saying rails are necessarily bad, but this train seems to go nowhere. As complex and intricate as the story is the narrative still follows the vauge, dream sequence style delivery from the first game. Only now the player has to keep track of names and locations to understand what is going on, great. Even when armed with a notepad and a wiki page I still don't finding a plot with any real meaning to it. So if the story fails to deliver on its goals, what was the point of restricting player choices and breaking the flow of the level proggression? That is the point that I rest on with Wrong Number. For a tighter and sharper expierience, stick with the original. While I give props to Dennaton for the risk they took in attempts to create a deeper meaning in the Hotline Miami franchise, I cannot say I'm a fan of the compromises their ambitions created.

EDIT - apparently 20 minutes doesn't justify this review as vaild. If we ignore the psychology of making snap judgements and the fact I know what kind of games I like, I'm going to give a longer review based on my short time and explain how I game to my conclusion of "not good", why I don't feel someone else would enjoy it. This doesn't make me a hater, because I really enjoyed the 2D Adventure Quest.
THE GAMEPLAY:
You move with W/S, and A/D turns the camera around behind you. You can also move the camera around with the mouse. Basic click on things, do actions based on what said thing is. Collecting loot is annoying, with no real feedback on if you actually picked up the loot, and you can only pick it up by clicking on it, not by walking over it. In my short game time, I managed to get through the intro stage and to the main town. Enough to firgure out the gameplay was fairly standard drivel. Nothing exicting. Nothing fun. Nothing that got me hooked. I don't really have much to say other than I didn't enjoy it.
THE INTERFACE:
It's awful. You can tell it was designed with mobiles in mind, and then the interface for mobiles was just updated to work on PCs. Games can be designed to work on mobiles and ported to PC just fine - see Timberman, that was orginally a mobile game - and this game doesn't do that very well. The font is awful and I could notice some of the textures didn't scale nicely to 1980. Speaking of textures...
THE GRAPHICS:
I really liked the design and style of the 2D game. It looked good, and had a nice aesthetic to it. I'm not a graphics over gameplay kind of guy, and do enjoy games you could argure had poor graphics - Proteus, for example, or Moirai - however this game is selling itself as a MMO. That means it's hoping I'll play it loads. If that's the guess, I'm kind of hoping for something a bit better. It has PS1 esquie graphics, and not in the good way. I'm guessing this is because of the fact it's designed for mobiles.
THE WRITING/STORY:
You might feel I can't give a fair review of the story and I would 100% agree with you. I'm going to talk about it anyway. The writing is dire, cringe worthy and really unthoughtful. You can tell it wasn't done by someone who knew the first thing about writing. It's not even done in a casual way, just boring unfunny unwitty words on a screen. It didn't hook me in, it didn't want me to find out more or want me to play. It was just bad.
IN SUMMARY:
I find this game bad and I didn't enjoy it. If you played hours upon hours of the 2D game, then this is going to suck and you won't enjoy it. If you've never played Adventure Quest before, then who knows you may enjoy this, but it is nothing like the game it's based on. Personally, save your time and effort and try a different game.

This is a really fun, chaotic game to play.
You control a block-like creature that wields... probably a multitude of weapons, depending on the outfit you choose. Your goal is to platform the best that you can while blasting away the block obstacles and avoiding various deathtraps such as fireball shots, drills that destroy a column full of blocks, and many other traps.
The presentation is great. Hitbox is clear. The music is energetic techno, which for a fast-paced game that gets hectic, it's really beneficial.
Z and X are used to shoot, and the arrow keys are used to move your character, especially the up arrow key because that's also your jump key. Doing specific things while a stage is going on can unlock outfits. The outfits you choose before selecting the various stages gives you various abilities, such as a slower descent or a double jump. However, you have 3 stats; Jump (how high you jump), Power (How much damage you're capable of doing to the obstacles), and movement speed. Depending on the outfit, you get different stats, which adds a plethora of replay value. While the asthetics of choosing a stage are just asthetics, the types of traps you encounter vary from stage to stage. Playing through a different stage with a different outfit adds wonders to even more replay value.
There's multiplayer, but sadly, I can't play it because I only have one friend that has this game. However, it's a really fun, easy-to-pick up game that I recommend.

I cannot recommend this game in its current state. It's so close to being a respectable puzzle experience like Tetris, but it has problems that hold it back.
First, and most glaring, is that the text that pops up whenever you level up, level down, or destroy blocks will block your vision of falling blocks and traps. It is incredibly irritating to not be able to react to a falling trap because the game felt the need to say "groovy" in big annoying letters smack dab in the middle of the playing field. Or you couldn't position yourself just right to get out of the way of falling blocks because of the same reason. It's annoying, it's unfair, and it's unneccesary.
Second, the traps feel unfair most of the time. Not taking into account my previous complaint, in the fourth level, (Cookin' Caves) there are fire stick traps pulled straight out of Super Mario Bros. that limit your mobility severely. If you aren't blind sighted by the thing coming down, you'll be hard pressed to find a safe spot to destroy it. Sometimes even more will come down at once, limiting you to about 25% of the playing field. When I'm trying to setup large combos, avoid falling into spikes or lava, and move out of the way of falling blocks, it feels extremely unfair to have some kind of trap fall in and completely screw up your plans AND likely end your game.
My last big problem is that there is no way to push blocks around. Why not? It would only serve to make the game more enjoyable and give the player more control over the field. It would add greatly to the gameplay. Instead you have to wait around for blocks to drop into places you want them to. I can't tell you how surprised I was to find that such a potentially good feature was not in the game. Maybe one of the unlockable characters can, but that's no excuse. It should be available from the start.
Despite all this, the music is top notch and the graphics are really appealing. And when I wasn't getting screwed over by being blinded by text or unfair traps, I did have a good time. But it could be SO much better than this.

This game gets you on your toes and gets the general out of you that has been hiding inside of you for some time. You work your way up from peasant, to a feared general or even a king. The adventure is yours for the taking. Every action has consequences, every decision has different outcomes and the more important in the game you become, the more people you impact.
The mechanics of the game are great, you over see a map which you choose where your army goes and camps. On the way, you can recruit more men for your army, even having to supply them with food. You can see hordes of bandits, when battles are taking place and assist your allies in that battle if you choose. When you do, you can choose to just send your troops, or participate in the battle. Already before the battle, you have all of this freedom and choices you can make that impact your adventure. Afterwards, loot the dead bodies and sell the gear (that is what I always do).
The game is satisfying, it gives the player complete freedom to do whatever they want. The goal of the game? Its whatever you want it to be. You can capture a region and make it yours, you can become a general and command your army, stay as a small time mercenary or dominate the world. I recommend this game because of the freedom, the adventure and the impacts your choices have on your adventure.

Volume is a game developed and published by Mike Bithell and Bithell Games, the same person behind Thomas Was Alone. Volume is a top down stealth game where the emphasis lies on manipulating the guards' movements, rather than waiting for the right time to strike
The gameplay is at it's best when you're fluidly navigating around the map between multiple guards, distracting them and ducking into cover to get to your objectives. Sadly, only a quarter of the levels pull this off well, and the game suffers from some poor decisions later on; certain aspects, such as shadows and veil, simply seem to take more from the gameplay than they add
Ultimately, however, the stealth is satisfying, and the majority of the puzzlelike levels are fun to beat. My biggest gripe would be the low difficulty. The majority of the 100 levels are too easy, taking under five minutes each to beat
The game itself has a gorgeous art style and soundtrack, with a surprisingly decent story. I experienced only a single bug, and that was that the game first initialized with a very low resolution, in windowed mode, meaning I had difficulty navigating the menus to up the settings. After that however, the game played perfectly
If you want a distilled stealth experience, Volume is the game for you!
The music audio level when discovered is painfully loud. To counter balance it the music audio level has to be turned down so far that the music is basically inaudible the whole time. :/

This is my first review and because I enjoyed this game I figured It was a Decent place to Start. I appologize if its to long or seems a bit haphazard.
Vermintide is a very compelling and enjoyable first person slasher that is pretty much a blend of Chivalry, Killing Floor and  Left 4 Dead, that is set in the Warhammer fantasy Universe. Having played each of the five classes and completed the first five missions, I am still amazed at how ballenced each class is, although at the start some classes are easier to play than others. Players must utalize each characters unique weapon set and cooperate in order to prevail. Normaly having a class that take practice to become decent would be a problem if there were only 4 four charecters like in L4D, but thankfully you have five characters to chose from so you will always have two characters to choose from (the one your currently play as along with whichever class is open). This means you wont be "stuck" playing a character no one else wants.
Your level applies to all five characters, but as far as i have can tell, ranking upgains you two things. every rankup grants you a weapon, and once you reach lvl 33 you earn better weapons after each rankup. As for the gameplay, it is truly spectacular. When playing this game I actually fear for my life as a horde of rats pour from the sewers and surround my triends and I, and we realize there is nowhere to run, or when my team stupidly angers a patrol of stormvermin and they stop there marching and let out a screaching battlecry as they charge towards us. I have enjoyed most every game I Have played thanks to the stunning level design and the brutal melee combat. For me at least  I find the story gripping and immersive, if not a little repetitive, but like Killing Floor, Vermintide turns the repetative rat slaying into the driving factor that has you wanting more.
There are however two major problems I have encountered when playing this game.
First of which is that i have found that if i want to actually finish a level, you either need a very cooperative team (unlikely) or you need to play a private lobby with friends. That being said L4D had the same problem so ive gotten used to it, but its still a problem.
The second issue is related to the console or PC you are playing vermintide on. If you are like me, and have a gaming computer, then you might encounter some serious FPS problems if you set everything to max. Even with most of the extras turned of or on low there are some parts of the game, Primarily large rat hordes that drop my framerate down to very frustrating 12-15 FPS. Like Dead island vermintide requires solid CPU and GPU in order to play at max video settings.
Even with those problems which, although they are problems, dont really take away from the masterpeice that is Vermintide.
Overall i would give Vermintide: End Times a 8/10, and would Recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a decent first person slasher.
(this is based on soly on my experience playing this game by no means reflects what other players experience).
Rating Breakdown
NOTE: most of Vermintide's failings have nothing todo with the actual game itself, Which is a 10/10, but like most online Co-op progression based game there is a  50/50 chance that you are paired with competent and cooperative teammates.
Gameplay: 10/10
Co-op: 6/10  (Im tierd of playing with whinny 6 year olds)
Long term apeal: 10/10
Optimization: 9/10 (CPU issues mostly)

If you've seen my Hotline Miami review you'll know that it's one of my favorite games. When I heard that the 2nd one was confirmed, I tried my hardest not to get my hopes up too high. The first one was so good that it'd be near impossible to live up to... or so I thought. Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number blew me away. At first I thought it might be the fact that I might've just been expecting it to be good, but then I found myself clearing rooms with a pistol while a guitar riff started going off in the background and dismissed the the notion almost instantly.
Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number took all of the great aspects of the first installment such as the intense, fast gameplay, the action-movie grade music, and the pleasant graphics, then put all of those on steroids. The story wraps up nicely, answering most questions the first game asked, introducing a bunch of new interesting characters. Unfortunately since it does this, the game had to compromise the freedom to choose whichever mask you want on whatever mission you wanted to use it on, instead only allowing certain masks to be used on specific missions.
I definitely recommend this game to anybody and everybody that enjoyed the first game.

-Very often i'll move from point to point with enemies in plain sight and not fire at them
-Very often I'll be firing at an enemy but for some reason will disengage and move on to next point regardless of the fact that the not killed enemy is still firing at me
-Cannot set rotation points at key spots (like, doors/breaching), which makes the "Live Play" or "Finish in a single set of waypoints" objectives near impossible without just random dumb luck of the positioning of the enemies upon entering a room

My experience so far in singleplayer...
Pros:
-Great Gameplay
-Chock full of different items and costumization options for your character and structures
-Plenty of time can be spent in just the exploration
-Beautiful graphics and scenery
-Weather is amazing and has a large impact on your gameplay
-Large and diverse Flora ecosystem
-Im able to run on ultra graphics without any stuttering or frame rate issues (at the beginning there were some but they went away) my computer isn't cheap though.
In Between:
-Fauna seems lacking
-In game shop, it only sells cosmetics so far though... (Skins, Emotes, ect..)
-Not very difficult in terms of fighting for survival and staying full, enemies tend to die pretty quick, and those that dont are rare and easy to avoid
Cons:
-Construction is very difficult to get perfect, not all the materials fit together properly, and building simple structures can be ugly and overly time consuming.  You could build a house, and if you dont get the perfect measurements for length and width, your house will end up looking shabby and will probably have holes in it.
-Complete lack of other "Human-Like" NPC's, finding a cabin or campfire but no person can be disappointing, though this is an issue that the devs have said they will resolve in future updates.
-Low optimization, or more like "Extremely" low optimization.  Despite being early access I will still put in here that this game is VERY buggy.  Your movement can be jumpy (as in your character randomly climbing up short trees and bushes will traveling).  While breaking things, like a fallen tree, you could end up chopping down a tree behind your character, or one 10 feet away.  The boats are also incredibly buggy, as there is a chance while jumping into one that you can randomly fall through the map.  Rope ladders (so far i've only seen this on boats) will somtimes end up teleporting you.  I would go up one rope ladder on a boat, and end up at the top of another on a different boat.  To fix this you need to destroy BOTH ladders and replace them (not a permanent fix), if you only destroy one, the ladder will end up teleporting you beneath the map.
-You can't set your spawn point (so far).  If you die you'll be put on the closest yland, and if you glitch out of or underneath the map (happens a lot), you have to /unstuck 1 which will take you back to your original starting point, that could be on a whole different yland.
-The horse call is a hit or miss.
TLDR:
In short, the gameplay is amazing and has so much potential, but the bugs are so frequent and frustrating that I must make this review a negative, until they fix the game.

I played this back on the gamecube when it was available. It was quite revolutionary back then as Sonic came out in full force in 3D and the tracks were no longer linear and some freedom regarding movement was given. I will say this about the PC version though, Sega definitely betrayed their gamers by not making this game complete and by adding DLC to it (which was common core to the old game - such as 2 players local).
In Sonic Adventure 2 you may play as the "good" side with Sonic (featuring Knuckles and Tails) or the "bad" side with Shadow, Eggman and Rouge). Although six playable characters in total, all have their own unique features in the game. Sonic and Shadow have speed runs where they run through a level. Knuckles and Rouge have sort of a free roam mode where they are able to glide/fly and use their powers to achieve whatever their goal is (activate 4 beacons for example). Tails and Eggman control their robot mech's which add a sort of total destruction to the game. Each level is uniquely different and it seems they really cared about what they did when making this. Emblems and Chao's are also available to collect throughout the game. Chao's can be sort of used as power ups but are treated as pets in a separate realm in game. I should add the two player modes are absolutely awesome (especially when racing one another on foot). Some of the game modes include action race, treasure hunt race (free-roam sort of thing), mech battle mode and lastly a go-kart sort of racing feature. Some modern day gamers may become tired of playing through a story mode with such a rhythm... then again, some how people are still buying CoD.
